monologue: It won’t be long before we hear the pitter-patter of little devil worshipping weirdoes.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Elvis Presley would have been 75 today. He was a deputy in Nixon’s war on drugs. That’s like having Tiger Woods give out promise rings.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It was so cold in Washington D.C. today that Sen. Harry Reid actually enjoyed being in hot water.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Signs There's Trouble at NBC

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This weekend no one was seriously hurt, but a 6.5 earthquake hit California. The earthquake was so powerful that it knocked Jay Leno’s show from 10 p.m. to 11:35.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Everybody now wants to know what my plans are. All I can say is that I plan to continue putting on a great show night after night — while stealing as many office supplies as humanly possible.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid is under fire for discussing whether or not President Obama has a “negro dialect.” Reid is also in trouble for saying Joe Lieberman “talks all Moses-y.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NBC has some pilots to fill the 10 p.m. time slot. They are talking about bringing back “All in the Family,” with Harry Reid as Archie Bunker.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NBC said the show performed exactly as they expected it would, and then they canceled us. Don’t confuse this with when we were on at late night, performed better than expected, and then they canceled us, that was totally different.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In his weekly radio and Internet address, President Obama said, “We are on the verge of guaranteeing Americans health insurance whether they lose their job, change jobs, move, or get sick." Which means Jay, Conan and I are gonna be just fine.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Four TSA workers at Los Angeles International Airport were videotaped snorting drugs. It was the first time people had ever seen lines go that fast at the airport.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Sarah Palin just signed on to be a contributor to Fox News. She chose the job after carefully weighing her other option, “just going away.”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hello, my name is Conan O’Brien, and I may soon be available for children’s parties.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: NBC says they’re planning to have the late night situation worked out before the Winter Olympics start. And trust me, when NBC says something — you can take that to the bank!

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid is still under fire for remarks he made about President Obama’s “blackness.” Sources say Reid could face congressional censure, or even worse, be promised the “Tonight Show” at 11:30.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The CEO of Domino’s Pizza, Patrick Doyle, says their pizza has been bad in the past but they’re coming out with a new recipe. Perhaps, part of the problem is their pizza’s made by a guy named Patrick Doyle.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid got himself into hot water when during the election, he described Barack Obama as a “light-skinned African-American with no Negro dialect.” That may explain why Reid is the majority leader and not the minority leader.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama forgave Reid. Obama said today that he has nothing against really light-skinned people.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NBC announced they are pulling the plug on our show Feb. 12. Here’s the amazing part: That is the exact date that the Mayan calendar predicted we would go off the air.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Archaeologists in Egypt now say it’s not true that the pyramids were built by slaves. They say the pyramids were built by paid workers. You know how they financed it? A pyramid scheme.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Conan O'Brien said tonight in a written statement, that he will not do the Tonight Show after Jay Leno, which means he quit, I think. He also said he wants to make the Tonight Show the best it can be, which means he didn't quit, I think.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: An American comedy legend is calling it quits. He made us laugh for years, we followed him through his ups and downs, but he's made a decision to leave the pinnacle of American broadcasting. That's right, David Hasselhoff has quit America's Got Talent.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Jay Leno's back on at 11:30, people are getting their old jobs back all over the place. Dick Cheney's showing up at the White House like, "Hey! I heard you turned my dungeon into a breakfast nook!"

name: David Letterman
monologue: Conan O' Brien announced that he will not follow Jay Leno at 12:05 a.m. You know what that means: I knocked off another competitor.

monologue: Top Ten Highlights of Sarah Palin's First Day at Fox News

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Sarah Palin made her debut as a Fox News contributor tonight on The O’Reilly Factor. It's the darndest thing, though — I tried to record it, but my DVR quit halfway through.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A company in Texas has started a new social networking site for cowboys. The site would have launched earlier, but it took several days for a lawyer to explain to the cowboys that the name "Yahoo.com" was taken.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The New Jersey Senate just approved a bill to legalize medical marijuana, a week after New Jersey voted not to allow gay marriage. Which means the New Jersey Senate was like, “Gay people getting married? What are you, high? No? Well let’s get high then.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Simon Cowell announced that he is leaving American Idol. He says he wants to spend more time at home telling his maid she doesn't know how to do the dishes.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Sarah Palin is going to be a commentator for Fox News. Well, maybe now she can afford to buy some clothes for Levi Johnston.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Palin will be a regular contributor to Fox News. She signed a three-year contract, which means she'll be there for six months.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tiger Woods has not been seen since Thanksgiving. He's so hard to find, people are speculating that he may be working in customer service at Home Depot.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hi, I’m Conan O’Brien, and I’ve been practicing the phrase, “Who ordered the mochaccino grande?”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new TV Guide poll, 83 percent of voters want me to stay at 11:35. When he heard this poll number, President Obama asked, “How can I get NBC to screw me over?”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Natives on the Pacific island of Vanuatu recently apologized to the great-great-grandson of a missionary who their ancestors ate 170 years ago. Witnesses describe the conversation as “awkward.”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The other day in Turkey, villagers in a small town were shocked when a sheep gave birth to a calf with a human face. Sounds like there’s one guy in that town who has a lot of explaining to do.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Passengers aboard a United flight from Chicago to Newark broke into applause and called the pilot a hero when he landed the plane after a total landing gear failure. Then, of course, came the really dangerous part — the cab ride through Newark.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Cold weather all around the world. The heaviest snowfall in over 60 years is being reported in Beijing, China. People there are being warned not to throw snowballs because they contain lead.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sarah Palin has signed on to be a Fox News correspondent. In a related story, John McCain just picked up an endorsement deal to be a spokesman for the Scooter Store.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The former president of the Psychiatric Association of Quebec, Canada believes there are benefits to smoking. Especially if you work in the portable oxygen tank and funeral home industry.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There are reports that Tiger Woods has entered rehab for sex addiction. It's a standard process, 28 days, one for every mistress.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: For those of you that don't remember Tiger Woods, he's the guy we used to make fun of in the olden times before late night TV went nuts.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm sick of late night TV. Late night TV bores the crap out of me, and I think I prove that every night on this show.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Another black eye for baseball: Yesterday, Mark McGwire announced that he took steroids when he was on his big home run tear. He said they really didn't help his performance — he just took them because he enjoyed the fresh minty taste.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Messages on Jeff Zucker's Voicemail

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: North Korea announced today that it plans to allow more American tourists into the country after years of restrictions. I'm not sure I'm a fan of their tourism slogan though: "Come to North Korea! There's only a 36 percent chance we'll throw you in jail under fraudulent charges."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During a recent interview on C-SPAN, IRS Commissioner Douglas Shulman said he doesn’t do his own taxes because he finds “the tax code complex.” That’s like a surgeon saying, “You guys, blood grosses me out. So I don’t wanna . . . ”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During a house fire in the Bronx last night, fire fighters discovered a massive weed growing operation. When the firefighters got there, they immediately called for backup . . . and several bags of Funyuns.

monologue: Walmart announced this week that it will close 10 Sam’s Club super-stores to reduce costs. Wow, even their bad news comes in a 10-pack.

monologue: People magazine says they know where Tiger is: He's where all celebrities go when they do something embarrassing — rehab.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A report says that he checked into a clinic for sex addiction. It also said he'd be out by Valentine's Day. Perfect. I want to push that back to President's Day.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There’s a rumor that NBC is so upset with me, they want to keep me off the air for three years. My response to that is, if NBC doesn’t want people to see me, just leave me on NBC.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night the CEO of Chrysler was giving a speech at the International Auto Show and people in the crowd started heckling him. He got so angry, he walked out, got right in his car and stalled.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It’s been reported that an 8-year-old boy from New Jersey is on the government’s Airport Watch List because he has the same name as a possible terrorist. So it’s been a bad week for little Skippy bin Laden.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Sweden, a group attending a Weight Watchers meeting were lined up for a weigh-in when the floor collapsed. Police at the scene are describing the accident as "hilarious."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: With all the controversy here at NBC, "The Tonight Show" with Conan O’Brien’s ratings have gone up. So, you’re welcome.

monologue: NASA says that a mystery object passed by Earth yesterday morning. They’re not sure what it was, but it missed the Earth by 80,000 miles, so it could have been a Northwest flight.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As you know, security is being upgraded at the airports all across the country. In fact, today Osama bin Laden was placed on the “no-fly” list.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new study by researchers at MIT, men are evolving faster than women. Not the ones on "Jersey Shore," the regular ones.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You know why I do this show every night? Because no one else will.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: One of our lovable broadcasters, the great Andy Rooney, turns 91 today. Compared, of course, to the other "60 Minutes" cast members, he’s just a whippersnapper but he’s 91 today.

monologue: Project Runway is back in New York City. I’m glad because putting a fashion show in L.A. is ridiculous, it’s like putting Jay Leno in prime time.

monologue: NBC announced that they are putting the NBC peacock on the endangered species list.

monologue: Donald Goerke, the man who created SpaghettiOs, has died at the age of 83. Apparently, his last words were “Uh-oh.”

monologue: First Lady Michelle Obama says she doesn’t let her daughters watch the show “Jersey Shore.” When asked why, the first lady said, “Because I love my children.”

monologue: Some scholars of ancient Hebrew are now suggesting that certain portions of the Bible could have been written centuries earlier than others. The scholars say they know this because the newer portions all begin, “Previously, on ‘The Bible.’”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The heaviest snowfall in over 60 years is being reported in Beijing, China. To give you an idea of how bad it is, the army is now using snowplows to run over dissidents.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to “Time” magazine, executives at the Wall Street firm Goldman Sachs were paid an average of $600,000 last year. And that was just by Congress.

monologue: Televangelist Pat Robertson said the earthquake in Haiti happened because they were cursed. He says when they were a French colony, they made a pact with the devil to get rid of the French. Pat, please! You don’t need a pact with the devil to beat the French.

monologue: NASA officials said today that they found a small plastic container of cocaine inside the space shuttle. They think it may have been placed there by illegal aliens.

monologue: President Obama recently said, “We’ve spent so much time talking about the House bill versus the Senate bill that we haven’t been able to talk about how great the bill is overall.” Then someone asked him how great it was, and he was like, “Not that great.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study revealed that losing a few pounds prior to surgery could help reduce the risk of complications. When they heard this, Americans were like, “Eh, we’ll take our chances.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Oregon was arrested after police searched his car and found a half-pound of marijuana, mushrooms, hashish, two rifles, a machete, and a samurai sword. Or as TSA screeners would call it, “nothing suspicious.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Authorities investigated a plane in Michigan after a man locked himself in the bathroom and said he had a bomb. The man says he’s very sorry, and will definitely find a new way to refer to going to the bathroom.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The White House issued a statement today blaming government inefficiencies on old computers. Apparently, they've all been crashing, and everyone knows the only crashing tolerated at the White House is during state dinners.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: They're replacing any technology that's obsolete, broken down, or causes problems. Desktops, laptops, Joe Biden...

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Usually, destruction doesn't mix well with comedy, just look at the NBC late night schedule.

monologue: Conan is getting $30 million to leave NBC. That’s like getting a bonus to leave the Titanic.

monologue: Top Ten Signs the New York Jets are Getting Cocky

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hi, I'm Conan O'Brien and I need all of you to write me a letter of recommendation.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: NBC has a new slogan and the slogan is "More colorful." They may be telling the truth because they are about to get rid of the whitest guy on television.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night at the Golden Globes Julia Roberts said that NBC was in the toilet. NBC was upset and toilets were furious.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday, the founder of Taco Bell passed away at the age of 86. Still no word on whether he's going to have a funeral — or a funeral supreme.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Thanks for coming out on Dr. Martin Luther King’s birthday. As you know, all the banks are closed. I understand tomorrow some of them might even reopen.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A big storm hit L.A. today. For the first time, there were more cancellations at LAX than there were on NBC.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There’s a new thing out called “Incinolet.” It’s a toilet that incinerates human waste instead of flushing it. There’s an invitation to a barbecue you might not want to accept.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A year into Obama's first term in office, unemployment is higher, the national debt is higher, and there are more soldiers serving in Afghanistan. When asked about it, Obama was like, "Yes, but technically — that is change."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s raining so hard here in L.A., I saw Jay Leno steal Conan’s umbrella.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was a nightmare in L.A. last night, and it wasn’t the rain, it was because Mel Gibson was out on the road.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today’s the start of the “Christmas hangover.” The holidays are over and everyone is getting their credit card bills. I just got mine and I can’t believe I spent that much on the Thigh Master.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hi, I’m Conan O’Brien, and I’m just three days away from the biggest drinking binge in history.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday, there were rallies for me in cities across the country, including in Chicago. You can tell things are bad when even Cubs fans feel sorry for you.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Of course, there are other entertainment stories in the news. Some people who have gone to see “Avatar” say it’s caused them to have headaches, dizziness, nausea, and blurry eyesight. Meanwhile, James Cameron says it’s caused him to have a billion dollars.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new $65 tour called the “L.A. Gang Tour” is being offered in Los Angeles that takes tourists through L.A.’s most dangerous neighborhoods. The gang tour is also known by its other name, “A cab ride from the airport.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There were so many rain clouds in L.A. today, I could barely see the dark cloud hanging over NBC.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It looks like California is about to legalize marijuana. And you thought Gov. Schwarzenegger was hard to understand before.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It's getting so expensive to check baggage that people who aren't even terrorists are hiding stuff in their underpants.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The French Health Ministry issued a warning to watch out for heroin that has been contaminated with anthrax. What is the world coming to?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: New Jersey legalized medical marijuana. Finally, the cast of "Jersey Shore" can get a prescription for something other than penicillin.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Martha Stewart today had a pole-dancing lesson. The audience learned a lesson in gravity.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm not surprised at the success of "Avatar." People always like heroes that are brightly colored: The bright blue people in "Avatar," the light green guy in "Shrek," and the orange people on "Jersey Shore."

name: David Letterman
monologue: Ted Kennedy's Senate seat, which he had for many years, is now up for grabs. The election is pretty close, but my money is on Jay Leno.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I just heard that Starbucks recently raised the prices on almost all of its popular drinks. A company spokesperson said Starbucks is confident that people will still buy their coffee, because it was already way too expensive before.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I just read that President Obama plans to deliver his State of the Union address next Wednesday, January 27. Until then he’s just at home going, “Please everything get better by Wednesday, please get better by Wednesday . . . ”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Sarah Palin is saying that her deal with Fox News wouldn’t keep her from running for president in 2012. However, Palin did admit that her deal with Fox News will keep her from winning.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s a new iPhone app that alerts you if your spouse is trying to read your e-mails and text messages. Experts are calling it a revolutionary product. Meanwhile, Tiger's calling it "about two months too late."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They say it could rain 20 inches this week, which is bad news for Jay Leno. He just had all 600 of his cars washed.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Sunday night was the Golden Globes. Where else can you see all the stars of TV and film getting drunk together?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was raining so badly, there was water spilling into the dress that Mariah Carey was spilling out of.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's raining like crazy in L.A. and there's flooding everywhere. So I'm thinking to myself, "Whoa! It's a good thing Conan is getting sandbagged."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hello, I’m Conan O’Brien, and sorry if I’m a little late . . . I had a job interview at Lady Foot Locker.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I should have known something was up when NBC sent me that 2010 calendar that only went up to January.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Earlier this week in California, a goat somehow got into a strip club and caused $2,000 worth of damage. Then it got up on stage and earned all that money back.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This rain in L.A. couldn’t have come at a worse time. Today was the day NBC was supposed to burn down the studio for the insurance money.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s hard to believe that President Obama has now been in office for a year and it’s incredible. He took something that was in terrible shape and brought it back from the brink of disaster: the Republican Party.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You know the question, “What can Brown do for you?” Apparently he can stop the healthcare plan.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama called Martha Coakley and said, “Well, we can’t win them all.” Same thing he said after the New Jersey governor’s race, the Virginia governor’s race, the 2016 Olympic bid, and the Copenhagen climate summit. Between all of them, it’s been a rough couple of weeks.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Boston’s Logan Airport will soon be offering free Wi-Fi to all its passengers. And in related news, Newark airport will soon be offering flights.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There was a huge Senate race in Massachusetts yesterday, and Republican Scott Brown pulled off the upset. Now some Democrats are accusing their candidate, Martha Coakley, of running a lackluster campaign. They were especially confused by her campaign slogan, "I guess we can?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Erroll Southers — Obama’s pick to head the TSA — withdrew his name because he performed an illegal background check on his ex-wife’s boyfriend. Still, that’s an improvement from the TSA’s normal procedure of not performing background checks.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I've had it with the bad weather we've had for . . . two days so far.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I don't look at this rain and these floods as a bad thing. I prefer to see it as all of Los Angeles turning into "Splash Mountain."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Today is President Obama's first anniversary. Traditionally, on the first anniversary, you're supposed to give paper, so I got him his birth certificate.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The cable news networks are talking about how much Obama's approval ratings have dropped, but rest assured, he is still the most popular African-American president in American history.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I’m Conan O’Brien, future Donkey Kong champion.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: NBC and I have finally reached a separation agreement. I knew it was official this morning when NBC dropped off all my CDs and picked up its lava lamp.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: As you all know by now, tomorrow is our last show here. I’d like to apologize to the guests that were scheduled for next week: President Barack Obama, the Pope, the queen of England, and our good friend, Elvis Presley.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Conan will be leaving The Tonight Show, and I’ve chosen to stay on the Titanic.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It hailed in Los Angeles. People thought it was raining crack.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Republican was elected to the U.S. Senate in Massachusetts. This could tip the delicate balance of power in Washington from the completely incompetent to the morally corrupt.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s Thursday, Jan. 21, or as John Edwards calls it, “Father’s Day.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s a great day for America, and a great day for American television. And no, I’m not resigning.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: MTV expects three million people to watch the season finale of “Jersey Shore.” People love watching other people embarrass themselves on television, which is why we’re doing so well.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The entire cast of “Jersey Shore” is now famous, and they may do a second season of the show. The governor of New Jersey has asked for an emergency lift of Jagermeister and spray tan.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Massachusetts elects a Republican who drives a truck with 200,000 miles on it. It’s a Chevy truck. Which is harder to believe? Massachusetts elects a Republican or Chevy makes a truck that can go 200,000 miles?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Surprising Facts About Scott Brown

monologue: During his acceptance speech Tuesday, newly-elected Sen. Scott Brown told the crowd that his daughters are both “available.” Man, so many great American speeches. “Four score and seven years ago,” “Ask not what your country can do for you,” “I have a dream,” and now, “My daughters are both available.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Supreme Court ruled today that the government cannot stop corporations from spending money on political candidates. This explains why Sarah Palin just accepted $1 million to change her name to Pizza Hut.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s a new iPhone app that translates a baby’s cry into words. The most common translation? “Can you stop looking at your damn iPhone for one second and pick me up? I’m a crying baby!”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I just want to mention that if anyone wants to pay me $45 million to go home, I’ll go.

monologue: It’s raining so hard in L.A., experts are recommending umbrellas.

monologue: The Supreme Court ruled today that corporations can now spend as much as they want on political candidates. I can’t see that having any negative repercussions, can you?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things To Be Happy About

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Ladies and gentleman, we have exactly one hour to steal every single item in this studio.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: We’ve a had a lot of fun being here these last seven months, but like everything in life, the fun has to come to an end a decade too early.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The terms of my settlement say that I can’t host another show for seven months. So next week, look forward to the “Andy Richter show” with his sidekick, me.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: As I set off for exciting new career opportunities, I just want to make one thing clear to everyone listening out there: I will do nudity.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The big healthcare fight is not going well for the Democrats. Nancy Pelosi said yesterday that the House doesn’t have enough votes to pass the Senate’s healthcare bill. A few more elections and the House won't have Nancy Pelosi, either.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: An employee at a Taco Bell in Alaska was sentenced to one day in jail for throwing a taco at his manager. He'll spend the whole day pleading with fellow inmates to think outside the buns.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in the UK was banned from a public park after he tried to have sex with a tree. I don’t know about you, but I think Al Gore has finally gone too far.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I read that stray dogs in Moscow have figured out how to use the subway. Crazy right? At least in New York, it only smells like dogs have figured out how to use the subway.

monologue: Japan has invented a machine that you put 40 sheets of regular paper into and it converts them into rolls of toilet paper. It’s actual paper that you can use as toilet paper. Or, as we call it here, “an NBC contract.”

monologue: Do you know who will be in charge of healthcare? The IRS. You thought getting audited was bad? Wait until your next prostate exam.

monologue: This is still America. I can own a gun and say whatever I want, and no one can make me wear pants.

monologue: Have you guys been watching March Madness? The “Sweet 16” starts on Thursday, and I can hardly wait. Although part of me wishes there were just 13 teams so they could call it a “Bar Mitzvah.”

monologue: In the same interview, President Obama said that his family has decided not to join a single church because he causes too much of a disruption at services. At their last service, the priest was like, "In the name of the father, the son, and the — holy cow, it's the president!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in New Jersey was arrested after he crawled through the window of a McDonald’s drive-thru because his Filet-O-Fish was taking too long. And they say pot makes you less motivated.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Supermodel Kate Moss is going to make her theater debut in the Shakespeare play “The Tempest” this summer in London. The play is about a girl stranded on an island with her dad, who uses a magic wand to summon a tempest. Kate, of course, plays the wand.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: During a fundraising trip to California, some young Republicans took the Republican Party credit card to a club in Hollywood that has nude dancers doing bondage shows. Usually when Republicans find themselves in dark rooms with whips and chains, it’s in Dick Cheney’s basement.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It must be very embarrassing for the people involved. I’m sure the strippers didn’t want anyone to know they were hanging out with politicians.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: At least it was the young Republicans that did this. Could you imagine Bob Dole and John McCain walking in there?

name: David Letterman
monologue: The bad news: The subway crime in New York City is completely out of control. The good news: Your third visit to the emergency room is free.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Highlights Of Barack Obama's Oil Drilling Plan

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A photo of Sandra Bullock’s husband, Jesse James, doing a Nazi salute has been released. They said he’s a history buff. I would have dressed like Lincoln, but that’s just me.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: James is now in sex rehab. “I’m addicted to sex” is the new, grown-up version of “A dog ate my homework.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was elimination night tonight on “American Idol.” Inmates on death row get eliminated in a more expedient fashion than the contestants on this show.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today, President Obama canceled the White House Easter Egg Hunt. Instead, the kids will be on the White House lawn drilling for oil.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Obama has opened up to drilling along the Florida coast. Environmentalists say that it’s a protected habitat. Not for marine life, but for Cuban swimmers.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Iran’s top nuclear scientist has defected to the CIA, and he has frightening information. He says Iran was just weeks away from developing their own Toyota Prius.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Karl Rove was heckled at a book-signing by war protestors and he quickly snuck out the side door. Finally, somebody from the Bush administration with an exit strategy.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This Jesse James story keeps getting worse. Now, his fifth mistress says she’s planning to go public. And I guess Tiger Woods is feeling the heat of competition. He just announced that he’s quitting golf again so he can concentrate on his affairs.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Sarah Palin has a new Fox News series, which is being described as a show about people with “real-life tales of overcoming adversity.” She should do a story about that guy who became the first black president.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Scientists just discovered that toads can provide early warning of an earthquake by suddenly leaving their mating sites. But how can they tell the difference between an earthquake warning and a toad doing the walk of shame?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s Al Gore’s birthday today. He ate a giant cake and a gallon of ice cream, and then realized that it’s his birthday.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In Geneva, scientists are celebrating because they’ve got a new multi-billion dollar atom-smasher there and it’s giving us information on how the universe began. I’m thinking that they could have saved the money and just asked Larry King.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Sarah Palin is hosting a show on Fox News, where she will be interviewing celebrity guests. Hold on, Palin. There’s only room for one perky, middle-aged woman who interviews celebrities on television and that’s me.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Guess who’s coming to New York City — King Tut. He’ll be here with his wife, Catherine Zeta Tut.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things To Ask Yourself Before Waiting In Line For The iPad

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama issued a proclamation declaring Cesar Chavez Day. So this week has both Passover and Cesar Chavez Day. One holiday celebrates the flight of the Jewish people from Egypt to Israel, and the other celebrates the flight of the Mexican people from Tijuana to Los Angeles.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You know what I’m doing for Easter? I’m gonna be hanging with my Peeps.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Because it’s Easter, Catholic priests have been hearing confession all week — mostly from other Catholic priests,

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today is April 1, April Fools’ Day, a day that people try to fool their friends and relatives. Don’t confuse that with April 15, when people try to fool the IRS.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It's been such a busy week. So many things coming out — the iPad, “Clash of the Titans,” Ricky Martin.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today is April Fools’ Day, that day of the year when you can’t get anyone to believe anything you say — or as Gov. Paterson calls it, “Any day.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: As part of an April Fools’ Day prank, Google renamed itself “Topeka.” As part of a really desperate prank, Yahoo renamed itself “Google.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During a speech at the White House, President Obama said that “teleworking” from home can boost efficiency. Kind of interesting advice from a guy who just flew 13 hours to Afghanistan to say “what’s up.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Some people aren’t turning in their census forms because they’re angry at the government. But that’s silly because the census is how they figure out who gets represented. If you don’t send in your forms, your state will get less congressman — which might be perfect.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: When it comes to taxes, there are two types of people. There are those that get it done early, also known as psychopaths, and then the rest of us.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Sunday is Easter. They were going to move it to Tuesday, but there was a conflict with “American Idol.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: This Sunday is Easter, the holiest day in Christianity. We celebrated by feeding the kids chocolate. Because honestly, if there’s one thing the kids need, it’s more sweets.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Signs Your Baseball Team Isn't Ready For The Season

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Under President Obama's new airport security plan, anyone traveling to the U.S. will be stopped if they match the description of a potential terrorist. Wait, we weren’t doing this already?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night, President Obama gave a speech at the Boston Opera House. It was a long night, because you know what they say about the opera: It ain’t over ‘til the fat lady gets lectured on her eating habits by Michelle Obama.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama unveiled a new gas mileage program that he says is “like taking 58 million cars off the road for an entire year.” Or as Toyota calls it, “business as usual.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Ford is teaming up with Microsoft to create an all-electric car called the “Microsoft Hohm.” That’s smart. Because if there’s one company that knows how to avoid crashes, it’s Microsoft.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s a big weekend for Apple, because the iPad comes out, although its thunder was stolen last week when Ricky Martin did the same thing.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: “Clash of the Titans” does look pretty good because it’s based on Greek mythology and has the Greek icons: Zeus, Mount Olympus, the big fat weddings.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The iPad comes out on Saturday and then on Sunday, the improved iPad comes out, which you will actually want to buy.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A 7.2 earthquake originating in Mexico struck on Easter Sunday. There wasn’t much damage, which was good because I wouldn’t want to be killed wearing a pink pastel shirt.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Obamas hosted the Easter egg roll at the White House. Dozens of children gathered on the White House lawn to roll eggs toward a finish line as the president cheered them on and Republicans tried to block them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tiger Woods gave a press conference ahead of his return to the Masters. I kept waiting for something to happen and nothing really did. It was a lot like watching golf.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: About 30,000 people showed up at the White House for the annual Easter egg roll. Or as Fox News called it, a “socialist free food giveaway.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Kids are so spoiled today. You know how they hunt for Easter eggs? They use Google Earth.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This was the holy weekend, so Apple’s Steve Jobs came down from the mountain with a new tablet under his arm.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This iPad thing is so advanced, it actually has an airbag in it for when you crash your car while surfing the Internet.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tiger Woods gave a major press conference, and he said he’s going to start appreciating his fans more. Although that was kind of how he got into trouble in the first place.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tiger’s getting ready for the Masters, so today he played a practice round with golf legend Fred Couples. Of course, Tiger only showed up because he heard there’d be some “couples action.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama threw out the first pitch at the Washington Nationals game. Obama took a short wind-up and threw a high, arcing pitch. Democrats saw the pitch as moderately close to the middle, while Republicans are calling it “way to the left and possibly socialist.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A Jet Blue flight leaving Newark had to return to the airport after takeoff when an engine cover fell off the plane. Passengers on the plane don't know what was worse — having an engine cover blow off mid-flight or having to go back to Newark.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There was a 7.2 earthquake in Mexico and we could feel it here in L.A. Parts of me are still jiggling.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The quake really messed up our studio. It caused like $3,000 worth of improvements.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: During the quake, I did what I was supposed to do, I immediately ran into the bathroom and cried. Stop, drop, and cry.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The tremors lasted for more than a minute and people were really scared. You couldn’t tell though, with all the Botox.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Sarah Palin was speaking at the alcohol convention in Las Vegas, Nevada. Because nothing says family values like gambling and liquor.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: John McCain told Newsweek that he doesn’t really consider himself a “maverick.” What kind of man would call himself a maverick for years and then suddenly say he doesn’t think of himself as a maverick? I’ll tell you what kind — a maverick.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The iPad has only been out for a few days and it has revolutionized the publishing industry. You can download books, you can read them and store them, and for religious fundamentalists, there’s a new app that lets you burn them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was Beatles night on “American Idol.” Some of the worst performers of all time paid tribute to some of the best performers of all time.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Having the “Idol” contestants sing Beatles songs is a bad idea. It’s like having “spandex night” on “Biggest Loser.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sunday was the big White House Easter egg hunt. Of course, the Catholic priests didn’t have time to hide eggs, they were too busy hiding each other.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As you know, the Roman Catholic Church continues to be rocked by this sex abuse crisis. In fact, they’re thinking of changing their name to the Roman Polanski Catholic Church.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Spirit Airlines has become the first airline in the U.S. to charge passengers for carry-on luggage, $45 to put a bag in the overhead bin. Which is odd, because if you had an extra 90 bucks to spend, you probably wouldn't be flying Spirit Airlines.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: KFC is about to unveil a new sandwich called the “Double Down.” It’s two chicken breasts in place of bread and in between that is jack cheese and bacon. I forgot to mention one other thing it comes with — the knowledge that you've simply given up.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last week, a pizza delivery man in Harlem managed to fight off two robbers with a gun and still deliver two pizzas to their destination. Stoners are already calling him the “Captain Sully” of munchies.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don’t really follow college basketball, so when I heard that Duke beat Butler, I thought it must be a scandal at Buckingham Palace.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In 2001, a blind American climber reached the summit of Mount Everest. At least that’s what they told him.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Kathmandu is very commercialized these days. Do you know what’s on top of Mount Everest? A Starbucks. It doesn’t have a bathroom, but the Starbucks next door to it does.

name: David Letterman
monologue: This month was murder-free in Newark, N.J. It makes sense — who can afford bullets?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Thoughts That Go Through Every Accountant's Mind On April 15th

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Sandra Bullock put out a statement today officially denying the rumor of a sex tape of her and her husband, Jesse James. She says there never was a tape and there never will be a tape. I think the “never will be” part goes without saying.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tiger Woods will play his first golf tournament in five months, and his first tournament in six years without lipstick on his lucky underwear.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It’s elimination night on “American Idol.” At this point, they’re really just mercy killings.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama has restricted the use of nuclear weapons to only be used against Iran, North Korea, or Fox News.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Scientists have claimed that toads can predict an earthquake, and they will flee five days before it strikes. So if you’re ever stuck on the San Diego freeway behind a long line of toads, you’re screwed.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Buzz Aldrin was kicked off of “Dancing With the Stars.” For some reason, on the moon, he seemed so much lighter on his feet.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As if we are not fat enough, Kentucky Fried Chicken is about to release its “Double Down” sandwich. It’s a bacon and cheese sandwich and the bun is two pieces of fried chicken. After you eat it, you go from KFC to the ICU where you’re pronounced DOA.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Michelle Obama held a town hall meeting on C-SPAN to answer questions from kids about her anti-obesity campaign. The most popular question from kids: "Why are you doing this to us, lady?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Pennsylvania was arrested after he got drunk, urinated on himself, took off his clothes and then broke into a stranger’s house he thought was his. And the craziest part, I don’t even know how I got to Pennsylvania.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Heidi Montag is saying that because of her new F-cup breasts, she can no longer go jogging. She tried it and ended up needing another nose job.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Please try to save some applause for later, because the show is crap tonight. It’s one of those crazy things that we keep around. We don’t really need it anymore, but we love it.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Deforestation is threatening all kinds of species. Who knows what kinds of animals are lurking in these forests? There could be unicorns, or hobbits, or maybe even more Baldwins.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: My 9-year-old son loves dinosaurs. He shows me pictures of dinosaurs and asks me what their names are and I don’t know. “That, son, is a ‘thesaurus.’ That dinosaur can tell you any word and any other words that mean the same thing.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I watched golf today. It’s boring. There was no sex at all, just a bunch of middle-aged white guys and one guilty-looking black guy walking around.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tiger Woods returned to golf today. President Obama and Russian President Medvedev signed the necessary documents and just like that, relations have been normalized.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Bristol Palin is continuing her campaign about teen pregnancy. It’s funny that she’s going around telling kids not to get pregnant when her mom is telling people, “Drill, baby, drill.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Bristol was a pregnant teen herself. She named her baby “Tripp,” with two p’s, which is reason enough for teens not to have kids.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The mayor of L.A. wants to shut down city agencies two days a week. I have a better idea — why don’t we shut down the mayor’s office five days a week?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The president of Iran, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, has called President Obama a big bully. When you’re 5 feet 2 inches tall, everyone seems like a bully.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sarah Palin’s daughter Bristol is speaking out. She realizes that she was totally unprepared to be a mother. It’s better than being a mother that’s totally unprepared to be vice president.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A new survey shows that an obese man is more likely to suffer serious injury from a car crash than a normal weight man. Unless, of course, the obese man falls on top of the normal weight man.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tiger Woods made his return to golf at the Masters today. While talking about Tiger, the tournament chairman said, “This year will not be just for him, but for all of us who believe in second chances.” Then someone whispered in his ear and he was like "I'm sorry — 17th chances. All of us who believe in 17th chances."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: United Airlines and U.S. Airways are in talks to merge, creating one of the world’s largest airlines. You know how this works, first the merger will be announced. Then it’ll be delayed. Then they’ll give everybody a free hotel room and then you’re on standby for another announcement.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Apple is admitting that its iPad sometimes has a hard time connecting to the Internet, and some people are returning them. That’s just wrong. If I returned everything that had trouble connecting to the Internet, my grandparents would be in big trouble.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Archaeologists in Greece found the oldest man-made structure in a prehistoric cave. Meanwhile, archaeologists in Beverly Hills found the youngest man-made structure having dinner with her husband, Spencer Pratt.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: President Obama signed a historic treaty with the Russian president. Fox News said it was a summit between a powerful communist leader and the president of Russia.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The treaty is about reducing the number of nuclear weapons we have pointed at each other. I thought we were friends with the Russians but we’ve really been “frienemies” this whole time.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: When I went to Moscow, I saw the tomb of Lenin. They keep his body preserved in a glass coffin. It’s waxy, it’s falling apart — it’s like Joan Rivers after a Brazilian.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In Afghanistan, President Hamid Karzai is mad at the United States. We said his government is riddled with bribes, corruption, and pay-offs. I guess they’re trying to pass healthcare over there too.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the Pentagon, al-Qaida has been so weakened financially that they’re turning to crimes like drugs, prostitution, and adjustable-rate mortgages.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: An Irish airline has announced that it will charge $1.50 to use the toilet on the airplane. A lot of people will find a whole new use for the airsick bag.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In South Africa, a 96-year-old man has become the world’s oldest bungee jumper. The funeral will be this Tuesday.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Pennsylvania was arrested for leaving marijuana in his son’s Elmo backpack. The cops became suspicious when Elmo laughed for two hours without being tickled.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Happy Birthday to Hugh Hefner, he turned 84 today. He must be the toughest person to buy a gift for. I mean what do you get for the guy who’s had everyone?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A Bank of America employee in North Carolina was arrested for installing a program on ATM machines so he could steal thousands of dollars. If convicted, the man faces a sentence of 20 years, 40 years, 60 years, or “other amount.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man from Thailand spent three extra years in an Indonesian prison because of a typo. It turns out he only roped a cow.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I watched so much golf this weekend. Tiger finished in 4th place, which means he only won $330,000, which is barely enough to pay his text messaging bill.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tiger’s obviously under a lot of stress. It’s very difficult to play when you have a padlock on your underpants.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Conan O’Brien announced today that he will move his show to TBS. Later in the day, Jay Leno announced that he will also move his show to TBS.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Tiger Woods said he would try to keep his emotions under control, but after a bad swing, he used the F-word. Who does he think he is — vice president of the United States?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the Pentagon, al-Qaida is in financial ruin. You know what broke them? Healthcare premiums.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Justice John Paul Stevens is leaving the Supreme Court. This won’t affect as many Americans as when Paula Abdul left “American Idol,” but it’s still a big deal.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In a speech, the chairman of the Republican National Committee, Michael Steele, said “I am the first here to admit I’ve made mistakes.” Then the stripper giving him a lap-dance said it will still be 20 bucks.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s a rumor going around that Hillary Clinton could be Obama’s choice for the next Supreme Court justice. It’s a lifetime appointment that would take up all her time, or as Bill Clinton calls it, “She’ll take it.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Vice President Joe Biden hosted a big lunch today with foreign leaders at the Naval Observatory. Unfortunately, he spent the entire time asking everyone to observe his navel.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: CNN is hoping to spice up the show “Anderson Cooper 360” by adding a live audience. After that, they're hoping to spice up “Larry King Live” by adding a live Larry King.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Barry Bonds said he is “proud” of Mark McGwire for returning to baseball. And it really means a lot coming from Bonds — it’s like Tiger Woods getting a high five at the Masters from Jesse James.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was announced today that Conan O’Brien has a new talk show on TBS and a lot of people are asking how it will affect this show. It will not — people that watch this show cannot afford basic cable.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There are rumors that Elizabeth Taylor is getting married for the 9th time. One more and she qualifies for a free chicken sandwich at Quizno’s.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: KFC restaurants have unveiled the “Double Down,” which is two slabs of fried chicken with bacon in the middle. Why not — we all have free health insurance.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Sarah Palin has made more than $12 million this year. That is a lot of money for someone that can’t say words that end in “g.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They say $12 million is a conservative estimate, but she may have made more. Yet she continues to blame Obama for the bad economy.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Adam Lambert is the celebrity mentor on “American Idol.” I’m pretty sure they’ve given up on the contestants this year, when the mentor is the guy that lost last year.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The president of China, Hu Jintao, is in Washington this week. It’s caused a bit of controversy, as President Obama was seen bowing to the Chinese leader. Well, he has to — the rent is going to be late again this month.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: John Paul Stevens, an 89-year-old Supreme Court justice, has announced he is retiring. He’s going to be 90 this year. In fact, the other Supreme Court justices had to keep reminding him to close his robe.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: People were surprised that Tiger Woods came in 4th place at the Masters. Tiger said his back swing wasn’t working. After the past year, I’m surprised his back was working at all.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Vatican is updating its policy on sexual abuse. They are now against it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I just read that the number of female multi-millionaires has risen by 40 percent in the last five years. Most did it through hard work and innovation, while other women just promised Tiger they wouldn’t say anything.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In a new interview with Playboy, Eliot Spitzer’s call girl Ashley Dupré said that Tiger Woods’ mistresses are wrong for coming forward. So I hope you heard that, ladies. You used bad judgment, according to a prostitute.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama announced that in 2012 he’s going to hold his next nuclear security summit at a site in South Korea, right near the North Korean border. Seriously? That's like if you held a biker chick rally right across the street from Jesse James' rehab facility.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last week, two escaped prisoners in Argentina got away from police by disguising themselves as sheep. Guards said they should have known something was up, when they saw two sheep walking out of a prison.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Al Gore was ambushed for an interview with Fox News and he refused to do the interview. What’s wrong with you, Fox News? If you want to interview Al Gore, just leave a trail of ham into the studio.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight is the season premiere of “Deadliest Catch.” It’s a show about crab fisherman in the Gulf of Alaska in the frigid waters between North America and Asia. And up there, if the sun hits just right, from their boats they can see both Russia and Sarah Palin’s house.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I couldn’t be on “Deadliest Catch,” because I get seasick in my hot tub.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I won’t eat anything that’s too ugly or too cute. I won’t eat rabbits or chickens or Justin Bieber.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tomorrow is the day to mail in your tax returns, which means tonight is the night to start making fake receipts.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Two “American Idol” contestants were sent home tonight. To which I say, why not send them all home?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: According to a new study, children who are spanked are twice as likely as those that aren’t spanked to get into fights and destroy things — which is probably why they get spanked in the first place.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Obama administration’s top science and technology official has warned that the United States cannot expect to be No. 1 in science and technology forever. Did anyone know we were No. 1 now?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Pentagon says that al-Qaida is now in financial ruin. Goldman Sachs really screwed everyone over.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Al-Qaida should have seen it coming. Do you know who’s in charge of their finances — Osama bin Bernanke.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Mexico’s tourist industry is concerned that drugs and violence are scaring away tourists. The only thing you used to have to worry about in Mexico was Montezuma’s revenge.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This Friday is the deadline for mailing in your Census form. People all around the country put down how many people live in their houses — while Tiger Woods and Jesse James put "kind of a tricky situation right now."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama is launching a new $6 billion space policy that will ultimately take astronauts to Mars. Of course, it’s $6 billion and $45 if the astronauts have a carry-on.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Obama says the new $6 billion program will let us engage in deeper space exploration, while Biden says this will let us engage in open dialogue with Alf.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yahoo is producing a daily video series based on its most popular news stories, in partnership with Toyota. Of course, they’re having a tough time getting the site up because it always ends up crashing.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s fitting that April 14 is National Pecan Day because today, we recognize nuts. And tomorrow, on April 15, we pay our taxes to support them.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A pecan tree can live for 300 years and when they’re old and gnarled, they can still bear fruit. They’re like the tree world’s Larry King.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Scientists are saying that eating pecans every day may decrease your cholesterol. So in case they’re right, I wrap all of my pecans in bacon.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was tax day today. Don’t forget to set your bank account back $10,000 tonight.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The government wants us to count how many people live in our home, and then to calculate how much money we owe them. I actually got confused and sent a check to the census and a member of my household to the IRS. Sorry Grandma, we’ll get you back.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A volcano erupted in Iceland a couple days ago and it’s still going. Researchers say this is the only interesting thing that has ever happened in Iceland.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Larry King has filed for divorce from his wife, Shawn. He may have thought he was filing taxes, I don’t know.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s April 15, the day we all curse like Joe Biden.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama turned in his tax return today. He didn’t owe a lot because he has a lot of dependents: his wife, two daughters, AIG, General Motors, Goldman Sachs.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s being reported that al-Qaida is in financial ruin. In fact, today I saw a terrorist buying a shoe-bomb at Payless.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: More and more men are coming forward claiming they were sexually harassed by former congressman Eric Massa. It’s getting so bad that Massa is considering going into the Vatican protection program.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: At a tea party rally in Boston yesterday, Sarah Palin praised the crowd for winning that Senate race in Massachusetts. She said, “Shoot, look at what you did in January, you shook up the United States Senate.” Unfortunately, no one heard the Senate thing because after she said “shoot,” three hundred guns went off.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Larry King and his wife are ending their marriage. In divorce papers, Larry King requested joint custody of his two sons. But it won’t be easy because they’re pretty comfortable in their retirement home.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In 2012, a cruise line is going to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the Titanic sinking with a special nine-day cruise to the site of the disaster. It's on a brand new ship called the “S.S. What Could Possibly Go Wrong?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Scientists in Britain have created embryos with the DNA of one man and two women. It's the closest any of those scientists will ever get to an actual threesome.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: More details are coming out about Larry King’s divorce. I’m friendly with Larry King and making fun of him would be wrong. So I’m going to do the right thing — and stop being friends with him.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Apparently, Larry’s estranged wife says he cheated on her with her sister. He probably just didn’t have on his glasses.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Larry has been married eight times. Liz Taylor was also married eight times. Both Taylor and King are single right now, and scientists are saying this is the first time that has happened in over 200 years.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If no one paid their taxes, imagine what it would be like: America would be broke — more broke.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In an interview with GQ Magazine, Lou Dobbs said he’s considering running for president. Hey, stranger things have happened — Lou Dobbs being in GQ Magazine being one of them.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s a new comic book coming out about Arnold Schwarzenegger’s life. In the comic, Arnold battles his life-long nemesis: words.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A town in Tennessee elected a dead man as its mayor. Finally, a politician who won't cheat on his wife.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There are some new reports coming in from O.J. Simpson in jail. Apparently O.J. has been playing a lot of baseball. He’s pretty good apparently. The only problem is that every time he runs home, he murders two people.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Willie Nelson is here tonight. He was once branded an outlaw. Outlaws are more scary than in-laws.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Jonas Brothers don’t conform to the rock ‘n’ roll lifestyle, so why aren’t they considered outlaws? Because their music is crap.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I shouldn’t make fun of the Jonas Brothers. It must be hard being at the top of the Disney food chain.

name: David Letterman
monologue: I’m aware that the only reason you people are here tonight is volcanic ash. I know that.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A volcano in Iceland has shut down air travel all across Europe. Apparently they dumped too much baking soda and vinegar into the thing and it just won’t stop erupting.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: President Obama had to cancel his trip to Poland, and this morning he said he hopes the volcano will stop smoking soon. And the volcano said the same thing about him.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The German airline Lufthansa said it plans to resume some flights. Apparently there are so many Germans in France right now that the French government surrendered.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Today is Jesse James’ birthday. He’s the soon-to-be-ex-husband of Sandra Bullock, and he’s 41 today. Reservation for one please.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I am so stupid, I made a big mistake. I sent my taxes to Russia, and my adopted kid to the IRS.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In case anyone in Los Angeles is wondering, the volcano ash hasn’t made it over here yet — that’s just our air.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama has cut the space program and we will no longer be sending men to the moon. There has been one big achievement during his time in office. We did put an astronaut on “Dancing With the Stars.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sarah Palin made $12 million last year. In fact, she had such a good year that she was able to quit her part-time job as governor of Alaska.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A woman in Ohio says she opened a can of SpaghettiOs and found a dead rat. You know what’s even more disgusting — she also found SpaghettiOs.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The airports in Europe are closed due to the volcano erupting. Smoke and ash is spreading all over Europe. Meteorologists originally thought it was coming from Willie Nelson’s tour bus.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You can’t fly an airplane through an ash plume because the engines will be shut down faster than Mel Gibson at a bar mitzvah.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The volcano is erupting underneath a glacier, meaning everything kicks up through a hole in the ice. Some scientists are calling it an “ice-hole,” but other scientists are saying the problem is pre-existing ash, therefore it’s more of an “ash-hole.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: Because of the volcano in Iceland, thousands of travelers are stranded with no place to sleep, eat, or shower. This is the kind of thing that can really take the fun out of air travel.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Goldman Sachs Excuses

monologue: Today is April 20, which is like Christmas for pot-smokers. It all started in the 1700s when St. Patrick drove the stoners out of Ireland with a pack of Twinkies.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In celebration of 4/20, the volcano in Iceland is still smoking. And it just asked for Hot Pockets.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Travelers have been stranded in dozens of countries, but they’re finally allowing flights to take off to countries that no one likes.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Kate Gosselin was very upset when she was voted off of “Dancing With the Stars.” Some mothers only have two kids and they cry when they have to go home.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The giant cloud of ash over Amsterdam is so bad that you can’t even see the giant cloud of hashish.

name: Jay Leno

monologue: President Obama and some prominent Democrats proposed a solution to the erupting volcano — they want to pour money into it.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s a bad day for travelers. A second giant smoke cloud is shooting into the sky right now. Air traffic controllers are saying it’s not safe to fly anywhere near Woody Harrelson’s house.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s 4/20, a big holiday for the people that smoke marijuana. Because the rest of the time, they work very hard.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The bad news today: regular airline service is resuming.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Excuses Of The Guy Who Lost The iPhone Prototype

monologue: The Fox network had their annual telethon “Idol Gives Back.” I was hoping they would give back the hundreds of hours I’ve wasted watching “American Idol.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The new $100 bill was unveiled today. So if you have any old $100 bills, you can throw them away now.

name: Jimmy Kimmel

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justice Roberts is only 55 years old. He’s young enough to be Larry King’s next wife.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For those of you visiting from Iceland, happy Ash Wednesday.

monologue: The British government sent a warship to France to bring home stranded Britons. There was an embarrassing moment — when the ship pulled up to the port, the French immediately surrendered.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The volcano was spewing out so much ash that now, the Catholic Church is saying it couldn’t even see what it was doing wrong.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s the Queen of England’s birthday today. So happy birthday, Simon Cowell.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s a sad day if you’re a fan of Star Trek films, because Leonard Nimoy, who played Spock, is retiring. The bad news is, William Shatner is not retiring.

monologue: Sarah Palin celebrated Earth Day today by shooting wolves from a helicopter.

monologue: Top Ten Features Of The New Madden NFL 11 Video Game

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Happy Earth Day to everyone. An estimated one billion people celebrate Earth Day. Al Gore, in particular, is wasted right now.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A new poll found that a substantial number of Americans still aren’t convinced that President Obama was born in the United States. Only 58 percent believe that Obama was born here, and 20 percent think he was born in another country. I don’t believe Obama was born at all.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Vice President Biden appeared on “The View.” They were trying to set the Guinness Record for most Botox on one couch. And they did, so congratulations.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Happy Earth Day, or as they say in Iceland, “What On Earth Day. ”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Everyone says we need to do more to protect the Earth. With volcanoes, mudslides, earthquakes, hurricanes — who’s protecting us from the Earth?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Three bisexual men are suing a gay softball league. Apparently the league told them they couldn’t play because they are “not gay enough.” I think, if you’re a man and you’re suing over not being allowed to play softball, you’re already gay enough.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Happy birthday to Jack Nicholson today, and also it’s Earth Day. Planet Earth and Jack Nicholson are different, of course — one is a giant object ravaged by years of abuse and we’re running out of time to save it, and the other one is Earth.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The movie “Avatar” is out on DVD today. James Cameron wanted it to be released on Earth Day because nothing says “save the planet” like millions of plastic DVD cases.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s the 40th Earth Day, which is bad news for Earth. Once you get in your forties, your equator expands, your poles start to melt — soon you’ll look as bad as Uranus.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The volcanic ash cloud from Iceland is making its way to the U.S. and actually improving the air quality in New York City. I’ve been coughing up lava all day.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: One good thing came out of this volcano in Iceland. Economists say consumers can expect a huge drop in the price of lava lamps.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama gave a speech in New York about his plans to reform the rules for Wall St. A lot of Wall St. executives were shaking in their boots when the president showed up. The bad news is, they were $800 Italian leather boots that were bought with our bailout money.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Spirit Airlines announced it’s going to install non-reclining seats in their airplanes. They came up with this last month after they saw a passenger that looked comfortable.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: These are the same people that are charging $45 for a carry-on bag. Maybe Spirit Airlines should change their name to “Mean-Spirited Airlines.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: The New York Yankees visited the White House this week. Everyone from the champion team was there, except for Kate Hudson.

monologue: During the economic meltdown, employees at the SEC were using government computers to watch pornography. Ironically, while they were watching porn, the other employees were watching Goldman Sachs screw the entire country.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: One SEC employee spent up to eight hours a day looking at porn. And the worst part is, he billed them for 10 hours.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama gave a speech about his plans to reform Wall Street. In an embarrassing moment, the head of Goldman Sachs was going through security and had to empty his pockets — and five Republican senators fell out.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The U.S. Treasury issued its new $100 bill. They had to come up with a new one because China has all the old ones.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: George W. Bush’s memoir is coming out on Nov. 9. On the cover, Bush is wearing a dark suit and holding a briefing book with his head turned slightly from the camera, or as Bush calls it, "posing all serious-like."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The book is called “Decision Points,” and 1,000 signed copies will be sold for $350 each. Each one says, “Thanks for reading about my decisions — Sincerely, Dick Cheney.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama met with the Yankees to congratulate them on their World Series win. Derek Jeter said, “You never get tired of meeting the president.” And then John McCain said, “Eh, I’m pretty much over it.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A radical Islamic cleric said that women who wear revealing clothing are responsible for earthquakes. In response, scientists said, “Worth it."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Former President George W. Bush is working on his memoirs. I’m excited just to hear him pronounce the word “memoirs.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This is supposed to be an incredibly honest account of the key decisions in the president’s life. There’s a whole chapter dedicated to “smooth vs. crunchy.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Is it really a good thing for President Bush to remind us of the decisions he made? I would have just let people forget.

name: David Letterman
monologue: They’ve opened an exclusive nightclub in New York City, just for dogs. This is why the rest of the world hates us.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Senate held hearings on what role Goldman Sachs played in the mortgage meltdown of 2008. They allegedly sold bad mortgages to their clients and then bet against them to make profits for themselves. I think that’s what the “American Idol” judges are doing to us this season with these crappy singers.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They’re down to the final six contestants on “American Idol.” It’s not a great crop of singers this year. They’re thinking of renaming the show “America Doesn’t Got Talent.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Stephen Hawking says that not only does he believe that aliens exist, but that we shouldn’t make contact with them, as they could be very angry. Especially aliens from Arizona.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Arizona has recently passed the toughest immigration law in history. The idea behind it is to drive illegal immigrants out of Arizona and back to their homeland of Los Angeles.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The top executive from Goldman Sachs testified before Congress today, which proves that crooks always return to the scene of the crime.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama is now considering approving the development of a hypersonic missile that can deliver its payload anywhere in the world within an hour. It was a joint venture between the U.S. military and Domino’s Pizza.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Charlie Brown “Peanuts” brand is going to be sold to Joe Boxer for $175 million. Because nothing’s more macho than a pair of boxer shorts that says “Peanuts” right across the front.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Apparently the Icelandic volcano crisis cost the airline industry more than three billion dollars. Which explains why Delta's new bag-check fee is $400,000.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Amy Winehouse is being treated for bruised ribs after she fell at her home over the weekend. When she got to the hospital, they offered to give her morphine, but she was like, "Nah, it’s cool. I brought my own."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A 15-year-old boy here in New York has been accepted to Harvard, MIT, and Caltech. Though he's still hoping to get accepted by his top choice . . . girls.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Ben & Jerry’s was giving out free ice cream and Starbucks was giving out free pastries all day. Everyone is getting cocky because we have free health insurance.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was announced today that pigeons will have their own reality TV show. It will be hosted by Mike Tyson. He collects pigeons the way Fabio collects my fan letters.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Pigeons are great messengers. They can fly at speeds up to 60 mph. They’re dangerous though, as sometimes they can’t stop in time. They’re like flying Toyotas.

name: David Letterman
monologue: George W. Bush’s memoir is coming out in November. It’s called “Decision Points” and it’s about big decisions in his life. I’ve already made a decision not to read it.
