monologue: Top Ten Signs Your Governor Is Nuts

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Arizona has passed the strictest immigration bill in American history. A hundred people have been stopped already — and that was just in one van.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congress has voted against giving itself a pay raise. They thought giving themselves a pay raise now would be unpopular. I think giving them any pay at all right now is unpopular.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama’s National Security Adviser James L. Jones apologized for telling an ethnic joke at a speech. Political insiders were shocked — someone said something stupid and inappropriate and it wasn’t Joe Biden?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: An oil slick the size of Rhode Island is making its way across the Gulf of Mexico. An oil slick the size of Rhode Island — isn’t that called New Jersey?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During a Goldman Sachs hearing yesterday, Sen. Carl Levin used the S-word 11 times on live television when quoting an e-mail. Which begs the question — if a guy swears on C-SPAN and there’s no one watching to hear it, does he really make a sound?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new survey found that one-third of married women with pets say their animals are better listeners than their husbands. When husbands heard that they were like, "Huh? You say something?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A woman in Staten Island is facing charges after she gave her daughter’s friend a peanut butter and jelly sandwich containing the painkiller Oxycodone. There was some miscommunication. When the girl asked her to take the edge off, she was just talking about the crust.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Rolls-Royce is offering the Pentagon a special deal on engines for the Joint Strike Fighter jet. Not to be outdone, Toyota is offering a special deal on engines for kamikaze pilots.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Gov. Rick Perry of Texas shot a coyote while he was jogging. Who carries a gun while jogging? I can barely manage my iPod.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I like the idea of runners carrying guns. Think of how interesting the Boston Marathon will be.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The International Olympic Committee stripped China of its bronze medal in the women’s team gymnastics event from the 2000 Olympics because they fielded an underage athlete. Ten years later, when she still hadn’t finished high school, they figured it out.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Stephen Hawking says he does believe in aliens but we shouldn’t try to contact them. I want nothing to do with aliens — I’m fine with Canadians though.

name: David Letterman
monologue: CBS has a show called “The Mentalist,” about a detective with heightened powers of observation. He’s so good, he can tell the difference between a Goldman Sachs executive that’s a lying crook, and a Goldman Sachs executive that’s a lying weasel.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Once again, Los Angeles has been named the smoggiest city in the United States. Take that, hell.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There are fears that the oil spill in the gulf will merge with a massive slick of self-tanner from the cast of “Jersey Shore” in Miami.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Colombian pop singer Shakira was in Phoenix to join the fight against Arizona’s tough new immigration law. It reminds me a lot of the '80s, when the Beastie Boys came to Arizona to fight for our right to party.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I think that if every immigrant looked like Shakira, there would be no immigration laws except the ones that would keep immigrants in the country.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: About 210,000 gallons of oil per day are leaking into the gulf. That’s equivalent to 10 buckets of fried chicken.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The oil companies are promising to clean this whole mess up and, believe me, if you’ve ever been to a gas station restroom, you know how good they are at cleaning up.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Stephen Hawking says that aliens probably do exist, but that we should not interact with them. He’s even against giving them driver’s licenses.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Rielle Hunter appeared on “Oprah” to discuss her love affair with John Edwards. And not to be outdone, next week John Edwards is appearing to discuss his love affair with John Edwards.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A funeral home in Puerto Rico propped up the body of a dead man on a motorcycle for his wake. Some people at the wake called the sight “offensive,” while Sandra Bullock called it “an awesome idea.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man on a Delta flight from Paris to Atlanta claimed he had explosives in his luggage. Officials told the man it was a federal offense, while Delta told him he’d have to pay an extra $15 per carry-on bomb.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Florida was arrested at a traffic stop for trying to swallow a baggy of marijuana along with a double cheeseburger. Either he brought the marijuana from home, or McDonalds is making some awesome new combo meals.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s one of my favorite days of the year: International Dance Day. It’s one of two things that unite the international community — international dancing and . . . the International House of Pancakes.

monologue: Line dancing and square dancing are kind of hard to tell apart, like this show and public access.

monologue: The way you dance says a lot about you. My favorite dance is the “Macarena,” so what does that say about me?

name: David Letterman
monologue: It’s prom time. One year, I had to take my cousin to the prom. I don’t know who was more embarrassed — him or me.

monologue: Top Ten Other Revelations in the Laura Bush Book

monologue: This oil spill in the Gulf keeps getting worse and worse. They’re calling it the greatest threat to New Orleans since George Bush was president.

monologue: Arizona has passed the strictest immigration bill in history. Police can now ask for your papers if they see you coming out of El Pollo Loco.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A lot of people are boycotting Arizona Iced Tea, which is made in New York City. But that’s irrelevant to the boycott organizers — Snapple.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s a new nasal spray that uses the “cuddle hormone” oxytocin to help men feel more affectionate. I thought I was clearing my sinuses with Afrin, and I ended up spooning with my pharmacist.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Georgia passed a new measure that requires adults in pickup trucks to wear a seatbelt. Not only that, they also have to use a cup holder for their beer.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Arizona Senate passed a bill making it illegal for a person to “intentionally” create “a human-animal hybrid.” And right afterward, one farmer was like, "Define intentionally."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The villain from “Nightmare on Elm Street” is Freddy Krueger, who kills you in your dreams. That’s impossible, but it is possible to have your dreams killed — it happens to me here every night.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Freddy Krueger doesn’t scare me that much. He’s a dude with gloves and a hat. He’s basically Mr. Peanut in a bad mood.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I like when characters in scary movies have scary names like Count Dracula, Hannibal the Cannibal, or Mel Gibson.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Welcome to the "Late Show," the other bomb on Broadway.

monologue: Top Ten BP Excuses

monologue: This week is Teacher Appreciation Week. Teacher Appreciation Week began in 1985 when state and federal governments decided that giving teachers a holiday was cheaper than paying them more.

monologue: A man named Jason Pfeiffer claims he was Michael Jackson’s boyfriend. Pfeiffer says he told the story to prove that Jackson wasn’t a pedophile — although it seems like that would have been more helpful during the trial.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There were big demonstrations protesting Arizona’s new immigration law. Despite the controversy, the state is going ahead with their Cinco de Mayo party. I guess it’s a going-away thing.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad spoke at the U.N. today. He arrived in New York Saturday night, rented an SUV, parked it in Times Square, changed his shirt in an alley, and went to the hotel.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Someone tried to detonate an SUV rigged with explosives in Times Square. It was a Nissan Pathfinder. The bombing suspect realized that if he drove a Toyota, he would be putting his own life in danger.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Experts are saying that the last time an SUV got this much attention, there was a 9-iron sticking out of the window.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The environmental impact from the Gulf oil spill is unbelievable. They say a lot of birds are trying to leave the area. Arizona said that any birds entering from out of state will be arrested.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: While he was on the Gulf Coast yesterday, President Obama said, “Let me be clear: BP is responsible for this leak. BP will be paying the bill.” And BP was like “Uh, bailout?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Pakistani Taliban has claimed responsibility for Saturday’s failed car bomb attack in Times Square. I’m no terrorism expert, but I don’t think it makes you scarier when you claim responsibility for something that failed.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Saturday night, Chris Brown sang the national anthem before the Mayweather-Mosley fight in Vegas. Chris Brown sang the National Anthem before a fight? That's like Michael Vick opening the Westminster Dog Show.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I read that a cafe in Brooklyn is now selling a $12 cup of coffee. Inside the cup you’ll find hints of apricot, pineapple, kiwi, and lime. And outside the cup you’ll find an idiot who spends 12 bucks on coffee.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I will have to see everyones’ papers to make sure you are in CBS legally. We have had hobos sneaking in from Canada.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Apparently some of the lawyers that wrote the Arizona immigration law are tied to Belgian extremists. I didn’t know that Belgians could be extreme about anything — except maybe waffles.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: At least here in California, immigrants end up doing the jobs Americans don’t want, such as talk show hosts, or governor of the state.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It’s so nice today in New York City that people were leaving bombs in convertibles.

monologue: Top Ten Dumb Guy Ways To Fix The Oil Spill

monologue: They caught the guy that they think tried to bomb Times Square last weekend. It’s amazing that he made it through security and onto an aircraft. I still can’t get my tweezers on the plane.

monologue: Lots of oil is still leaking off the coast of Louisiana. BP has a plan to create a giant vinegar spill to turn the Gulf of Mexico into a delicious salad dressing.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was elimination night on ”Dancing With the Stars.” I don’t like all this eliminating that goes on, it’s so negative. I would like to see a show where they add people every week.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: They made an arrest in the failed Times Square bombing attack. It turns out the suspect is a foreign-born, naturalized American citizen. He would have been fine in Arizona.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Some of the suspect’s neighbors said he claimed to work on Wall Street. They were relieved to find out he was just a terrorist.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: BP has promised to pay for all of the clean-up costs for the spill in the Gulf. They say they don’t care how high they have to raise gas prices, but they’ll pay for it.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Former aides to John Edwards claim that Rielle Hunter lied to Oprah during an interview. You can lie in court, you can lie at work, but when you lie to Oprah, that is downright un-American.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: We caught a suspect in the failed Times Square attack. The suspect says he acted alone — even his bomb wasn’t in on it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A DMV clerk in Massachusetts hacked into the state computer and cleared her driving record of $1,400 in parking fines. She was arrested for the crime, but rewarded for actually doing something while working at a DMV.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: According to the NYPD, the most stolen cars in New York City are Toyotas. Actually, most of them aren’t really stolen — they just take off on their own.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The world’s oldest living person, aged 114, passed away. The cause of death — you guessed it — a knife fight.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This curse of the world’s oldest person continues — they always seem to die.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today is “Star Wars Day.” The “Star Wars” movies have endured for so long because the characters are iconic. There’s Darth Vader, Obi-Wan Kenobi, that big lovable furry thing — Harrison Ford.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The “force” itself was like a character — an all-powerful presence that dominates the entire galaxy. These days we call it “Oprah.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: Last night, the audience was awful. It was as quiet in here as Cinco de Mayo in Arizona.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things Overheard At BP Headquarters

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Cinco de Mayo commemorates the Mexican Army’s surprise victory over sobriety back in 1862.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Oddly, Cinco de Mayo is more popular here than in Mexico. Cinco de Mayo to us is what David Hasselhoff is to Germany.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Authorities say Faisal Shahzad, the Times Square bombing suspect, used the wrong kind of fertilizer, which is what happens when you don’t watch Martha Stewart.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was reported that Shahzad went to terrorist camp in Pakistan. Honestly, who are these parents that are sending their kids to terrorist camp?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Happy Cinco de Mayo. This is the only day they do this — if you get pulled over for drunk driving, they put salt around the rim of the breathalyzer.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Cinco de Mayo is a holiday celebrated by over 80 million Mexicans — and that’s just here in Los Angeles.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday was “Youth Day” in China, so the kids only had to work a 15-hour day.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The United Nations has appointed Iran to sit on the Women’s Rights panel. Also on the panel: Ben Roethlisberger, Chris Brown, Phil Spector, Robert Blake, and chairman, O.J. Simpson.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It’s Cinco de Mayo, or as they call it in Arizona: May 5th.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Police in Texas arrested a man who was using the alias “Barack Obama” while trying to steal money from 35 ATMs. They could tell something was up when a guy named Barack Obama was trying to take money from banks instead of giving it to them.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Happy Cinco de Mayo. If you don’t know what that means, maybe you’re a little out of touch — or maybe you’re the governor of Arizona.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A lot of the U.S. used to be part of Mexico, including Arizona. But they’re a bit touchy about that right now.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don’t drink anymore for Cinco de Mayo. I celebrate with Mexican food, or as it’s known in Mexico: “food.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: It was hot in Arizona today. Folks there were fanning themselves with their birth certificates.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I finally signed up for Twitter yesterday. I waited to do it because I was afraid it would ruin my life — and it did.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It turns out the suspect in the failed Times Square bombing is not the brightest. He left the keys to the getaway car and the key to his apartment in the SUV with the bomb in it. Maybe it was really a bong in the car and not a bomb.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday was Cinco de Mayo and today was Cinco de Dow Jones.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The market was so bad today that Goldman Sachs had to lay off three congressmen.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Greece has overspent on large social programs, with a national debt so large that they can never pay it back. Thank God that could never happen here.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: British Petroleum is planning to stop the oil leak in the “Gulf of Texaco” by lowering a box down over the leak. Who thought of this, Wile E. Coyote?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Royal Caribbean says that 94 people got sick with vomiting and diarrhea on one of its cruises. BP was like, “Good luck cleaning that up.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: An employee at NBC won the $266 million lottery jackpot. The last time anyone at NBC made that much money, they were being paid to leave the “Tonight Show.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The night before leaving his bomb-packed SUV in Times Square, Faisal Shahzad did a practice run with a white Isuzu. People became suspicious when they realized it was 2010 and someone was still driving an Isuzu.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s Election Day in Britain. I’m excited about it as you are. And I know you’re excited about this as Mel Gibson is about Hanukkah.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It looks like David Cameron of the Conservative Party might win. The Conservatives are like the Republicans, except with bad teeth.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The prime minister now is Gordon Brown of the Labor party. He has spent more time in Labor than the Octomom.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don’t really follow British politics since coming to America. I follow American politics, which is why I support whichever political party you support.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Welcome to New York City, where there’s something happening every minute and most of it goes unprosecuted.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Pieces Of Advice For Being A Good Mother

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We have Mother’s Day this weekend, but it’s also National Cheeseburger Month. That shows you our priorities in this country — moms get one day, cheeseburgers get a whole month.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Although it seems like nothing is getting accomplished in the Gulf, and the situation is getting worse every day, the government has been involved in the clean-up effort since the beginning. They said that, as proof of their involvement, nothing has really been accomplished and the situation is getting worse every day.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The stock market crisis is so bad that Wall Street is starting to look like Wal-Mart Street.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The crisis in Greece is being blamed on overspending, but the government claims that the spending is necessary to stimulate the economy, according to Greek President Barack Obama-opolous.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s speculation that the 1,000-point drop in the Dow may have been sparked by a typo, where someone entered “billion” instead of “million” on a trading order. Economists are saying a single letter hasn’t caused this many problems since the letter “Dubya.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s a doctor in Britain who lets his patients watch their favorite DVD during surgery to distract them, and avoid the need for general anesthesia. Here's how it works: it doesn't.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week is the 50th anniversary of the birth control pill. At least, I’m like, 99 percent sure it is.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A “Planet of the Apes” prequel is coming out next summer called “Rise of the Apes.” It will cover the apes' growth, evolution, and the summer they spent together at a house on the Jersey Shore.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Aren’t the standards for late night lower than they used to be? We’re here, so I’d say so.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: “Iron Man 2” is opening this weekend. The bad guy is called “Whiplash.” That doesn’t sound very scary to me. What does he do, drive people around and then slam on the brakes?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Whiplash can only be defeated by one thing: the personal injury lawyer.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It was chilly in Times Square this weekend. The tourists were huddling around smoking SUVs.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things You Don't Want To Hear From A Guy Dressed As Iron Man

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Oprah did her show from New York to celebrate the 10th anniversary of O magazine. Dr. Phil allowed them to shave his moustache, which is currently being used to sop up oil in the Gulf.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Bobby Brown got engaged over the weekend. They say it’s the first time he’s been on one knee without the help of a police taser.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I tweeted a lot this weekend. It’s amazing how you can go from thinking Twitter is the biggest waste of time ever to it actually becoming the biggest waste of time ever.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The government announced today that they’re making big changes to the No-Fly list. Apparently, asking terrorists to be on the honor system has not been working.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It was reported that Supreme Court nominee Elena Kagan used to date Eliot Spitzer when they were both at Harvard but he denied it. Spitzer said he didn’t start dating until well after he was married.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Obama administration has revealed the size of America’s nuclear arsenal. We have 1,000 warheads aimed at China, 1,000 aimed at Russia, and the rest aimed at Fox News.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood said that soon, the U.S. will reopen the Mexican border to trucks. This came as a shock to Mexican truck drivers, who didn’t even know it was closed.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tiger Woods withdrew from the Players Championship yesterday and said, “I’ve been playing with a bad neck for quite a while, I might have a bulging disk.” Then, reporters started giggling and Tiger had to repeat "I said bulging disk. Come on guys, grow up."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: President Obama nominated Elena Kagan to be the next Supreme Court justice, against the advice of Joe Biden, who wanted Iron Man.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A porn star from Poland claims that she has been having an affair with Mel Gibson. I thought Mel would have gone for a German.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Britain’s current prime minister, Gordon Brown, announced that he is stepping down and his replacement might be the education secretary, a gentleman named Ed Balls. I would like to make a plea on behalf of late night talk show hosts and bad comedians everywhere — I implore the voters of Britain to make sure that happens.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The BP executives responsible for the big oil spill in the Gulf testified before Congress. They were criticized by the same guys that approved drilling in the Gulf.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Thoughts That Went Through Dallas Braden's Mind While He Threw His Perfect Game

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The June edition of Playboy magazine will be printed in 3-D. Haven’t we had that for a while? It’s called a strip club.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tiger Woods’ swing coach announced that he is quitting. Apparently he discovered that Tiger had 19 other swing coaches around the country.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The swing coach quit by text message, which is like karma shooting a hole-in-one.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: That idea about using a concrete dome to cover up the oil leak in the Gulf did not work. Experts are calling this the worst use of a concrete dome since they built that stadium for the Detroit Lions.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congress told BP that they can’t “label this catastrophic failure an unpredictable and unforeseeable occurrence.” Congress used that excuse already for not catching the financial meltdown in time.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Greece is a relatively small country, much like a state in the U.S. But it overspent and over-borrowed, promised expensive pension plans, overtaxed, and it over-regulated business. So the state it would be here is California.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In Colorado, one of the gubernatorial candidates has taken out a Craigslist ad to find a running mate. Is that a good idea? It didn’t work so well when John McCain tried it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: BP is now using a special containment dome called a "top hat" that shoots methanol into the oil leak. A top hat that shoots methanol? That doesn't sound like an emergency device — that sounds like something Lady Gaga would wear to the VMAs.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Department of Agriculture has decided to set new, stricter salmonella standards for poultry. I’m no expert, but I’m pretty sure the standard should just be “no salmonella allowed.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A physics professor recently noticed a 99-year-old error in the Oxford English Dictionary that mistakenly defines the word “siphon.” In response, Oxford has sent the man a certificate, which correctly defines the word "nerd."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A report found that hotel guests ordered fewer movies in the first quarter of this year than last year. That probably has something to do with the fact that golf has gotten so "porny."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tyra Banks is writing a new series of kids’ books. She is the first supermodel to write a kids’ book since Kate Moss wrote “Green Eggs and Crack.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Google’s new Android phone is outselling Apple’s iPhone. I don’t know what an Android can do, besides dance the robot or become the governor of California.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new study says that 77 percent of people admitted using their phones while driving. The other 23 percent are lying.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: President Obama said that we rely too much on gadgets. He gave a passionate speech about technology, but he had to stop when the teleprompter broke.

name: David Letterman
monologue: BP is now dispersing dispersants to counter the oil spill in the Gulf. I think we can trust BP with toxic chemicals, don’t you?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Surprises At The Senate Oil Spill Hearing

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: “American Idol” is the BP oil spill of television. No matter what we do with it, we cannot get it to stop.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Larry King and his wife are not getting divorced despite allegations of cheating. The family spokesman said Larry loves his wife, and loves being a family, and when they started to divide the property, he realized how ridiculous he would look wearing only one suspender.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: BP still has not managed to stop the oil leak in the Gulf. The plan now is to plug the leak this week with a “top hat.” But first they have to find an enormous game of monopoly that has the piece.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They’re considering a plan to fire golf balls and rubber tires into the leak to clog it. Toyota and Tiger Woods may finally have a chance to redeem themselves after all.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: BP, Transocean, and Halliburton are all blaming each other for the Gulf oil spill. And you know what? They’re all right.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A man in his 70s known as the “geezer bandit” has held up his ninth bank. He says he’s going to keep robbing banks until he finds one with money in it.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Happy birthday to the birth control pill, which turns 50 years old this week. You know what that means? If you’re 51, there’s a good chance that your parents didn’t want you.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The new Coors Light case of beer has a window in it, and when it turns blue, that means you know your beer is cold. That’s way more convenient than the old way: touching the cans.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Disney is partnering with a South Korean company to launch a Korean-language Disney channel. Mickey will still be known as “Mickey,” and Minnie will still be known as “Minnie.” However, Pluto will now be known as “Delicious.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Police in Cairo have detained an American man who arrived from JFK with two handguns, 250 bullets, swords, daggers, and knives in his luggage. When they heard this, JFK screeners were like, “Sure he had all those things but what he didn’t have was bottled water or nail clippers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Prison inmates in Louisiana are now pitching in to clean up the Gulf oil spill. At this point, the solutions have been: dump chemicals into the ocean, shoot a bunch of garbage underwater, and release prisoners. If none of that works, they’re going to have al-Qaida come take a look at it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Sarah Palin has a new book coming out called “America by Heart: Reflections on Family, Faith, and Flag.” Coincidentally, “Faith” and “Flag” are the two names Palin has picked out if she ever has twins.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s the beginning of the Cannes Film Festival. Everyone that matters in TV and movies is in Cannes right now — which explains why I’m here.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: How can you judge movies? It’s very subjective. You can’t compare a movie like “Police Academy” to a real work of art like “Police Academy 7.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The top prize at the festival is the “Palme d’Or.” It sounds fancy but it translates to “straight to DVD.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The judges gave Roman Polanski the Palme d’Or a few years ago. That was back when Polanski wanted to appear before judges.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It’s such a beautiful day in New York City that the terrorists are using propane tanks for barbecues.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Signs You're Not Going To Win The Miss USA Pageant

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I’ve never been more glad that I’m not a Gulf shrimp than I am today.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The state of Hawaii passed a new law allowing the state government to ignore requests for President Obama’s birth certificate from the “Birthers.” From now on, every future president should be required to be born on camera and in front of a national landmark.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Obesity-related illnesses cost around $150 billion a year, and cause long-term health problems for our children. But on the plus side, the fatter they are, the less likely it is that they’ll run away from home.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: You have to weigh everything. Not just the kids — everything.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the top people in the petroleum industry, the oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico will not affect gas prices. They were going up anyway.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: One in 8 people are saying that they will not buy gas from BP any more. That is, unless they’re cheaper than the gas station across the street.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: They tried a big dome to stop the leak and that didn’t work, and then they tried a little dome and that didn’t work, and then they tried to stuff the hole with garbage. Now they’re talking about dumping lettuce and croutons into the Gulf and declaring it a giant salad.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Following their financial meltdown, bankers in Iceland are being thrown in jail. The prosecution is using a little-known thing called “justice.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A hotel in the United Arab Emirates has installed a vending machine in its lobby that dispenses gold bars and gold coins. You think you get frustrated when your Doritos get stuck in the machine? Try losing a bar of gold.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A woman in Britain is selling wallabies as a good alternative to lawnmowers. They say the wallabies work just as well as regular mowers — until you get drunk and try to ride one of them into town.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that a certain species of fish has a gene that can cause STDs in humans. So if you get an embarrassing STD, you now have the perfect excuse — just say you got it from that trout you slept with.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A survey found that 20 percent of parents have second thoughts on the name they gave their baby. But that doesn’t mean we love you any less, little Adolf Jonas Brothers McGillicutty.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: They’ve just noticed that the planet Jupiter is missing one of its rings. They should try looking in Uranus.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Economists are saying that a college degree may not be necessary to succeed in life. Look at me, I didn’t go to college and here I am. Seriously kids, go to college.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You always hear about the late night wars, but you never hear about the daytime wars, and that’s because no one dares to compete against Oprah. She’s like the Kraken, but helpful.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Tonight is our season finale. Usually, you only have a season finale when Jay Leno wants your time slot.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Ways BP Can Improve Its Image

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This has not been a good day if you’re a BP stockholder with playoff tickets for game seven with the Cavaliers.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Phoenix, Ariz. is getting its first-ever Hispanic bishop. He will be appointed July 19, and then deported July 20.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Nancy Pelosi told Catholic leaders they need to support the Democratic version of immigration reform, and to preach it from the pulpit. She would have said more but she had to leave to attend a rally for the separation of church and state.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama said he’s angry and frustrated with the oil spill in the Gulf and the oil companies behind it. He said he’s tired of all the finger-pointing — then he blamed the Bush administration for everything.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: NBC canceled “Law & Order” after 20 seasons. It’s too bad, but they had to make room for the new Jay Leno show, “Jaw & Order.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: An 87-year-old woman in Florida was arrested for selling crack cocaine. She was sentenced to two months in jail — or as she calls it “life.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: “Robin Hood” opens this weekend. Robin Hood is famous for stealing from the rich and giving to the poor, which made him a folk hero in 12th century England. Nowadays, we call that sort of thing “communism.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If someone was stealing from the rich and giving to the poor in America, Glenn Beck would go insane — more insane.

name: David Letterman
monologue: BP has lowered a hose down to the oil spill in the Gulf. They’re pumping the leaking oil up to a tanker. The bad news is that the tanker is the Exxon Valdez.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For the first time, an Arab-American, Rima Fakih, won Miss USA. Rima is very excited and she hopes this will help get her name off the No-Fly list.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Scientists have developed a car that can run on water. The only problem is that the water has to come from the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: British Petroleum is starting to get defensive. Their new slogan is, “Yeah, like you’ve never spilled anything before.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sarah Palin and George Bush both have books coming out this fall. This could plunge America into a huge crayon shortage.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: At a rally this weekend, Sarah Palin said, “We’re all Arizonans now." At which point every immigrant in Arizona was like, "So . . . we can stay?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In a new interview, BP’s CEO Tony Hayward said the Gulf oil spill is “relatively tiny” compared to the “very big ocean.” That’s like telling someone who’s just been shot not to worry about the bullet, because they’re really, really fat.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A woman in Texas was arrested for shooting at a census worker who wouldn’t leave her property. The census worker was pretty committed to her job, though. Even as she was being fired at, she was like, "Is that your only firearm? Do you share it with a loved one, a spouse, or a common-law partner?”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A fertility clinic is now offering parents the option to select the eye and hair color of their babies. Don’t you miss the days when people would just get pregnant, have their eight babies, and go on “Entertainment Tonight”?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: We have as a guest tonight Archbishop Desmond Tutu. I’m going to ask the question that’s on everyone’s mind: “As a bishop, do you always have to move diagonally?”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Desmond Tutu is from South Africa, which I think is a fantastic name for a country, because it tells you exactly where it is.

name: David Letterman
monologue: This is the time of year that networks bring out their new TV shows. NBC has announced their fall line-up, and BP has promised to help with the clean-up.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things I Want To Do As Miss USA

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Another Arizona boycott is brewing. The Phoenix Suns are refusing to play defense.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Suns played so badly that the Arizona legislature voted to deport them.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Attorney General Eric Holder has said that he may sue Arizona for their new immigration law, though he admitted that he had not read the law yet. That didn’t stop them from passing healthcare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Supreme Court declared that sex offenders can be held indefinitely, even after their sentence is complete if they are considered dangerous — unless they won an Oscar or they have a lot of friends that are celebrities.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Have you heard about this guy, Richard Blumenthal, a Democratic candidate for Senate in Connecticut? It turns out he actually lied about serving in Vietnam. Not good. In fact today, he said this was the most scared he’s been since he became the first man to walk on the moon.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Officials in Naples, Italy believe that local pizza makers are digging up coffins from a cemetery and using the wood to heat their ovens. Which explains one restaurant's slogan, "Naples Pizza: It tastes just like Grandma used to . . . taste!”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After admitting to an affair with a staffer, Indiana Congressman Mark Souder said he is leaving office to focus on repairing his marriage, and renewing his walk with the Lord. And today, the Lord was like, “Uh — why don’t you start without me.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Aviation officials in Europe announced new rules that will allow planes to fly through the volcanic ash if they get special approval. I’d love to hear the pilot on one of those flights: “To your left, you’ll see a massive ash cloud . . . windows are sort of useless right now. I might as well come back and sit with you guys.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was my birthday yesterday. I celebrated the way I always do. I stayed home and I called Bob Saget.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: My mother used to make me clootie dumplings for my birthday. By the way, “Clootie Dumplings” is the name I used to dance under.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I’m glad no one threw me a surprise party. I don’t like being surrounded by people that are waiting for me to say something funny. That’s just not my thing.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The season finale of “Lost” is coming up. I know how the show ends — their luggage shows up.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Spoilers for the ‘Lost’ Finale

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Yesterday, Justin Bieber was nominated for a BET award. BET stands for Black Entertainment Television. Justin Bieber is none of those things.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I don’t know how Justin Bieber was nominated for a BET award. This is what happens when you let Stevie Wonder choose the nominees.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In Louisiana, BP claims that it’s making progress with the leaking oil in the Gulf. They’re working on a plan to heat the Gulf up to 600 degrees and use it to fry chicken.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Larry King and his wife have called off their divorce. They both had to make concessions: His wife no longer has to say “King me,” and Larry agreed to wear a “Do Not Resuscitate” sign.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Pulitzer Prize for fiction was handed out today. It was given to Richard Blumenthal for his Vietnam war claims.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Blumenthal is under fire for claiming that he served in Vietnam, when he actually didn’t. The only combat experience he has is shooting himself in the foot.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: BP has inserted a siphon tube to suck up all the oil out of the damaged Gulf well. They have a lot of experience in this area. It’s the same tube they’ve been using to suck the money out of our wallets for years.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During a speech in Ohio yesterday, President Obama reminded the crowd that the economy was much worse a year ago. Then the crowd reminded him that he was already president a year ago.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During halftime at the Celtics-Magic playoff game last night, a referee threw a basketball at an obnoxious, rowdy fan. The ref shouldn’t have done that, but on the bright side . . . I got a free basketball.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: According to new research, unattractive defendants are 22 percent more likely to be convicted than good-looking ones. Although to be fair, the good-looking defendants have a much harder time after they're convicted.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that the average man tells 1,092 lies a year. I’m sorry, I don’t know why I said that — it’s actually 1,091.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Pete Townsend of “The Who” turns 65 today. He has won a Grammy award, a Tony award, and best of all, today, he gets a lifetime supply of Metamucil.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Peter Mayhew also has a birthday today. He played Chewbacca in the “Star Wars” movies. Chewbacca and Pete Townsend are very different. One is a big hairy ape who, I think, is secretly in love with Harrison Ford, and the other one is Chewbacca.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today is International Museum Day. Museums are an important part of our culture, and they need an international day, just like pancakes, which have an international house.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It’s such a nice day in New York City that I wanted to go down to the beach and wait for the first tar ball.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things Overheard At The White House State Dinner

name: Jay Leno
monologue: At the White House state dinner, Mexican President Calderon said that he and President Obama have a lot in common. They’re both presidents of beautiful countries, they’re both left-handed, and they both preside over 40 million Mexican people.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Kansas City used car salesman has admitted sending over $23,000 to al-Qaida. Just when you thought al-Qaida couldn’t get any lower, they link up with used car salesmen.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The U.S. Navy announced this week that they’re using sea lions to fight terrorism. They hid a bomb in the water and a trained sea lion found it in less than a minute. The bad news is, the sea lion balanced the bomb on his nose and then threw it back at the trainer.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Richard Blumenthal says he will not apologize for misleading people about his military record. He says that he misspoke, using the word “in,” instead of “during,” in reference to Vietnam. Sort of like using the word “misspoke” instead of ”lied.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In case you haven't been watching, the two final contestants on “American Idol” are Crystal Bowersox and Lee DeWyze. Or as they’ll be known in six months, “who?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new social networking site called “Togetherville” was launched this week, aimed at kids between 6 and 10 years old. They’re calling it “Togetherville” because “To Catch a Predatorville” was too long.

name: Jimmy Fallon

monologue: It’s so hot in L.A. that Lindsay Lohan went to rehab just for the air conditioning.

monologue: Some people think the Chupacabra originates in Mexico because all of the sightings have been along the border states, except for Arizona, because they don’t carry papers.

monologue: Today is a day of cautious optimism. The BP well has been capped and Lindsay Lohan is in rehab, but we’re not sure how long either one is going to hold.

monologue: For the first time since April, oil has stopped gushing into the Gulf of Mexico. I’m not sure what engineers they used to fix it but I think we can rule out the guys who created the new iPhone 4.

monologue: Apple will now offer a free iPhone case for all iPhone users. It’s not going to help reception, but it protects the iPhone after you throw it against the wall.

monologue: Experts are now saying that these thousands of accidents caused by Toyotas were really driver error. The driver error was buying a Toyota.

monologue: BP stopped the oil leak at 3:25 p.m. Eastern Time. And at 3:26 p.m., Mel Gibson and Lindsay Lohan began jockeying for the title of "biggest disaster."

monologue: Someone in Utah is sending an anonymous letter to state lawmakers with names of people who are suspected to be illegal immigrants. Some lawmakers saw members of their own communities on the list and were like “No way — Jose?”

monologue: To celebrate National Ice Cream Day on Sunday, Baskin Robbins is retiring five flavors. Really? That’s like celebrating Grandparent’s Day by pulling the plug.

monologue: Rumors are that Bristol Palin and Levi Johnston are going to film a reality show. Sarah Palin says she can’t wait to start shooting, but that’s totally unrelated.

monologue: O.J. Simpson’s lawyer, Robert Shapiro, has agreed to represent Lindsay Lohan, but only if she agrees to go to jail. Where was this deal when O.J. was on trial?

monologue: Dick Cheney is recovering from heart surgery in the hospital. I understand Fox sent flowers, and MSNBC sent a large pepperoni pizza with extra cheese.

monologue: There are reports that Mel Gibson is moving back to Australia and Australians aren’t happy with that. They’re like, “Why do you think we sent him to you in the first place?”

monologue: They want to build a mosque near the site of the World Trade Center. If you put a mosque there, there’s no way terrorists will blow it up. If I was in charge, I would put a mosque on top of every building in America.

monologue: BP’s oil cap seems to be working. The cap they’re using is childproof, so it’ll never come off.

monologue: Dentists always tell you that X-rays are harmless, and then they throw this lead blanket on you and leave the room.

monologue: They’re expecting 120,000 people and three of these people will be female.

monologue: A new survey found that more parents are teaching their babies sign language before they learn how to talk. Babies’ favorite word in sign language? Whatever putting your whole hand in your mouth means.

monologue: A Burger King employee in Long Island was arrested for selling crack in the restaurant’s parking lot. Most people turned him down though. They were like “No thanks, that stuff’ll kill you. Can I get a double whopper with cheese and bacon, two onion rings, and a milkshake?”

name: Craig Ferguson

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I’m too cheap to make a real costume. I’m just going to take everything off except for my socks, and I’ll be Charlie Sheen.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I’m looking forward to Halloween, seeing all the monsters and the nightmarish imagery. Then I’ll turn off the campaign ads and wait for the trick-or-treaters.

monologue: I don’t like when people make their lawns into graveyards with zombies writhing around on the ground. If I want to see a scary creature twisted on the ground, I’d throw David Hasselhoff a hamburger.

monologue: Pontiac is out of business. If you want to see a Pontiac now, you have to go to Cuba — or to Jay Leno’s garage.

monologue: No one came to my house to trick-or-treat. I think the moat might be scaring people away.

monologue: I have all this candy left at my house now. This morning, I had a Skittles omelet.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I hope you all had a nice Halloween. How many are sick today from too much candy? How many are sick from too many political ads on TV?

monologue: Authorities believe those suspicious deliveries by UPS last week may have been a dry run for a terrorist plot — or a really smart move by FedEx.

monologue: It seems most experts are predicting that Republicans will win back the House tomorrow. When Americans heard that they were like, “Wait, we can win back our houses?”

name: Craig Ferguson

monologue: Republicans are saying, “It’s time for a change.” And Democrats are saying, “Stay the course.” And Charlie Sheen is saying, “Where are my pants?”

monologue: Charlie Sheen filed for divorce from his wife. I guess he finally had enough of her shenanigans.

monologue: Top Ten Reasons I'm Glad To Be Named Justin Bieber

monologue: On the bright side, at least now there will be some leftovers at Thanksgiving.

monologue: If you want to find out how many of your Facebook friends are real friends, post an update that says you’re moving and you need help. The people that respond are your real friends.

monologue: Congratulations to the San Francisco Giants who won the World Series. People in San Francisco haven't been this excited since Lady Gaga's last album came out.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: China started conducting its nationwide census this week. That’s right, parents will be required to list each child’s age, grade, and occupation.

monologue: Martin Sheen, the father of Charlie Sheen, is reportedly having a family intervention in Ireland. I’m sorry? They’re sending an alcoholic to Ireland? That’s like sending Lindsay Lohan to Bogota, Colombia.

monologue: I’m pretty sure an intervention in Ireland is where your loved ones all confront you and say you don’t drink enough.

monologue: All of the election coverage was constantly being interrupted by the computers, updates, and text messages from Brett Favre.

monologue: The tea party needs to pick a tougher name. “Tea party” sounds like something I do with my ferrets every Sunday.

monologue: Ohio Republican John Boehner will take over for Nancy Pelosi. Those are some big eyes to fill.

monologue: The government will pump an additional $600 billion into the economy. I guess they have to make up for what Meg Whitman isn’t spending anymore.

monologue: The unemployment rate has gone up — by about 65 Democrats.

monologue: This weekend is the New York City Marathon, the one race in America that has yet to be insulted by Mel GIbson.

He worked his way through school and became the first person in his family to graduate from college. Then, sadly, he fell in with the wrong crowd and wound up in Congress.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Levi Johnston said in an interview that Sarah Palin is "not qualified" to be president. And believe me, if there's anyone who knows about not being qualified for something, it's Levi Johnston.

monologue: Lady Gaga went to a yoga class in London this week wearing platform boots, sunglasses, and a dress. You'd think that would be pretty impractical, but she totally nailed the position "Downward-Facing Weirdo."

monologue: The New York City Marathon is very prestigious. In front of the Plaza Hotel, runners will have to hurdle over furniture thrown out by Charlie Sheen.

monologue: It’s not easy doing a late night show on a channel without a lot of money, that viewers have trouble finding. That’s why I left NBC.

monologue: Obama’s in India for two days and Republicans are already accusing him of being a Hindu.

monologue: Nancy Pelosi says she will seek to become the House minority leader. Who better to be the minority leader than the person who led their party to become the minority.

monologue: Keith Olbermann was suspended from MSNBC for giving money to Democratic candidates. If only he had given his money to prostitutes, like Eliot Spitzer, he would have a primetime show on CNN.

monologue: Isn’t fall in New York City great? The colors are brown, gold, and orange. And that’s just John Boehner’s face.

monologue: In an interview with USA Today, George W. Bush said that he was “blindsided” by the financial crisis. Bush said he was also blindsided by the fact that he knew the word “blindsided.”

monologue: Apple just launched its online store in China. Apple said this is an exciting opportunity to sell iPods to the kids who make them.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama was in India yesterday visiting our jobs. Tomorrow he goes to China to visit our money.

monologue: Obama says India is one of our most important trading partners. We give them our jobs and they give us . . . Wait, what do we get?

monologue: The Disney Channel canceled the Jonas Brothers’ TV show. Even worse, they had Goofy deliver the news.

monologue: The Kentucky Derby winner Mine That Bird may actually star in his own biopic. You know who else would be good in that role? Any horse.

monologue: NASA is working on a robot capable of running the International Space Station. It was reported in the Journal of Things That Could Never Possibly Go Wrong.

monologue: Americans are stranded on a cruise ship for two days and they have to haul in 60,000 pounds of food. Meanwhile the Chilean miners were underground for 69 days with nothing but a can of tuna fish and they were fine.

monologue: Nancy Pelosi is throwing a party to celebrate her time as speaker of the House. If you would like to get her a gift, she's registered at Bed, Bath and Don't Blame Me.

monologue: I'm not sure what kind of a party it will be, but I think we can rule out a tea party.

monologue: Former star of “The Bachelor,” Jake Pavelka, is back to flying planes for Delta Airlines. And his former fiancé Vienna is back to making little sausages.

monologue: You can catch me next fall on my new show on VH1, “Coning for Love.”

monologue: A man in Kentucky cut off another man’s beard and forced him to eat it during a fight. In a related story, I’m staying the heck out of Kentucky.

monologue: We have an all-military audience today. A lot of these men and women have seen more action than Charlie Sheen.

monologue: They finally found a place to put the inmates from Guantanamo Bay: a Carnival cruise ship.

monologue: A Carnival cruise ship was stranded and had to be towed back to land. The ship had no electricity, no hot water, and no air conditioning. If they wanted that, they could have stayed in Mexico.

monologue: For two days, the ship drifted with no power, earning the nickname “the Democratic Party.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Passengers on the stranded Carnival cruise ship had no power, no food, and no working bathrooms. It was like spending a week with Randy Quaid.

monologue: The ship was towed back into San Diego and the cruise line gave passengers a refund and tickets for another cruise. That’s like getting food poisoning at a restaurant and then being offered a doggy bag.

monologue: Jimmy Buffett has a cruise and he doesn’t even go on it. That’s like going to see Hootie & the Blowfish and just getting Blowfish.

monologue: I shouldn’t make fun of cruises because I’ll probably end up working on one.

monologue: Travelers can now get flu shots at JFK Airport. That’s good, because whenever I see how things are run at an airport, my first thought is, “These people should be in charge of more stuff.”

monologue: A woman gave birth to a healthy baby girl in the back of a New York City cab this week. You could tell the woman wasn’t going to make it to the hospital. Her contractions started coming every $4.60.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: China is expected to overtake the United States as the world’s biggest economy in the next two years. Americans couldn’t believe it. They were like “That hasn’t happened already?”

monologue: Before the Muppets, our forefathers had to catch and gut possums to entertain their children.

monologue: President Obama said on "60 Minutes" that he wants to bring back the 8 million jobs we’ve lost. Today India said "no."

monologue: Obama’s overseas trip has been such a disaster that people in Kenya now claim that he has an American birth certificate.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The U.S. Postal Service announced today they lost $8.5 billion this year. They said they blame it on people using e-mail. And the fact that terrorists have switched to UPS.

monologue: A lot of pest control companies are offering bedbug-sniffing dogs, but it turns out that they’re not very reliable. Either that or there’s a serious bedbug epidemic in other dogs’ butts.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Animal Control discovered a woman here in New York with 50 cats in her two-bedroom apartment. That’s insane. I mean, how can a crazy cat lady in New York afford a two-bedroom apartment?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: One of Apple’s oldest computers is expected to go for about $200,000 at an auction. It’s probably not the best purchase though, because you know they're just going to come out with a new oldest computer in three months.

monologue: I hope they build a bullet train in California. Not because it would cut down on traffic, but because it makes everyone look 10 years younger.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I’d like to have a model train, so that when I stand next to it, I could feel gigantic.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: We have to take a break to class this place up. So we won’t be back.

monologue: In San Diego, a man refused to be patted down by airport security and some people are calling him a hero. I don’t mind being patted down by airport security, but I don’t like it when the guy says, “Now you do me.”

monologue: Reports suggest that parts of former President Bush’s new book may have been lifted from other books. Especially the parts about Dumbledore and Voldemort.

monologue: Voters in Arizona have approved a measure allowing medical marijuana. Arizona is now the 15th state where you can pretend to have glaucoma.

monologue: A thief broke into a house in Alaska and found $100,000 but only took $20,000. Police are searching for a man with simple dreams.

monologue: The lame duck Congress started today. Not to be confused with before the election — that was a lame excuse for a Congress.

monologue: “Sarah Palin’s Alaska” got huge ratings for its premiere. It was followed by “John McCain’s Mesopotamia.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama wrote a children’s book. If only one person reads it, it will be double the number of people that read the healthcare bill.

monologue: Rep. John Boehner is the new speaker of the House. Turn-ons include tax cuts and spray tans.
