monologue: Congress has voted to extend the Bush tax cuts. Is it me, or is George W. Bush getting more done now than when he was in office?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama met with leaders of 60 American Indian tribes. I don't want to say the country's in bad shape, but he offered to give it back to them.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The president was honored by the Indians with his own Indian name. They now call him, "Dances With Republicans."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Michelle Obama wore a vintage thrift-store dress from the 1950s for the Christmas in Washington concert. She's not the only one going vintage. In fact, her husband just agreed to a tax plan from the early 2000s.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The EPA just announced that the artificial sweetener saccharin is not a cancer threat after all. Or as I’ll be reporting the story 10 years from now, “The EPA just announced that the artificial sweetener saccharin is definitely a cancer threat after all.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Southwest Airlines has announced that it could soon begin making international flights. Which may finally answer that age-old question: What would it be like to take a bus across the Atlantic?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Police in the U.K. rented a bouncy castle to cushion the fall when a man threatened to jump off of a building. That must have been an interesting talk. “Sir, do not jump. But if you do, please take your shoes off, and no rough-housing once you’re in there.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: “Yogi Bear” is opening in theaters. You know what that means: It’s Oscar season.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I think this movie is dangerously misleading because bears don’t walk on their hind legs, and they eat their food on all fours — like David Hasselhoff.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: “Yogi Bear” is just pro-bear propaganda. Bears are not our friends.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Bears look very cuddly on TV, but in real life, they’re very dangerous and unpredictable — like Katie Couric.

name: David Letterman
monologue: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is out on bail and under house arrest at a 600-acre estate. That will teach him.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten New York Giants Excuses

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It’s been raining in Los Angeles for four days. God is upset that Larry King quit.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Senate voted to allow gay soldiers to serve in the military. This is good news for gay soldiers, but bad news for straight soldiers who were going to say they were gay to get out of the Army.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: “Jersey Shore” star Ronnie has been charged with assaulting a man during a taping of an episode. If convicted, Ronnie could face up to three years — in a library.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It has been raining hard here in Los Angeles. We have gotten so much water, illegal immigrants are literally coming in waves.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A survey found that men spend twice as much on their mistresses for Christmas as they do on their wives. On the other hand, men spend half their income on their wives once they find out about their mistresses.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama read his new children’s book to a classroom of second-graders in Virginia. It did not go well. Fifty-nine percent of the kids disapproved, and 83 percent of the children felt the story was headed in the wrong direction.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: After playing the beautiful ballerina in the movie "Black Swan," actress Natalie Portman was asked if she'd consider doing "Dancing With the Stars" and she said no. The reason: She can really dance and she’s actually a star.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama said he walks his dog Bo on the White House lawn, but sometimes he has to scoop up Bo’s poop. They probably should find someone else to do that. If there’s one thing Obama’s not good at, it’s cleaning up a mess that was left for him.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: London’s Heathrow Airport was closed because of snow and ice. In fact, Heathrow canceled so many flights, it changed its name to “LaGuardia.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Levi Johnston reportedly has a new girlfriend in Alaska named Sunny Oglesby. Which raises an interesting question: Is there anyone in Alaska with a normal human name?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Singapore has a new campaign to clean up 70 percent of its public toilets by the year 2013. Or in much grosser news, Singapore has admitted that 30 percent of its public toilets will not be cleaned for three years.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Do you know how many packages were handled by the Post Office this year? This is scientifically accurate: Fifty-three gazillion.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: With that many packages, they’re bound to lose a couple hundred. Keep that in mind, my friends and family.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s important to appreciate postal workers this time of year. That’s why I always greet them with a warm smile and an open robe.

name: David Letterman
monologue: On this date in 1620, the Pilgrims arrived in America. Two years at sea with only bread and water and a bucket for their personal hygiene. Wait a minute — that’s a Carnival cruise.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Surprises In The 2010 Census

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Driving conditions in Los Angeles were so bad last night, I saw Lindsay Lohan slide on to the road.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s been raining heavily in Los Angeles. There were 260 traffic accidents. Most of them were caused by people texting while hydroplaning.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Vice President Joe Biden said there has been no "substantive damage" to the United States by Julian Assange in the whole WikiLeaks scandal. He says it has been embarrassing, but you can't prosecute people for embarrassing the United States. If that were true, Joe Biden would be serving life in prison.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A new poll shows President Obama ahead of Sarah Palin 54 percent to 39 percent in a potential match-up. You know what that means? John McCain could get Barack Obama elected twice.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: On a flight from Cuba to Canada, a man threatened to shoot flight attendants after they stopped serving him drinks. He has been charged with making death threats and if convicted, he could lose his pilot's license.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Police officers just found two chickens in midtown Manhattan. Or as pigeons call them, tourists.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Happy birthday to Chinese President Hu Jintao. President Obama was going to get him a present, but it’s a little weird buying someone a gift with their own money.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Madame Tussauds’ wax museum in Washington, D.C. will open a new gallery next year featuring all 44 presidents. The Obama statue is very lifelike. In fact, Biden spent an hour telling it about his weekend.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that there are only 786 mountain gorillas left in the world, and that number could go down even further after the premier of the new show, “Sarah Palin’s Congo.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s my second wedding anniversary. Two years is a long time to be married in Los Angeles. What’s my secret? I take whatever Larry King does and do the opposite.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s Joseph Stalin’s birthday. It’s great having your anniversary on Stalin’s birthday, because you’re reminded by all the Stalin’s birthday sales.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s the winter solstice, when the earth’s axial tilt is furthest from the sun. I have no idea what that means.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s also the shortest day of the year. Congratulations, midgets.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Donald Trump is flying JetBlue, but they make him put that thing on his head in a pet carrier.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Signs It's Christmas In New York

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It has been raining so much in Los Angeles that talk show hosts are legally required to do jokes about the rain.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It’s been raining so hard that the rain briefly washed the hair out of Justin Bieber’s eyes.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It’s been raining so hard that Charlie Sheen locked a mermaid in his closet.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Welcome to Los Angeles. We’re now a federally protected wetland.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: With all this water, suddenly the name “L.A. Lakers” makes sense.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: 7-Eleven is now selling their own brand of wine. It makes a great holiday gift for the man who has nothing.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The census shows there are more than 308 million people living in America. The amazing part is: More than half of those people are Americans.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: “Sarah Palin’s Alaska” has been such a big hit for TLC, they’re trying to get her to do another season. You know who doesn’t want Palin to have a second season? Elk.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Congratulations to “All My Children” actress Rebecca Budig, who won on “Skating with the Stars.” She beat the two other finalists: somebody else and whoever it was.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Security officials say that al-Qaida once considered spreading poison through salad bars across the U.S. But they abandoned the plan after Sizzler beat them to it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Another actor was injured during production of the new Spider-Man musical after he fell 30 feet into the orchestra pit. At this point, they’re just going to change the name to “Jackass 4.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Christmas is very special in Hollywood. When people wish you happy holidays in Los Angeles, 5 percent of them actually mean it.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A lot of people prefer Christmas shopping online, and I understand because I like to shop wearing nothing but my underpants.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I buy most of my gifts from Amazon. Not the website, the actual rain forest.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Lindsay Lohan is out of rehab. Gentlemen, start your blenders.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Signs Your 2011 Is Off To A Bad Start

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Happy new year. My new year’s resolution this year is the same as last year: Eat more gluten.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: During the first two weeks of January, people often resolve to lose weight, which is great for me because the line at Sizzler is much shorter.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It’s been raining in Los Angeles for the past couple of weeks. I was forced to scrape rain off my windshield this morning.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We have a new governor in California. Former Gov. Jerry Brown replaces Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger. I don’t know if I trust a governor who’s never done steroids.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s been raining so much in Los Angeles that the Chia Pet I threw in the garbage is now blocking my entire driveway.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The economy is still hurting. Every Christmas tree lot that I passed this morning was out of business.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s so cold back east, Christine O’Donnell is using her leftover campaign funds to buy a new house in Florida.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Christine O’Donnell is being investigated for using campaign funds to pay for personal expenses. I think it’s a witch hunt.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama says he read three books while he was on vacation. Or as Sarah Palin put it, “showoff.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A grey-colored snow fell in Russia over the weekend, or as they call it in Russia, “sunshine.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Paula Abdul said she’s never had a drinking problem, and that she’s just goofy. When asked how goofy, she said, “Probably about 0.8.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s the sixth anniversary of our show. It was six years ago today that I stood here with no idea what I was doing. And nothing’s changed.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If today is the sixth anniversary of the show, that means tomorrow is the sixth anniversary of me not giving a crap.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I resolve to make 2011 the best year we’ve ever had. On a scale of 1 to 10, I vow to make this show a four.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Resolutions just set you up for failure. My resolution last year was to learn Spanish, and that only lasted about dos weekos.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Thousands of birds fell dead around midnight on New Year’s Eve. Where was Obama? Vacationing in Hawaii.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten New York Department of Sanitation Excuses

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A photograph of Justin Bieber kissing Selena Gomez came to light. If you don’t know who Selena Gomez is, she’s the sweet little girl from the Disney Channel — whose car is now covered in eggs.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On Twitter, there were death threats directed at Selena Gomez. This is exactly what happened to me when I was 16 and I started dating Kenny Loggins.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Season three of “Jersey Shore” premiers Thursday night on MTV. Didn’t season two just end on Christmas Eve? You’d think it would take a month just to sterilize the hot tub.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The captain of the USS Enterprise aircraft carrier has been relieved of command for appearing in raunchy videos on the ship. They are calling this the most embarrassing video involving Navy personnel since that guy from the Village People.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The top things people give up for the new year are junk food, alcohol, smoking, and gambling. So basically, people are giving up on 7-Eleven.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Over the weekend, thousands of dead birds fell out of the sky in Arkansas. Apparently this is Arkansas' version of the New Year’s Eve ball drop.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the Japanese press, Sony is coming out with a smartphone that has a PlayStation built in to compete with the iPhone. It’s called the "I-just-crashed-my-car-phone."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Hugh Hefner reportedly gave his new fiancée a $90,000 diamond engagement ring. It’s not that impressive. Back when he bought it, it was still a lump of coal.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Nickelodeon just renewed “SpongeBob SquarePants” for a ninth season. You can tell SpongeBob is growing up because he wants to be called “SpongeRobert.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: As Nickelodeon announced the ninth season of “SpongeBob SquarePants,” the NFL announced that this was the last season of “Brett Favre NoPants.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Kate Middleton’s uncle is reportedly getting over a drug problem so that he can be invited to her ceremony, and Prince William’s uncle has to clean up his act too. At a luncheon last week, he used his salad fork on the beef tenderloin.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In 2010, the average American watched more TV than ever before in history, at 34 hours a week. That’s longer than court-appointed rehab for Charlie Sheen.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Nowadays, people have TV in their cars, on their phones, and in exercise equipment. Soon, people will have TVs in their foreheads.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The weather outside is 36 degrees, with a 20 percent chance of falling birds.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Things Overheard During The Republicans' First Day In Charge Of The House

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Republicans took control of the House for the first time in four years. They say they’re going to stick to a strict interpretation of the Constitution. I hope you didn’t like voting, women and non-whites.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They’re also hoping to cut back on government regulation on Wall Street. I think we can all agree that Wall Street does a good job policing itself.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The last speaker, Nancy Pelosi has a frozen face and John Boehner has an orange face. If you put them together, you’ve got the Creamsicle of the House.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: According to a new study, Mexico is now the fattest country in the world. Seventy percent of Mexican adults are said to be overweight or obese. When your national dish is the burrito, 70 percent actually seems low.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama plans to sign a $1.4 billion food safety bill. The most dangerous thing about American food? The portions.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: They now say that our national debt will have to be paid off by our children. So thank God for Kate Gosselin and the Octomom.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The commander of the USS Enterprise was relieved of duty because of his involvement in making raunchy videos while onboard the Navy ship. The good news: Today he was offered a job as a producer on "Jersey Shore."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A professor at Utah State University is now studying people who suffer from what he calls a compulsive obsession with morality and religion. They had these people when I was a kid. They were called parents.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Congress was broadcast live on Facebook for the first time in history. Now you can waste time and not get work done by watching Congress waste time and not get work done.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: New York has fired 90 percent of its official kosher inspectors. It was the first decision from New York’s newest elected official, Gov. Mel Gibson.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The fast food chain Chick-fil-A is reportedly sponsoring two anti-gay marriage conferences. A lot of people are upset about this, especially their competition: Chick-on-chick-fil-A.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that two thirds of the instructional CPR videos on YouTube are incorrect. But if you need help and your buddies are looking for CPR instructions on YouTube, you’re probably going to die.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Two people won the Mega Millions lottery. If you missed the drawing, the winning numbers were . . . not yours.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I hope the lottery winner is someone who needs the money, who’s been living in their car and eating out of the garbage, like Randy Quaid.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Playing the lottery is just gambling. I don’t need money to be happy. I get my happiness from the small things — literally, midgets.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The lottery preys on peoples’ hopes of getting rich without doing anything. People should get their money the old fashioned way: Be born a Kardashian.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Now that the Republicans have taken over the House, they’re going to repeal everything President Obama has done. They even told Michelle Obama that her vegetable garden has to go.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: According to a group that monitors government waste, the Republicans’ reading of the Constitution cost taxpayers a $1 million. Only politicians could spend money reading.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Constitution is one of the most important documents in the history of the world, but it’s also very boring. It’s the kind of thing that makes you wish you never learned to read.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The new Congress adopted a rule that permits members to use electronic devices on the floor of the House. So let the sexting begin.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Two people won the $380 million Mega Millions lottery drawing. It was the biggest single jackpot since Elin Nordegren divorced Tiger Woods.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The first order of business for the 112th Congress: blaming everything on the 111th Congress.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Borders bookstores are struggling to stay in business. This could be the first time in our country that borders are actually closed.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: January is the month that people are most likely to be fired — especially if you’re an elf.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Iran has arrested an American woman, accusing her of spying with a device in her teeth. As opposed to Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, who lies through his teeth.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: An escaped prisoner in Alaska was on the run for six hours before he was finally caught near Sarah Palin’s hometown of Wasilla. When I think of safe places to run, I think “the woods near Sarah Palin's house.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There was a three-hour hostage standoff that ended peacefully at a mall food court in Arizona. It would have ended a lot sooner, but it took the cops two hours to find the gunman on the mall map.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A 39-year-old cat in Britain was just named the oldest cat ever. The cat’s really getting up there. Instead of playing with a ball of yarn, it uses it to knit sweaters.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Christina Aguilera has reportedly been living in the same house with her boyfriend, her son, and her soon-to-be ex-husband. She even sings about it in her new hit song, “Awkward.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I love nature documentaries, because you see the animals in their natural habitat. Speaking of which, the third season of “Jersey Shore” begins this week.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I’m not too hip to “Jersey Shore.” I couldn’t tell the difference between a JWoww and a ShamWow.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Some Italian-American groups have complained that “Jersey Shore” perpetuates negative stereotypes of Italian-Americans — unlike “The Sopranos” or “Real Housewives of New Jersey.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: Happy birthday to Elvis Presley. He would have been 76 years old. His fans are already converging on Graceland for a candle-light buffet.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Questions To Ask Yourself Before Marrying A 110-Year-Old Man

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Hugh Hefner’s new 24-year-old wife claims that she can’t see the 60-year age difference. She apparently can’t tell the difference between a grape and a raisin either.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: He’s 84 and she’s 24. In six years, she’ll be 30, and he’ll be — dead.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Hefner’s wife says they like doing things together, like taking long walks — to the bathroom.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Obama administration announced that the economy added 103,000 new jobs in December — mostly to homeless radio announcers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: California Congresswoman Lynn Woolsey referred to the war in Afghanistan as a “national embarrassment.” Then she watched the premiere of “Jersey Shore” and was like, “Never mind.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that humans started wearing clothes about 170,000 years ago. In fact, the first sentence ever spoken was, “Me look fat in this?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A teenager in the northwest survived 10 hours on a mountain using tips from the Discovery Channel show “Man vs. Wild.” And also, because it was only 10 hours.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: TLC is coming out with a new show called “Extreme Couponing.” But it takes so long that all the other shows behind it are asking to open up another channel.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It’s a great day because Khloe Kardashian dyed her hair red. The reaction has been mostly positive, except for the people that mistake her for Chuck Norris.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I’m not worried about Khloe Kardashian getting mad at me, but I’m a little worried about Chuck Norris.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A 105-year-old woman in New Zealand has become the world’s oldest driver. She uses the car mostly to annoy the heck out of people.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The main attraction at the Consumer Electronics Show was the 3-D television. It’s the first time the cast of “Jersey Shore” showed any depth.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Lawmakers are getting tough on bullying. New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie signed some of the toughest anti-bullying laws in the nation. Then someone gave Christie a wedgie and said, “Ha ha. You’ve got a girl’s last name.”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Mickey Rourke says he’s removing his two front teeth for an upcoming movie role. The movie is called “The Mickey Rourke Story.”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A company created a bathroom scale that allows you to tweet your weight to your friends. The company immediately went out of business.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A new study shows that a woman's tears can chemically lower the level of testosterone in a man. When that happens, the man will also start to cry and then eventually be elected speaker of the House.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Illinois officials report that drug sniffing dogs are wrong as much as 70 percent of the time — probably because they're sniffing drugs all day.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Starting in march, Starbucks will be introducing a new logo to celebrate their 40th anniversary. They're also marking the milestone by charging the same price that they charged for a cup of coffee back in 1971: $3.75.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Cosmetic surgeons says that two years of recession has devastated their industry, and that fewer people can afford to have plastic surgery done. In Beverly Hills, a lot of people say they are actually starting to get feeling back in their faces again.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The movie “True Grit” is doing very well at the box office, but I don’t know why. It doesn’t have any aliens, explosions, or karate, and it’s not even in 3-D.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Hollywood is getting lazy trying to fool us with quality.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The star of “True Grit” is Jeff Bridges. His movies are too good, too often. He needs to make a crappy movie about a cat that plays basketball or something.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Mayor Bloomberg has really taken a beating over the snow, and he’s begging folks from out of town to take some snow with them when they leave New York City.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Reasons To Buy The New Snooki Book

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Over the weekend, more birds came crashing to the ground in Pennsylvania. I guess the Eagles didn’t bring their A-game.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A writer is suing MTV for stealing his idea for “Jersey Shore.” In fact, he just hired Jersey’s best lawyer, “The Representation.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Snooki was signing copies of her novel at Borders in New York. When she got to the book store, she said, “These places are real.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We’re 10 days into the new year. Today is the day that your Christmas lights have officially been up too long.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Oprah’s new television channel, OWN, is up. Oprah said her mission for her new channel is to create a network that has mindful, not mindless, TV. She’s done it with shows like “Miracle Detectives” and “Anna & Kristina’s Grocery Bag.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I tried to find the new Oprah network, but my universal remote tried to kill itself.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The date 1/11/11 only happens once every hundred years. When Larry King heard, he said, “This again?”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: “American Idol” producers say that when the show returns with two new celebrity judges, there will be less put-downs and more support for the contestants. In other words, this will be the last season.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: MGM Studios announced that despite their financial trouble, they will be releasing a new James Bond film this year. In light of the tough economic times, it will be titled: “License to Kill — and Sell Real Estate on the Side.”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Swedish firm has designed an efficient city featuring buildings on wheels that can be moved in or out of town as desired. This ingenious city of the future is known as a trailer park.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Due to the recession there are now 15,000 less lawyers. Nobody ever talks about the good things that happen because of the recession.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: At the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, LG unveiled a line of appliances that can send text messages. Would you want appliances that can text you? You’re in a business meeting like, “Excuse me, I have to take this. It’s from my can opener.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In a few months, they will have upgrades for the iPhone 4G. This will give your phone the ability to send and receive telephone calls.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Former U.S. House Majority Leader Tom DeLay was sentenced to three years in prison. The judge sentenced him to two years for money laundering and tacked on an extra year for his performance on "Dancing With the Stars."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Verizon announced that they will start selling their version of the iPhone. This version will actually make calls.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Celebrities used to get in trouble for throwing their cell phones at people, but nowadays the phones are so light that if someone threw a phone, you’d be like, “That’s cute.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I used to think phones would be built into everyday objects, like a shoe-phone or a watch-phone, but it’s gone the opposite way. Now everything is part of the phone, and if you lose it, you lose everything. You may as well change your name to Randy Quaid.

name: David Letterman
monologue: A thousand doves dropped dead out of the sky in Venice. That leaves only about 50 million more.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Top Ten Ways New York City Is Preparing For The Blizzard

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: New York City is bracing for another blizzard. In fact, I saw people shopping for groceries, buying up batteries, and preparing to stay inside — and that was just the sanitation workers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Feb. 10, the iPhone will be available to Verizon customers. Or, to put it another way, on Feb. 10, AT&T; customers will become Verizon customers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that ESP could actually be real. I read about it in tomorrow’s paper.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On the season finale of “Hoarders,” they showed a man who lets over 2,000 rats run around his house. Clearly, that guy has a problem — he doesn’t need half of those rats.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: New York City’s Mayor Bloomberg introduced a 15-point plan to get rid of all the snow. Fifteen points seems like a lot to me. I think two would be better: a snow-blower and maybe some salt.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: NASA released photos of a mysterious green blob floating out in space. Either that or someone sneezed on the telescope.

name: Jimmy Kimmel

monologue: Oprah Winfrey's longtime boyfriend Stedman Graham has written a book about being proud of who you are. It's not helping that the cover of the book says, "Written by Oprah Winfrey's boyfriend."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Welcome, lotto losers. Remember, you're not just losers. You're mega-losers! If it makes you feel any better, the odds of winning were 176 million to 1 — about the same odds the Supreme Court will pass Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There were three winning lotto tickets. I guess we're not sure who the three winners are yet. But when they do come forward, two things happen immediately. You get a call from the IRS asking for half. Then you get a call from your friends and relatives asking for the other half.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: That was so much money that the JetBlue pilot could afford to go nuts on his own private plane.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Betty White has a new show on NBC called "Off Their Rockers" where senior citizens prank young people. It's kind of like what we're doing to them with Social Security.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday was April Fools' Day. Mitt Romney's staffers played a prank on him by staging a fake campaign event in an empty room — or as Newt Gingrich put it, "My staff has been playing that prank on me for six months."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I read that the odds of winning the Mega Millions jackpot were only 1 in 176 million — or as most people put it, "Well, yeah. That's why I bought two."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Saturday the Empire State Building went dark for an hour to draw attention to climate change. Of course, 10 endangered eagles then crashed into the building.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Mega Millions jackpot added up to a record $656 million. Three people correctly picked all six numbers. Now the plan is to throw them into a pit of some kind and have them fight to the death.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The winning tickets were sold in Illinois, Kansas, and Maryland. All we know is their first names are Khloe, Kourtney, and Kim.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I always think it's funny that people wait in line for hours and hours when it's $640 million, but if it's a hundred million, it's not really worth it. None of the people in that line were winners in any sense of the word. They stood in line for nothing, wasting a whole day.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight's the end of March Madness. It will be an entire year before we hear the word "Gonzaga" again.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Mitt Romney is trying to get female voters and Rick Santorum said, "What? Women can vote? Are you kidding me? "

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Goldman Sachs sold their shares in the New York paper "Village Voice" because its back page has ads for prostitution. Goldman Sachs said the only people that should pay to get screwed are their clients.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Tony Awards announced Neil Patrick Harris will host for a third time. So once again they've snubbed Mike Ditka.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new study claims that four out of 10 Americans are now obese. The study was conducted by anyone working at a water park.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Well, congratulations to Kentucky. They won the NCAA championship 67-59 over Kansas, very nice. Did you see the news after the game? People in Kentucky flipping over cars, they were burning couches. That was all on the same front lawn.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Oh, here's your tax dollars at work. This is what makes people furious. The head of the GSA, a woman named Martha Johnson, has resigned after they found out she spent over $830,000 on a four-day government conference in Las Vegas. And the president is furious. Not President Obama, the president of China. It's his money. It's his money she spent.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Up in Sacramento this week a man jumped on the hood of a police car that was moving. Started screaming his name. He was wearing a puffy winter jacket, a sombrero, one boxing glove. Police say the guy was in a total state of delirium. They didn't arrest him. Turns out just a JetBlue pilot on break. He was just on break.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day here at the CBS network. Today the network announced that David Letterman and I extended our contracts until 2014. Yes! Which is good news here, of course, two more years of Dave. Bad news, two more years of me.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: What people are really talking about, of course, is the $650 million Mega Millions lottery. If you missed the drawing on Friday, the winning numbers were not yours.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If I won the Mega Millions, I'd buy an island. Not for me. I'd send all the Kardashians on it. I'd send all the Kardashians there and make them hunt each other.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Osama bin Laden was so wealthy that one of his houses had an elevator for his camels.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Recently at the White House, President Obama admitted he's a Trekkie. Although Trekkies say he doesn't qualify because he has a wife and a job.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today Allegiant Airlines will start charging $35 extra if you have carry-on bags. Meanwhile, JetBlue is charging $35 extra if you want a pilot who isn't insane.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I want the crazy pilot, too. Makes a long flight more interesting.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Dartmouth College, a fine institution, has named their medical school after Dr. Seuss. Because nothing is better than hearing your doctor say, "You don't have cancer on your nose, you don't have cancer on our toes."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congratulations to Mitt Romney, the big winner in yesterday's primary. He won in Wisconsin. Rick Santorum finished second. Newt Gingrich came in fourth behind Ron Paul. But Wisconsin was not a total loss for Newt. He did make off with a 45-pound wheel of cheese.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Best Buy announced they're going to close stores in the United States while opening 50 new stores in China during the same time. Well, they say opening the stores in China will save shipping costs because all the stuff is made there anyway.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Supreme Court has ruled that anybody can be strip-searched for any kind of arrest. That's something to think about the next time you bring 12 items into a 10-item-or-less lane.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sarah Palin co-hosted the "Today" show. She did a pretty good job, and they want to bring her back for a new version of "Where in the World is Matt Lauer?" What they're going to do is release Matt into Central Park, and then Sarah will track him down "Hunger Games" style.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night Mitt Romney went three for three by winning the primaries in Maryland, Wisconsin, and Washington, D.C. Not to be outdone, Rick Santorum went three for three by offending women, atheists, and Latinos.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A Delta Airlines flight attendant was removed from a plane this morning because he was acting unstable. He was saying crazy stuff you never hear on a Delta flight, like "Prepare for an on-time arrival.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Delta flight attendant was removed for acting unstable, but on the bright side he was immediately hired as a pilot for JetBlue.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The New York Mets are now offering peanut-free seating for fans with severe allergies. Mets officials said they want to make sure that gagging and choking only occur on the field.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There is a strange new law making its way through the Arizona Legislature that would make it illegal to post negative comments on the Internet. The penalty for annoying or offending someone is up to six months in jail. That is good. They're always saying the prisons aren't full enough.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Ryan Seacrest was on the "Today" show. He is joining the NBC family. This on top of six or seven other jobs. America's job growth is lacking and the cause is Ryan Seacrest. ABC, NBC, radio, cable — hundreds of jobs and he is not satisfied.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Mitt Romney is catching heat for a possible violation of election rules. He was at a sub shop handing out free sandwiches. Special Romney sandwiches — they come on really, really white bread.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Romney gave the sandwiches to people and apparently this is against the law. The Democratic Party in Wisconsin fired a formal complaint. Not sure with who — Quiznos, maybe.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Tomorrow night is the Jewish holiday of Passover. Or as we call it here in Los Angeles, "Cinco de Matzo."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Mega Millions controversy is getting stranger by the day. The Maryland woman who claims she is the winner held a press conference where she not only failed to present the winning ticket but quickly asked the press to leave. In other words, she is full of mega B.S.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Even though this woman claims she won, surveillance footage shows the ticket was purchased by a man. Either she is lying or we're all trapped inside a new Tyler Perry movie.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was opening day for baseball today. Remember baseball? It used to be our national pastime before Facebook.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I'm glad baseball is back. I was getting sick of paying only $2 for a beer.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: China has overtaken the United States as the world's biggest food and grocery market. That means they buy and consume more food than we do. Which — when you think about it — of course they do. A half hour after they eat, they're hungry again. It's Chinese food.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Last year, China spent $964 billion in groceries, whereas we only spent $908 billion. China has a billion people. We have 300 million. Why weren't they always the biggest market for groceries? Are they allowed to eat now?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The earth's population is now well past 7 billion people. And still, the Republicans can't find one candidate they really like.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Rick Santorum's campaign is now formally calling on Newt Gingrich to drop out of the race. But you know Newt. He has vowed to stay in. And believe me, when Newt Gingrich takes a vow, he keeps it — unless, of course, you know, marriage.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama signed a bill preventing members of Congress from profiting from insider trading. Didn't you think that was already illegal?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: So they were profiting from insider information. Why didn't they use inside information to pay off the $15 trillion debt?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new picture was just released of President Obama giving the Star Trek Vulcan salute at the White House. Even Spock was like, "Whoa — look at that guy’s ears!”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday Ryan Seacrest finally made his highly publicized "major announcement" on the "Today" show — revealing that he will take part in NBC’s coverage of the London Olympics. The other thing he revealed? That he doesn't know what a major announcement is.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The sister of Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg is making a reality show about young people in the tech world — while the sister of the MySpace founder is making a reality show about a guy who has to move in with his sister.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Kim Kardashian said that she wants to be a more private person. Then she was like, "And you can see me try in my new reality series ‘Kim Kardashian: Private Person.’”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The woman who says she bought the winning Mega Millions ticket now says she's hidden it inside the McDonald's where she works. That's the dumbest plan I've ever heard. Doesn't she already know there's a hamburglar already inside the building?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Google announced they are making glasses that have embedded technology that projects data on the lenses in front of your eyes. Some people formed a group online to stop the new technology. An online group to stop new technology — does anybody see the irony here?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The protesters say Google is underestimating the dangers of merging man with machine. Well, they're a little late to stop that half-man, half-cyborg thing. They're already here. One of them just captured the Republican nomination.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Hundreds of barefoot Filipinos marched on the roads through the Philippines carrying heavy wooden crosses and whipping their backs until they bled to prepare for Easter. Call me old-fashioned but I just like coloring the eggs.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Tim Tebow is scheduled to deliver an Easter sermon at a church in Texas. And, although it's not official, there's now rumors that the church has been talking to Peyton Manning.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: New York's famous Carnegie Deli honored Tim Tebow's move to the Jets by naming a sandwich after him. The Tim Tebow sandwich. Pretty amazing. Two pieces of fish, five pieces of bread, feeds 5,000 people.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Best Buy announced they will close 50 stores in the United States while opening 50 new stores in China at the same time. Remember the old days when we just sent the jobs overseas? Now we're sending the whole store.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Mitt Romney has spent $53 million on ads, and Rick Santorum has spent $9 million. Meanwhile, Newt Gingrich drew a poster with his name on it and showed up in the background of the "Today" show.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A woman recently gave birth to a healthy baby boy while she was onboard a Delta flight — marking the first time someone flying Delta actually arrived early.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: According to a recent study, most people think that they are thinner than they really are. Which explains why the other day I saw Newt Gingrich buying a Speedo at Forever 21.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new report found that high schools across the country are not doing enough to teach kids about safe sex. But on the bright side, it looks like we’re getting a fifth season of "Teen Mom."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Next week is the 100th anniversary of the sinking of the Titanic. It is a terrible tragedy. And what better way to mark this somber anniversary than with a big Hollywood movie in 3-D.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's pretty amazing that computer programs can transform older movies into 3-D. They take something flat and two-dimensional, and then make it seem real. They should try that with Mitt Romney.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The whole idea of re-releasing old movies does bother me a little bit. If they're going to re-release an old movie, I should be able to get in with my old ticket.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight's presentation of "The Late Late Show" is brought to you in 3-D. Now you can experience shame and total disappointment in three dimensions.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Newt Gingrich says he still has a chance. He say people walk up to him all the time and beg him to stay in the presidential race. It's a group of people known as Democrats.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's being reported that 74-year-old Morgan Freeman is planning to marry his 27-year-old step-granddaughter. The whole story sounds a little creepy unless you hear it narrated by Morgan Freeman.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Kansas, the Mega Millions winner who took home $157 million has chosen to remain anonymous. A spokesman for the winner said his client just wants to blend in with all of the other people in Kansas who have $157 million.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The media are reporting that American universities are being infiltrated by foreign spies. They say everyone should be on the lookout for any student who is paying attention and taking notes.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today was the annual White House Easter Egg Roll, or as Republicans call it, "President Obama's socialist egg redistribution."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Mitt Romney had an Easter egg hunt as well. He does it a little differently. He hides money offshore, then the kids hunt for the nest egg.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A number of passengers recently discovered maggots in a bag of snack mix they were given aboard a flight from Los Angeles to Australia. How unbelievable is that? An airline that still serves snacks?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Keith Olbermann is suing his former employer, Current TV, for $70 million. That comes out to $10 million per viewer.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Maryland state officials say they're being invaded by a dangerous fish called a snakehead. The problem with these fish is they eat everything in their path. A few snakeheads will go through a lake's ecosystem faster than Johnny Depp goes through a bottle of mascara.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I used to love going fishing. I think it was really about the clothes. Nothing says real man like a vest with 38 pockets and a mesh hat with hooks in it.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There's something very satisfying about waking up early, catching fish, gutting it, and cooking it up yourself. But there's something even more satisfying about staying in bed all day and then going to a restaurant and having fish.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Bad news for the governor of New Jersey, Chris Christie. While celebrating Easter they rushed him to the hospital with an impacted peep.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Over the weekend, Mitt Romney was actually spotted bodyboarding in California. Yeah, Romney would have gone surfing, but you know — he hates standing for something.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, it turned out there weren’t enough waves that day, so Romney asked Newt Gingrich to do a cannonball.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Joe Biden launched a new Twitter account to give supporters updates from the campaign trail. Like his most recent update: "They still won't let me go on the campaign trail.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Thirty thousand kids and their parents participated in the annual White House Easter Egg Roll, which has been going on for years. At this point there has to be thousands of undiscovered Easter eggs on the lawn of the White House. Future civilizations will think we were ruled by chickens.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Newt Gingrich admitted to The Washington Post that he knows he probably won't be the Republican nominee for president, but he's not bowing out of the race because he's $5 million in debt. So he needs to keep raising money. How do you continue to raise money when you've already admitted you probably won't win?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A woman accused Lindsay Lohan of pinching her at a hotel in L.A. The only problem with the story is that Lindsay and the people at the hotel say she wasn't there. If only there was a group of people who chronicled her every move with cameras and video equipment — then we would know if the charges were legit.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Bubba Watson won the masters. Tiger Woods finished in 40th place. A lot of people picked Tiger to finish first, but it was his worst finish there since his start as an amateur. One more performance like that and they might demote him to miniature golf.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today's the opening day for the Dodgers. There was an awkward moment during new owner Magic Johnson's pep talk when he told the players to get out there and beat the Celtics.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Maryland three teachers came forward to claim the Mega Millions lottery prize. They all said they would remain at their jobs. They want to keep teaching kids that if you work hard and study, it won't mean crap unless you win the lottery.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: American universities are being infiltrated by foreign spies. In other words, Iran may have the technology to build their own beer bong.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night Melissa Gilbert suffered a concussion on "Dancing With the Stars." It's the first time anyone connected with that show has actually seen stars.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Miami Marlins' manager Ozzie Guillen has been suspended for five games because of his comments praising Fidel Castro. Now he's apologizing after talking it over with his good friend Hugo Chavez.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today was opening day at Dodger Stadium. Actually it was a little different this year. Instead of throwing out the first pitch, they threw out the last owner.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama's popularity is starting to dwindle among well-known liberals like Matt Damon and Gene Simmons. In fact, you know the number one liberal to turn against President Obama? Mitt Romney.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today is National Be Kind to Lawyers Day. This is a day celebrated by no one.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is a tough day for Rick Santorum, who suspended his presidential campaign. I don't think it's a coincidence that he dropped out the day hot dog pizza was announced. Seeing this abomination, Rick realized that humanity has veered just too far off the path of moral righteousness.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Hot dog pizza raises two important questions. Who came up with this monstrosity? And how quickly can it be delivered to my house?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Hot dogs and pizza don't go together. It's like Rush Limbaugh and skinny jeans — it just shouldn't happen.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Hot dogs and pizza — it's like monogamy in a Kardashian. It's like a dog show and Michael Vick. It's like dancing and stars.

name: David Letterman
monologue: A hundred years ago the Titanic sank. It was supposed to be unsinkable. If they were going to make that same cruise again today, thanks to global warming they would not have to worry about icebergs.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, Rick Santorum officially dropped out of the Republican race. Gettysburg was a great choice because he should've dropped out four score and seven years ago.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The New York Mets have started the season with four straight wins. I don't want to say it's surprising, but today the Mets tested themselves for steroids.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s apparently a 102-year-old man in New York who still works as a valet parking attendant. It’s not easy for him. Every time he parks a car, he has to pull over three times for a bathroom break.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: You can tell he’s old. When you tip him a five, he’s like, "Hey, it's my old roommate, Abe Lincoln.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We had a new "Dancing With the Stars" tonight, an elimination night and Sherri Shepherd was evicted. I feel bad for her because not only is she off "Dancing With the Stars," but she has to go back to "The View."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I hate to see people get kicked off. Just for once I'd like to see someone get kicked onto a reality show.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Facebook is buying the photo-sharing service Instagram for a billion dollars. Instagram is an app that makes your photographs look like vintage Polaroids. Meanwhile, poor Tom from MySpace just announced he's selling his mom's Polaroid camera on eBay for $5.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A billion dollars — I don't know. Unless they have some faded, washed-out photos of Mark Zuckerberg killing a hooker, it doesn't make sense.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: George W. Bush said he wishes people would stop referring to his tax policy as the Bush tax cuts. He also wishes people would stop referring to his presidency as the eight-year oopsy.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Alabama, a meth lab was found operating inside a Walmart bathroom. On the bright side, Walmart is finally selling products that are made in America.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Burger King has announced they are testing a new bacon sundae. They also announced that they're changing their slogan to "Have it your way to die, humans, die!"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The average wedding now costs $27,000. Well, no wonder Newt Gingrich is broke. He's constantly shelling out all that money.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Newt Gingrich's campaign paid $500 to get his name on the Utah primary ballot, and the check bounced. You know, if Newt is spending money he doesn't have, maybe he really is qualified to be president.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The price of gasoline has now doubled under President Obama's administration. He and Jimmy Carter are the only presidents ever to have had that happen. But in fairness, at least under President Obama we don't have to listen to disco.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It looks like Kanye West and Kim Kardashian are dating, and apparently they're getting serious. Friends say Kanye is the man Kim wants to spend the rest of her month with.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Snooki said today she's put in blond hair extensions. I don't think Snooki should go blond. People will think she is dumb.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Bird-like dinosaurs were found with eggs. It is a big deal because fossils of dinosaurs and their eggs have never been found in the same place. I think it is nice that scientists found the eggs on Easter week.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If I were one of the scientists, I would have played a trick on the others and secretly switched the dinosaur eggs with Cadbury's Creme Eggs.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Rick Santorum has dropped out of the race. He wanted to ban gambling and outlaw pornography. And this is a guy who claims Romney is out of touch with America.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It turns out that Newt Gingrich’s campaign wrote a $500 check to participate in the Utah primary, but it bounced. Even M.C. Hammer was like, "Manage your money, bro.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Louisiana Governor Bobby Jindal announced that he is supporting Mitt Romney for president. Jindal said he couldn’t think of a better way to show his support than waiting until Romney was the only guy left.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After dropping out of the GOP race, Rick Santorum emailed his supporters to ask for help paying off his campaign debt. So if you believe in his message of responsible spending and no handouts, just give him a handout to cover all his irresponsible spending.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Harvard Law School will soon offer a class called "Understanding Obama" — while Barnum & Bailey Clown College will offer a class called "Understanding Biden.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Another strange story from Arizona. A bill signed by the governor would declare a woman to be pregnant two weeks before conception. So congratulations, ladies, you are all Arizona pregnant.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I wonder if they realize in Arizona that they will not be able to report any female illegal immigrants because they are all pregnant with babies who will be citizens.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Florida congressman Allen West made an interesting statement yesterday. He believes there are about 78 to 81 members of the Democratic Party who are members of the Communist Party. Really? I think it's time for someone to lay off the Tom Clancy novels.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: West is a guy that some think should be Mitt Romney's running mate. I would like that. We haven't had a truly crazy vice president . . . well, until now.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In an interview, once again President Obama called Kanye West a jackass. In other words, President Obama's finally found an issue that can bring this country together.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I believe that hardcore social conservatives, liberals, and everyone else is together on this one. I think even Kanye agrees.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today Newt Gingrich is blaming the failure of his presidential campaign on Fox News. Newt's also blaming the failure of his diet on Cinnabon.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: JK Rowling has a novel now aimed at adults. It's called "Harry Potter and the 30-Year Adjustable Rate Mortgage."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Obama administration is trying to distance itself from remarks made by long-time Democratic adviser Hilary Rosen. She said that Mitt Romney's wife, Ann, a stay-at-home mother of five who has cancer, has never worked a day in her life. The ironic part — because of that idiotic statement, she may never work another day in her life.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Let me tell you something — if you're the mother of five boys, you never had a day off in your life, OK?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: And now, even vice president Joe Biden is furious. He said, "Making stupid comments that hurt the president, that's my job. She has no right."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Rick Santorum has suspended his presidential campaign. He dropped out after spending a weekend in prayer, and then realizing he didn't have one, he dropped out.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for David Letterman, who is 65 years old today. I called him and asked him what he wanted for his birthday. First of all he's like, who's this? Then he said the same thing he wants every year, for me not to call him.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for our friends to the north, Canada. I'm a big fan of Canada, our neighbor to the north populated by the beautiful, docile, bovine creatures called Canadians.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today the Royal Canadian Mint announced they're getting rid of coins and paper money. They're developing something called the mint chip — which I thought, what, ice cream for money?

name: David Letterman
monologue: There is a new medical study that says men make better decisions about life when they're drinking beer. I think I made my best choices in life after about six Coronas.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday Newt Gingrich gave a campaign speech at a senior center, scheduled between a Jazzercise class and a Bingo game. That’s when you know you’re in trouble – when your campaign speech is the least exciting thing happening at a senior center.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Newt Gingrich gave a speech at a senior center. Or as audience members put it, "Unplug me.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Gingrich spoke to seniors, right before the Bingo game — which was awkward, because one of the Bingo players turned out to be Ron Paul.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Happy birthday to David Letterman, who turned 65 years old today. I don't want to say he's getting old, but today, he read the Top Ten reasons to get off his lawn.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The deadline to file your tax returns is coming up. You only have five days left to frantically dig through your car for Burger King receipts that you can claim were business dinners later on.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There's certainly nothing fun about paying taxes. But you have to remember that all the money goes to a good cause, like paying the salaries of the meter maids who give parking tickets, keep welfare checks flowing to the Octomom — important things like that.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: To reduce the chance of being audited, I always send my return tucked into a freshly baked loaf of banana bread.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Arnold Schwarzenegger did something interesting yesterday. On his Facebook page, he asked fans to give him ideas for things to write about in his autobiography. Apparently, he's unfamiliar with the auto part.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Today is Friday the 13th. You know what that means? Turn your clocks back.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This is the 100th anniversary of the Titanic disaster. On its maiden voyage, it collided with an iceberg and sank into the ocean. But it still made it further than that North Korean rocket.

name: Jay Leno

monologue: During his commencement speech at Liberty University, Mitt Romney revealed that his campaign staff loves Chick-fil-A. The other thing he revealed? — that he doesn’t know what to say in a commencement speech.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: We have Chef Gordon Ramsay on the show tonight. I thought he burned something when I saw smoke backstage — but then I remembered we also have Willie Nelson on the show tonight.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week investors will be able to buy shares of Facebook stock for the first time ever. It’s great — now you can lose all your money in the same place you lost all your time.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Saturday President Obama and Joe Biden spent more than four hours playing golf together. Joe Biden’s handicap is 20, while Obama’s handicap . . . is Joe Biden.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Shakespeare is inaccurate. When I read "Hamlet," I was disappointed it wasn't about a little ham.

monologue: Glamis Castle is on a 14,000-acre estate. It has over 50 rooms, seven of which are now Starbucks.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A secret room is apparently in Glamis Castle. It has been walled off. I have a secret room in my house too. It is covered in Ryan Gosling posters.

monologue: The queen mum moved to Glamis Castle when she was 4. Later, during the Second World War, she refused to leave when London was being bombed. At night, my guess is she would put on a bat suit and fight crime.

monologue: President Obama went on "The View." He went on the "The View" because they're the only group of women the president trusts his Secret Service agents to be around.

monologue: As of Friday you'll all be able to buy shares of Facebook. This is perfect for anyone who's ever logged on, looked at pictures of their friend eating a sandwich, and thought, "Now there's a sound investment."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The head of the banking giant JPMorgan has apologized for losing over $2 billion in a bad trade. This morning he said, "Hey, it could have been worse. We could have signed Albert Pujols."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Researchers are developing a stay-sober pill that will prevent you from getting drunk off of alcohol. It's perfect for the drinker who wants all the calories of alcohol but none of the fun.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The average college graduate now leaves school $27,000 in debt. But the good news is that now it means they are more than qualified to work as financial advisers at JPMorgan.

monologue: The New Jersey tanning mom now says she wants to pose nude for Playboy magazine. Well, Playboy says they're looking for women who are hot, not burnt orange.

monologue: The Octomom has finished her porn movie. The producers saved a lot of time on the credits because nobody wanted any.

name: Jay Leno

monologue: Officials in London plan to use high-pitched and painful sounds to disperse large crowds at the Olympics this summer. Or as the cast of "The View" put it, "Looks like we're going to the Olympics!"
