monologue: If it turns out that the Mayans are right and the world is going to end, you know what this means? Lindsay Lohan is a genius. She’s been partying her brains out. She owes taxes. She’s crashing cars. She’s a genius!

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday a judge in Los Angeles revoked Lindsay Lohan's probation and Lindsay could get 5 to 10 behind bars. Not years, that’s minutes. This is L.A. jail time.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Army has started kicking out overweight soldiers, and they're refusing to admit recruits that are obese. That shows you how times have changed. Back in the '60s, you had to go to Canada to stay out of the Army. Now, you just have to go to McDonald's.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Barbara Walters chose General David Petraeus as the most fascinating person of 2012. What a coincidence. So did Paula Broadwell.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Golden Globe nominations were announced this morning. Usually I go into a diatribe about how the Golden Globe people are a scandal-ridden group of suck-ups whose only joy in life is getting within 10 feet of movie stars. In other words, "my people."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Golden Globes are given out by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association. The entertainment journalists are from tiny foreign newspapers like the Luxembourg Pennysaver, the Oslo Tattler, and the Rotterdam Bugler.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The favorite in the comedy/musical category is "Les Misérables." Because what's funnier or catchier than prison breaks, poverty, and the guillotine?

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's award season. They start off with the Nobel Prize awards. Then they go to the Golden Globes.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The satellite that North Korea launched on Tuesday is apparently unstable, and could collide with several American satellites. Or as North Korea calls that, “The point.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: HBO is planning a new movie similar to “Game Change,” but based on the 2012 election. The network said they’re not sure who will play Mitt Romney — then Mitt Romney said, “Hey, I’m not doing anything.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week, police in Ohio had to break up a fight between two neighbors with the last names Hall and Oates. But don’t worry. It was quickly broken up by officers Simon and Garfunkel.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, the Senate floor was reserved for farewell speeches from retiring senators. Each senator received a fitting gift: a gold watch that stopped working years ago.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There are only 11 days before Christmas Eve. I give a lot of gifts on Christmas and I get a lot of gifts on Christmas. But I don't open them right away. I like to save my gifts and I open them during shark week. It's just more exciting.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The nominations for the Golden Globes were announced this morning. If you got a screaming phone call at 4 a.m., you were either nominated for a Golden Globe or you're Charlie Sheen's girlfriend.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Golden Globes are very important because whoever wins the Golden Globe may or may not win the Oscar.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Steven Spielberg's movie "Lincoln" had the most nominations of any film this year. Seven. "Lincoln" was nominated for best picture, best director, best beard without a mustache, and furriest top hat.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Christmas is just around the corner. It's just under two weeks away, and today Santa released 10 years of tax returns.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Golden Globe nominations were announced yesterday morning, and "Lincoln" got seven nominations. Finally, a Republican who might win something.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: On Wednesday night, Barbara Walters asked Governor Chris Christie if he was too fat to be president. A lot of people are criticizing Barbara for asking that question. But in fairness, Barbara asked that exact same question when she interviewed William Howard Taft.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke said a failure to reach a deal for the fiscal cliff will hurt the recovery. The good news is most Americans will not be affected by this because they had no idea there WAS a recovery.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The U.S. Census Bureau says that by the year 2043, white people will be in the minority in the United States. By that time, the country will be 15 percent black, 31 percent Hispanic, and 1 percent Republican.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The new movie "The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey" came out today. It is almost three hours long. This marks the first time people are saying, "I'm going to save myself some time and just read the book."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Airlines in Europe are testing a new robot that can make drinks for passengers instead of having flight attendants do it. This way, flight attendants can stay focused on their most important job — ramming the beverage cart into your elbow.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night the Lakers lost to the Knicks for their fourth loss in a row. I don't want to say that it was an easy night for the Knicks, but even Woody Allen finished with nine points.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The DEA says drug smugglers in Mexico are using canons to shoot marijuana over into the U.S. They have three distances — far, really far, and Willie Nelson's house.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Hobbit opens today. It's going to make a ton of money this weekend. It will make more money than Mitt Romney spent losing the election.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Gollum's back as well. He's my favorite character. According to "The Lord of the Rings," Gollum was once a normal man. But wearing the ring drained him of his youth, vitality, and energy. That's why some men view him as a symbol of marriage.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Secretary of State Hillary Clinton collapsed, passed out, banged her head, got a concussion. She is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On Saturday night someone stole the cover off my daughter's Prius. My daughter is away at college. I'm determined to catch these guys. Who steals the cover off a car? That's like stealing the cap off a pen.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you thieves are watching right now, I want you to know that my name is Jimmy Kimmel and you stole the cover off my daughter's Prius and I will not rest until you are brought to justice.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I never felt more like Liam Neeson than I did a moment ago.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: To get you in the Christmas spirit, we booked a rapper by the name of 2 Chainz who reminds me of a young Bing Crosby.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In what's being called a stunning literary find, a Danish historian has discovered the last remaining, unpublished fairy tale from Hans Christian Andersen. It's called "Congress Solves the Fiscal Cliff."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Police are now looking for a man who robbed a bank wearing a Mitt Romney mask. He robbed the bank, fled the area, and then stashed the money somewhere in the Cayman Islands.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Over the weekend, Hillary Clinton passed out, hit her head, and suffered a minor concussion. Well, we found out today why she passed out. Apparently, she heard the Lakers won two games in a row.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Animal control officers have now shut down a rat-breeding business here in California due to animal neglect. That's when you know things are bad — when your business is too unsanitary for rats.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It’s rumored that John Boehner and President Obama are considering a partial deal to avoid the fiscal cliff at the end of the year. Yeah, it’s RUMORED that a PARTIAL deal is being CONSIDERED — or to put that in layman’s terms: We’re going off this cliff.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: ABC is working on a new show inspired by Justin Bieber’s life before he got famous. It makes sense — I mean, there’s just so much we don’t know about that week.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A woman in Spain was arrested for stashing three pounds of cocaine in her breast implants. I thought, "That's quite a bust."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Anne Hathaway was photographed stepping out of a car last week with no underpants on. That's still not as embarrassing as the time she hosted the Oscars.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You know the economy is bad when the most successful celebrities can't afford underwear.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Only 12 shopping days left before Christmas. The big toy this year is the Furby. It's a toy that came out in 1998. It's weird how old junk suddenly becomes valuable and you wish you hadn't thrown them out — kind of like the way CNN feels about Larry King right about now.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The world's oldest woman passed away at 116. They keep dying. I think that title may be cursed.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I was thinking about Santa Claus. When you really think about it, this has to be the biggest, most elaborate prank in the history of the world. It's like we're all in on a huge joke we're playing on kids. And eventually they figure it out and they start lying to their kids, too.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Christmas is on Tuesday, provided that the world doesn't end on Friday, which is the end of the Mayan calendar. Some believe there will be massive earthquakes and floods. Others think a planet will collide with the earth. I believe the end of the world will come about in a much stupider way, like Joe Biden spilling a Mountain Dew on the nuclear launch panel.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: And as silly as this all may seem, a worldwide survey shows that one in 10 people believe the world is going to end on Friday. A Chinese man even designed a survival pod. The inventor says they can hold 14 people comfortably, or roughly three American people comfortably.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you buy one of these pods, you might survive the end of the world. But since it is made in China, you will also die of lead poisoning.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It looks like President Obama is going to pick John Kerry to be our next secretary of state. This is a very strategic move when it comes to foreign policy. Obama plans to use Kerry to bore our enemies to death.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A 2009 Ford F-150 pickup truck, once owned by President George W. Bush, is going up for auction in a couple of weeks. All the proceeds will go to military families. President Obama should buy this truck because when something goes wrong he can blame it on Bush.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NBC's foreign news correspondent Richard Engel has been freed after being kidnapped and held at gunpoint for five days in Syria by rebels. Even though he was psychologically tortured, he said he was still treated better there than he was here by Comcast.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sources told ABC News today that Defense Department official Michael Vickers gave sensitive inside information about the capture of Osama bin Laden to the producers of the movie “Zero Dark Thirty.” It’s also being reported that John McCain gave firsthand inside information to the film “Lincoln.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, President Obama and John Boehner talked about the fiscal cliff for 45 minutes, but the White House will not release a transcript of their conversation. However, they did offer to have Joe Biden re-enact it with puppets.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Wait, we’re facing one of the biggest threats to our economy and they only met for 45 minutes? That’s not even the opening credits of “The Hobbit”!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last week a group of chefs baked the world’s largest pizza, which is gluten-free and contains 9,000 pounds of cheese. Or as Americans put it, “You had me at ‘world’s largest pizza’ — you LOST me at ‘gluten-free’ — then you won me back with “9,000 pounds of cheese.’”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There’s talk that Jackie Chan may join the cast of “The Expendables 3,” along with Sylvester Stallone and Arnold Schwarzenegger. Stallone, Schwarzenegger, and Chan — which explains the movie’s next title: “The Can’t-Understandables.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: New Jersey became a state on this day in 1787. New Jersey Governor Chris Christie celebrated with a giant cake and a bucket of ice cream. Then he remembered today was New Jersey's birthday.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A Charlie Brown Christmas aired on CBS for 35 years. But since 2001 it's been airing on ABC. I can't believe CBS let a classic like that get away, yet they keep this crappy show on the air.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I love Charlie Brown. He's a pretty mopey kid. His whole demeanor is depressing. The first time saw Charlie Brown, I couldn't believe he wasn't Scottish. And he wears the same yellow and black shirt every day. It makes him look like a Steelers fan.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Here is what I think is weird about Charlie Brown. People always call him by his full name. I'd like it if people referred to me by my complete name: Craig Dingleberry Mcpennywhistle Susan Ferguson.

name: David Letterman
monologue: According to the Mayan calendar, Friday is the end of the world. You know what? There is a sign of the apocalypse. The New York Knicks are in first place.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As you know, the Mayans said the world will end tomorrow, and like everybody else, they blame Bush.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As we get closer to Christmas, these Christmas tree lots try to rip you off because they know you're desperate. They know you need a tree. I was at a lot last night. I went to buy a tree. Needles sold separately. I couldn't believe it.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Michigan lawyer has been arrested for manufacturing crystal meth in his office. I hope the fact that this guy's a lawyer doesn't send the message that somehow all meth dealers are sleaze balls.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Tim Tebow and actress Camilla Belle have called it quits. it just didn't work out. Kind of like Tebow and the quarterbacking thing, just didn't work out.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After three years and six seasons, the final episode of “Jersey Shore” aired tonight. Or as the Mayans put it, “So we were off by one day.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There's a photo going around with President Obama playing with a staffer's son who's dressed as Spider-Man. Obama was like, "Shouldn't you be fighting the Green Goblin?" And the kid was like, "shouldn't you be working on the fiscal cliff?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The kid was really excited to meet the president, while Joe Biden was real excited to meet Spider-Man.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm sure the new movies are good, but I'm upset there are no real Christmas movies. Like "It's a Wonderful Life," where Jimmy Stewart finds himself in a world where no one can see him. It's like nobody's aware of his existence. I know that feeling.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a Wonderful Life is the one where the angel earns his wings. Because remember, kids, an angel without wings is like Tom Selleck without a moustache, or like "Two and a Half Men" without a cast member going crazy.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Instead of remaking an old Christmas movie, maybe Hollywood could make a sequel to a Christmas movie that people liked. Like that Tim Allen movie, "The Santa Cause." There are people who'd love another one of those movies. By people, I mean Tim Allen.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's the shortest day of the year. Now the longest day of the year is any day you have lunch with Regis Philbin.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Well folks, it is December 21, or as the Mayans call it, April Fools Day.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We have Terry Bradshaw on the show tonight. The only reason we booked him is because we thought the world was going to end. He thinks we are doing a show so now we have to do it.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Tim Tebow and actress Camilla Belle have called it quits. The rumor is, she caught him not having sex with another woman.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sources say Tim was unhappy because he felt she was using him — and coach Rex Ryan wasn’t.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It’s late Friday night, which means the world did not end after all! So the good news is, we’re still here. The bad news, I got A LOT of Christmas shopping to do.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today, President Obama announced that he's giving all federal employees Christmas Eve off. And when Joe Biden heard that he was like, "But not Santa, right?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Ireland is coming out with its own version of the show “Cheers.” Yeah, a sitcom about people who sit around drinking at a bar all day — or as they call that in Ireland, “Reality TV.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Mayan calendar didn't go past Dec. 21, 2012. There is one problem with the Mayan prophesy. It is crap. Every serious Mayan scholar says close reading of Mayan texts reveals they believed the world would go for thousands of years past the end of the calendar. But let's listen to the wacko locked in the basement with 500 pounds of spam because he knows what is going to happen!

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I've got to admit, I love the show "Doomsday Preppers." It's about people making bunkers to survive catastrophes they know will happen. A nuclear war, viral epidemic, Fox canceling "Glee." It's all going to happen.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Personally, I think people who are panicking about what the Mayans believed says more about our society than it does the Mayans. I don't know really where I'm going with that, but it sounded good, didn't it? It sounded like I was really smart. I've got something to say.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You know what I really am feeling awkward about? If this is really the end of the world, I'm going to my doom wearing this tie. I'm going off to the hereafter with a tie with a little snowman on it.

name: David Letterman
monologue: You're looking at a very happy man. I made $500. You know how I did that? Betting against the Mayans.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Some people are concerned 2013 will be an unlucky year because of the number 13. As compared to those lucky years like 2012 and 2011.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congress has approved some version of this fiscal cliff bill thing. Well, taxes are going up, and now, they're looking to make cuts just about everywhere. In fact, oil companies today had to lay off 15 senators.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This has been a tough week for NFL coaches. Seven NFL head coaches got fired on Monday. That's a lot of job openings. That's the most job openings we've had in this country in the last four years.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to Forbes magazine, the Dallas Cowboys are the most valuable team in the NFL. They are worth $2 billion. So I guess that old adage, "winning isn't everything," is true.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After hours and hours of tough negotiation, the most powerful people in America have finally come to an agreement — that’s right, if it’s a girl, they’ll name it Kim, and if it’s a boy, they’ll name it Kanye.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: While working on a deal to avoid the fiscal cliff, members of Congress spent New Year’s Eve at the Capitol. Yeah, even the guy watching the Twilight Zone marathon with his parents was like, “Talk about a lame New Year’s.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I heard that Dunkin' Donuts is testing a new line of gluten-free pastries. So if you're looking to eat healthy, still no.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Monday night, thieves broke into the Apple store in Paris and stole one million dollars worth of iPhones and iPads. That’s right — they took four iPhones and two iPads.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Has anyone seen Al Gore's Current TV? I don't mean by mistake. I mean, who's actually watched it?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: John Boehner was re-elected speaker of the house, which is pretty amazing — a Republican winning anything these days.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Chris Christie also lashed out at Congress for doing nothing for the victims of Hurricane Sandy. But in their defense Congress says, "Hey, we don't do anything for anybody."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama signed the new fiscal cliff tax increase into law while vacationing in Hawaii today. He used an autopen, an electronic way of signing your name when you're not even there. Politicians can now raise your taxes while they're on vacation in Hawaii. This is a Democrat's dream come true.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The National Journal says that Joe Biden may be the most influential vice president in history. Joe Biden got this exciting news while he was walking President Obama's dog, Bo.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today, members of the 113th Congress were sworn in at the Capitol. After which, they were like, “Well, that's enough work for the year.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today the Senate swore in a record 20 female senators. Yep, the women said they’re very excited, and look forward to proving they can accomplish just as little as male senators.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Older members of the Academy are having trouble submitting their Oscar votes this year because for the first time, they are voting online. The good news is that "Les Miz" has gotten a lot of votes for Best Picture; the bad news is, most of them were typed into a microwave.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This week Congress approved some version of the fiscal tax bill, which raises taxes on rich Americans. President Obama was determined to do this right away — while there are still some rich Americans left.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Americans from all sides of the political spectrum seem to be upset about this fiscal cliff deal. Imagine how the Chinese must feel. It's their money.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Al Gore's Current TV has been sold to Al-Jazeera for a reported $500 million. Experts believe that Al-Jazeera overpaid for Current TV by approximately $500 million.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The National Journal says Joe Biden maybe the most influential vice president in history. Is that really a compliment? Isn’t that like being the tallest hobbit?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tomorrow is the start of the NFL playoffs. The Bengals are playing the Texans at Houston; the Vikings are playing the Packers at Green Bay; and the Jets are playing the Giants at Scrabble.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: That’s right, the NFL playoffs start this weekend. Yep, I can’t wait to just plant myself on the couch and watch all the games — or as that’s also known, “Tebowing.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Congrats to “Star Wars” creator George Lucas, who just got engaged to his girlfriend of seven years. Yeah, seven years. Of course, since it’s George Lucas, people say the first three were great but the ones after that were kinda disappointing.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, George Lucas’s fiancé is 25 years younger than him. Or as his lawyer put it, “May the pre-nup be with you.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: The hockey lockout is over. We had no hockey in October. I knew the NHL lockout would be settled once it was purchased by al-Jazeera.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Tickets to President Obama's inauguration have sold out. At least that's what the president is telling Joe Biden.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Tonight Notre Dame plays Alabama in the BCS championship game. That's big. I was home for the holidays so I've had quite enough of the Fighting Irish.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: After 113 days, the National Hockey League has settled its contract dispute. So finally Americans can get back to not watching hockey.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last week photos surfaced of Justin Bieber smoking marijuana. Fans of Justin Bieber were really upset and fans of marijuana were really embarrassed.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today Democrats said they want another trillion dollars in taxes. Didn't we just give them $620 billion last Wednesday? Is that gone already? Who is running this, "The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills"?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Scientists in China say obesity may be caused by bacteria in your stomach. Three of the most common carriers of the bacteria are pizza, cheeseburgers, and doughnuts.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Police in Brazil have apprehended a cat that has been traveling in and out of a men's prison with various escape tools, like saw blades and drill bits, taped to its body. The judge was pretty harsh. Today, the cat received nine life sentences.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Lance Armstrong now says he may admit that he used performance enhancing drugs. I guess he realized he’s the only person in the world who still wasn’t sure about it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Joe Biden and his wife left D.C. this weekend for a five-day vacation in the Caribbean. Of course, most of that time will be spent telling him that Margaritaville isn’t a real place.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Lance Armstrong’s lawyer is denying reports that he will admit to using performance-enhancing drugs. He said that Lance has been very consistent about his intentions to just keep lying about it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that our personalities change about once every 10 years. And if you disagree with the study — well, just give it 10 years.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Friday a passenger on a flight to JFK had to be restrained with duct tape after he got drunk and started yelling at other passengers. Duct tape to hold someone in their seat — or as Southwest Airlines calls that, "a seatbelt."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Two beloved institutions have returned. Yesterday the NHL agreed to end their strike. On the same day, "Downton Abbey" began season three on PBS. I would love to see more hockey on "Downton Abbey."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Hockey and "Downton Abbey" are very different, of course. One's a vicious game played by scary people with bad teeth. The other one's hockey.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Over here, "Downton Abbey" is on PBS. That's why I'm glad I watched it in Britain. I don't feel guilty about not giving PBS any money.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If you watch cooking shows on cable, they have lots of British people. Because when you think good cooking, you immediately think Britain.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night Alabama won football's national championship by defeating Notre Dame 42-4. Irish people haven't been this depressed since — all the time. Every day. Constantly.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Good news for hockey. After 113 days, the National Hockey League has settled its contract dispute. The last time Americans went 113 days without watching hockey, it was during last year's hockey season.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A political opponent is accusing Governor Chris Christie of praying for Hurricane Sandy. In response, Christie said the only weather-related thing he's ever prayed for is a Dairy Queen Blizzard.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new poll, Congress is now less popular than head lice, Nickelback, and Donald Trump. In a related story, head lice is insulted that it's being lumped in with Donald Trump and Nickelback.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to several reports, a lot of people think 2013 is going to be bad luck because it has the number 13 in it. You know what you call these people? Notre Dame fans.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Do you know what BCS stands for? “Beating Catholics Soundly.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Let me tell you how bad it was. Today the Pope suggested that Notre Dame might want to be a Lutheran college.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The game was basically over at halftime. It was like a Lakers game.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The great David Bowie turned 66 today. To celebrate, he released a new music video. I wish I could be like David Bowie and just disappear, stay under the radar and out of the spotlight for 10 years. Well, I've been doing this show for eight years, so just another two to go.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: David Bowie is fantastic. I like to think I have some things in common with him. He's from Britain. I'm from Britain. He used to have a problem with cocaine. I used to have a problem with cocaine. He's considered a genius. I used to have a problem with cocaine.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I started listening to Bowie back in the 1970s. A big part of his mystique back then was his sexuality. He was ambiguous. Bowie made androgyny cool. In the decade before Bowie, music was dominated by macho, manly men. Like Elvis, Frank Sinatra, and Liberace.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Bowie's been married to Iman, the model, now for 20 years. Marrying a model is a great idea because you save a fortune on food.

name: David Letterman
monologue: We're $20 trillion in debt so somebody at the treasury department says that what we'll do is print a coin for a trillion dollars. I've seen a prototype. It has a beautiful profile of Regis Philbin.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night Alabama crushed Notre Dame 42-14 in the BCS National Championship. I haven’t seen such an ugly night for the Fighting Irish since Thanksgiving with my family.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Archeologists investigating an ancient shipwreck in Italy have discovered pills over 2,000 years old. Meanwhile, my mom was like, “That date is just a recommendation. They're still good.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: To celebrate his birthday, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un sent two pounds of candy to every child in the country. Which explains why Honey Boo Boo has applied for dual citizenship.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A new time slot. We used to be on at midnight. Now we're on at 11:35. Now I'm 25 minutes closer to my lifelong dream of co-hosting "The View."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Nightline is on after us now, but just because this isn't "Nightline," that doesn't mean we're not going to talk about important stuff. For instance, did you know Honey Boo Boo's mother is afraid of mayonnaise?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: My New Year's resolution this year was to get a gym membership, use it twice, and then never use it again. I'm already halfway there.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Alabama won the college football championship game. It was a tough loss for the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. If only Irish people had some kind of tradition of drowning their sorrows in something, it would have been so much easier.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Consumer Electronics Show is happening in Las Vegas and the most amazing gadgets are being talked about. One of the gadgets this year is a fork that tells you when you're eating too fast. In a related story today, Chris Christie was spotted yelling at his fork to mind its own business.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Chris Christie said to his fork, "Shut up or I'm going to switch to my friend — spoon."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's being reported that Apple may be making a less-expensive version of their iPhone. They're calling it a Samsung.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Baseball Hall of Fame voting results are in, and for the first time since 1996, not one player was voted in. They turned down Roger Clemens, Mark McGwire, Sammy Sosa, and Barry Bonds. Here’s how bad it was: Lance Armstrong got more votes than any of those guys.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The mayor of Los Angeles, Antonio Villaraigosa, was seen partying in Mexico with Charlie Sheen. I believe that celebration is called “Cinco de Career-o.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The mayor is denying it. He said he only saw Charlie for a minute, but Charlie said he and the mayor had a wild time in Mexico partying with a number of hot women. Who are you going to believe — a party boy who has never done anything in his life or Charlie Sheen?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Here is a shocking statistic. You know who are the most frequent binge drinkers? Seniors! That explains Brent Musberger’s comments about Miss Alabama.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Earlier tonight on Fox they aired a show called "Stars in Danger: The High Dive." I can hear you mumbling at your TV, "Reality TV stars in a diving competition? Who'd even watch crap like that?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I only watched the first half-hour. In my defense, I didn't know there'd be water in the pool.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: One of the contestants on this show is Antonio Sabato Jr. I'm a big fan. I can tell you everything about him. His dad is Antonio Sabato Sr.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Right here on CBS was the annual People's Choice Awards show. It had fantastic categories like "favorite Kardashian" and "favorite late-night Jimmy."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The White House announced that the theme for President Obama’s inauguration will be “Faith in America’s Future.” Which is proof that no one in the White House has ever seen "Here Comes Honey Boo Boo.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama’s team is promising special perks for donors who give at least a million dollars to the inauguration. Which is cool, but you know what else can get you a lot of perks? Keeping that million dollars.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today, the president hosted a screening of NBC’s White House comedy, “1600 Penn,” which centers on a goofy guy who keeps embarrassing the White House. Or as Joe Biden put it, “Why’s everyone looking at me?”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It's the second night of our new time slot. We had a big show last night. Unfortunately, I found out this afternoon we have to do it again tonight. I don't know what these people want from me.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On Fox tonight, they aired a two-hour celebrity diving show called "Stars in Danger: The High Dive." I think the only thing worse than being a celebrity contestant on a competitive diving show is being a celebrity judge on a competitive diving show.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On CBS tonight is the People's Choice Awards. The People's Choice Awards is basically an annual reminder that we have too many awards shows.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It's voted on by the people instead of academy members. That's all good until "Battleship" wins best picture.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A 9-year-old was nominated for an Oscar, making her the youngest nominee ever. She says she's dreamed of winning an Oscar ever since last week.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama's inauguration is coming up. During next week's inauguration, he will be sworn in with not one, but two Bibles. Relax, Mr. President. We get it. You're not a Muslim. You're overcompensating.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Justin Bieber is being sued for allegedly beating up his ex-bodyguard. Which begs the question — who hires a bodyguard that Justin Bieber can beat up?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The University of Arizona now offers a degree in hip-hop. Trust me. That's one class where you don't want to cheat off the Asian kid.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today was a big day in Hollywood. The Oscar nominations were announced. "Lincoln" leads the list with 12 nominations. This is a first — not the most nominations, but the first time Hollywood has ever voted for a Republican president. That is amazing.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congratulations Denzel Washington. He got nominated for best actor for "Flight." It’s about a pilot who's an alcoholic. Or as we call that now — a documentary.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The White House announced today that the theme for President Obama's second inauguration will be "Faith in America's Future." The idea is to get our minds off of America's present.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The makers of the Monopoly game announced they are going to replace one of the famous board game's tokens. If they want to modernize Monopoly they should just throw the banker into prison and put Lindsay Lohan on the “Get Out of Jail” free card. That’s how you modernize the game.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Oscar nominations were announced. The movie "Brave" was nominated for best animated feature. I did a voice in that movie. A few years ago, "How to Train Your Dragon" was nominated. I did a voice for that too. I'm sensing a pattern. Accolades are only given to work in which I don't show my face.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The movie that got the most nominations was "Lincoln." It's the first time Hollywood has ever supported a Republican.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Ghost Rider 2: Spirit of Vengeance got zip. Nothing. It is an outrage! Nicolas Cage played a motorcycle-riding skeleton on fire. Let's see Daniel Day-Lewis do that.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: John Williams was nominated for his "Lincoln" score. It's his 48th nomination. I wonder if John Williams even pretends to care at this point.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Baseball's Hall of Fame had its selections for players who are voted in. This year, nobody gets in. Lots of players were eligible, but nobody got in. However, Pete Rose is already taking bets for next year.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The 2013 Oscar nominations were announced today. "Lincoln" earned the most nominations of any movie. 12 nominations for "Lincoln." I have a feeling that if he were alive today, Lincoln would say, "What is a movie?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Chilean movie "No" received a nomination for best foreign language film. The producers are working on the sequel called "Maybe."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama recently came under fire over the lack of diversity in his cabinet. Then Obama said, "You guys know I'll be there, too, right?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Prostitutes in Brazil have started learning English so they can communicate with out-of-town clients during the World Cup. They are learning key phrases like, "You are very handsome" and "Nice to meet you, Mr. Sheen."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Did any of you get nominated for an Oscar? Me neither. Apparently you have to be in a movie to get nominated, which I think is unfair.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I was looking through a list of the best picture nominees. Some of them are very obscure. The rule should be that a movie is eligible only if I've heard of it.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Lincoln led the field with 12 nominations. Lincoln I've heard of. The guy from the money, right?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In the best actress category, two records were set. An 85-year-old actress became the oldest nominee. And a 9-year-old became the youngest nominee. That is until Honey Boo Boo next year.

name: David Letterman
monologue: This year nobody was elected to baseball's hall of fame. No player has ever gotten into the hall of fame without winning Ohio.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Centers for Disease Control announced that the flu has officially reached epidemic status. Epidemics are rarely good. You rarely hear about balloon epidemics.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Our huge state budget deficit is gone. Governor Jerry Brown announced the state budget for next year is projected to net an $851 million surplus and this year we'll have a surplus of $785 million. You hear that, meter maids? Maybe you can stop giving us tickets for a couple of months.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It's a huge achievement for Governor Jerry Brown. Apparently you can get a lot done when you're not walking around saying "I'll be back" all the time.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber is being sued by a former bodyguard. The bodyguard's lawsuit claims Justin punched him repeatedly in the chest. He's seeking $420,000. I think I would pay $420,000 to keep the fact that I got beat up by Justin Bieber a secret.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama will be sworn in with his hand resting on two Bibles. Is that how screwed up Washington is now? One Bible can't get the job done anymore?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: U.S. customs officials recently discovered 310 pounds of marijuana hidden in some frozen carrots. That's one way to keep kids away from drugs — put them in vegetables.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Carrots and marijuana — how good will your vision be after THIS combination?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A former bodyguard for Justin Bieber is now suing Justin Bieber, saying that the star assaulted him. Well, you can see why he's suing. Good luck getting anymore work as a bodyguard when find out that you got beat up by Justin Bieber.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new survey found that 77 percent of Americans think politicians do serious harm to the country. Politicians are like, "Cool, at least they think we do something."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday American Express announced that it had to cut more than 5,000 jobs. Even worse is how they told their employees. They said, "American Express. Don't leave home."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tim Tebow is now selling his own line of headphones. You can tell they are Tim Tebow headphones. Once you hook it up to your iPod, it barely plays.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There is a big new movie out today that I'm excited about: "Gangster Squad." The leader is played by Josh Brolin. He's a real tough guy. He looks like he can go toe-to-toe with even the toughest adversary. That'll happen when your stepmom is Barbra Streisand.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Gangster Squad is set in 1948, when L.A. was ruled by a ruthless gang that defended its turf with threats and deception. Sort of like the Kardashians, but with better style.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Sean Penn is also in this movie. Sean Penn is a villain who says crazy things and punches out the good guys. I'm not sure what he does in the movie.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Penn plays legendary gangster Mickey Cohen. In the 1940s Mickey Cohen and his gang ran this town. Now it's run by Mickey Mouse and the Disney gang.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Golden Globes last night had a lot of great moments. During Jodie Foster's emotional speech she said she was gay, 50, and friends with Mel Gibson. Afterwards, her publicist told Jodie, "I'm going to need a raise."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama's half-brother is running for political office in Kenya. Donald Trump has already accused him of being born in the United States.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There is a new app that is coming out that shows you how alcohol will age you. When I was a kid, we did this by looking at our fathers.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Steven Tyler and his fiancée have reportedly broken up. The fiancée explained she just wants to date other old gypsy women.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This flu epidemic is just terrible. Experts say that those hit hardest are the very old and the very young. So that's especially bad news for Hugh Hefner and his new bride.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Daniel Day-Lewis won a Golden Globe for playing Abraham Lincoln and Julianne Moore won for playing Sarah Palin. The foreign press realized that the greatest challenge for an actor in Hollywood is pretending to be a Republican.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Florida couple got into a fight resulting in the woman biting off half her boyfriend's ear. She said her biggest complaint is that he never listens.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The mayor of Los Angeles, Antonio Villaraigosa, was seen partying in Mexico with Charlie Sheen. When will Charlie learn that people judge you by the company you keep?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's cold here in L.A. We broke records last night. It was so cold, Charlie Sheen filled his bed with porn stars just to stay warm.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was so cold, Mel Gibson was seen drunk driving in a snowmobile.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was so cold Matthew McConaughey was seen wearing a shirt. It's never that cold.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today is the first day of the Detroit Auto Show. They also give out awards in many different categories. The prize for 2013 light truck of the year went to Daniel Day-Lewis. He's winning everything this year!

name: David Letterman
monologue: Thirteen years ago today doctors had me split open like a lobster and they performed the highly dangerous bypass surgery. Today I said, "Doctor, I'm calling to thank you very much. Thirteen years ago today you saved my life." And he says "Well, Dave, it seemed like a good idea at the time."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Everyone was talking about how cold it was on the Golden Globes red carpet. The temperature was in the low 50s. In fact, it was so cold, Ryan Seacrest had to get his hair defrosted.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Black Sabbath is reuniting with Ozzy Osbourne for their first album together in 35 years. You can tell they're getting up there because now all Ozzy can do is gum at a bat's head for 30 seconds until it flies away.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Congrats to 23-year-old Mallory Hagan from Brooklyn, who won the Miss America pageant on Saturday. You could tell that she is from Brooklyn because instead of saying she wanted world peace, she was like, "War? Forget about it."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Republicans and Democrats are working on a new bill to streamline the healthcare system. It will reduce the cost of mammograms and prostate exams. But don't worry. They'll still be free at the airport.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: President Obama held the final press conference of his first term in office this morning, talking mostly about the debt ceiling. He announced if Congress doesn't raise the debt ceiling America will go into default on its loans and we might have to say goodbye to Florida.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: An economist is suggesting that the U.S. Treasury mint a trillion-dollar county and deposit it in the federal reserve — which is how "The Lord of the Rings" starts, isn't it?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Treasury will not mint a trillion-dollar coin. That is a shame. Wouldn't it be nice to mint up nine or 10 and say we're even?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Oprah Winfrey says she conducted "an intense two and a half hour interview with Lance Armstrong." Oprah said she never would have had the stamina if Lance wouldn't have given her something to keep going.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama told Congress it must raise our debt limit because the U.S. "is not a deadbeat nation." Then the president added, "By the way, if China calls, I'm not here."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Wal-Mart made plans to hire 100,000 U.S. Veterans. Which can only mean one thing: Wal-Mart is going to invade Costco.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Actress Megan Fox compared fame to being bullied in high school. I agree. I'll never forget that day in high school when jocks cornered me in the gym and paid me millions of dollars to star in "Transformers."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Lance Armstrong confessed during his interview with Oprah Winfrey that he did use performance-enhancing drugs to win the Tour de France seven times. This came as a complete shock to as many as a dozen people.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Although he denied it for years, it was starting to become obvious. Like that one year he won the race on the stationary bike. Remember that?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Lance said that he felt like a great weight had been lifted — a huge, oversized weight that he never could have lifted naturally.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The interview with Oprah will air on Thursday. Then on Friday, Lance will appear on a very special episode of “Cheaters.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Wikipedia celebrates its 12th birthday today. Of course, I have no idea if it's true. I read it on Wikipedia.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Lance Armstrong admitted he used performance-enhancing drugs throughout his career. He confessed in front of the most respected judge in the land, Oprah Winfrey.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: His interview with Oprah lasted almost three hours. At one point Lance said he propagated one of the greatest frauds in American history. And Oprah said, "Whoa. Easy there. I'm the one who discovered Dr. Phil."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Whether or not you support Lance Armstrong, you can agree on one thing. The admission allows us all to go back to not giving a crap about cycling.

name: David Letterman
monologue: I asked my doctor yesterday what the difference is between a cold and the flu and he said, "About $80."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama’s inaugural parade will feature eight floats, including a Hawaii float to honor his birthplace, an Illinois float to honor the first lady’s home state, and a Kenyan float just to mess with Republicans.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The president will push for a path to citizenship for 11 million illegal immigrants in the U.S. Obama says it’s all part of his plan to give every man, woman, and child the chance to pay more taxes.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Education Secretary Arne Duncan announced that he will stay at the White House for President Obama’s second term. He said his mission is to make the U.S. number one in education, and won’t stop until our students are doing gooder.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: MGM is coming out with a remake of the classic 1959 film “Ben-Hur.” You can tell it’s a remake because instead of being about a Jewish prince who is betrayed by his Roman friend, sent into slavery, and then seeks revenge — it’s just about sexy vampires.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg held a press conference to announce that if you post one more picture of your cat sleeping, they're going to delete your account.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Zuckerberg introduced a new feature called Graph Search. It delivers search results from your network of Facebook friends, so you can ask questions like, "Who are my friends that live in San Francisco?" By the way, if you have to ask that, you don't have any friends in San Francisco.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It's an interesting new feature. Soon you'll be able to find anything you want on Facebook, except for the thousands of hours of your life you lost going on Facebook.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A health advocacy group has criticized The Cheesecake Factory for offering meals that contain over 3,000 calories. Today the CEO of The Cheesecake Factory said, "What part of factory of cheese and cake don't you understand?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: That's like going to Fat Burger and complaining.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The director of "Zero Dark Thirty" has come out against torture. And the director of "Lincoln" has come out against going to the theater in 1865.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: An American worker was arrested for paying someone in China to do his job for him. The man is being called lazy, irresponsible, and three years ahead of his time.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama said this week that he wants to find a "pathway for citizenship" for immigrants in the United States. Don't we have that? It's called the Rio Grande river.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Thousands of dead fish have now washed up on shore along the coast of South Carolina. Today the NRA said that this wouldn't have happened if those fish had guns.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Ann Romney, the wife of Mitt Romney, has reportedly turned down a chance to appear on “Dancing With the Stars.” Apparently, she has something called "self-respect."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It seems a doctor in Germany is being sued by the family of a patient who died after 16 items were left inside of him after the surgery. The doctor said he felt terrible. He tried to call the family but couldn't find his cell phone.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: American Idol starts tonight. This is the third season without Simon Cowell. People thought the show wouldn't survive without him. And those people are called "Simon Cowell."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I think each new judge will bring something unique to the show. Mariah Carey: wisdom. Nicki Minaj: sass. And Keith Urban will bring stubble.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Apps make everything easier these days. To think just a few years ago I had no idea what an app was. Of course a few years ago I had no idea what a Kardashian or a Bieber or a Honey Boo Boo was.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Over the weekend, during a routine cleanup, park crews discovered a cannon from the Revolutionary War that was still loaded. Old, loaded, and ready to go — it's like me before the show.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I’m sorry if I seem a little distracted; I just confessed to Oprah that when I played T-ball in kindergarten, I was on Juicy-Juice.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Oprah’s big interview with Lance Armstrong is getting a lot of attention. Oprah said she prepared 112 questions. The first question was, “Did you use steroids?” while the next 111 questions were, “Oh, come on. You used steroids, right?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A week after saying, “I’m not leaving Oregon for the NFL,” Chip Kelly has agreed to be the head coach of the Philadelphia Eagles. Even Lance Armstrong was like, “Pick a story and stick with it.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The beginning of the movie “Lincoln” has been slightly changed to explain the Civil War to foreign audiences. Or as Lincoln put it, “I would have preferred a different ENDING.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight we as a nation usher in a new season of "American Idol." Will it be the final season? Let's hope so.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The judges are almost all new on "American Idol." They include the guy who's married to Nicole Kidman — Keith Urban, who's Australian. Are we really going to let an Australian pick our "American Idol"? Doesn't sound very American to me.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Steven Tyler added a little extra something to "American Idol." He'd zero in on the female contestants. He'd stare at them like a hungry cheetah stalking a gazelle, and I miss that.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Flu season is here. There's always a group of people who are too paranoid to get a flu shot, even though about half of them have between one and 80 tattoos. What these people are saying is: "I do not trust the doctors to tell me the flu shot is safe and effective, but I do trust the guy with a nose ring to inject me repeatedly with ink."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Notre Dame player Manti Te’o is being accused of fraud and deception over his imaginary girlfriend. Some say this hoax could harm Manti's ranking in the NFL draft. On the other hand, it could open up an entire new branch of fantasy football.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Sources are saying that Tiger Woods wants to marry his ex-wife and might be willing to go for a no-cheating clause. This special clause would be known as a wedding vow.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Facebook's new search engine is getting a lot of attention. CEO Mark Zuckerberg pointed out that Facebook can now help people find new friends. He doesn't know that Facebook is for stalking old ones.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A group of nutritionists criticized The Cheesecake Factory for a pasta dish that has 3,000 calories. A representative from Olive Garden said, "What is pasta? Tell us more of this interesting dish."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Notre Dame’s superstar linebacker Manti Te’o apparently had an online girlfriend who didn’t really exist. They're calling it the biggest hoax involving Notre Dame since they were ranked number one in the nation.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Happy birthday to first lady Michelle Obama. She turned 49 years old today. She told a reporter she’d like a nice gift from Barack, but nothing extravagant. Oh, don’t worry. Obama is very responsible when he's spending his own money.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the Center for Science in the Public Interest, the top two most unhealthy restaurant dishes were from The Cheesecake Factory. The Cheesecake Factory? It's always the last place you'd expect.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The most unhealthy dish at The Cheesecake Factory was something called the bistro shrimp pasta, with 3,120 calories. And that's before the cheesecake.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today Russia announced plans to send a probe to the moon by the year 2015. Russian scientists say they're excited to see what they could discover on the moon's surface. I'll tell you what they're going to discover — an American flag!

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Sundance Film Festival begins today. The jury is choosing among 87 different films. I'd like be on that jury. I'd bang my gavel and say, "I find your film guilty of being self-indulgent and boring the crap out of me. I hereby sentence you to watch "Weekend at Bernie's," and anything by Pauly Shore."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don't know if I could be a judge. Watching five movies a day sounds exhausting. But maybe that's just a sign of how out of shape I am.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There are some great documentaries this year. One's called "Linsanity: the Movie." It's about basketball player Jeremy Lin. He's America's most interesting athlete who's never had a fake girlfriend.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Notre Dame has a kid named Manti Te’o, a linebacker. It turns out his girlfriend was imaginary. But in his defense, Brent Musberger said she was really hot.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Notre Dame linebacker Manti Te’o is being accused of making up an online girlfriend, and then lying about her death last year so that it would help him win the Heisman Trophy. Or as Manti Te’o put it, “I’m gonna have to talk to Oprah, aren’t I?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Manti Te'o's online girlfriend was a complete fabrication. When they heard that, nerds were like, “Man, even IMAGINARY girls only like jocks.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In a recent attack ad, the NRA claims that President Obama cares about his own children more than he cares about other children. In response, President Obama was like, “Yeah, that's how families work.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Cirque du Soleil just announced that it is cutting 400 jobs. So on the downside, hundreds of clowns will lose their jobs. But on the bright side, it’ll free up, like, two spaces in the parking lot.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Have you been following the Manti Te’o story? Apparently Te'o, a well-known college football player, was in a relationship with a woman he met online. But it turned out that the woman was Bruce Willis and he was dead the whole time.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Manti Te’o is a linebacker at Notre Dame. In September, his girlfriend passed away. The media ran with the story of the football hero overcoming personal tragedy. But it turned out she never existed. Some people play fantasy football. Manti Te’o plays fantasy people.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The first part of Oprah Winfrey's big interview with Lance Armstrong aired tonight. At one point, Lance broke down and cried. And here's a funny thing. Wherever a tear landed, a new muscle grew.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I just hope that this one painful online experience doesn't cause Manti Te’o to give up on all imaginary girlfriends.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Now people are saying that Manti knew it was a hoax way back in early December. He’s gone from being the “Fightin’ Irish” to the “Lyin’ Hawaiian.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new study, seniors are the most frequent binge drinkers — followed closely by juniors, sophomores, and freshmen.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Kim Kardashian said today that in a perfect world she would love being divorced from Kris Humphries before having Kayne’s baby. On the other hand, in a perfect world no one would know who she is.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Did you see Oprah’s Lance Armstrong interview? Well, a lot of people are saying that Lance said all the right things in the interview, but he seemed to lack emotion. It's almost like he needed a little something for more energy.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After their interview, Oprah said that Lance Armstrong was honest and contrite about his doping. “Yeah, I’ll believe it when I see it,” said Manti Te’o.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday Joe Biden defended the White House's gun-control initiative by saying that he actually has two guns himself. Then Biden was like, “And I never leave home without 'em.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Hey, this week was the season premiere of “American Idol.” And this year people are able to nominate their talented friends who don't want to audition. Yeah, making someone try out for something they don’t really want — or as Republicans call that, "the Romney plan."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: At the inaugural ball, President Obama was caught doing some very stiff and awkward dance moves. In other words, Obama is already reaching out to Republicans.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Video game-maker Atari has filed for bankruptcy. Atari fans are so upset they're organizing a massive letter-writing campaign to President Reagan.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: For 49 cents McDonald's is giving customers the option to add bacon to any order. Not to be outdone, Olive Garden announced that for 50 cents they will add Italian food to any order.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Lindsay Lohan has turned down an offer to appear on "Dancing With the Stars." Lohan said, "If I want to see the stars, I'll crash into a telephone pole."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: On the news they made a big deal out of the fact that four years ago there were twice as many people at President Obama's first inauguration than there was at this one. That's because four years ago, twice as many people could afford to stay in hotels.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Actually, you know who gave the shortest inauguration speech in history? George Washington. It was only like three minutes long. Well, sure. George Washington couldn't tell a lie.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The CEO of Whole Foods is criticizing Obamacare, once again calling it fascism. He did this before when he called it socialism. And he said the problem with socialism is eventually you run out of other people's money. As opposed to shopping at Whole Foods, where you eventually run out of your own money.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The post office may sue Lance Armstrong for all of the money they spent sponsoring his team. In fact, after all these lawsuits, they say that Lance Armstrong could end up as broke as the post office.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: More than a million people gathered in our nation's capital yesterday, and tens of millions more watched from home to celebrate the first lady's new haircut.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Most people seem to like the hair style, though some Republicans are demanding further cuts. But bangs aren't easy to pull off. As far as I know, the only other women who have done it successfully this decade are Jessica Biel and Justin Bieber.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The president gave a brief but powerful speech. He did not shy away from the many challenges he faces: a massive federal deficit, a conservative majority in the House, an aging population, runaway entitlements, humongous ears.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Steven Tyler defended Beyoncé after she lip-synced at President Obama's inauguration. That's right. Steven said, "I know how she feels. I did the same thing at Harry Truman's inauguration."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Arnold Schwarzenegger signed on to a brand-new "Terminator" film. Now, due to his age, this one features the catchphrase, "I'll be back, right after 'Wheel of Fortune.'"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Japan a senior official is in trouble for saying in order to save money, elderly people should, quote, "Hurry up and die." Of course, if he loses his jobs, he has a bright future writing Mother's Day cards.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Joe Biden made another one of his famous gaffes on camera Monday, saying he was proud to be president of the United States. I guess he forgot he wasn't at home standing in front of the bathroom mirror.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In his inaugural address, President Obama praised the patriots of 1776, and said they were much better than the Patriots of last Sunday.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There's been a lot of criticism over the NFL for not hiring enough minority coaches. And, of course, the NFL is trying to spin it. They said, "What are you talking about? We got two brothers coaching the Super Bowl."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new study out of the University of Wisconsin, as much as 81 percent of people lie on online dating websites. To which Notre Dame's Manti Te'o said, "Now you tell me!"

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Make sure to watch this show tomorrow night, because for the first time in 10 years, Matt Damon will be my guest. You may know Matt as the least-talented member of the cast of "Ocean's 11."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We had a hard time squeezing him into the show since 1993, but tomorrow night it happens. The Garfunkel to Ben Affleck's Simon, Matt Damon will be here.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber just surpassed Lady Gaga as the most followed person on Twitter. Justin now has 33,410,000 — 28,000 more than Lady Gaga. If you want to confuse your grandfather, wake him up right now and scream, "Bieber beat Gaga on Twitter!" He'll think you're possessed.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber reminds me a lot of myself at that age except instead of 33 million followers, it was two followers. Instead of Twitter followers, it was employees of a comic book store following me to make sure I didn't steal anything.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Apple has reported a drop in profits this quarter, a big drop. Experts warned that Apple could run out of money — 600 years from now.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Pentagon has allowed women to serve in combat. Yeah, the hope is that we can now finally defeat the Taliban by giving them the silent treatment.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: North Korea said it will test a rocket that they hope will hit the United States. In other words, watch your back, middle of the Pacific Ocean.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The New Orleans Hornets have announced plans to change their name to the New Orleans Pelicans. Meanwhile, the Lakers want to change their name to the Clippers.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A scary moment at John Kerry's secretary of state confirmation hearing. One of the senators had taken his Ambien the night before and combined with the stuffy room and Kerry's boring speech, he slipped a coma.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday House Speaker John Boehner said that President Obama's focus is to annihilate the Republican Party. Do the Republicans look like they need help from President Obama?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Manti Te'o sat down for an interview with Katie Couric today. Katie asked him at what point did he know something was amiss? My guess is when he found that she wasn't a miss.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Lakers are so bad that the only ring Kobe Bryant is going to see this year is if he goes to see "The Hobbit."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I am your host, Matt Damon. Hey, just for starters, let me ask you guys this. As an audience, is it weird to see a person with actual talent host this show?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I'm very excited to be here. Jimmy has bumped me from his show 1,205 times. For 10 years, every night I wait in that green room. And every night, Kimmel says, "Apologies to Matt Damon, we ran out of time." So I've been waiting for this moment for a long, long time.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Jimmy Kimmel is to late-night talk show hosts what Magic Johnson is to late-night talk show hosts.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Hey Jimmy, did you hear the joke about Lindsay Lohan? Because I have — 1,205 times.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: You might be wondering what makes me qualified to fill in tonight. I think I can do this. How hard can it be to read from cue cards anyway?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Most of the East Coast is experiencing freezing temperatures. It is so cold, Lance Armstrong put his blood in the microwave instead of the refrigerator.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It is so cold, the Lakers could see their own last breath.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new study, as much as 81 percent of people lie on online dating websites. Researchers said they were surprised by how many people actually hate long walks on the beach at sunset.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A man named Peter Robbins, a 56-year-old guy, was the voice of Charlie Brown in the TV specials. He was arrested for stalking. Apparently, Charlie Brown did not have the money to post bail. You know why? He's working for peanuts.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tomorrow is our 10-year anniversary. To commemorate that, the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce gave me a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. They say you haven't made it in Hollywood until your name is permanently displayed where homeless people go to the bathroom.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight Nicki Minaj is here, or else I saw a rainbow in the green room. I am not totally sure.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Interesting fact about Nicki Minaj. She washes her hair in Skittles.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie is getting big-time financial support for his re-election campaign, a fundraiser hosted by Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg. That means the creator of the world's largest social network is raising money for the world's largest governor.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Why does Mark Zuckerberg need to raise a fundraiser worth $12 billion. Write a check and be done with the whole thing.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Secret Service dog died during a fundraiser where Vice President Joe Biden was giving a speech. The dog is being described as "lucky."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Iran has successfully sent a monkey into space. Iran is calling it a huge advancement in not letting women drive.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A fan is suing the San Antonio Spurs because at the game he attended the star players were benched. Meanwhile in L.A., a fan is suing the Lakers because at the game he attended, the star players played.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In a big meeting of the Republican National Committee, Louisiana Governor Bobby Jindal told the GOP to "stop being the stupid party." Then Texas Governor Rick Perry gave the rebuttal.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the New England Journal of Medicine, smokers lose at least one decade off their life compared to nonsmokers. However, the cost of living has gone up, so it's cheaper to buy cigarettes now and die sooner.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new report, it now costs $351,000 to raise a child for 18 years. And you can double that again waiting the next 18 years for that lazy kid to move out of the basement.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Subway has officially apologized to any customer who was served a foot-long sub that didn't measure a foot long. Is that how fat we've gotten in this country now — where we're threatening legal action if our subs are an inch too short?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The price of a stamp goes up a penny today, to 46 cents. To make sure everyone received the news promptly, the U.S. Postal Service announced it by email.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This cent-by-cent thing by the post office is annoying. It's how CBS gives me raises.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Some people think email has ruined the art of letter writing. I disagree. Email has us writing more than ever. But email has ruined the art of licking.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Most stamps these days are self-adhesive. You don't even need to lick them anymore. So now I've got all this extra saliva.

name: David Letterman
monologue: If I seem a little woozy, it's because I'm wearing a pair of those Hillary Clinton double-vision glasses.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night President Obama and Hillary Clinton appeared on “60 Minutes” for their first joint interview. It was a little awkward when they both showed up wearing the same suit.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last week Iran launched a monkey into space, and it actually returned to Earth alive. It was great news for the space program and terrible news for the monkey who thought he’d finally gotten out of Iran.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today is the 200th anniversary of the classic Jane Austen novel “Pride and Prejudice.” Fans of the novel celebrated the way they always do: reading about halfway through and then giving up.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Our 10-year anniversary was Saturday night so this is the first show of our second decade on television. We have had a goal for 10 years, and that is to put on a great show. One day we're going to put on a great show. Until then, we will wait.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The U.S. Postal Service raised the price of a stamp yesterday. Stamps are something that the pilgrims used before we had the Internet.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It will now cost you 46 cents to mail a letter. Some people are complaining about the price even though it's a penny more than the old price. You're not allowed to spend $4 on a cup of coffee and complain about a cent.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In Iran last week, the government successfully launched a live monkey into space. I like that they specified it was a live monkey as if there was a chance they would send a dead monkey into space.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This will be the first Super Bowl ever where the head coaches are brothers. Jackie Harbaugh, their mother, said she would like the game to end in a tie. However, just to be safe, she's got 20 grand on the Ravens.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's being reported that Korean pop star Psy will appear in a Super Bowl commercial and then finally he will go away forever.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This weekend the Pope released a dove from his window only to see it get viciously attacked by a sea gull. So either there is no God or there is a God and he's hilarious.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Ben and Jerry's has announced a new flavor based on a popular TV show. But I'm not sure people want a scoop of Law and Order: Special Victims' Yogurt.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Boy Scouts of America is now considering an end to its longstanding policy of banning gay scouts. How about that? And the girl scouts have a new policy during cookie season. It’s called "Don't ask, just sell."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The whole world is changing. In fact, today, the Olympic Committee said soon they may allow straight male figure skaters.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new poll, 50 percent of Americans think the country is divided. The other 50 percent think it isn't.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to reports from a journal called Psychological Science, people eat more junk food and gain weight during tough economic times. How ironic is that? The biggest obstacle to Michele Obama's war on obesity is President Obama's economic policy.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is a great day for two American icons who share a birthday today. The ruler of Hawaii, Tom Selleck, and the ruler of the rest of the world, Oprah Winfrey.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: What do you buy Oprah Winfrey for her birthday? She has everything — except a successful TV network.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Oprah was in the news recently for her Lance Armstrong interview. It was TV at its most powerful. Armstrong tearfully admitted to using steroids, and Oprah reciprocated by tearfully admitting she once had to pump her own gas.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I greatly respect Oprah because she is from a tough background. Her story's fantastic. She was born dirt poor in the Deep South, then went on to help millions. She was her generation's Honey Boo Boo.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The Super Bowl is on Sunday and both teams are coached by Harbaughs. I'm sick and tired of hearing about Harbaughs. They're now getting their own shows, "The Harbaughs" and "Keeping Up With the Harbaughs."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: “60 Minutes” anchor Steve Kroft is defending Sunday’s interview with President Obama and Hillary Clinton, saying that he didn’t have enough time to ask hard-hitting questions. That would be easier to believe if the name of his show wasn't the amount of time he had.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The president just announced that same-sex couples will be included in his immigration reform bill. When they heard, same-sex couples were like, “You know we're already citizens, right?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today was media day for Super Bowl 47, and both teams shared their predictions for Sunday’s game. It was pretty crazy. One team thinks THEY'RE going to win — but the other team thinks THEY'RE going to win.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Speaking of the Super Bowl, 49ers wide receiver Randy Moss told his teammates that they are in New Orleans on a business trip and they’re not there to have fun. Then he went back to his job: catching a ball for money.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Kim and Kourtney Kardashian are here, and so is Kim's unborn baby. So technically tonight, we have two and a half Kardashians — which is a show that CBS should make immediately.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: According to multiple reports, singers Chris Brown and Frank Ocean got into a tussle over a parking spot on Sunday night. Chris posted a painting on Instagram last night comparing himself to Jesus on the cross. Fighting guys in parking lots: That's so Jesus.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Apple unveiled a new version of the iPad today. This iPad has all the same features as the last iPad plus more memory. It comes with a trash can for you to store all the iPads that you already have.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: At this point, I would like to have Apple just set up a system where we send them a check for $700 every four to six months and they just promise not to make new things.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The head coaches for the Super Bowl are two brothers, Jim and John Harbaugh. Their mother promises that whatever the outcome she is going to call the loser after the game and telling him he was adopted.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: China is launching their own version of the TV show "Friends." Six attractive young people live together in an iPad factory. They get yelled at if they don't work fast enough.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new study has found that leafy greens are the leading cause of food poisoning. In other words, Americans have nothing to worry about.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Zimbabwe's finance minister revealed yesterday that his country has only $217 left in the government Treasury. Today President Obama said, "Stop bragging!"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday President Obama went to Las Vegas and spoke about his new immigration plan. Afterwards he was harshly criticized by the locals for speaking in English.

name: Jay Leno
