monologue: The Senate has overwhelmingly approved John Kerry as the next secretary of state. In his farewell speech today to the Senate, Kerry spoke for 51 minutes. So, apparently he does believe in torture.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: John Kerry is the first white male to hold that job since 1997. So finally middle-aged white guys with gray hair are breaking through the glass ceiling.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new show premiered tonight on the FX network called "The Americans." It's about Russian spies embedded in Washington, D.C., during the Cold War. They're Russian agents who look like us, talk like us, but all of their relationships are based on a big lie. These days that only happens to college football players.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Keri Russell stars in "The Americans." She plays what intelligence services call a "sleeper agent." That's the kind of spy I'd want to be, a sleeper agent. My skill — taking naps in five languages.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don't think I'd make a good spy. All that lying, duplicity, pretending to be someone you're not. No, I prefer good old-fashioned honest Hollywood.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The first episode of this spy show was great. Their mission was to fake a drivers license for a young socialist Kenyan boy living in Hawaii.

name: David Letterman
monologue: More trouble in the world of big-time athletics and steroid use. Turns out now that Alex Rodriguez may have been using performance-enhancing drugs for quite a long time. Calling Oprah!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Super Bowl between the San Francisco 49ers and Baltimore Ravens is this weekend. The big news today is that Ravens linebacker Ray Lewis may have used a performance-enhancing substance called deer antler extract. That explains how Lewis has been preparing for the game — staring into a set of headlights.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A zoo in California announced that its monkey has randomly picked the 49ers to win the Super Bowl. And not surprisingly, the zoo's deer picked Ray Lewis and the Ravens.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: An employee of the U.S. Postal Service is retiring after 44 years without using any of her sick days. Friends describe her as “dedicated,” while co-workers describe her as “that lady who gave me the flu.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We are four days away from the Super Bowl. Super Bowl parties are a lot of fun. It's also a really great way to give your friends all the flu at once.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On Sunday the San Francisco 49ers battle the Baltimore Ravens. A study conducted by a religious research institute says 27 percent of Americans believe God has a hand in determining which team wins. So if you're praying for a new kidney this Sunday, sorry, God has the Ravens and the 49ers.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Of course God cares about football. He created a girlfriend for Manti Te'o out of nothing.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If God really is influencing NFL games, that would mean he isn't in church on Sunday, so why should I go?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Are you thrilled about Super Bowl XLVII? Are you ready to go? The 50-yard line is where you'd want to sit, right? From there you are so close you can smell the deer antler spray.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On Sunday the 49ers take on the Ravens in Super Bowl. Here's what I don't get. They spend a lot of money on the commercials. Shouldn't they run the beer and chip commercials BEFORE the Super Bowl?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I have a lot of eating planned for Sunday. Hot wings. Nachos. Sausages. The inside of my stomach is going to look like a Michelle Obama nightmare.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There's a petition going around asking President Obama to make the day after the Super Bowl a national holiday. That's a good idea. After a long, exhausting day of sitting on the couch watching TV, I need a day off.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The petition has almost 12,000 signatures. Do we need a day off after the Super Bowl? Isn't that kind of disrespectful to our real holidays?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Former Miami Dolphins quarterback Dan Marino has admitted he fathered a child while having an extramarital affair with a CBS production assistant. And today Manti Te'o said, "See, that's why you have imaginary girlfriends."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today Dr. Phil spoke to the guy who was behind the Manti Te'o hoax in a special two-part episode of "Dr. Phil." That's when you know somebody's really screwed up — when Dr. Phil needs two shows to fix him.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Ravens linebacker Ray Lewis once again denied using the banned substance deer antler velvet extract. He says these accusations are nothing more than a trick of the devil. Today Patriots coach Bill Belichick said, "Why am I getting dragged into this? I had nothing to do with it."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In his farewell speech to the Senate this week, John Kerry spoke for 51 minutes about Washington being gridlocked. The cause of the gridlock? Senators giving 51-minute speeches.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Former NFL quarterback Dan Marino has admitted to fathering a secret child back in 2005. I don't know why people are surprised — the Dolphins never gave him good protection.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: To compete with the Super Bowl on Sunday, TNT is airing a marathon of “Law & Order.” Now viewers have two places to see Ray Lewis.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Lance Armstrong has turned down a spot on the new season of “Dancing With the Stars.” Even weirder, Manti Te'o's girlfriend said yes.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A bipartisan group of senators has unveiled a plan that would create a path to citizenship for illegal immigrants. Or as immigrants call that, "a tunnel."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today is the anniversary of the very first daytime soap opera. It was called "These Are My Children," and it premiered in 1949 on NBC. There aren't many soap operas left. They're going away, like newspapers and compact discs and Lance Armstrong fans.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: With Facebook, now you can watch any person's life like it's a soap opera, assuming it's a real person. Am I right, college football players with fake girlfriends?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Growing up in Scotland, I watched the soap opera "Coronation Street." It was on TV over there for 50 years — like Larry King in this country.

name: David Letterman
monologue: I'm very excited about the Super Bowl, and how can you not be? It's the Ravens-Niners. I mean, it makes you want to run out and buy a team scarf.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Beyoncé finally admitted that she did lip sync the national anthem during the inauguration. Now Donald Trump is claiming that since she did lip sync, President Obama is not legally president. He said it invalidated the whole thing.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It’s going to be quite the halftime show at the Super Bowl. Beyoncé is going to perform her smash hit "Single Ladies." then Dan Marino will come out and sing "Love Child."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: That’s the big story that broke this week — former Miami Dolphins quarterback Dan Marino fathered a secret love child back in 2005. Obviously, his wife is not too happy. In fact, he could become the first NFL player to sustain more concussions AFTER he retired.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I love this story; the state of Washington is now looking for a marijuana consultant now that marijuana is legal up there. I think this is one of those green jobs President Obama is always talking about.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Super Bowl is on Sunday, and both teams are already in New Orleans getting ready for the big game. And during their practice yesterday, the 49ers actually piped in fake crowd noise to simulate the loud conditions for Sunday’s game. Yeah, fake crowd noise — or as Manti Te’o put it, “They sounded real to me!”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This is interesting. A new survey found that 27 percent of Americans think God plays a role in who wins the Super Bowl. Then Tim Tebow was like, “No. No, he doesn't.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Here’s some news out of Washington. Today, President Obama honored more than 20 researchers for their contributions to science and technology. Unfortunately, it was overshadowed by the football game — or as those researchers put it, “Man, high school never ends, does it?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The director of Jewish outreach for the White House announced that he is stepping down. He says it’s time to move on, while his mother says he's still a real catch and other presidents would be lucky to have him.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Congratulations to the Baltimore Ravens. And congratulations to Ravens coach John Harbaugh. He was named the game's most valuable Harbaugh.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I lost $200 on last night's Super Bowl. I bet on electricity. I thought that was a sure-fire bet. It never goes out during the Super Bowl.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: During the Super Bowl there was a 35-minute blackout. Afterwards Lindsay Lohan said, "So that wasn't just me."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: After the game, Baltimore quarterback Joe Flacco announced his wife is pregnant. Apparently he went against NFL rules and impregnated the woman that he is married to.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: U.S. employers just added 157,000 jobs to the economy. Of course, most of those were for backup dancers for Beyoncé.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: So deer antler spray works. How about that! Congratulations to the Baltimore Ravens, the new Super Bowl champs. But how about that blackout? That’s what happens when Beyoncé actually sings live.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: When the lights first went out, out of force of habit Ray Lewis started running from security.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congratulations to coach Harbaugh — and to coach Harbaugh, better luck next time.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad said he would like to become the first Iranian to go into space. And today Israel said, "Flight's on us! No problem. We've got everything covered."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night was one of the highest rated Super Bowls ever, with 108 million people watching. This year’s game added $430 million to the New Orleans economy — apparently none of which was used to pay the electric bill.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The lights in the Superdome went out for 33 minutes at the beginning of the third quarter. The 49ers were just standing around on the field, not knowing what to do — and then the blackout happened.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The lights went out in the third quarter, which is weird because normally I don't experience a blackout until after a Super Bowl party.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Saturday Punxsutawney Phil did not see his shadow. And you know what that means — nothing, because that's not how weather works.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Excuse me if I seem tired. I just got back from New Orleans. I have a pretty bad gumbo hangover.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: What a Super Bowl that was. During the first quarter, Will Ferrell was sitting a few rows in front of me. Channing Tatum was over here and Jay-Z was over there. There were so many important people that I kept waiting for someone to tell me to leave.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There was a power outage that is still not officially explained. When the lights first went out, it was kind of scary. They thought they'd pop back on, and we'd see one of announcers slumped over with a knife in the back.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I was with a bunch of CBS people when the lights went out. They were freaking out because when it gets dark around CBS, Dan Marino gets a little frisky.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: What a kooky Super Bowl it was. Strange stories keep coming out. During the Ravens' celebration, it was revealed the Super Bowl trophy went missing. Coach John Harbaugh called his mother and said, "Make Jim give it back. Make him give it back now!"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: After the game, Super Bowl quarterback Joe Flacco announced his wife's pregnant. In response, Dan Marino said, "I can explain."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Justice Department memo claims that President Obama has the right to order the assassination of an American anywhere in the world. Isn't that crazy? In a related story, Donald Trump has gone into hiding.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Scientists have found the remains of England's King Richard III under a parking lot. Unfortunately, they couldn't find his ticket. So he'll be charged the day rate.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: People are still trying to figure out why the power went out Sunday at the Super Bowl. Today they found out the reason. Turns out China cut off the electricity for nonpayment of our bill.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: CBS is now facing a possible fine because Ravens quarterback Joe Flacco was overheard dropping the F-bomb on the air. CBS is arguing they could not have foreseen this happening — you know, someone on the Ravens breaking the law who isn't Ray Lewis.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In Great Britain the bones of King Richard III, who was killed in 1485, have been discovered under a parking lot. And you know how he died? Fighting over a parking space.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new traffic study, it takes longer to get to work in Washington, D.C., than any other city in the country. On the other hand, they don't do any work once they get there, so it’s pretty much a wash.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Canadians got rid of their penny today. There are no more one-cent coins in Canada. So now if you're in Canada, and say to someone "a penny for your thoughts," that is now illegal. They will put you in jail.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Prison in Canada is probably fun. The prisoners are so polite, they ask you nicely before they stab you, "Where would you like to be stabbed?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Canadians have a one-dollar coin. They call it the loonie. Here in America, the loonie is what we call Mel Gibson.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Remember the expression, "Find a penny, pick it up, all day long you'll have good luck?" Well, what are they supposed to do in Canada now? Without the penny, everyone in Canada is now doomed to a luck-free life of clean air, civilized social discourse, and free health insurance.

name: David Letterman
monologue: They had the Super Bowl blackout and now we're learning that they also lost the Super Bowl trophy. The Lombardi Trophy — they give you that giant silver football, and now it's missing. So that explains the blackout. It was a heist!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The White House is warning North Korea that it will face significant consequences if it moves forward with a new round of nuclear tests. Not only that — it’s also warning South Korea that it will face serious consequences if Psy makes another ad for pistachios.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Pakistan is opening an amusement park and a zoo in the same town where the raid on Osama Bin Laden took place. The zoo is pretty cool, but I’ve heard you won't be able to see the seals until it's too late.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Department of Justice is trying to block Anheuser-Busch from buying Corona. So they did what everyone else does — got their older brother to buy it for them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A French tattoo artist met a young lady and less than 24 hours after they met, she allowed him to tattoo his name on her face. That means she either really loves him or really hates her parents.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They say they're planning to get married. Once you get a name tattooed on your face, you might as well give it a shot.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On the bright side, if the marriage doesn't work out . . . Well, actually there is no bright side, so good luck.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Next year's Super Bowl is already in the news. It takes place in New Jersey. The NFL says it wants to prevent another blackout. This one involves keeping Chris Christie away from his microwave.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Beyonce's publicist is busy trying to get seven unflattering photos of Beyoncé removed from the Internet. The publicist is described by friends as hard working and new to the Internet.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A member of Congress is criticizing Steven Spielberg after he discovered parts of the movie "Lincoln" are historically inaccurate — particularly the scene where Lincoln dies in the mouth of a great white shark.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A new study says that working fewer hours can slow global warming. So you know what that means? President Obama's economic policy is also his climate change policy.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This is kind of disturbing. The Justice Department has concluded that the president can order drone strikes on American citizens. And today, Rush Limbaugh came out in favor of Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The U.S. Postal Service announced they are ending Saturday delivery of the mail. Now if you have a problem and you want to complain, you can email them at USPS.com.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Some Democrats in Congress are now trying to change the marijuana laws, making it legal so it can be taxed and increase revenue. Is that what the government's come down to now? We're selling drugs to pay off our debts? When did Uncle Sam become Scarface?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is a great day for fans of Monopoly — the game that introduced generations of kids to the concept of mortgage debt.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today Monopoly added a new game piece: the cat. The new piece was chosen after weeks of online voting. Is that a surprise? Whenever there's a vote for something on the Internet, the cat always wins.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: To make room for a cat, Monopoly's dropping one of the old game pieces. So the iron is going away. Take it from me. You should never put a cat and an iron together. No matter how wrinkly the cat is.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You know what I never understood? — why they sell Ouija boards in the "board game" section. I don't think that is really a game, is it? Nothing says "family fun" like communicating with the dead.

name: David Letterman
monologue: After the Super Bowl game, the winning team, the Baltimore Ravens, lost the trophy. But that's not the only thing. The 49ers lost the trophy in the first quarter.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: PETA is criticizing Beyoncé for the leather costume she wore during the Super Bowl halftime show. Or as the ball that got thrown and kicked for three solid hours put it, “Yeah, THAT'S the leather you should be worried about.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It was just revealed that the Federal Reserve was hacked on Sunday. It’s pretty serious. In fact, they say the hackers could've made off with as much as negative $14 trillion.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After thousands of people voted on Facebook, Monopoly is replacing its iron game piece with a cat. And if that surprises you, remember — these are the people who had enough free time to vote on a new Monopoly game piece.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un recently got a smart phone. And you can tell it’s a smart phone because today it left North Korea.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A major announcement from the makers of Monopoly today. They're retiring their least-popular game piece — the iron. It will not be a part of the game from now on. They have to keep updating these poor games to keep them fresh. Candy Land just changed its name to Fresh Organic Vegetable Land.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Monopoly let people in 120 countries vote through Facebook. The choices for a new game piece were a diamond ring, a little robot, helicopter, guitar, and the winner which was a cat. This goes to show you if you let the Internet decide, it will always choose cats.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I hope this doesn't cause a problem with the little Scottie dog. I can't have animals chasing each other on my board.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Now what do you do with the Monopoly iron? There are still ways to enjoy it. You can use it as a paperweight for Post-it notes.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This is crazy. The justice department is saying that President Obama can order drone strikes on American citizens, that he can do that. In a related story, this is the last Obama joke I'm ever doing on this show.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: When asked about gay marriage, Donald Trump said, "It's not my thing." Trump went on to say marriage is a sacred bond between a man and a woman he will replace in six years.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Home Depot plans to hire 80,000 new employees. The CEO said, "If your skills are avoiding customers and hiding in the break room, give us a call."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: More bad news for A-Rod. It looks like there is more evidence linking Alex Rodriguez to a Miami doctor who prescribed performance-enhancing drugs. Here's how bad it is for A-Rod. He is now favored to win this year's Tour de France.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Several states are now looking into the possibility of taxing marijuana as a source of revenue. That is so typical of the government, isn't it? Trying to squeeze blood from a stoner.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad said he wants to become the first Iranian to go into outer space. He wants to study the effects of anti-gravity on anti-Semitism.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Monopoly is getting a big makeover. They want to make the Monopoly game more modern and bring it up to date to reflect our current culture. Like, in the new version of Monopoly, the banker never goes to jail.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new report by economists lists the world's most expensive cities. It turns out the most expensive city is Tokyo, Japan. Tokyo unveiled their new tourism slogan today. Their slogan is: "Tokyo: We'll leave you brokeo."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'd love to go to Tokyo. It's not just expensive; it's also one of the most crowded cities in the world. A city full of people with thick wallets? It makes me pine for the days when I was a Dickensian pickpocket.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Paris finished number eight. The people in France were very annoyed today. Then they heard about the list. And then they said, "Just do not raise the price of soft cheese."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Oslo, Norway, is number five on the list. Apparently it is very expensive to buy umlauts. That's what they have in Norway. Umlauts are those dots they put above vowels.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's Fashion Week in New York City. And by the way, if you're keeping track, this is Fashion Week XLVII.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Northeast is bracing for a snowstorm this weekend. Some forecasts say it will be only two inches while others predict 30 inches. When asked why they couldn’t make a better prediction, meteorologists were like, "Uh, we're meteorologists."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, they’re saying New York could receive up to 12 inches of snow this weekend. Or as Subway calls it: 11 inches.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Supporters of Hillary Clinton have already started a 2016 super PAC on her behalf called “Ready for Hillary.” And more cautious Democratic supporters have started another super PAC called "Bracing for Biden.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night runners from around the world competed in the annual race to the top of the Empire State Building. But there's already a scandal brewing. It turns out one of the competitors tested positive for elevator.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Dr. Phil is with us tonight — and make no mistake, if any of you are pretending to be a football player's imaginary girlfriend, he will find you and you will confess.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This weekend a couple from Connecticut will have the longest marriage ever recorded in the U.S. They got married more than 80 years ago. You see how long a marriage can last if you don't meet on "The Bachelor"?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They got married Nov. 25, 1932. They bonded over their mutual love of music, travel, and not dying of polio.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They said the secret to their long-lasting marriage is love, compromise, and the fact that neither one of them has been able to hear a word the other one has said in more than 30 years.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Happy Chinese New Year. It's the Year of the Snake. Here's how dumb I am. All day long on my checks I've been writing "Year of the Dragon."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a leaked report from an upcoming U.N. study on climate change, solar activity may play a greater role in global warming than previously thought. The sun may be involved in global warming. It's always the last place you'd think, isn’t it?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Time magazine is reporting that since Al Gore sold his TV network to Al Jazeera, he is now worth more money than Mitt Romney. Can you believe that? They're still publishing Time magazine.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Geologists say in a hundred million years, Asia and America will smash into each other and become one big super-continent. How ironic is that? Just about the time when we have our loan to China paid off, we ARE China.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Someone recently threw a shoe at Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad. They say throwing a shoe is the supreme mark of disrespect in the Arab world. I would have to go with beheading. I would rather have a shoe hit my head than have my head hit my shoes.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This big winter storm could dump three feet of snow on the East Coast and knock out power to 24 million people. This storm is really a big deal. In fact, the Weather Channel is expecting totals of 12 to 20 viewers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It was just announced that a third "Night at the Museum" movie is coming out. You can tell they're running out of ideas because it's called, “Night at the Museum 3: Maybe Go to the Museum During the Day?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Florida was arrested for drunk driving on a motorized shopping cart at a Walmart. He led cops on a chase that reached 90 aisles per hour.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a big weekend over in Asia. Sunday night is Chinese New Year. So let me be first to say, "Gung hay fat choy." That means "Best wishes for a prosperous new year." Either that or I just threatened to invade Taiwan.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Astrology is derived from the root word "astrologia" — a Latin word that means "crap."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don't put much stock in astrology. It's all made up. But then, I'm a Taurus so I would think that.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Astrology is very different from "astronomy." Astronomers spend years in school and know a lot of facts and stuff about science. Astrologers just spout mystical mumbo jumbo that sounds good but isn't true. It's like the difference between Dr. Oz and Dr. Phil.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Pope Benedict announced he's retiring. This is a pretty dramatic change. It means he will go from wearing a robe all day to wearing a robe all day.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Some self-portraits painted by former President George W. Bush have leaked onto the Internet. Bush said, "If you like these, wait until you see my self-portraits of other people."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Navy SEAL responsible for killing Osama bin Laden says he's having trouble finding work. My advice: Charge $10 per high five. He will be a billionaire by the weekend.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Pope is resigning! I guess he took that Notre Dame loss to Alabama a lot harder than people thought.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Pope said he was stepping down at age 85 because he could no longer handle the job physically. To which Lance Armstrong said, "I've got some stuff that can help you with that."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Pope said that at age 85 he cannot physically go on. Meanwhile, Hugh Hefner is going to be 87 and he just married a 26-year-old. So much for that celibate lifestyle!

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Reportedly, President Obama's speech will focus on jobs. Hopefully he'll explain to us why anybody in Congress still has one.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The big news today is from the Vatican. The Pope is resigning. He's hanging up his giant hat.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Pope will be replaced, of course. When one Pope goes, another one popes up in his place.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: CBS announced today the Pope will be replaced by Ashton Kutcher.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Actually, when the voting's done, the cardinals burn their ballots. People wait outside the Sistine Chapel to see what color the smoke is. If it's white smoke, they've agreed on a Pope. If it's black smoke, no decision's been made. If it's green smoke, Willie Nelson has somehow gotten into the Sistine Chapel.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Anybody here for the annual Westminster Dog Show? It's an important event and quite a competition — and they say that it is usually a pretty good indicator of the Academy Awards.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today, Pope Benedict surprised everyone and announced that he is stepping down at the end of the month. Or as God put it, “Well, at least he gave me two weeks’ notice.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Pope Benedict is resigning. And you know what that means: Hillary in 2013?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night was the Grammy Awards, and Gotye won Record of the Year. Parents were like, “Who’s Gotye?” while their kids were like, “What’s a record?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tomorrow President Obama gives his annual State of the Union address. If you're not familiar, the State of the Union is where the president faces Congress and asks them to work together and fix America's problems and Congress says, “No.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Did you watch the Grammys last night? The Grammy Awards celebrate the albums and songs we download illegally.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Pope announced he is resigning. He doesn't feel he is strong enough to continue with his papal duties. What will he do for work now? He could be the most overqualified Walmart greeter of all time.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Pope will step down on February 28, which means he gave Jesus two weeks' notice.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Vatican was struck by lightning after the Pope announced he was retiring. That really happened. Sounds like someone's not handling the breakup well.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama gave his State of the Union address tonight. The rebuttal will be given by Marco Rubio. Or as he's known in the Republican Party, "our black guy."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Lean Cuisine has recalled some of their frozen dinners because they may contain shards of glass. It's too bad because people were really losing weight with those.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Atlanta Braves baseball team has decided to stop using their screaming Indian logo because they say it's offensive. Unfortunately, the logo they've replaced it with is an Asian kid getting into Harvard.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Earlier tonight President Obama gave his State of the Union address. At every State of the Union address the president is introduced by some guy who walks in and says, “Mr. Speaker, the president of the United States!" If we're really serious about reducing the size of government, start with that guy. What does he work, one day a year?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This is a real break with tradition. When the president walked into the chamber, instead of "Hail to the Chief," they played “Hey, Big Spender.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Pope is resigning. I just hope it’s not steroids.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Pope Benedict says he is resigning because of physical problems. Apparently it’s an old football injury from throwing all those Hail Marys.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight is Mardi Gras. I'll lose control and do things I'll regret tomorrow, trading my dignity for a few small trinkets. Then when I'm done doing this show, I'll go and celebrate Mardi Gras.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Mardi Gras is only the fourth-biggest drinking holiday of the year. The top three are St. Patrick's Day, Cinco de Mayo, and Tuesdays at Mel Gibson's.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Years ago Mardi Gras started as a Catholic celebration before Lent. So now we know why Pope Benedict quit. He just wanted to get in one last party.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Mardi Gras is French for "Fat Tuesday." Unfortunately, we're all so politically correct now, Fat Tuesday is now officially known as "Big-Boned Day After Monday."

name: David Letterman
monologue: Anybody in town for the Westminster Kennel Club's dog show? All of the dogs competing in the competition stay at the same motel. Have you been there? Oh, what a flea bag!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: With the Pope retiring, more than 100 cardinals will sequester themselves in the Sistine Chapel to choose the next Pope. They’ll send out white smoke if they've chosen somebody, black smoke if they haven't chosen somebody, and a text message when they find out that it's 2013.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Do you know why the White House scheduled the State of the Union address for Lincoln's birthday instead of Washington's birthday? Well, it's because Washington was famous for saying, "I cannot tell a lie."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi said on Fox News Sunday that it's a false argument to say that we have a spending problem. You know something? I think she may be right. I think what we actually have is a "You don't have a clue" problem.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tomorrow is the first day of Lent, when Catholics begin fasting for 40 days. Some Catholics will give up chocolate, some Catholics will give up alcohol, and one Catholic is giving up “being Pope.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: President Obama made his fifth State of the Union address tonight. Traditionally, following the State of the Union address, the opposition party rebuts what the president said. They don't know what the president is going to say, but they know they won't like it.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Following the State of the Union speech, Republicans gave their rebuttal. But yesterday Democrats held a press conference to deliver a pre-rebuttal to the Republicans' rebuttal. Democrats decided to pre-emptively rebut their rebuttal.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: So Democrats gave a speech, responding to a speech no one had ever heard, which itself was in response to a speech no one had ever heard — which I think is the plot to "Inception," isn't it?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Sports Illustrated's swimsuit edition came out today. This is the 50th anniversary of the swimsuit edition. The first one was published in 1964. And after 50 years, they still are yet to sell a single swimsuit.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This Valentine's Day, White Castle restaurants are going to offer a discount to couples who dine there. Yeah, because there's no better way to tell a woman you love her than to pay even less at a White Castle.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Vatican said that as soon as the Pope resigns, he will no longer be infallible. The Vatican said it's the same thing that happened to Oprah.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Republican response to President Obama's State of the Union address was given by Senator Marco Rubio. It's just one more example of rich white guys getting a Hispanic to do a job they don't want to do.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Experts are predicting that the success of Amazon is going to lead to the closure of many RadioShacks. When reached for comment, the CEO of RadioShack said, "Wait, there are still RadioShacks?"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama wants Congress to increase the minimum wage. Believe me, when it comes to doing the minimum for their wage, Congress knows what it’s talking about.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The most impressive thing about President Obama's State of the Union speech last night was that he did the whole thing without a single drink of water.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Be honest. How many of you never heard of Marco Rubio until last night? How many thought Marco Rubio was a game you played in a pool with the kids?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As you know, the Pope is resigning. He said he feels there's just no room for advancement. It's a dead-end job.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Last night while the president was speaking, the Westminster Dog Show wrapped up. The dog show and the State of the Union address are very different, of course. One's a lot of yapping and prancing and sniffing. And the other is the dog show.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If you're a dog, winning at Westminster is like an actor winning an Oscar, a tennis player winning at Wimbledon, or an NBA player winning a Kardashian. It's a big deal!

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Last night's Best in Show was a little affenpinscher. It's a German dog. The affenpinscher's name is Banana Joe. Banana Joe's being treated like royalty today in New York. This afternoon, he went to a steakhouse. Then he gets to spend the rest of the week serving as Donald Trump's toupee.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The dog is going to be in a Broadway play. I'm not sure which one. Maybe "Fiddler on the Rrrufff."

name: David Letterman
monologue: Welcome to "The Late Show," ladies and gentlemen. It's the best place to be if you're giving up entertainment for Lent.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The trend this year is couples saying they don’t need to get each other anything for Valentine’s Day, because they love each other EVERY day. I think that’s sweet, but to all the guys out there watching, I just want to say it’s a trap!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Before the State of the Union address last night, President Obama did an exploding fist bump with Republican Senator Mark Kirk. Which really goes to show you — it doesn't matter if they're black or white, Republican or Democrat, politicians are really awkward.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama also gave House Speaker John Boehner a thumbs-up before the start of his State of the Union address. Or as Boehner put it, "Beats the finger I usually get!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A college student in Pennsylvania is suing her school for the C+ she got in a class. She said, “I'm suing whoever's responsible for this!” And her professor said, “Don't you mean WHOMEVER?”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: President Obama made the annual State of the Union address last night. Then Florida Senator Marco Rubio rebutted for the GOP. He said you can't have a middle class without the rich. He's right. Just like you need "Biggie" fries to have regular-sized fries.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: While Rubio covered a lot in his State of the Union rebuttal, everyone seems to be focused on him grabbing his water bottle. That's what you get when you eat a whole bag of pretzels before a speech.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: How about the way Rubio never takes his eyes off the camera when he's reaching for the water. It's like, "Drop the gun on the floor. Put down the gun."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: But what a night for Poland Spring water. You cannot buy that kind of product placement. At least I hope you can't buy it, but in Washington, who knows?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I want to say if any of you are alone today, it could be worse. You could be on a cruise ship right now — the most miserable cruise in the history of the world.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new poll, a majority of women want their man to propose on Valentine's Day. And the same poll revealed men would rather propose on April Fool's Day.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Lent officially began yesterday. Do you know what the Lakers are giving up for Lent? The playoffs.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For those of you who are not Catholic, the idea of Lent is you're supposed to give up something so you can experience suffering. Or you could just go on a Carnival Cruise.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: My heart goes out to those poor passengers stuck on that floating bedpan in the Gulf of Mexico. For four days, 4,000 people stuck on a ship with foul odors, the toilets aren't working, and there's long lines for food. And here's the worst part. The karaoke machine is still working.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Donald Trump called the Beyoncé Super Bowl halftime show "inappropriate" and "a national scandal." Apparently, it lacked the quiet dignity of Gary Busey and Meat Loaf screaming at each other on "The Apprentice."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The biggest gifts on Valentine's Day are flowers and chocolate. Because what says true love better than murdering a plant and then making someone fat?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: For me, the best Valentine's Day gifts don't cost anything because they come straight from the heart. That's why I composed a special Valentine's Day poem for you, my audience. "Roses are red, love's but a fable. I'm really sorry you can't afford cable."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Valentine's Day is celebrated a little differently here in L.A. Nobody eats chocolate because of the calories, so people give each other tofu-shaped boxes filled with bean curd. Then they fantasize about what their Pilates instructor would be like if he was straight.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's day five of that Carnival Cruise trip. You know you're on a bad cruise if you wake up on day two, you look out your little porthole, and you see the captain and the crew in a lifeboat.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today was Valentine's Day. And if you just found that out, that's why you're in trouble.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Taylor Swift's ex-boyfriend Connor Kennedy was arrested yesterday for handcuffing himself to the White House gate to bring attention to climate change. He's bummed about the arrest, but he's glad to attach himself to something that won't write a song about him.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Scientists have discovered a species of fish that surrounds itself with uglier fish in order to look more attractive. However, scientists could not identify which sorority it belongs to.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Georgia was arrested for stealing a Krispy Kreme doughnut truck and leading police on a high-speed chase. The police charged him with one count of grand theft irony.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I hear from a lot of women who swear they don't care about Valentine's Day. In my experience, you can tell how much someone cares about Valentine's Day by how much they tell you they don't care about Valentine's Day.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A survey by the national retail foundation said that some people even give their fish Valentine's Day gifts. A good way to tell that you've lost your mind is if you give your fish a Valentine's Day gift.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The song "Gangnam Style" has been named best song for kids to listen to while brushing their teeth. However, it is the worst song to listen to during everything else.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Personally, I think most parents would rather have all their kids' teeth fall out than hear that song one more time.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Yoko Ono turns 80 years old today. People sometimes say or suggest that Yoko broke up the Beatles. Now that she's 80 the only thing she's breaking up is bingo games.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday President Obama played golf in Florida with Tiger Woods. Well, you thought Michelle got mad when Barack ate a cheeseburger. She told him, “No hanging out with Tiger afterwards. You come right home.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A top geneticist at Stanford says human intelligence is declining. You know what that means? We are seeing Congress at its smartest and most effective right now.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We're learning more about the Pope's condition. The Vatican announced that Pope Benedict hit his head during his March 2012 trip to Mexico. In fact, right after that, the Pope said he's sworn off spring break forever.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The big question: Who's going to replace the Pope? Where's the new Pope going to come from? I think they should check out Whole Foods. I've seen plenty of holier-than-thou people walking around that place.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The White House’s immigration plan was leaked over the weekend, and Florida Senator Marco Rubio is already calling it “dead on arrival.” That incidentally is also Florida's state motto.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, NBA legend Michael Jordan turned 50 years old. Scottie Pippen actually helped him blow out his candles, but nobody seemed to notice.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that humans are slowly getting less intelligent. I was going to read the whole study, but I’ll just wait for the movie.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A judge in California announced that Kim Kardashian’s divorce trial from Kris Humphries will begin on May 6. The pre-show on E! will begin on March 1.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Happy Presidents Day. Today we celebrate an American tradition — immigrants working on your day off.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Most stores are open on Presidents Day. What better way to celebrate our presidents than by offering a sale on tires? Yes, four score and 20 years ago, our forefathers got two-for-one on steel-belted radials.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You can tell how important a president was based on his monument. Lincoln was important because his monument shows him sitting in a chair looking serious. And George Washington got an even better one — a monument shaped like a giant middle finger pointed at England.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: People sometimes forget that George Washington was very rich, had a pony tail, and grew hemp on his farm. He was America's original Willie Nelson.

name: David Letterman
monologue: I have a special treat for the audience here tonight. Save your ticket stubs, all right? Somebody's going on a Carnival Cruise!

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Italian press is reporting that the next Pope could be the cardinal from Boston. If he gets the job, he'll be the first Pope to make you kiss his 2007 World Series ring.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A top food manufacturer is reporting that some of their pasta meals contain horse meat. So if I were you, I'd stay away from the "Rigatoni, My Little Pony."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Massachusetts, a dad promised his daughter $200 if she would get off Facebook, which is ridiculous, because every parent knows the best way to get a kid off of Facebook is to join Facebook.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday Burger King's official Twitter account got hacked. When asked for comment, people who follow Burger King on twitter were too embarrassed to identify themselves.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You knew this was going to happen. Dozens and dozens of lawsuits have already been filed against Carnival Cruise Lines. Well, if you thought the ship was filthy, slimy, and disgusting, wait until these lawyers get involved.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Over the weekend, President Obama played golf with Tiger Woods. Tiger said the president was a very good golfer for a guy who plays only five days a week.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Actually, you know what the president's handicap is? He doesn't understand economics.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Actually, Tiger Woods gave the president some very valuable tips. The most valuable one? Erase all of your text messages.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In a new interview, Bill Gates said he’s not satisfied with the level of innovation at Microsoft. He would’ve said more, but he had to hang up the phone so his assistant could use the Internet.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today North Korea announced that its tourism has steadily increased over the last 10 years. You can tell they're trying to boost tourism with their new slogan, “North Korea: You'll Never Want to Leave, Because We Won't Let You.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Reader's Digest has filed for bankruptcy, just one week after the Pope resigned. Man, my grandmother hasn't been this depressed since Michael Bublé got married.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Lawmakers in Montana are considering a bill that would make it legal for people to take road kill home and use it as food. When Montana residents heard that, they were like, “Wait, that was illegal?”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for a bunch of thieves in Belgium. They got away with more than $50 million worth of pure, uncut diamonds. This diamond heist is the biggest robbery ever pulled off at an airport if you don't count them charging $25 to check a bag.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The thieves got away in a minivan. Police are blaming the Serbian crime syndicate. In a minivan? I think it's diabolical soccer moms.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: When I hear about a crime like this, part of me thinks it's kind of cool. But it's not right. Stealing is never cool. They took something without it being funny. This wasn't "Ocean's 11." These guys just came up and took someone's hard-earned money without being at all funny or cool. So it's more like "Ocean's 12."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I've got the latest Oscar buzz. Many Pakistanis are saying that "Zero Dark Thirty" contains factual errors. Then someone explained to the Pakistanis that being directed by a woman does not qualify as a factual error.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's been reported that after the Pope retires he'll receive a relatively small pension. So don't be surprised to see an elderly German on the sidewalk with a sign that reads "Will Pope for food."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's being reported that the next Pope could be a cardinal from Boston. That means the Vatican may soon endorse birth control but only for Yankee fans.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Former Senator Pete Domenici of New Mexico revealed that while in office he fathered a child with the daughter of another senator, who was a friend of his. He cheated on his wife with the daughter of another senator and they had a baby. When did the Senate become "The Jerry Springer Show"?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Domenici is defending himself by saying that he is no better or worse than the next guy. And he’s right, because you know who the next guy was? John Edwards.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The former San Diego mayor, Maureen O'Connor, told federal prosecutors she went broke after gambling away more than a billion dollars she inherited from her late husband at casinos playing video poker. But to be fair, at one point, she was up 300 bucks.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Former Chicago Congressman Jesse Jackson, Jr. pled guilty to misusing hundreds of thousands of dollars of campaign funds for personal use, including buying a $43,000 Rolex watch. How ironic is that? All that money on a watch, and now he's going to wind up doing time.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for the city of Los Angeles. We've become the first city to synchronize all of our traffic lights. This will make it easier to get downtown and watch the Lakers lose.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today the Bulgarian prime minister, Boyko Borisov, stepped down. He's stepping down like the Pope, but with a funnier name and a smaller hat.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm not sure who'll replace Boyko Borisov. My money's on Ashton Kutcher.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Robert Plant told Australia's version of "60 Minutes" that he'd be willing to reform Led Zeppelin. When I heard this, I said, "What? Australia has a "60 Minutes?"

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's still winter here in New York City. It's 28 and bitter, like Lindsay Lohan.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I guess to appeal to a younger audience, this year's Academy Awards are just being referred to as the Oscars. And to appeal to an even younger audience, they're spelling Oscar with a "z" — and backwards in crayon.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There's talk that the White House may fine China for its recent cyber attacks on American companies. The fine could total in the millions of dollars, which is great because we could really use that money to pay back China.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In an effort to reduce its debt, the U.S. Postal Service is launching its own line of clothing and accessories. They come in one size, embarrasses all.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A woman in New York has been arrested for hiring strippers to perform at her son's 16th birthday party. Even Dina and Michael Lohan were like, "That's a really bad parenting choice."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Florida Atlantic University announced a new corporate sponsor for their football stadium. It happens to be America's second largest operator of for-profit prisons. I guess they figured a lot of the athletes end up in prison anyway.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The school, Florida Atlantic University, says very little will change. The only change they're making is that hot dogs will now go for two packs of cigarettes.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In November, Colorado voted to legalize the recreational use of marijuana. Currently, only Colorado residents can purchase marijuana in the state. But they may open it up to nonresidents too. The new state slogan is "Come for the legal marijuana, stay because you forgot to leave."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Oscars are this Sunday. Everyone will be tuning in to the telecast, and "Lincoln" is one of the big favorites. Of course, like Lincoln, most people won't stick around for the whole show.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This year producers have dropped the name Academy Awards. They're just calling it "the Oscars," since that's how people refer to it. And for the same reason, the Tonys are being renamed "the Gay Olympics."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: At this year's show, instead of attractive models handing out the Oscars, six college film students have been chosen to hand them out. So now every winning actor will receive a trophy and a crappy screenplay.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Fox news host Bill O'Reilly is writing a new book about the killing of Jesus. It will be the first time Jesus' death is blamed on Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Scientists at the University of Maryland say they have found a chemical that causes women to talk more than men. It's called red wine.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the new study, women talk almost three times as much as men. Well, you know why? Because they know men aren't listening the first two times.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Officials in Oklahoma now say it is possible that a 65-year-old man recently died of spontaneous combustion. This is not an isolated case. I think the last guy we saw go down in flames was Congressman Jesse Jackson, Jr.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The price of gasoline went up again in Los Angeles for the 34th straight day in a row. Gas is so expensive that NBC can’t even afford to drive this network into the ground anymore.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Someone hacked into Donald Trump's Twitter account. It's filled with offensive nonsense and stupid jokes. Then it got hacked.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The U.S. Postal Service is launching a fashion line. Some people think it is a bad idea. But I think if the post office gets behind something, it'll eventually turn out to be a good idea. Just look at sponsoring Lance Armstrong.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This postal service clothing line gets my stamp of approval.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Folks are excited about the Academy Awards on Sunday. Ann Hathaway will probably win. She's won so many awards she's being tested for banned substances.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It was just announced that President Obama will speak at Ohio State’s graduation in May. The president has a lot in common with those students. He’s currently in his fifth year and swamped with debt.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Officials in Pakistan are complaining that the movie “Zero Dark Thirty” contains a lot of errors. They were like, “The movie makes Pakistan out to be a hellish wasteland of corruption and intolerance — but in real life, it’s WAY worse than that.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After the success of his book, “Killing Lincoln,” Bill O’Reilly is coming out with a new book called “Killing Jesus.” He's going to be disappointed when he finds out there's already a book about that.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Researchers have discovered that a chemical in the brain causes women to talk more than men. It’s called “Chardonnay.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Kim Kardashian said her boyfriend Kanye West has taught her a lot about privacy. She said that to a writer who was printing it in a magazine.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Oscars are airing live this Sunday. The ceremony takes place right across the street from us. I know this sounds like a cliché, but it is an honor just to be located across the street from them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There's an interesting contest going on in the best actress category. Both the youngest and oldest actresses are competing. The one is only 9, which makes your kid's performance as tree number two in the school play seem a little less impressive, right?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Excited about the Academy Awards? It will be a lot of people you've never met thanking people you've never heard of.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Al-Qaida has issued a list of 22 ways that al-Qaida members can avoid being killed by U.S. drones. Here’s a good one: Don't join al-Qaida.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A huge snowstorm has now hit 18 states. In fact, it is so cold that former Chicago Congressman Jesse Jackson Jr. had his hands in his own pockets.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The price of gas is so high, Lindsay Lohan is now forced to choose between drinking or driving. She can't afford both.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The very first Woolworth's five-and-dime opened on this day in 1879. They went out of business in 1997. You know why? They were nickel and dimed to death.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: We have first lady Michelle Obama on the show tonight! I plan to ask her some serious questions, like, "Do you think that I could pull off bangs?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: That’s right, Michelle Obama is here! Everyone at the White House is excited. In fact, I heard they’re even letting Biden stay up to watch.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Michelle Obama is actually here tonight to talk about her fitness initiative “Let’s Move.” Meanwhile, Chris Christie will be on next week to talk about his initiative "Let's Sit."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A 104-year-old woman is complaining that she can’t put her real age on Facebook because the birthdates only go back as far as 1910. Facebook said it will solve the problem by either adding the dates or just waiting it out.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Oscars are on Sunday. So is the Daytona 500. It will be a great day for gay NASCAR fans.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Oscars are a perfect representation of Hollywood Because Hollywood releases hundreds of movies a year, and three are good. The Oscars is 800 minutes long, and three are entertaining.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If you haven't seen "Life of Pi," you really must. And then tell me what it's about.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This is my theory about the Oscar. If you're in an action movie or comedy, you're not worthy. But if you put on Elizabethan trousers and act serious, that's it. You're a great actor.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Anybody see the Academy Awards last night? The show last night was so long that by the middle of the show the audience was begging Daniel Day-Lewis to free them.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Welcome to the show. I'm Conan O'Brien — or perhaps I'm Daniel Day-Lewis in his greatest role yet.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night a toilet flooded the lobby where the Oscars show was being held. The show won an Oscar for best portrayal of a Carnival cruise.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Big winner last night was "Life of Pi," a story of a young man who wakes up in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orangutan, and tiger, which oddly enough, is also the plot of "The Hangover 3."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: South Korea's first female president was sworn in. Meanwhile, North Korea said, "We're just going to stick with men named Kim."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Life of Pi took home four Oscars. It's about a young boy trapped at sea on a small boat with a man-eating tiger. Yet with all that, it’s still a better way to travel than a Carnival cruise.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Jennifer Lawrence won for best actress and worst stuntwoman.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There was one glaring omission in the “In memoriam” reel: Lindsay Lohan's career. Didn’t that die last year?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Pizzas in Denmark have been discovered with horse meat. Pizzas with horse meat. How fast does THAT get delivered to your house?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night's Academy Awards lasted about three hours and 40 minutes. Even Jennifer Lawrence's dress was like, “That's way too long.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The entire cast of “Les Miserables” performed a song from the movie, featuring Russell Crowe. Or as the cast of “Zero Dark Thirty” put it, “Now this is torture.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The company that owns Olive Garden announced that its revenue has dropped 5 percent in the last quarter. Which explains their new promotion: limited bread sticks.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Last night the biggest stars in the world squeezed into the theater across the street. But it's nice to see our neighborhood getting back to abnormal.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I don't know why the Oscars needs a best actor and actress category. You don't separate best director and best directress.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Daniel Day-Lewis now has one Oscar for each of his names.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Monday night I usually update you on the number of times "amazing" is said on "The Bachelor." Tonight was 22. We also collected every "amazing" that was uttered on or near the Oscars' red carpet. That's 101. There were as many "amazings" as there were Dalmatians. Can someone in the world please send us more adjectives. We need them.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: People still are talking about the Oscars — at least my comedy writers are.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Somebody noticed that none of the Oscar winners thanked God. To add insult to injury, at his last sermon, the same day, the Pope thanked Harvey Weinstein and Meryl Streep.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's being reported that next season, "Downton Abbey" will feature its first black character. The producers hope this will lead to "Downton Abbey's" first black viewer.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Longevity scientists said that compared to last century, 72 is the new 30. However, they said that Larry King is still very, very old.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Researchers in Germany now say that human longevity has improved so rapidly over the past century that 72 is the new 30. That is bad news for parents. You'll never get the kids out of the house now. "Dad, I'm only 50. That's, like, 17."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A storm dumped 17 inches of snow on Amarillo, Texas, yesterday. It was really confusing for people sneaking over the border. They thought they'd gone all the way to Canada.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In a White House briefing, Homeland Security Secretary Janet Napolitano warned that sequestration would affect border security. Her remarks raised eyebrows in Washington and got big laughs in Mexico.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Doesn't sequestration sound like some kind of side effect from a bad medicine?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today they announced the new cast of "Dancing With the Stars." Guess who they got this year? Ingo Rademacher. I can't believe they got him or her.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The show also got Dorothy Hamill and Andy Dick. I know Dorothy Hamill and Andy Dick. One is the prancing ice princess who stole my heart in Montreal and the other one is Dorothy Hamill.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The White House officially released portraits of the White House gang. You can all see the portrait of Hillary Clinton. It will be on next month's cover of the "Sports Illustrated" pants suit issue.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Manti Te’o was apparently one of the slowest linebackers to run the 40-yard dash at the NFL's scouting combine yesterday. You can tell he took it to heart because today he spent three hours on an imaginary Stairmaster.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Kim Kardashian said that she and Kanye West want to get married, but they’re not going to rush it. And also because they have to wait until Kim is actually divorced.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Beyoncé has actually designed her own pair of sneakers. The sneakers are made of stingray, ostrich, cat hair, crocodile, and anaconda skins. So if you want a pair of those sneakers, you'd better order it now while species last.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The online college, the University of Phoenix, could lose its license because of questionable billing policies. Which makes sense when you find out they got their accounting degree from the University of Phoenix.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The cast of "Duck Dynasty" is here with us today. Some of our camera guys are so excited, they wore camouflage to work today.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Our originally scheduled music guest, Morrissey, cancelled. He is a staunch animal rights activist. He said he "couldn't morally be on a show where cast members of 'Duck Dynasty' will also be guests." While I respect his stance, there's a very good reason I didn't dump the "Duck Dynasty" guys for Morrissey. It's because they have guns and Morrissey doesn't.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This morning on "Good Morning America," ABC unveiled the new cast of "Dancing With the Stars." It was a who's who of who needs money.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: TLC announced that "Here Comes Honey Boo Boo" will soon be on the air in Australia, Latin America, and the Netherlands. Personally, I'm not in favor of exporting our reality shows to other countries. Deporting our reality shows, yes. But exporting, no.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's tax season. Has anybody been to their accountant? I used to go in with a short form and be out of there in 10 minutes. Well, now I went to the guy and the first thing he says to me when I walk into the office is, "Are you sure you weren't tailed?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today the Pope made his last public appearance. That is, until the new season of "Dancing With the Stars."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Pope said that the past few years have been very difficult for the church and at times he felt that "the lord seemed to be asleep." When asked for comment the lord said, "You try staying awake through a Latin mass."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Big international controversy about the Oscars. When they aired in Iran, the Iranian government digitally added sleeves to Michelle Obama's gown. They also altered the video so that Jennifer Lawrence is now deliberately tripped by the Israelis.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hundreds of employees of Weight Watchers are complaining about the company's low wages. The employees said, "They're paying us peanuts. By the way, they're only six points per serving."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This horse meat scandal just keeps growing. And it isn't happening only in Europe. According to a new report, donkey meat has been found in hamburgers in South Africa. Consumers said when they were eating the burgers, they sensed something was wrong but they couldn't quite pin a tail on it.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In fact, in South Africa more than two-thirds of the meat products tested contained undeclared ingredients. Or as we call that in this country, a hot dog.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For the first time ever, NBC finished fifth in the ratings. Fifth! If we were a racehorse in England, we'd be a Burger King Whopper now.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama said this week that after four years as president, "you realize all the mistakes you've made." so apparently he DOES watch Fox News.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: TLC has renewed its reality show, "Breaking Amish," for a second season. Parents of those kids would be so proud if they had any idea what that meant.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Americans are bracing for this thing called the sequester — when $85 billion will be cut from almost every part of the budget. So teachers, meat inspectors, and TSA workers will all be affected. So if you're someone who teaches people how to keep bad meat off airplanes, this is a tough weekend.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In his final speech before resigning, Pope Benedict said that he is not abandoning the Catholic Church. Like most Catholics, he'll be back for Christmas and Easter.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Italy just had its elections. There's no winner. There's no government in Italy. People over there have been running wild through the streets, waving their hands in the air. And then they heard about the elections.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: All this turmoil, of course, is nothing new in Italy. Until the late 19th century it was just a bunch of feuding states. And the women had tiny mustaches. It was like the Kardashians.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Italian women are some of the most beautiful in the world. This is why the Vatican is in Italy. If a man can walk across Italy and retain his celibacy, he's got what it takes to be a priest — or an interior decorator.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A lot of Americans can't believe how crazy the politics are in Italy. A comedian might become prime minister. We would never do that in America. A pro wrestler? Sure. Stuart Smalley from "Saturday Night Live"? Yeah.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today was Pope Benedict's last day at work. Don't be sad. All the other cardinals are buying him shots at the Vatican Applebee's.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Pope spoke to 100 cardinals and said, "Among you is the future Pope." And then he said, "Now enter The Octagon." They're going to fight it out with holy relics.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: We are 24 hours away from massive across-the-board budget cuts. If the cuts go into effect, major airports could face delays up to 90 minutes — or as JetBlue calls it, an on-time departure.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: These budget cuts are serious. It could negatively affect water and sewage services. In other words, all of America is about to embark on a Carnival cruise.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Pope Benedict has become the first Pope to retire in 600 years. You have to wonder what a Pope does in retirement. I heard a rumor he already cashed in his 401(k).

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: My favorite part about today was when the Pope left the Vatican, he left in a helicopter — just like "The Bachelor."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Did you know the Pope is a helicopter pilot? He has a helicopter pilot's license, but never got a driver's license. He can fly a helicopter, but he can't drive a car — just like Jesus before him.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: As you know, the Pope stepped down today. There’s a lot of cardinals running for this Pope position. Some of the slogans are pretty catchy. My favorite: “Yes, We Vati-can.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We are now in the middle of Lent. The most common thing people are giving up for Lent this year? Watching NBC.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For the first time in history, NBC is fifth in the ratings. We are now behind the Spanish language channel Univision. As we call that here in Los Angeles, "Cinco de Ratings."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The ratings are so bad that today NBC called Manti Te'o to bring in some imaginary viewers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Pope Benedict officially retired today. People are actually placing bets on who the next Pope will be. At least that's what I heard during my fantasy Pope draft.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday the Senate confirmed Jack Lew to be President Obama's new Treasury Secretary. Unfortunately, if the sequester happens he'll have to be let go due to budget cuts.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, with automatic spending cuts scheduled for tomorrow, 300 illegal immigrants have been released from jail in Arizona. Or as officials put it, "Catch ya later."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The NFL is investigating reports that several teams have asked players about their sexual orientation before drafting them. They've been asking questions like, "Do you have a girlfriend?" and "Is she real?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: According to a new study, Hawaii is the happiest place in America to live. And I thought it was just a great place to pretend you were born in.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Pope Benedict is officially retired. Apparently there was some last-minute tension at the Vatican because they wouldn't give the Pope his security deposit back.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: He left glue on the walls from his Def Leppard posters.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In the next few weeks, a group will assemble in the Vatican. Their job is to select a new Pope. The group will consist of 120 top cardinals and Simon Cowell. He'll say, "Your Pope-ing is rubbish. You're not going to the Vatican."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Welcome sequestration survivors. Congress did not reach an agreement and Congresswoman Maxine Waters said 170 million jobs could be lost. There are only 155 million workers in America. Are you beginning to understand why we're in this situation in the first place?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The cuts have already begun. Just yesterday, the Pope got laid off.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: At this point, we have no idea who the next Pope will be. How about Mitt Romney? He's not doing anything.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Gas is so expensive, today I saw Bill O'Reilly carpooling with Bill Maher.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, Groupon fired the founder and CEO of the company. Yeah, he could tell something was up because today's deal was his parking space.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that at least 50 percent of all pets in the United States are overweight. Veterinarians plan to treat this as a serious problem, or as fat pets put it, "Did you say treat?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Kim Kardashian said that couples should be together for at least six months before they decide to get married. And they should stay married for at least six days before they decide to get divorced.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that pessimistic people actually live longer than optimists, which would be great news for pessimists if they believed in great news.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There's a big movie out today. It's called "The Last Exorcism Part 2." How can it be called "The Last Exorcism Part 2"? By definition, a movie called "last anything" can't have a sequel. It's not possible. Unless — unless Hollywood is run by profit-hungry liars.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In the first "Last Exorcist," a young girl gets possessed by Satan. The priest performs an exorcism to try and cast him out. I guess in part two, the devil returns because he forgot his wallet or something.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Some people think I got this show because I made a deal with the devil. It's true, actually. Nine years ago, the devil promised me great fame and untold wealth in exchange for my soul. But I broke the deal. Now I'm condemned to this place for all eternity.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If you're scheduling an exorcism, you need to make sure someone's actually possessed. If a young woman looks sickly and pale and vomits all the time, she may just be an actress.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The search for a Pope has begun. The cardinals are all starting to gather together in Rome right now. It's like a "Star Trek" convention but less celibate.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Dennis Rodman visited North Korea. Rodman came back and said President Obama should call North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. But President Obama was busy discussing Iran's nuclear capabilities with Scottie Pippen.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today Kenya is holding elections for the first time since 2007. It's getting nasty. Each presidential candidate is accusing the others of being born in Kenya.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Horse meat was found in some products at Taco Bell. Which explains Taco Bell's new slogan, "You can lead a horse to Taco Bell. We will take it from there."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A new season of Donald Trump's "Celebrity Apprentice" started last night. It includes Steven Baldwin and others who are celebrities — in the way that "I Can't Believe It's not Butter" is butter.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The show has Dennis Rodman, our new ambassador to North Korea. Dennis is back home safely after visiting the North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un. And apparently they hit it off. Rodman called him a friend for life. But he said the same thing when he married Carmen Electra.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: President Obama's half-brother is running for office in Kenya. He's a political novice who was born and raised in Africa. I don't know much about the half-brother.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Many people don't realize Chicago is the home of two major cookie companies — Keebler and Nabisco. They are intense rivals. No one will forget the Great Keebler Elf Massacre of 1934.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The massacre was horrible. Hats and pointy shoes everywhere. Three elves were found face-down in a pool of their own fudge.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Police described the scene as delicious.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Cardinals from all over the world are gathering in Rome to select the next Pope. You can watch the whole process on "Vatican's Got Talent."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The top choice to be the new Pope could be a Canadian. If elected Pope, his first act is to grant sainthood to Wayne Gretzky.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Researchers say they have figured out exactly what caused the crash of the Hindenburg. The culprit: a time-traveling Lindsay Lohan.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night Justin Bieber outraged fans by showing up two hours late for his concert. In fact, I've got to tell you, I almost left.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber made a lot of fans angry in London last night. He had a concert that was supposed to start at 8:30 but Justin didn't get out there until 10:30.
