Half the audience was kids on a school night, which means they were late getting home and had to go straight to bed without brushing their teeth, and the British really can't afford to miss a night of teeth brushing.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: How can you ever be late for anything in London? They have a huge clock right in the middle of the town.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We have a lot of fat dogs in this country, which makes sense. We give them treats if they sit and stay; it's the worst thing you can do. We're enablers.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is Election Day. We're going for a new mayor. At one point, our mayor was hanging around with Charlie Sheen. Everyone was wondering: Why would the most powerful guy in the city, a role model, and pillar of our community, want to hang around with the mayor?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's been almost a decade since we've had a new mayor. It's starting to seem like the mayor of Los Angeles was one of those jobs for life. Like Supreme Court judge, or host of "The Tonight Show."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: One candidate is named Kevin James. Not the actor. This Kevin James is a former lawyer. And a gay Republican. Kevin James the actor and Kevin James the politician are very different, of course. One is the king of queens. And the other . . . well.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: L.A. has never had a female mayor, a Jewish mayor, or gay mayor. I'd be really impressed if a candidate was all three. This is who I want.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A major snowstorm has hit the East Coast. In Washington, D.C., everything ground to a halt — and then the snowstorm hit.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Due to budget cuts, all tours of the White House have been canceled indefinitely. When he heard, Joe Biden said, "Now I'll never see it."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Lawmakers in Hawaii passed a new law called the Steven Tyler Act. Basically the law gives men the right to gradually morph into old women.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Wrangler is coming out with a pair of jeans that claims to fight cellulite as you wear them. Finally a pair of jeans your boyfriend can say you look fat in, but not for long.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They just passed something in Hawaii called the Steven Tyler Act. It's a sweeping piece of legislation that says you must wear a scarf at all times.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Actually it's designed to protect celebrities from paparazzi by making it illegal to take unwanted pictures or video of them in private to sell for profit. No offense, but isn't every photo of Steven Tyler an unwanted photo?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Doesn't the Steven Tyler Act sound like something we would create to protect ourselves from Steven Tyler?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The world's cardinals are meeting to prepare for the conclave that will choose the new Pope. The rumor is they already have a candidate selected and they're just waiting on the results of the urine test to come back.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Former president of Venezuela, Hugo Chavez, died yesterday. Sean Penn actually went down to Venezuela and met Chavez a few times. He's a polarizing figure that a lot of Americans really don't like. Chavez was, too.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today Chavez is being mourned all over South America. If he were here today, I'm sure he'd say, "Don't cry for me, Argentina."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The people of Venezuela aren't sure who'll replace Hugo Chavez. CBS suggested Ashton Kutcher.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: South America was the birthplace of the Incan civilization. The Incans were sort of like the Mayans, except they didn't go around falsely predicting the end of the world.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama took a group of Republicans to dinner last night. And at the end of the meal, the president personally picked up the tab. Afterwards, Republicans said "Typical Democrat. Spend, spend, spend."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: North Korea has threatened to nuke the United States. Which begs the question, what the hell did Dennis Rodman say over there?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last week horse meat was covered in IKEA's meat balls. This morning it was discovered in IKEA's hot dogs. This is making me think twice about taking my family to dinner at a furniture store.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Scientists have recently created a robot that can bake cookies. And by scientists I mean two stoned kids who work at RadioShack.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Mark Zuckerberg unveiled a new Facebook news feed today. It promises to revolutionize the way we see pictures of our friends' feet on vacation.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Zuckerberg said that with this improved news feed Facebook hopes to give the world "the best personalized newspaper that we can." He's playing it a little bit loose with the word "newspaper." A newspaper tells us that North Korea is threatening to attack us, not that your friend went to Panera Bread this afternoon.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg has a new crusade. He wants people to stop listening to loud music in their headphones. Wasn't that the plot of "Footloose"?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Mayor Bloomberg must throw the worst parties ever. How long before he just starts showing up on street corners and whacking the hot dogs out of people's hands?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: All tours of the White House have been canceled due to budget concerns. Don't worry, there's another way get into the White House if you don't belong. Fake your birth certificate.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight there's a comet. A comet making the closest approach ever to earth. Now is it really a comet? Or is it one of President Obama's drones?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: They say the comet is visible to the naked eye. The naked eye? My eyes are always naked. Do people wear eye clothes now?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There are a lot of people watching the comet tonight. I'm surprised that advertisers aren't sponsoring it.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There is a big movie out today: "Oz the Great and Powerful." It's a prequel to "The Wizard of Oz." I'm thinking this is a little risky making a prequel to that movie. It is an American icon. That's like the French making a prequel to the Statue of Liberty.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I hope this movie isn't some hipster version of "The Wizard of Oz" where the Tin Man gets taken to the recycling center and the Scarecrow is exchanged for a sparkly vampire.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: James Franco plays the man who eventually becomes "Oz." He's a conman who tries to trick gullible people into thinking he has special talents. I don't know what he does in the movie.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Franco's performance is already generating Oscar talk. As in people saying, "Hey, isn't that the guy who ruined the Oscars a couple of years ago?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I feel bad for James Franco, being remembered as the guy who ruined the Oscars. Halfway through he realized that the audience hated him, and then he just gave up.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Today the groggiest day of the year because of monkeying with our clocks. But the biggest waste of time about resetting your clocks is trying to line up that little hole in the clock with the nail in your wall.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Obamas' dog Bo still travels with his own motorcade. After hearing this, Vice President Joe Biden said "Wait, why am I still taking the train?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: After tours of the White House were canceled due to budget cuts, Donald Trump offered to pay for them. All he's asking is they rename it the Trump White House and Casino.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Cardinals are starting to vote on a new Pope. Apparently for someone to become Pope, they have to receive 77 of the votes from the cardinals. They also have to win Ohio and Florida.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The former mayor of Detroit has been convicted of racketeering and extortion charges. The sentence is pretty hard. He has to serve another term as mayor of Detroit.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In Venezuela they held the funeral for dictator Hugo Chavez. Many world leaders were there: Iran sent their president, Mahmoud Ahmadinejad; Cuba sent Raul Castro; and we sent Dennis Rodman.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Now that Hugo Chavez is gone, the crazy nut-ball dictator void will be filled by North Korea's Kim Jong Un. It's nice of him to step in and fill that.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A new poll indicates that President Obama is no better than George W. Bush at protecting civil liberties. In fact, the pollster had some follow-up questions but split when he saw a drone fly overhead.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In England, gas is $10 a gallon. In fact, gas is so high in England that people have stopped eating horses and started riding them again.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tomorrow the College of Cardinals will gather at the Vatican, where they will vote four times a day until they select a new Pope. And if that doesn't work, they'll move onto the tiebreaker: “Rock, Bible, Scissors.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: “Oz the Great and Powerful” made $80 million at the box office in its opening weekend. It tells the story of a con artist dealing with a bunch of witches. Or as he's called these days, "The Bachelor."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It was announced that China is opening its own Disneyland, which Disney says will be both "authentically Disney and distinctly Chinese." Which explains why the parents of Huey, Duey, and Louie had to pick just one.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Thanks to daylight saving time, we lost an hour this weekend. If you're watching this show, you're about to lose another hour.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Everyone is talking about is these Google glasses. When I say everybody, I mean me.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Google glasses are the next stage in the evolution of eyewear. Wear these and record everything you see. It's like you have a memory!

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: People are already worried about radiation from cellphones. So why not make a device that you can put next to your eyes all day?

name: David Letterman
monologue: With the selection process going on for the new Pope, there's a lot of papal trivial. For example, did you know that no Pope has ever in the history of the church been elected without carrying Ohio?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Everyone's waiting to find out who the new Pope will be. Did you know the Pope gets to choose his own name? Experts say the number one choice for the new Pope's name is John and the number two choice is Leo. A distant third: Jayden.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The cardinals at the Vatican will release black smoke if they don't reach a decision and white smoke if they do. And blue smoke means they're working on the Vatican Oldsmobile.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The cardinals are in seclusion until they choose a new Pope, and they don't have access to the Internet. This is to keep them from being exposed to any press rumors and any "Walking Dead" spoilers.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A company is developing drones that can be used to pick up and develop items for customers. So if you see a drone, someone in the neighborhood either joined al-Qaida or Netflix.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The latest rumor, according to the Italian press, is that Pope Benedict did not retire. They say he was forced out by NBC.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A judge overturned Mayor Bloomberg's ban on large sugary drinks. The judge made his decision after testimony from a prominent physician. I believe it was a Dr. Pepper, if I'm not mistaken.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: McDonald's announced they are dropping its fruit and walnut salad from the menu. The two people who go to McDonald's for fruit and walnuts are really upset about this.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to reports, Saudi Arabia is considering dropping public beheadings because of a shortage of government swordsmen. You don't want amateurs to cut people's heads off because that could be barbaric.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today was the first day that cardinals started voting for the new Pope. Everyone has already voted except the cardinal from Florida, who's still trying to figure out how the ballots work.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In accordance with Vatican tradition, the cardinals in the papal conclave will release white smoke when a Pope is chosen. The practice was started by those two ancient leaders, Cardinal Cheech and Cardinal Chong.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There are reports that Joe Biden will handle more foreign policy matters during President Obama's second term. Though you know it's bad when world leaders are like, "Can you just send Dennis Rodman instead?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A 106-year-old woman in Ohio just received her high school diploma after 88 years. She may even go to college, but only if she gets that volleyball scholarship.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The nation of Iran is threatening to sue the makers of the movie "Argo." They say the movie was an unrealistic portrayal of their country. You can't do that! That would be like Scotland suing over the movie "Shrek."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: As of yet no Pope has been elected. Experts say the thick smoke seen pouring out of the Vatican indicates either the first ballot was a deadlock or that Willie Nelson has arrived for the vote.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A New York City judge struck down a proposed law to ban sodas larger than 16 ounces. I think Mayor Bloomberg should spend his time trying to improve stuff like education. New York needs a better education system if kids didn't figure out they could get around the 16-ounce soda ban by simply purchasing two 12-ounce sodas.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: How would the government try to enforce something like that? It's not like Obama's got a secret fleet of robotic aircraft circling over, watching everything people do with little cameras.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The big news is the new Pope. His name is Jorge Mario Bergoglio. If you're saying to yourself, "Boy, that name sounds familiar," you're right. For seven years he was the ace reliever for the Yankees.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: We have a new Pope. The Vatican has chosen the first ever Argentinean Pope. So once again, a bunch of old white guys got a Hispanic to do a job they didn't want to do.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The new Pope has chosen the name Pope Francis. A little advice for the Vatican: If you really want to make a strong stand against homosexuality, don't go with a girl's name.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Moscow, '90s action star Steven Seagal hung out with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The meeting lasted two hours and then went straight to DVD.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: McDonald's has introduced a yoke-free Egg McMuffin has only 260 calories. After hearing this, every McDonald's customer said, "Sweet, I'll have six of them."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We have a new Pope! He is Cardinal Jorge Mario Bergoglio. He is from Argentina. Tens of millions of Hispanics celebrated. And that was just here in L.A.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: People all over the world celebrated differently. In Rome they prayed. In Dublin, they sang. In New York, they chugged super-sized Mountain Dews.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: But their job is not done yet. The 115 cardinals are going to stay in Rome a few extra days and try to find a replacement for Joy Behar on “The View.”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We’re learning more about the dead Venezuelan dictator Hugo Chavez. It seems he amassed about $2 billion in personal fortune while president — and he was a socialist. Imagine how rich he could have been if he didn’t believe in redistribution of wealth.

name: Jimmy Fallon

monologue: U.S. officials have revealed that America is ready to launch cyber attacks of its own. We have a program that can totally crash someone's computer. It's called "Microsoft Windows."

monologue: It's the Ides of March. That means today you have to be extra careful to avoid a disaster. If you're watching this show, you clearly didn't heed the warnings.

monologue: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March. He was stabbed in the back by someone he thought was his friend. It was like he worked in show business.

monologue: Have you heard about this alleged feud that I'm having with NBC? I think it’s going to be OK. To make it up to me, they are sending my wife and me on an all-expenses-paid Carnival cruise.

monologue: Usually when you hear Harvard students and upset, it's because someone ended a sentence with a preposition.

monologue: There's no way I'd make my dog take an IQ test. He's already busy enough doing my taxes.

monologue: Pope Francis met former Pope Benedict over the weekend at a Vatican retreat. They spent the weekend in prayer trying to figure out exactly what marshmallow Peeps have to do with Easter.

monologue: Infectious disease experts are now warning people around the world to stay away from bats. Do you have to tell people that, really? You know which bats are not dangerous? The ones the Chicago Cubs use.

monologue: Some say being a poet is a dying profession. It's like being a video store clerk, or a blackberry salesman, or a late-night talk-show host.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama held a press conference today. He said he still wants to close the Guantanamo Bay prison facility, but he doesn't know how to do it. He should do what he always does. Declare it a small business and tax it out of existence.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday Tim Tebow was cut by the New York Jets, although today he did sign with somebody: ChristianMingle.com. So good for him.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There's now talk here in California of letting noncitizens serve on juries. The bad news: If you're ever on trial for underpaying your nanny, you could get the death penalty.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Happy birthday to Willie Nelson. He's 80 years old. God bless him. Willie has finally reached the age he's looked for the last 30 years.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: New reports say New York Governor Andrew Cuomo will not run for president in 2016 if Hillary Clinton does. In a statement, Hillary said that she appreciates the decision and the support. Then she added, “Because I would crush him.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: New York City is testing a new plan that would make the average school day longer by over two hours. Parents haven't commented on the plan yet because they're busy high fiving everyone they know.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that the air quality in New York City subways is actually the same quality as the air in New York streets. Even crazier, that's supposed to be good news.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that certain fish use sign language to communicate. Apparently they have a sign for everything — except for “big metal hook.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In the Netherlands today there is much celebration as they swear in a new king. William is the first Dutch king in more than 120 years. Basically he's king of a bunch of pot and windmills.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: What do you actually do as king of the Netherlands? They don't seem to have any laws to enforce.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: King of the Netherlands sounds like something you would call a friend who got too stoned.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Martha Stewart has signed up with Match.com, the dating thing. And she's been taking dating tips from the CEO of Match.com. And I thought, "Wait a minute. That's insider dating."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: More news keeps coming out about Jason Collins, the NBA player who revealed he's gay. It turns out he's a free agent looking for someone to sign him. He's got some interest from Chicago. Not the Bulls, the Broadway musical.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Domino's Pizza customers can now order a pizza and watch it being made online. A spokesperson for Domino's said this way their customers can see exactly what went wrong.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Chicago Cubs are considering leaving Wrigley Field if they don't get a bigger scoreboard. Then someone reminded the Cubs for the amount of runs they get, they don't need a scoreboard.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new study reveals that up to 41 percent of college graduates are working in jobs that don't require a degree. By the way, I'm one of them.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Martha Stewart told Matt Lauer on the "Today" show that she is looking for a man on Match.com. You would think it'd be easy for someone like Martha Stewart, but it is not. It's tough for her. A lot of guys don't want to get involved with an ex-con.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In baseball news, the Chicago Cubs said they will move if improvements are not made to Wrigley Field. And today Wrigley Field said it will move if improvements are not made to the Chicago Cubs.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The U.S. government apparently spent millions of dollars in cash to fund various dubious government projects in Afghanistan — including solar panels and wind farms that never work. No, I'm sorry. That's what we did here. I had it backwards.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Researchers now believe the first settlers who settled in America, in Jamestown, resorted to cannibalism. The first settlers ate each other. Good thing that didn’t catch on. That would have changed Thanksgiving, don’t you think?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Vice President Joe Biden’s plane is apparently stuck in Arizona because of problems with its engine. Officials say they're trying to fix it as fast as they can. But Obama was like, “No rush.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: An elementary school here in New York City has become the first school in the country to serve only vegetarian food. Apparently the school board wants to give kids a head start in being difficult at restaurants.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: That’s right. A school is serving only vegetarian foods, like tofu. Now when bullies say, “Give me your lunch money,” students are like, “Here, take it.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The FDA has just ruled that girls as young as 15 can now obtain the contraceptive Plan B without a prescription. Before that, most teenagers’ Plan B was getting a show on MTV.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Martha Stewart is on the prowl. Martha Stewart is now on Match.com. She's 71, and says she's looking for a man between 55 and 70 and is not looking to have kids. What 70-year-old woman is looking to have kids?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Martha says she's a fan of the symphony, opera, and rap. I like that. She spent three months in prison and all of a sudden she's Tupac listening to rap.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: What kind of rap does Martha Stewart like? Gift wrap.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We ran all her information and we determined the best match for Martha. We looked to find someone who's single, successful, likes kids, age appropriate, athletic, and knows what is it's like to go through a scandal. I think we were able to find the right man. Arnold Schwarzenegger.

name: David Letterman
monologue: I was walking to work today and I ran into Pat Sajak, the host of "Wheel of Fortune." We had one of those funny little coincidences that you don't expect. At exactly the same time, Pat said to me and I said to Pat, "Is your show still on?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today former Pope Benedict is moving back into the Vatican. He is going to be mad when he sees that Pope Francis took down his Metallica posters.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: That's right. Two Popes now under one roof. Can you believe that? Yeah, they're just one-half Pope away from being a sitcom on CBS.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yahoo has put out a list of five dying careers, which includes reporter and insurance underwriter. The only one they forgot is Yahoo employee.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The owner of an ice cream truck named Snow Cone Joe was arrested for allegedly stalking his rival truck, called Mr. Ding-a-Ling. It's being called the saddest turf war ever.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama is in Mexico. He'll be on hand to celebrate Mexico's economic successes over the last few years. See, that’s how it works now. If President Obama wants to celebrate an economic success, he actually has to leave the country.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: While in Mexico, President Obama plans to promote his immigration policy. Is that really necessary? Seems the last place you have to promote immigration is Mexico. I think they've got it down. That's like going to San Francisco to promote gay marriage.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday, President Obama met with Treasury Secretary Jack Lew in the White House. The treasury secretary meets once a month with the president — and he meets twice a month with the Chinese president.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A New York City real estate company will give a 15 percent raise to any employee who gets the company logo tattooed on his body. Actually, I got the NBC logo tattooed on my body, but it’s just a temporary tattoo. It will be gone next spring.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad is in trouble. He was arrested this week for threatening to expose some sensitive government secrets. And you can tell it’s serious. His bail was set at 200 goats.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: That’s right. Mahmoud Ahmadinejad was arrested. He claimed that he had evidence that their elections were rigged. When authorities asked him to prove it, he was like, "Uh, I'm president, aren't I?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Jeff Foxworthy and Larry the Cable Guy are teaming up to build a new theme park in Alabama. You can tell because the sign on the roller coaster says, “You must be this shirtless to go on this ride.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new survey found that 49 percent of Americans think movie trailers give too much away about the plot. Especially that one trailer that starts with, "In a world where Bruce Willis is dead the whole time . . ."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new study finally explains what's wrong with young people. Researchers have proven that young people are greedy and more materialistic. The study is in something called a newspaper. It's like a blog. But everything in it is from yesterday.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The study refers to young people as millennials. It says they perform poorly in job interviews. There's nothing worse than a bad interview — realizing a person sitting across from you has checked out and just doesn't care. Ask any of my guests on this show. They'll tell you. It's a terrible experience.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I get annoyed when people do studies like this. They break society into different groups. Then they assign everyone in the group with the same set of characteristics. I can't stand that kind of small-minded thinking. Then again, I'm a Taurus. We're all like that.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don't consider myself a baby boomer. To me, that means hippies. What do I have in common with a hippie? I never went to Woodstock. I never wore flowers in my hair. I never took huge amounts of LSD and then battled killer ducks who I swear were out to kill me. All right, I did the last one but I didn't think it was groovy.

name: David Letterman
monologue: This weekend, on Saturday, is the Kentucky Derby. I think it's held in one of the Southern states.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You people sound like you’re all ready for Cinco de Mayo. I hate it when every holiday gets so politicized. Like today, the NRA said piñatas should be allowed to carry guns to defend themselves.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It is wildfire season here in Southern California; there’s a big wildfire about 20 miles from the studio. They are calling it the Lindsay Lohan fire. It’s not as hot as it used to be, but it’s still way out of control.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You ever notice that all these rehab facilities have names like Next Steps, Morningside, and Promises? Lindsay Lohan needs a place called Miracles.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It was so hot today in Burbank that Reese Witherspoon was sitting in a cop car just for the air conditioning.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This is a big weekend. On Saturday you've got the Kentucky Derby, and this Sunday is Cinco de Mayo. And Monday is the day you wake up and wonder why you're wearing a saddle.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday President Obama warned Congress not to delay the immigration reform bill. You can tell he's getting tough because if they keep delaying the bill, he says he might even warn them again.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man managed to hitchhike 100,000 miles without spending any money on travel. He says he did it all with a friendly smile, a positive attitude, and an ax.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There's a new summer camp for adults where using cellphones and computers is banned. The camp has an interesting name: North Korea.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Iron Man 3 opened today. In this one, Iron Man goes up against his most dangerous enemy yet: rust.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I like the fact that Iron Man doesn't keep his identity a secret. Everyone knows he's Tony Stark. So he's free to be himself. He won't let a uniform hide who he truly is. Like the NBA's Jason Collins.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Iron Man, of course, is played by Robert Downey Jr. He is fantastic. But he's saying that this will be the last time he plays Iron Man. That's Hollywood code for, "Hey movie studio. Pony up."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Robert Downey Jr.'s girlfriend is played by Gwyneth Paltrow. She plays the character of Pepper Potts. How'd they come up with that name? An executive said, "Give me a condiment and a cooking utensil."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: PETA is really upset at Chris Christie for killing a spider in front of a group of school children. Governor Christie said, "If PETA is upset by that, they do not want to know what I had for lunch today."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new report, Al Gore now has more money than Mitt Romney. Gore said Mitt and I are living proof that if you're a boring white guy, anything is possible.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Catholic bishop from Massachusetts was arrested for drunk driving. He told the cop, "I'm a bishop. I'm supposed to move diagonally."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Over the weekend President Obama gave the commencement speech at Ohio State University. He said, "I dare you to do better" — to which the students yelled back, "No, we dare YOU to do better. We need jobs!”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Mexico's economy has been on the upswing the last couple of years. They're getting investors from companies all over the world. In fact, Mexico is now home to 11 million undocumented Americans.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For the first time ever, girls in Saudi Arabia will be allowed to take part in school sports. Of course, their moms won't be allowed to drive them to practice. But hey, it's progress.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Taco Bell's chief marketing executive says they are now working on a new low-end menu. What? You mean the stuff they've been serving is the high-end stuff?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is raining in L.A. When it rains here, everybody loses their minds. In the rest of the country, everybody knows how the deal with weather, but in L.A. we don't. We're on storm watch 2013.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was very wet here in L.A. Nobody was walking anywhere. The traffic wasn't moving. And then the rain started.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: How wet was it? It's so wet today that NBC replaced Jay Leno with Aquaman.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was so wet, Reese Witherspoon got a DUI on a jet ski.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Sunday was Cinco de Mayo. I don't know exactly what that is, but I celebrate it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday President Obama spoke at Ohio State’s graduation, and told students that it’s their responsibility to make the world a better place. It got awkward when students were like, “Wait, isn't that literally your responsibility?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Over the weekend the Twitter account for the E! network was hacked. Apparently the hackers started tweeting fake stories about real celebrities — as opposed to what E! normally does, which is tweet real stories about fake celebrities.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Some experts are saying that the 2016 Democratic presidential race could come down to Hillary Clinton and Joe Biden. Biden is calling her a worthy opponent, while Hillary is calling him “practice.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The National Park Service is launching a new campaign to attract younger visitors. It has a very creative slogan: “National Parks: Nobody Knows You're Drinking in Here.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Iron Man 3 made $175 million in the United States and $680 million worldwide. It's the second biggest opening behind "The Avengers," which proves something I have known for a long time. We are all nerds now.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The only thing I didn't understand when I saw "Iron Man 3" was that Iron Man was in a lot of trouble and the world was in a lot of trouble but The Avengers were nowhere to be found. What happened? Did he lose their phone numbers? Did they unfriend him on Facebook?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Where were The Avengers? Seems like if the president is being held hostage, maybe bring the guy with the hammer that shoots lightning bolts.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I make it a policy to not get news from any network with an exclamation point in its name.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie revealed that he underwent a surgery that restricts the amount of food he can consume. As a result, 12 animals have been removed from the endangered species list.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Chris Christie had weight reduction surgery. As a result, I'll be going into surgery for monologue joke reduction.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Texas man has fired the first-ever gun created by a 3-D printer. Which raises the question: Don't you think a gun created by a printer would jam?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A cleric in Iran is warning that an earthquake is on the way, and it's the fault of women who wear revealing clothes. So yet another setback for the Tehran Hooters.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Chris Christie revealed he had lap-band surgery in February. President Obama wished him well. In fact, Obama is now thinking about having Joe Biden's mouth stapled.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: CNN anchor Carol Costello was robbed of her iPhone in broad daylight while walking down the street in Atlanta. Unfortunately it was on CNN, so there weren’t any witnesses.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Lindsay Lohan has checked into the Betty Ford Center. Celebrities who have been treated at Betty Ford swear by the place. In fact, they return again and again and again.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Rolling Stones played the Staples Center here. They are on their big Centrum Silver tour. Tickets went for as much $650. And that's minus the Medicare deductible.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Over the weekend, Arnold's son Patrick Schwarzenegger was kicked out of a nightclub in Hollywood. Apparently, Patrick threatened the DJ. It was a chaotic scene. Security rushed in and said, "Which one of you is Schwarzenegger's kid?" And 50 people raised their hands.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Over the weekend, the Rolling Stones played here at the Staples Center but they had to cut their ticket prices in half to fill the seats. I guess if people wanted go to the Staples Center to see old guys shuffling around way past their prime, they'd just go see the Lakers.

name: David Letterman
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie had stomach surgery so he won't be so big. His family gave him a choice. They said, "Look, you either have that surgery or get your own ZIP code."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Today President Obama and Joe Biden met with South Korean President Park Geun-hye, who is known as South Korea's “Iron Lady.” Or as Biden put it, "Can you introduce me to Iron Man?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Biden gave advice on how to avoid war with North Korea. Or, in other words, we're going to war with North Korea.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Mayor Bloomberg announced that large sections of New York City will get free Wi-Fi by the end of the year. Bloomberg says he's excited to bring a new service to New Yorkers. New Yorkers say they're excited to complain about it the moment it goes down.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night’s episode of “Dancing With the Stars” had the worst ratings in the history of the show. You can tell "Dancing with the Stars" is struggling because it was just named a contestant on "Dancing with the Stars."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie revealed that back in February he had a secret lap-band surgery, which explains why there's been so much food in New Jersey lately.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you examine the pictures, you can see that Christie actually might be getting fatter. He's the worst ad for lap-band surgery ever.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Lap-band surgery is said to be slower than other procedures. Typically, patients lose one to two pounds a week. Which means the governor could be down to a healthy weight in about 100 years.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In South Carolina, former Governor Mark Sanford won a congressional seat after dragging around and debating a cardboard cutout of Nancy Pelosi. Then someone explained that WAS Nancy Pelosi.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie says he's still adjusting after his surgery to reduce how much he can eat. He said, "I now have six free hours a day I don't know what to do with."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new poll, Americans trust Judge Judy more than they trust Supreme Court justices. She won her trust after her landmark decision in the case of Drunk Lady vs. Other Drunk Lady.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Former South Carolina Governor Mark Sanford is the guy who told his wife he was going for a hike and then went to Argentina to see his girlfriend. He was exposed as an unethical, lying, cheating weasel. In a stunning comeback, he has been elected to Congress, where he’ll fit right in.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today Sanford said his first order of business was improving relations with South America.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: New predictions claim that 42 percent of Americans will be obese by the year 2030. They say the only way to stop it is for government to step in. Oh, yeah, that will work. When it comes to trimming the fat and tightening your belt, who knows better than the U.S. government?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to Forbes magazine, Al Gore is now worth more than $200 million. This is what Gore meant when he talked about going green.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A volcano in Alaska has been erupting for about five days. Alaska is a huge state. It's so vast, white, and frozen, that the early settlers gave it the nickname "Nicole Kidman's forehead."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: They have some weird laws in Alaska. This is true. It is against the law in Alaska to awaken a sleeping bear. Who's going to break that law? "I've had a couple of drinks. I'm going to wake a sleeping bear."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: All this volcanic ash over Alaska can cause big problems. We're all worried about one thing: ash drifting into Canada and disrupting the hockey playoffs.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Volcanic ash can really mess with airplanes. And we can't let this volcano disrupt our air travel. That's the government's job.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Do you know what cicadas are? Every 17 years they come up out of the ground and then they attack everything. This year they're expecting a trillion cicadas. Mayor Bloomberg is advising New Yorkers to move their marijuana plants indoors.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, Delaware became the most recent state to legalize same-sex marriage. That marks the 11th state to make same-sex marriage legal and the first thing I know about Delaware.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This Sunday is Mother's Day. That means you have four days to pick out the perfect gift before just buying flowers on the way to brunch.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, a new survey found out the average American will spend $168 on Mother's Day this year. For any woman who's been through labor for a day and a half, remember, it pays exactly $168.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A movie version of "Dungeons and Dragons" is in the works. It's expected to set all-time records for people saying, "Ticket for one, please."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Former NBA player Dennis Rodman has asked North Korean dictator Kim Jong Un to release American prisoner Kenneth Bay. Rodman said, "I'm calling for Kim to do me a solid" and release Kenneth Bay." How do you think the Koreans will translate "do me a solid?"

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I'm sure Kenneth Bay would be thrilled to hear that Dennis Rodman is on his case.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Wouldn't it be something if it worked? How many can say they were saved from a North Korean prison camp by Dennis Rodman? Three, four. Eight, maybe.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Why do I feel this somehow ends with Michael Jordan being forced to fly to Pyongyang to sign the "Space Jam" poster hanging over Kim Jong Un's bed to prevent nuclear Armageddon?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hooter's is letting mothers eat for free on Mother's Day. What better way to tell your mother that she raised a cheapskate and a perve?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Long John Silver's has just hired a new executive to revamp their menu. For starters, he said they're going to start experimenting with something called fish.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Taco Bell has announced they're introducing a new $1 cravings menu. Here's how it works. You pay $1, you eat the food, and then you crave a toilet.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: On Mother's Day, Hooters is giving away free wings to all mothers who come in. Eating lunch with your mom at Hooters — I guess some guys never get tired of their moms saying, "Look at me when I'm talking to you!"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama said in his last press conference that he wants to close Gitmo. Gitmo? How about closing Dodger Stadium? How many people are being tortured there night after night?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Dodgers lost again last night. What is that, seven in a row? Their payroll is $239 million and they are in last place. They’re like NBC with baseball bats.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to researchers, people in the 25-to-35 age group are now experiencing mid-life crises. Who thinks the best years of their lives are behind them at the age of 25? Besides the cast of "Jersey Shore," of course.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Not a great day for Sir Paul McCartney. During a concert in Brazil, he got attacked by a swarm of grasshoppers. That's a very unusual thing to have happen to you. But it didn't faze him at all. He just thought he was having an acid flashback.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Yesterday police arrested 31 people involved in that big jewel heist in Belgium. That's a lot of people. Now $50 million worth of jewels sounds like a lot, but split 31 ways, it hardly seems worth the effort.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: One of the jewel thieves they captured yesterday was also a lawyer. That is a shame. Now lawyers will get a bad reputation.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Imagine being a jewel thief by night and a lawyer by day. You go from one job taking all that money and wrecking people's lives, and then onto being a jewel thief.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The Senate is now taking a look at the immigration bill and will provide sweeping changes if, in fact, the bill is passed. Passed? Tim Tebow's got a better chance of passing.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Senator John McCain will introduce a bill that lets cable customers pick which channels they want to pay for. For instance, HBO would cost you $10, AMC would cost you $5, and NBC would pay you $200.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week marks the 10th anniversary of the professional networking site LinkedIn. Which is weird, because on LinkedIn it says it has 15 years of experience.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that women think men holding a guitar are more attractive, even if they’re not playing it. In a related story, guys with an accordion will die alone.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new iPhone app can actually figure out how happy users are. Although if you need to download an app to tell you if you're happy, you're not.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Mother's Day is on Sunday. Americans will spend between $17 billion and $20 billion on Mother's Day. The average spending is about $169 per mom — which is the reason NBA players need so much money.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A giant African land snail was found. Authorities are worried there could be more. They can chew through stucco, and they carry potentially deadly meningitis. So far the snails have been found in Florida, Texas, and in the meatballs at IKEA.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The snails have no natural predators. In fact, city officials are considering bringing in giant French people to eat them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you're in Houston and you see a giant snail coming toward you, walk slowly for your life.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The Statue of Liberty is reopening on July 4. It has been closed since last year. What happened was she went in for lap band surgery.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama was down in Texas on his “Middle-class jobs and opportunity tour.” Don’t confuse that with his first term. That was the "Middle-class jobs and MISSED opportunity tour."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: While President Obama was in Texas, he told people to "Remember the Alamo and forget about Benghazi."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Sunday is, of course, Mother's Day, or as Kobe Bryant calls it, "April Fools' Day."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Kobe Bryant is suing his mother over sports memorabilia of his that she’s selling to raise money. He claims she stole his stuff and she’s going to sell it. Now the mom is countersuing. She wants a full refund on her Lakers season tickets.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama has been going around the country to rally support for his economic plan, and yesterday he said that a lot of sectors of our economy are doing better. When pressed for examples, Obama said, “Uh — the 'Iron Man' sequel sector?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Whole Foods is apologizing for switching the labels on some salads, which caused vegans to accidentally eat chicken. So if you're a vegan who mistakenly ate one of the salads, that's why it was so delicious.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new poll found that 54 percent of Americans are tired of Justin Bieber. It gets even worse when you hear that they polled only 54 percent of Americans.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There is a big movie out today: "The Great Gatsby." Leonardo DiCaprio is a billionaire who can have any woman he wants, yet he never seems happy. I don't know who he plays in the movie.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Great Gatsby is based on F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel. I was surprised when I saw that it's in 3-D. I guess they wanted Fitzgerald's sardonic critique of materialism to come right at you.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: They should have jazzed up the movie's title as well. They should have called it something like "2 Fast 2 Gatsby."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The movie has marketing tie-ins everywhere. Brooks Brothers has "Gatsby suits." The Plaza Hotel in New York is opening a "Fitzgerald suite." I think that is lovely. A room named after an alcoholic with tuberculosis who drove his wife mad before dying in his 40s. I want to stay in that room!

name: David Letterman
monologue: Barbara Walters is retiring. It was her own decision. She was not forced out, like Regis.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I was going to start off tonight with an Obama joke, but I don't want to get audited by the IRS, so forget that.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The IRS has now admitted that they targeted conservative groups for extra scrutiny. That's why Mitt Romney wanted to be president so bad — to keep the IRS off his back.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Barbara Walters announced her retirement today. Good, I'll have somebody to hang out with next year.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Tampa taco restaurant has pulled lion meat tacos from the menu due to protests from animal rights activists. However, lions announced today they will continue eating humans whenever they get the chance.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Saturday, the West Wing of the White House was evacuated when an overheated transformer set off a smoke alarm. Or as Obama put it, “Yeah, definitely check out that crazy transformer. Kind of smells like Marlboro Lights."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Wildlife experts are warning that giant, disease-carrying snails have been found in Texas. So if you see one, make sure you immediately saunter away from it at whatever speed you like.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: On Friday, a truck in Ohio overturned on a highway and spilled hundreds of hot dogs. It got even more annoying when another truck came along and spilled two less buns.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's an emotional day at "The View." Barbara Walters told her cast mates she is going to retire. The women were crying, shrieking, and talking over each other. Then Barbara announced she is going to retire.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was a very hot day here in L.A. It was so hot that "The Tonight Show" moved to New York just for the weather.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It was so hot that people in Beverly Hills actually drank tap water.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new study says by 2030 household robots will dominate every phase of our lives. The study says the No. 1 field for robot growth is medicine. That makes sense. Robots already perform well in surgery. That is, until there is a power outage. Then it's just a coat rack leaning over you as you bleed to death.

name: David Letterman
monologue: President Obama's right in the middle of three scandals. The IRS ratting out people it doesn't like. Benghazi, number two. And they say Obama has been phone tapping the AP. So three big scandals. Here's what I prefer: Weiner and Spitzer. Now those are scandals my writers can really work with.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The heat wave is continuing. There are warnings this could be a long, hot summer and they are telling everyone to cover up. Believe me. You don't have to tell the Obama White House twice. They know all about covering up.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today the White House unveiled its latest high-tech weapon: the IRS audit.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I love what IRS commissioner Steve Miller said today about this whole targeting conservative groups thing. He said, "Mistakes were made, but they were in no way made with a political or partisan motivation." Yeah, "Mistakes were made" — try saying THAT during your next IRS audit.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: First it was Benghazi, then the IRS scandal, and now this phone records scandal. Remember the old days when President Obama's biggest embarrassment was Joe Biden? What happened to those days?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It was just revealed that the Department of Justice secretly recorded the phone calls of AP journalists for two months. Obama promised reporters that the incident will be immediately investigated — by the Department of Justice.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The founder of Spanx announced that she is giving away half of her fortune to charity. She told her family, "We'll be fine. Things are just going to get a little tighter.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Philadelphia Eagles new coach, Chip Kelly, recently got rid of the team's long-running tradition of having fast-food Fridays. He says that he wants his players to live healthier lives. Then he sends them out to hit other people with their heads.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Officials in Belize say that a construction company accidentally destroyed a set of Mayan ruins that were 2,000 years old. Or as the Mayans put it, "Eh, it's not the end of the world."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There is a big novel out today. If you don't know, a novel is like a blog except it is on paper and it's all stuff that's made up. It's like CNN but it's written down.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The novel is called "Inferno." In "Inferno" it turns out that the epic poem "Dante's Inferno" is a set of clues. In "Dante's Inferno," Satan isn't red and he doesn't have a tail or pitchfork. But that makes sense. Why does Satan need a pitchfork? Is he doing a lot of farming down there?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The classic red-pitchfork devil didn't appear until the 17th century, in John Milton's "Paradise Lost." I know what you're thinking: "Oh, here we go. Another late-night talk show host going on about Elizabethan poets."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Didn't Jay Leno get fired for doing that bit about Milton's "Epitaphium Damonis"?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In a new interview, Joe Biden says he spends four or five hours every day with President Obama. In response, Obama said hiring that Obama impersonator was the best decision he's ever made.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Since President Obama took office, the Democratic Party has lost nine governorships, 56 members of Congress, and two Senate seats. In his defense, Obama said, "Well, I did promise change."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: China announced it will no longer buy recycled trash from the U.S. I don't have a joke here. I'd just like to give a round of applause to whatever genius has been selling trash to China.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: O.J. Simpson was in court this week trying to overturn his conviction on armed robbery and kidnapping. O.J. said, "I'm tired of everyone thinking of me as a robber and kidnapper and forgetting what a great murderer I am."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This week marks the 40th anniversary of the Watergate hearings. For those of you too young to remember, back then the administration had an enemies list. They were spying on reporters, and they used the IRS to harass groups they didn’t like. Thank God those days are gone forever.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A lot of critics are comparing President Obama to President Richard Nixon, which is unfair. Nixon's unemployment rate was only 5 percent.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This whole IRS thing has become a huge story. They apparently were targeting conservative groups like the tea party. You know it's bad when President Obama says, "Hey, why don’t we talk about Benghazi?"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The National Aquarium in Washington is going to close. But don't worry. If you're in D.C. and you still want to smell something fishy, stop by the White House. They've gone from "Change you can believe in" to "Changing the story until you believe it."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Cannes Film Festival was yesterday. Everyone who's anyone in show business is in France right now. "But Craig, you're here in Los Angeles." Exactly. I'm lower on the show business ladder than Justin Bieber's monkey.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Germans are like, "No, Bieber. We are keeping your monkey. It is never leaving Germany again. This Bieber monkey is the new Hasselhoff of Germany.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Every year there's a jury at the Cannes Film Festival. Getting on the jury is very competitive in France. Not because the French love cinema, but because they love to judge.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: One of the people on the jury this year is Nicole Kidman. She is letting them screen the movies on her forehead.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Have you folks been paying attention to what's going on in Washington? In a matter of six weeks we have three big scandals, and it looks like President Obama and all his buddies in the White House may go to prison. Finally, some good news for the Romney campaign.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama is not having a good week. With three scandals shaking the White House, they're saying this is one of the worst weeks of Obama's presidency. Obama was like, “How could things get worse?” And Joe Biden was like, “You rang?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A town in Minnesota has appointed a 4-year-old boy to be its mayor. People got pretty annoyed when he said his first plan was "waising taxes."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Next season “Dancing With the Stars” will be cut back from two nights a week to just one — while "American Idol" will be cut back from two nights a week to a puppet show at Ryan Seacrest's house.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: O.J. Simpson took the witness stand. He's serving up to 33 years on armed robbery, assault, and kidnapping charges. He won't be eligible for parole until 2017 and who knows if we'll have even have "Dancing With the Stars" by then.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The most notable thing to come out of the trial is that O.J. has put on a lot of weight in prison. I think he found the real killers and ate them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: He's hoping if he's granting a retrial they'll let him serve the remainder of his sentence under Waffle House arrest.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Chinese authorities recently arrested over 900 people for selling counterfeit mink. China warned the U.S. that the meat's being sold under the name "Arby's."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: JC Penny has a new ad out. It thanks customers for coming back to them. And then the customers explained they're coming back to return crap from JC Penny.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Earlier this week it was announced that Barbara Walters is stepping down. Footage just surfaced from 1962 of the young Barbara as an undercover Playboy Bunny. You can tell it was Barbara because she keeps asking men if they want their drink "on the wocks."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new survey, 42 percent of Americans have an unfavorable view of hipsters. When they heard this, hipsters said, "Big deal, we had an unfavorable view of ourselves way before you."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This week will mark the 37th time House Republicans have tried to repeal Obamacare. If Republicans really wanted to do away with Obamacare they should just endorse it as a conservative non-profit and let the IRS take it down.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama announced the appointment of a new acting commissioner of the IRS — the other guy was fired. See, they're called "acting commissioner" because you have to act like the scandal doesn't involve the White House.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A lot of critics are now comparing President Obama to President Nixon. The good news for Obama? At least he's no longer being compared to President Carter.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It has not been a good week for President Obama. You've got Benghazi, the IRS scandal, this AP records scandal, and, worst of all, his Chicago Bulls got eliminated by the Miami Heat. Do you know what that means? LeBron James is going to get audited by the IRS.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The IRS has a new boss after it came out they unfairly targeted tea party groups. The president says the new IRS chief is not only good with numbers, but he has more integrity than the last guy. It's Bernie Madoff.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: American Idol is in trouble in the ratings these days. They are down 40 percent since last year. This season, "American Idol" was beaten by "Duck Dynasty" in the ratings. You know, the show with two dudes sitting in a tree saying, "That a duck?" "No, looks more like a quail."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Duck Dynasty is like "Honey Boo Boo" if you replaced the little girl with a duck.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I wonder who they will get to judge "American Idol" next year? Probably people once at the top of their fields, but now with a lot of time on their hands. So maybe the old Pope. I think Pope Classic and Jay Leno would be good judges.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Today the White House released 99 pages of emails on trouble in Benghazi — and one shirtless tweet from Anthony Weiner.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tonight was the finale of the lowest-rated season in "American Idol" history. You could tell the show was in trouble when they said, "The winner is what's-her-face."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Eagles' offensive lineman Evan Mathis posted a picture on Instagram that shows him relieving himself on an IRS building with a caption that says, "Audit this!" Or as the IRS said, "OK, see you tomorrow at noon."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week, Oscar Mayer introduced a new hot dog with bacon cooked right into it. Or as Chris Christie put it, "Is it possible to reverse that lap-band procedure?"

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A 7-year-old boy wrote a letter to the vice president. He wrote: "I think guns should shoot chocolate bullets so no one will get killed and no one will be sad." Guns that shoot chocolate bullets would be a great way to liven up an Easter egg hunt, wouldn't it?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The sad part is that's the first letter Joe Biden has received since he took office.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight is the much-anticipated release of the new "Star Trek" movie. It's expected to make $100 million this weekend. That's a lot, but imagine how much it would make if the people buying tickets were going with dates.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Most "Star Trek" fans are men, or a reasonable facsimile.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama is in a lot of hot water lately. Despite the scandals, 53 percent of Americans say they approve of the job he's doing. The other 47 percent are being audited.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new report just came out. It says someone close to the president knew about the IRS scandal and kept his mouth shut. In other words, we can rule out Joe Biden.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's been reported that Californians donated almost $600,000 to Chris Christie's re-election campaign. And by Californians, I mean my monologue writers. They want that guy to stick around.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Lamborghini is celebrating its 50th anniversary. Lamborghini is so freaked out by turning 50, it just bought itself a Lamborghini.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: These White House scandals are not going away any time soon. I’ll tell you how bad it’s looking for President Obama: People in Kenya are now saying he’s 100 percent American.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Yesterday, the Senate minority leader, Mitch McConnell, charged that there’s a culture of intimidation throughout the Obama administration. Really, anyone intimidated by Barack Obama? He can’t even keep Joe Biden in line.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: So they spent the last five years claiming President Obama was weak and ineffective. Suddenly he’s Tony Soprano.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: After being booed at the Billboard Music Awards last night, Justin Bieber said, ''I'm 19 years old. I think I'm doing a pretty good job." Hey Justin. I'm 63. I thought I was doing a pretty good job. Welcome to show business, pal.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: We're almost done with May sweeps. Sweeps — that's when TV networks pull out all the stops to get ratings. In fact, on "Glee," one of the actors is going to come out — as straight!

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Ratings experts say the best way to get people to watch during sweeps is to leave the audience with a question that won't be answered until the next time the show is on. You know, like "Who shot J.R.?" I like to think I do this every night — the question is, "Is this show still on?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I prefer to judge the performance of this show on its "artistic impact." By that I mean the number of complaints we receive. We're up 30 percent year to year in key demos.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don't think you want to win ratings in late night. Look what happened on NBC. Who has been No. 1 over there for 20 years? Jay Leno. And what happened? He was fired. Twice! It's like "Well done, Jay. That was great. You're fired."

name: David Letterman
monologue: Anybody win the Powerball thing over the weekend? $590 million, one winner. That's the biggest single jackpot since — well, since Tiger Woods' divorce.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It turns out the winning ticket for Saturday’s huge $590 million Powerball drawing was apparently sold in a town called Zephyrhills, Florida. In a related story, Florida residents are getting an unusual volume of calls from their grandkids today.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: During a fundraiser yesterday, President Obama said there is a shortage of common sense right now in Washington. At which point the people who paid $5,000 a plate for their dinner applauded in agreement.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There are reports that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un may have another child with a woman who is not his wife. People say the baby looks just like him — though in fairness, pretty much ALL babies look just like him.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Navy announced that its specially trained dolphins found a rare torpedo off the coast of California. You can tell those dolphins are smart because they just turned the torpedo back at us and said, “How about YOU doing some tricks at Sea World?”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Yesterday I was presented with an honorary doctorate at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas. I will be writing medical marijuana prescriptions in the alley after the show.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I'm a doctor of humane letters and I don't know what that means. I didn't have to do anything to get it. I didn't have to read or write a thesis. I made a mockery of higher education this weekend and now I can invite strangers into my office and ask them to take their clothes off without getting arrested.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber received multiple honors at the Billboard Music Awards. He won for best male artist. I can count three lies in the title of that award.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber actually said he's an artist — in the same way the guy that makes my turkey sandwich at subway is an artist.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A lot of people are criticizing President Obama, including Michelle Obama. She recently said she could take a whole afternoon and talk about Barack's failures. She was immediately hired by Fox News.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new survey, white Americans are more likely to see President Obama as angry than black Americans. After hearing about it, Obama got really angry — according to white Americans.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A college student in Georgia was worried that his parents would be mad at him for flunking English. So he tried to fake his own kidnapping. The parents figured it out when the ransom note said, "We has your son."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A man gave a waitress a $1,000 tip so she could take a trip to Italy. Isn't that nice? It was an Olive Garden waitress who dreamed of one day trying Italian food.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Michelle Obama gave a commencement at a high school in Nashville. The first lady said about her husband, "I could take up a whole afternoon talking about his failures." And today she was offered her own show on Fox News.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama gave the commencement address at Morehouse College over the weekend. Great speech, very inspiring. He told the young graduates their future is bright — unless, of course, they want jobs.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The White House admitted President Obama's chief of staff had advance warning that the IRS was targeting conservative groups. President Obama says the first time he heard about the IRS and AP scandals was from the media. See, that’s why President Obama holds press conferences. It’s not to explain what’s going on. It’s to find out what’s going on.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Singer Mary J. Blige has been slapped with a $3.4 million bill from the IRS. I didn’t even know she was a tea party member.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Arnold Schwarzenegger has announced he will star in a low-budget horror movie called "The Toxic Avenger." He wreaks havoc. He's a monster. I have no idea what he'll do in the movie.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A museum in Sweden claims to have the world's biggest collection of ABBA memorabilia. They clearly haven't seen my bedroom.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: ABBA sold 370 million records, and two of those sales were to people who weren't white.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: ABBA sold 18 million albums just in Australia when the entire population of Australia at the time was 15 million people. How could that happen? There's only one explanation: Kangaroos were buying the album.

name: David Letterman
monologue: There's a new HBO movie this weekend — the Liberace story, "Behind the Candelabra." Liberace claimed that he was not gay. Well, that's good enough for me.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: These scandals at the White House are just getting worse. It turns out that President Obama’s chief of staff knew about the scandal at the IRS three weeks before the president found out. Obama was like, "Anything else you guys aren't telling me?" And Joe Biden was like, "Uh . . . I broke the copier."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama’s team knew about the IRS scandal but kept him in the dark about it. Or as Obama put it, "Guys, when I said 'no spoilers,' I was just talking about 'Game of Thrones.'"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Four women have qualified to race in this Sunday’s Indy 500. Yeah, four women going around and around in circles — or as that’s normally called, "The View."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A 19-year-old student in Lawrenceville, Georgia, was failing English and he didn't want to tell his parents about it. So he faked his own kidnapping. He texted his parents and said he's been abducted. It sounds like a terrible Liam Neeson movie.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The student camped out for a week and then came home when it rained. I guess he failed his "Fake your own kidnapping 101 class" too.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night at midnight, former Congressman Anthony Weiner officially announced in an online video that he is running for mayor of New York. Nothing says "I put my sleazy past behind me" like showing a video on the Internet at midnight.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: During a Senate hearing yesterday, Senator John McCain said it was too hard to always have to update apps on his iPhone. No one has the heart to tell him the device he was holding was a garage door opener.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Brad Pitt said in an interview that he has very few friends. In other words, just one more thing that Brad Pitt and I have in common.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In New Jersey a woman found her lost dog by luring the dog back with bacon. She also found the governor of New Jersey.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: White House officials insist that President Obama knew nothing about the IRS scandal until we all heard about it in the news last week. They said because there was an investigation under way, it would have been inappropriate to tell him. And besides, he was too busy not knowing anything about Benghazi.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Anthony Weiner has formally announced he is running for mayor of New York City. He posted a video announcing it just after midnight — and being online in the middle of the night has always worked so well for Mr. Weiner.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: O.J. Simpson is waiting to see if a judge will grant him a retrial. Have you seen how fat O.J. has gotten? He’s so fat, he’s changed his name from O.J. to "Au Jus."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: O.J. is so fat, he wants the judge to throw the cookbook at him.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: On this day in 1859, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle was born in Edinburgh, Scotland. He's the creator of Sherlock Holmes. Arthur Conan Doyle was a man of many talents. He was a writer and a doctor. If he were around today, he would be a frequent guest on "Oprah."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In the novels, Sherlock Holmes was a cocaine addict. But he still solved crimes. I would argue that cocaine does not give you crime-solving abilities. The only thing I ever tried to solve while I was on cocaine was how to get more cocaine.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Some people think Sherlock Holmes was a real person. These people are called "stupid."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I thought Holmes' address in London was real. He famously lived and worked at 221B Baker Street. When I was in London, I tried to find it. There's no 221B. It's just a bank. I walked up and down the street for an hour, being judged by snooty English bankers.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Hangover 3 opens this weekend. It's based on the famous novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Vice President Joe Biden met with two undocumented immigrants this week to promote the new immigration bill. When they learned they had to sit down with Biden, they went ahead and deported themselves.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: CBS has become the best-rated network among the 18-49 age group for the first time in 21 years. NBC is still No. 1 among pets whose owners left the TV on to keep them company.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Target is now selling a line of affordable wedding dresses. They say it's perfect for any woman who’s always dreamed of wearing a dress from the same place she buys chips and soap.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: New York City is getting a new professional soccer team that will be partially owned by the Yankees. You can tell it's owned by the Yankees because A-Rod won't be playing for that team either.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We had an election in Los Angeles yesterday. Three measures involved medical marijuana. The one that passed was a proposition that limits the number of marijuana dispensaries in the city. The rule now is there cannot be more marijuana stores than cupcake shops — because they feed on each other.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The proposition will limit the number of dispensaries in L.A. to 135. Unfortunately, right now there are about 800 pot shops, so the employees of 665 of them will be out of work. And on top of that, their resumes will say they used to work at a pot store. So I wish them luck.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A new study estimates that Colorado residents will legally smoke more than 2 million ounces of marijuana next year. That's like a reggae festival and Willie Nelson's birthday combined.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In November, Colorado passed an amendment that legalized the recreational use of marijuana. It's resulted in a surge of "pot tourism." People come for the weekend to smoke pot and the next thing they know, it's 30 years later they're still there working in a carbon-neutral coffee shop.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's coming out that in high school, President Obama signed a girl's yearbook by calling her sweet and foxy. Of course, now he calls her Secretary of Homeland Security Janet Napolitano.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Pope Francis said that atheists are still eligible to go to heaven. To return the favor, atheists said Popes are still eligible to go into a void of nothingness.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new international poll finds the least popular country in the world is Iran. After hearing this, North Korea said, "What do we have to do?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Pennsylvania, a couple stabbed each other in an argument over who should win "American Idol." At last we finally know why "American Idol" is losing so many viewers. They're killing each other.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Time magazine found a picture of President Obama at his high school prom back in 1979. Let me tell you how long ago that was. Back then, Obama had to ask a girl for her phone number. He couldn't illegally obtain it through the Justice Department.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It is not looking good for President Obama. Today, his teleprompter took the fifth. In fact, the White House has changed their slogan from, "Yes, we can" to "No, I can't remember."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The latest scandal in Washington, of course, is raising questions about the IRA. You know, I have a question. Why is it called the Internal Revenue Service? How is having your money confiscated a service?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Democratic congressman said that he worries that the IRA scandal might have a chilling effect on the IRA and that they might be afraid to audit people. So finally some good is coming out of all of this.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Time magazine just released a picture of a 17-year-old President Obama with his prom date. They would've published a picture of Joe Biden with his prom date, but his mom didn't want to be photographed.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Amtrak trains may soon have special cars where passengers can sit with their pets. Though it'll be awkward when you try to talk to your cat and he just slips on his headphones.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Justin Bieber is apparently making guests at his parties sign a contract promising not to post pictures of it on Twitter, Facebook, or Instagram. When they heard that, MySpace was like, "We're back, baby!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A woman in New Jersey just found her missing dog after she grilled pork in her backyard and he came home because of the smell. Unfortunately, he was immediately shoved out of the way by Governor Chris Christie.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Time magazine published President Obama's prom photos. He's with friends and their dates. Those girls in Kenya are very good looking.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Pope Francis made an extremely controversial statement. He says he believes anyone can go to heaven if you do good deeds, even atheists. Some Catholics were upset by his comments because it means we wasted a lot of Sundays going to church.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It would be fun to let atheists into heaven if for no other reason than to see the look on their faces when they get there.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Meanwhile, in Saudi Arabia the head of the religious police said he believes that Saudi citizens who use Twitter will go to hell. Let me get this straight. Tweeting leads to damnation. But filling a palace with kidnapped beauty contestants — that's OK?

name: Craig Ferguson
