monologue: Syrian President Assad says he is turning over his chemical weapons because Russia asked him to, "not because of the U.S. threatening to bomb him." Yeah, and Osama bin Laden is at the bottom of the ocean right now because he enjoys scuba diving.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Oneida Indian Nation wants the Washington Redskins to change the name "Redskins" because they consider it a racial slur. In a related story, the city of Jacksonville wants the NFL team, the Jaguars, to drop the name “Jacksonville” just because they stink.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the tabloids, they are saying that it looks like Khloe Kardashian and Lamar Odom are done. If that turns out to be true, then Khloe would get the 12th pick in the NBA draft.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Russian President Vladimir Putin wrote a scolding Op-Ed piece in The New York Times. He thinks people still read The New York Times.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If you haven't seen The New York Times piece, Putin said America should stay out of Syria. And then Putin said Khloe should dump Lamar because it's for his own good.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The 2014 edition of the "Guinness Book of Records" is out. Finally, we'll have answers to the most important questions of our time, like "Who's got the world's largest Afro?"

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's quite a week for me because Eliot Spitzer lost his race for comptroller and Anthony Weiner lost his race for mayor. So that means I am back to being New York City's biggest embarrassment.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Russian President Vladimir Putin actually wrote an Op-Ed piece in The New York Times where he said it’s dangerous for Americans to see themselves as “exceptional.” Then he said, "Except for that Justin Timberlake. That guy is amazing."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Putin said it’s dangerous for Americans to see themselves as “exceptional” and said that, quote, “God created us equal.” Then he got back to arresting people for being gay.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Dennis Rodman has been hanging out again in North Korea. He just announced that he will train the North Korean basketball team for the Olympics. He's going to teach them the key strategy that always worked for him — pass the ball to Michael Jordan.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Pope Francis just got a used car, a 1984 Renault with 190,000 miles on it. The Pope said he wanted an old car so he could drive around listening to his Billy Idol cassettes.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: How crazy is it that the Pope has a car? Imagine driving through Rome and a Renault cuts in front of you. You flip the guy off, and it's the Pope!

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The New York Times published an Op-Ed piece written by Vladimir Putin. Putin warns against American exceptionalism. He says it is dangerous to encourage people to see themselves as exceptional, whatever the motivation. He sounds like a fun dad, huh?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Putin said that when Americans claim to be exceptional it offends other countries. This from a man who arrests his political opponents, persecutes people based on sexual orientation, and put a girl band in a labor camp for singing songs he didn't like. We don't think we are better than everyone else. We just think we are better than him, specifically.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Dr. Phil is on the program tonight. You've got to hand it to Dr. Phil, he is a smart guy. He turned a phony medical degree into a media empire.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I've lost some weight. I am on that new Obama diet. Every day I let Vladimir Putin eat my lunch.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Today is Friday the 13th, and over in Finland the airline "Finnair" had a flight numbered 666 going to Helsinki — which has the three-letter designation "HEL." So on your ticket it says Friday the 13th, flight 666, going to hell. Even scarier? There’s a layover in Newark.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Mercedes has unveiled a self-driving car. The car drives itself. I’m begging every member of Lindsay Lohan's family to get one of these.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In Canada, a man was attacked by a polar bear and he scared it off with his cellphone. Apparently the bear got frightened when he saw the two-year contract.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The new season of “Survivor” premieres next week. It has a great twist. It has returning contestants competing for a million dollars against their own family members. So if you’re wondering what it takes for people to be willing to be stranded on an island with their families, the answer is a million dollars.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: We just had our primary for mayor here in New York City, and a new poll found that only 20 percent of New Yorkers voted. Which got even worse when 50 percent were like, “Wait, Giuliani's leaving?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Doritos is asking people from around the world to submit videos that could end up in its Super Bowl commercial. Yeah, then the Jets were like, "Sweet! Maybe we WILL be in the Super Bowl."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Officials in Washington, D.C., have proposed a 24-hour waiting period before people can get tattoos. Or as people who want tattoos put it, "You mean we gotta stay drunk for 24 hours?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's Friday the 13th. It is always considered unlucky. It got scarier when those "Friday the 13th" movies came out. That hockey mask Jason wears is terrifying. How did they come up with that? Who'd make a link between hockey and violence?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A few years ago, they made the movie "Freddy vs. Jason." They do that all the time. They take two franchises that are totally out of gas and put them against each other. There was "Dracula vs. Frankenstein," "Alien vs. Predator," "Khloe vs. Lamar," "Jay vs. Conan."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Godzilla was in tons of those movies, like "Godzilla vs. King Kong." The most uneven was "Godzilla vs. Mothra." How's that a fair fight? Godzilla is a giant fire-breathing lizard. Mothra is a big moth. What does Mothra do? Eat holes in all of Godzilla's sweaters?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: For the first time ever, Miss America is a woman of Indian descent. The judge asked her three questions: Why do you want to be Miss America?, What will you do with the prize?, and How do I get my laptop to reboot?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Vladimir Putin wrote that America should not view itself as exceptional. I disagree. Hey, Russia, we invented jazz and the elevators it plays in. We're the geographic sweet spot between frostbite and beheadings. Our roulette is way better than your roulette. And when you rearrange the letters in "Russia" — you get "USA, Sir!"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There's a new exercise trend out there. It's people using twerking to get fit. In just six weeks you can lose 10 pounds and your dignity.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new study found that toddlers who talk early tend to develop a drinking problem later on in life. Another warning sign is if the kid asks for his milk on the rocks.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Dancing With the Stars returned for a 17th season. Paula Dean was rumored to be one of the stars they tried to get to dance. Over the weekend, Paula made her first public appearance since she went into hiding. I knew eventually she would have to come out for butter.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Paula Dean held a cooking demonstration. Some fans paid $400 a ticket. Who pays $400 to watch a woman cook?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Paula told the crowd that the racism controversy taught her a lot about herself and her business. She promised that from now on the only N-word she will use is "nutmeg."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For the first time an Indian-American has won Miss America. A 24-year-old named Nina Davuluri won by answering a question no one else could possible answer: “What is the name of last year's Miss America?”

name: Jay Leno
monologue: California's legislature approved a bill allowing drivers licenses for illegals. I've got a better idea. Instead of giving them new licenses let's take away the licenses from people like Dina Lohan and Lamar Odom. Give them those licenses.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Dairy farmers now warn that there could be a jump in the price of milk by the end of the year. Milk could be as much as $6 a gallon. Today Senator John McCain outlined a new plan to invade Wisconsin.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new Harris Poll, America's favorite age is 50. Do you know what NBC's least favorite age is? — 63.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Saturday night was the big fight in Las Vegas between Floyd Mayweather and Canelo Alvarez. Justin Bieber and Lil Wayne actually walked Floyd Mayweather to the ring. It really psyched out Alvarez. When he saw the three of them together he was like, “I don't know who to hit first.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, Ravens quarterback Joe Flacco actually missed the birth of his son so that he could play with his team against the Browns. It was 8 pounds, 7 ounces. Not the baby — the diamond Flacco had to buy his wife to make up for it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Russia apparently has asked Cher to perform at next year's Winter Olympics. Because if there's one thing that'll keep gay people out of your country, it's holding a free Cher concert.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, Cher says she turned down Russia's invitation to perform because of the government's anti-gay laws. Russia said it’s no big deal. They'll just move on to their second choice: Liza Minnelli.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: We have a new Miss America. Nina Davuluri is the first Miss America of Indian-American heritage. A lot of people say having an Indian-American as Miss America is a sign of progress. I think it is. We should pat ourselves on the back for objectifying women without regard to ethnicity.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The big controversy in the pageant this year was that Miss Kansas had tattoos. Miss America's main competitor is the Miss USA Pageant, which is run by Donald Trump. Trump said tattoos made Miss Kansas look silly. Then he stuck his head into a cotton candy machine to whip up a fresh batch of hair.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Miley Cyrus and her fiance have officially called off their engagement. So we are about to see how Miley Cyrus acts when she's single. We've been getting the restrained Miley.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: They've already announced the most popular Halloween costume. The top one will be the Miley Cyrus costume. Just a warning: I'm not giving any candy to a kid who says "trick or twerk."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Joe Biden's niece was arrested. The hardest part about arresting a Biden is convincing them they have the right to remain silent.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There is a library that is stocked with thousands of e-books in San Antonio. But that's not really a library. It's called a Kindle.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A Stanford study suggests that social media is making us smarter. They examined hundreds of essays written by college freshmen between 1917 and 2006. By 2006, the papers were longer, better researched, and more complex. That’s because kids in 2006 cut and pasted them from Wikipedia.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The fact of the matter is that we are not getting smarter. Our phones are getting smarter.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I don't know my home phone number. My cell phone has that information. Phones in the old days were very, very dumb. It's not us. It's them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On Sunday night is the Emmy Awards. The Emmy Awards are a chance to honor the actors everyone loves and the writers, directors, and producers no one cares about.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Miley Cyrus and her fiance have split up. I guess it just didn’t twerk out.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This week marks the fifth anniversary of the collapse of Lehman Brothers, which sparked the recession. Think about how bad things were back then. We had unemployment over 7 percent. The debt was out of control. There were wars breaking out all over the globe. Thank God that's all behind us now, huh?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: USA Today had a front-page feature on the new healthcare law. It said that the opposition to Obamacare at an all-time high. It has gotten so bad that the president is now calling it "Bidencare."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new report, over the last three years Social Security overpaid by $1.29 billion — thus establishing itself as the federal government's most efficient program.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Joe Biden has people talking that he'll run for president after he was spotted at a fundraiser in Iowa this week. Unfortunately, he missed giving his speech because he spent four hours trapped in a corn maze.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Britney Spears has signed a $29 million contract to perform shows in Las Vegas for two years. Which explains that new saying: “What Happens in Vegas was Prerecorded at a Studio in L.A.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: NASA is sending chocolate to astronauts on the International Space Station. I guess it makes sense — I mean, it's not like those guys have to watch their weight. “Nope, still zero pounds.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In a town in Ireland, the people say they're being attacked at random by a clown who sprays them with seltzer. Victims describe the attacker as having pale skin, a red nose, and holding a bottle. It's Ireland! How are they going to find him?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The United Nations General Assembly was called to order. The streets of Manhattan were jammed with people in strange clothes, yelling in weird languages. Then the U.N. got started.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The U.N. building in New York is magnificent. It has lots of flags. It's like a giant IHOP.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: When the U.N. is not in session, the delegates like to take advantage of their "diplomatic immunity." They go all over Manhattan doing dangerous and crazy stuff with drugs and strippers. Some even dare to snap pictures of Alec Baldwin.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The CEO of Starbucks is asking customers to stop bringing guns into the coffee chain stores. He said, "It's our job to rob you guys."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Starbucks announced they don't want customers bringing guns into their stores. Meanwhile, Dunkin' Donuts said there is nothing you can bring in here that's more dangerous than what we serve.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It turns out that a man who had been struggling with unexplained drunkenness actually had microbes in his stomach that produced alcohol that made him drunk. I don't have a joke for this, but I just want to let everyone know that this excuse does exist, seriously.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Kelsey Grammer is taking over a part in the new "Expendables" movie that was supposed to go to Nicolas Cage. It's being called the most unbelievable performance by Nicolas Cage ever — him saying no to a part.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Today was a day of much downloading and updating for owners of the iPad and iPhone. Apple released its new operating system. It was nice to breeze through 40 pages of user terms and conditions again. It's been too long.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There are so many new features for Apple. The new features will make your phone the most technologically advanced piece of electronic equipment you will ever accidentally put through the washing machine.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Researchers at Ohio State say the number of pedestrians whose have been injured while using smartphones while walking has more than doubled since 2005. They also confirmed that those injuries are hilarious to watch.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Those studies say that not only do people walk into traffic, but people have walked off bridges. That's one of the injuries no one has any sympathy for. You are the idiot. You got what you deserved.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Starbucks has a new policy. If you have a gun, they're asking you to leave it at home — thus making it easier for them to rob you.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to the Orlando Sentinel, there was a rally to get Tim Tebow to play quarterback for the Jacksonville Jaguars. But the bad news: Only 12 guys showed up. The good news for Tebow? Those 12 guys were Matthew, Luke, Mark, John, Peter . . .

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The face value of tickets to this year's Super Bowl will be as high as $2,600. So that's what it will cost the Jacksonville Jaguars if they want to go to the Super Bowl — $2,600.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Cher has turned down an invitation to sing at the 2014 Olympics in Russia because of Russia's anti-gay laws. Their anti-gay laws are so strict, men can be arrested just for showing up at a Cher concert.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: North Korea says it's ready to resume nuclear talks with the U.S. for the first time in five years. But President Obama said it's going to be pretty awkward - not talking to North Korea, but having to thank Dennis Rodman.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Brazil’s President Dilma Rousseff is apparently so mad over the NSA’s spying scandal that she has canceled her trip to the White House next month. Of course it didn’t help when Brazil called to say they weren’t coming and the White House was like, “Yeah, we heard.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Senate leaders Harry Reid and Mitch McConnell admitted they have no Plan B if the House doesn’t avoid a government shutdown. Of course this raised a lot of questions, like: Since when did they have a Plan A?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Happy birthday to The New York Times. The Times shares its birthday with Lance Armstrong. Lance Armstrong and The New York Times are very different, of course. One has a history of telling lies and all kinds of crap but is now desperately trying to stay relevant. And the other one's Lance Armstrong.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The New York Times is very respected. They've won more Pulitzer Prizes than any other newspaper. By the way, if you don't know what that is, I'll explain. A newspaper is a big papery blog with yesterday's news.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Apparently some of the contestants on "Big Brother" were fired from their real jobs for racist remarks they made on the show. But this was the best season for "Big Brother" ever, according to Paula Deen.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Russian President Vladimir Putin said he may seek a fourth term but that's up to the people to decide. Then he laughed for 10 minutes . . . shirtless.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Chicago has now surpassed New York City as the murder capital of the United States. That's really surprising since New York has twice as many NFL teams.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Kevin Trudeau, the king of infomercials, has been sent to jail for fraud. The judge sentenced him to 10 years. But then he said, "Wait, there's more," and added another five years.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Kardashians insist their show is real and not scripted. It's a real look at their lives. Well, Kim, Khloe, and Kris posted pictures on Instagram shooting the Kardashian Christmas episode — in September.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: That's why it is so hard to keep up with the Kardashians. They're three months ahead of us.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: As soon as the new iPhone was announced, a weird thing happened. My old iPhone started begging for its life.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A high-ranking health official in Amsterdam is taking a strong stance against sugar. He says sugar is an addictive, dangerous drug that should be regulated by the government. He wants to put warning labels on sugar. This is coming from a place where you can get pot in your Happy Meal.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It looks like the federal government could be shutting down. The legal definition of a government shutdown is when Congress continues not to work, but they do it from home.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Pundits say President Obama is starting to lose support from his own party. To give you an idea how bad it’s gotten, today Jimmy Carter compared him to Jimmy Carter.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Syrian President Assad told Fox News that if he were ever to talk to President Obama he would tell Obama to “listen to your people." Is he the one to give advice about listening to his people? His people are shooting at him!

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A Costco in Arizona is now selling a 60-year-old bottle of scotch for $17,000. You know what you can buy for $17,000 at Costco? Everything else at Costco.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Powerball lottery was last night and somebody got a lot richer. A single winning ticket was sold in South Carolina for the $400 million grand prize. Lottery officials are urging that winner to sign the back of his ticket and then put it in a safe place. As opposed to what? Dipping it in hot sauce and eating it?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The creator of Beanie Babies has been fined $53 million for tax evasion. But, on the plus side, if he sells all of his Beanie Babies, he'll owe . . . probably about $53 million.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Two guys in New Hampshire were arrested after they tried to rob a group of people playing Bingo. Cops became suspicious when they saw a car driving away from the Bingo hall going more than 10 miles an hour.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This week the Kardashians are filming their Christmas episode. It’s a reality show, so they want to keep it real.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I know Christmas in September seems a little weird, but by the time December rolls around, Khloe is in hibernation.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A plane had to make an emergency landing in France because a dozen Scottish passengers wouldn't stop dancing. The police have released a statement saying that alcohol may have been a factor. Now, I am Scottish. I KNOW alcohol was a factor. There is no "may" about this.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Scientists here in California have discovered a rare species of legless lizards. Now don't confuse that with spineless snakes; those are called congressmen. That’s totally different.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Monday is Celebrate Bisexuality Day. I don't know if I'm going to celebrate. I could go either way.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A show on plants on the Discovery Channel said that plants have a way of signaling danger to each other. When there's danger, the plant releases a gas that other plants can sense. Well, here is my question. What good is a plant warning another plant about danger? What's the other plant supposed to do, run?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Jimmy Fallon is here tonight. What, it’s already February? That’s amazing!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: For the first time in 90 years, Time magazine has appointed a female editor. But while it's a big change for the publication, she promises it will still be the same magazine you briefly glance at before you buy an Us Weekly.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In a new interview, Elton John said that he will not cancel a performance in Russia later this year, despite the country's anti-gay laws. Vladimir Putin was pretty shocked when he heard. He was like, "Hold on. Elton John is gay?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The National Zoo says that so many people are watching its panda cam that it now has to limit each viewing session to 15 minutes. Though if you’re watching a panda on a webcam for more than 15 minutes, maybe YOU'RE the one who needs to be monitored.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that leading a healthy lifestyle can actually reverse the signs of aging. Although constantly talking about being a Vegan will still take years off other people’s lives.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The Emmy Awards had just one surprise after another. I thought the highlight of the show was when they brought out the undead Liberace.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This evening I will talk to the entire cast of "Breaking Bad." It might get a little awkward for me since I'm only halfway through season one.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Thanks to "Breaking Bad," the ratings for AMC have skyrocketed. You know what else has skyrocketed? — the number of high school kids now taking chemistry.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This Sunday is the very last episode of "Breaking Bad." So from now on, if you want to see psychotic murderers attack each other on Sunday, you will have to watch the NFL.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Traffic has come to a complete stop in Hollywood because we have a huge free concert with Paul McCartney tonight. Either that or all of those people outside just fell for our biggest prank ever.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I was out very late last night after the Emmy Awards. They had all of these parties going on. What are you going to do — not go to them?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It takes me so long to say goodbye to everyone at a party that I have to start over and say goodbye to everyone again. We need a socially acceptable way to say goodbye to everyone at a party at once.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: People complain that we don't have seasons in California. But that's not true. We have one season and it's the good one. We're fine with that.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Vladimir Putin lashed out again at the United States. This time it was for giving an Emmy Award to the Liberace movie, "Behind the Candelabra."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Congratulations to "Breaking Bad." It won the Emmy for best drama last night. When "Breaking Bad" won, they thanked their agents, their families, and of course the makers of Sudafed.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Don't confuse "Breaking Bad" with the New York Giants — that's “PLAYING Bad.” They lost to the Carolina Panthers 38-0. Their game was so bad it was featured in the Emmys "In Memoriam" segment last night.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Britney Spears has signed a two-year deal to perform at Planet Hollywood in Las Vegas. If you go to Vegas you don’t want to miss that show. They say seeing Britney in concert is the closest thing to seeing her sing live.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: California has been invaded by four new species of lizards, and they're legless. Every time a new species is discovered, why is it some kind of slimy lizard or slug thing? Why can't they discover a long-lost, extra-cute kitty cat or a super-cuddly ferret?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Isn't a legless lizard just a snake? No, it isn't. A snake doesn't have eyelids; a legless lizard does. A snake can coil up; a legless lizard can't. There are only two species that can shed the skin in one piece — a snake and Bruce Jenner.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Snakes lost their legs because they never used them. It's some evolution thing. Apparently, it's the same reason Scottish people lost their optimism.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Does anyone have the new iPhone? Analysts say Apple's actual manufacturing cost for the iPhone is $199. That's just parts though. When you add in labor, it's $200.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Psychologists now believe that adulthood begins at 25, not 18. They also believe that middle age begins the first time you eat at a Denny's while sober.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The NBA is considering introducing jerseys with players' nicknames rather than their last names. Players like the nickname jersey because it's easier for fans to relate to them and harder for women looking for child support to find them.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Miley Cyrus went skydiving for the first time. Actually she started twerking on a plane and the other passengers threw her off.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Texas Senator Ted Cruz began a filibuster on the Senate floor. He's trying to stop Obamacare and he vowed to keep speaking until he is no longer able to stand. And the good news: If he collapses from exhaustion he'll be covered under Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Tomorrow night AMC will begin airing a "Breaking Bad" marathon that will show every episode of the show leading up to Sunday's series finale. This is how it ends: Walter White dies in a hospital waiting room while filling out all the paperwork for Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: At the U.N. this week, President Obama met with the president of Nigeria, who advised President Obama to eliminate America's debt by sending out fraudulent emails.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama is now making a case for raising the debt limit. He said that raising the debt limit does not increase debt. And, you know, I have to defer to the president on this one because when it comes to increasing the debt, Obama knows what he's talking about.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Bill Clinton gave the keynote address today at the Clinton Global Initiative, the charity he started in 2005. Sometimes when presidents retire, they take it easy. But they quickly realize that if you're not the president, nobody cares about you or anything you have to say. It is a condition also known as "being vice president."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Being president is one of the most stressful jobs in the world. It's right up there with being Paula Deen's publicist.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I wonder what President Obama will do when he retires. I bet it will involve giving back somehow. He'll make sure those in the developing world have the most important things they need to succeed — like a fake Hawaiian birth certificate.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: At most companies the official retirement age is 65. Not in TV. In TV you can work as long as you want — as long as you don't make the mistake of winning your time slot. That will cause NBC to throw you out. Sorry, Jay.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Today's the annual grand opening of the U.N. We have leaders from all over the world, and when they come here they have diplomatic immunity. They can do whatever they want, break any kind of laws. I saw a dictator today walking up Broadway carrying a 16-ounce soda.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The U.N. General Assembly is here in New York City. Today, President Obama gave a big speech on the Middle East. The leaders from the Middle East said, "You have touched our hearts, and from now on we shall have peace." And Obama said, "Really?" and they said, "No, but the look on your face was priceless."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Home Depot just announced that that it will cut health insurance for its part-time workers because of Obamacare. Home Depot's CEO said he had a hard time breaking the news to employees. That's because it took him three hours to find one.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Russian President Vladimir Putin just revealed he may run for a fourth term in 2018. In fact, he already came up with a few campaign posters. One says, "I will put middle-class families first — on bus to Siberia."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Another Putin poster said, "Putin in 2018, whether you vote or not."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It has been an exciting week so far. Last night Paul McCartney was here. He played a big show in front of at least 10,000 fans outside. And tonight, Justin Timberlake is live. And then tomorrow America votes and one will be eliminated from music.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight on ABC is the premiere of "Marvel's Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D." It's the most highly anticipated show ever with six periods.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: S.H.I.E.L.D. is a secret government agency that helps The Avengers fight crime, so the show is not about superheroes. It's essentially a show about the administrative assistants to superheroes.

name: Conan O'Brien

monologue: Consumer Reports is now recommending that people sit back and wait a few weeks until the government fixes the problems. Really, a few weeks? When was the last time the government fixed anything in a few weeks? We still have troops in Korea, OK?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A new book claims that John F. Kennedy's brain was stolen by his brother Bobby. That seems almost unbelievable, doesn't it? — that there was once a time in this country when politicians actually had brains worth stealing.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Dodgers manager, Don Mattingly, said that just because he has a contract and took his team to first place in their division doesn't mean he'll be back next year. Hey, tell me about it!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Obamacare website has all these glitches and now tech experts are saying that the only way to fix it is to completely start over and redesign the whole website from scratch. While the guys from the Geek Squad said, "Turn it off, wait five seconds, and then plug it back in."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Only 12 percent of Americans think the rollout of Obamacare is going well, while 100 percent of Republicans think the rollout of Obamacare is going GREAT.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: With all the trouble with the Obamacare website, 12 percent of Americans actually think it's going well. Then people waiting for healthcare said, “Can you share some of the drugs you're on with the rest of us?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Here's some more news out of Washington. The White House has fired one of its national security officials for setting up an anonymous Twitter account that was leaking internal information. President Obama called the invasion of privacy “unacceptable,” while Americans called it “karma.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Halloween is just over a week away now. When it comes to candy bars, the term fun-sized is misleading. There is nothing fun about your candy bar being 1/8 the size of a regular bar. You should call them what they are: “disappointment-sized.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Market research released a list of America's favorite Halloween candies. No. 1 is Reese's Peanut Butter Cups. Can't argue with that. This year's least favorite candy — Lentil M&M;'s.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Despite our love of candy and fast food, the number of Americans who will live to be 100 years or older will increase dramatically. In 2010 there were 53,000 centenarians in the United States, and I have driven behind every single one.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you hit 110 years old, you become what now is labeled as a super-centenarian. Should we be putting the word "super" in front of someone who has no powers at all?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There's been a lot of speculation but now it's clear that Joe Biden will run for president in 2016. In an effort to appear presidential, today Biden launched a website that doesn't work.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: One of the contractors who built the Obamacare website testified before Congress today. You can tell he built the site because any time they would ask a question, he would freeze.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: German Chancellor Angela Merkel said the U.S. would have to regain her trust after the NSA eavesdropped on her cellphone. You know things are bad when we're being accused of having boundary issues by Germany.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: People have been speculating lately about what President Obama will do when he leaves office in 2016. The one thing I think we can safely rule out — website designer.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Some marketing experts are comparing the Obamacare website rollout to a Ford Edsel filled with New Coke. But they are making progress. They said today that if you find yourself getting too frustrated trying to log on, they’ve added a link to a suicide hot line.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: What the president should do is put the NSA in charge of the website. That way there’s nothing to fill out. They already have all our information. You just put your name in.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Saudi Arabia is now threatening to sever diplomatic ties with the United States over Syria. I hope that doesn't cause them to do something drastic, you know, like overcharge us for oil.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday Pakistan's Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif was in the Oval Office to meet with Obama and Joe Biden. Obama said, “It's an honor to have you here,” while Biden said, "Hello, I'm not supposed to talk.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There's talk that Apple is getting ready to stop making the iPod now that users can listen to music on their phones. Yeah, they say the product is quickly becoming dated and obsolete — and then RadioShack said, “We'll take a billion of 'em!”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new survey found that 25 percent of Americans will spend less on Halloween this year because of the government shutdown's effect on the economy. Which explains that new party game — “Bobbing for Ramen Noodles.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Last night was game one of the World Series between the St. Louis Cardinals and Boston Red Sox. I'll tell you one thing: These players need to shave. If I want to see a bunch of bearded men battling for a ring, I will watch "The Hobbit."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: YouTube has an interesting new way of making money. They are allowing users who have 10,000 subscribers to set up their own paid YouTube channels. My one complaint about YouTube has always been that it's free.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NASA has successfully tested a broadband communications system that’s built into the lunar atmosphere explorer probe. It sends data to and from the moon at the rate of 622 megabits per second. To the moon and back in a second. In a related story, the Obamacare website is still down.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I tried to log on to the Obamacare website today. I don’t think I'm doing it right. I lost 300 bucks playing Texas Hold 'Em.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The White House now says the Obamacare website will be fixed by the end of November. So if your doctor has only given you three weeks to live, sorry pal.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This seems kind of insensitive, but ABC announced that they are going to make a sitcom about a man with Alzheimer's. It's called “I Forget How I Met Your Mother.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Another scandal with the National Security Agency, the NSA. You know how they've been accused of spying on Americans? Well, it just came out that they actually spied on 35 world leaders. Yeah, it was 34 prime ministers and Oprah.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new report found that 700 IRS employees owe a combined $5.4 million in back taxes. When IRS workers got the news, they said, "Oh man, I hope I don't find out about this!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A man in Oregon was arrested for growing marijuana after police used Google Earth to track him down. So if you're one of those crazy conspiracy theorists who thinks the government is watching you with satellites from space, you were right.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new survey found that nearly half of people who join Twitter never actually use it. Which explains Twitter's new nickname: “the gym.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: Halloween is Thursday. I love Halloween. You open the door, and there are strangers in masks. Good idea.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There are new reports that the NSA has been monitoring communications of 35 leaders. Germany's Angela Merkel is one of our closest allies and she is not happy about this. She called President Obama to give him an earful — and it takes a lot to get those ears full.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If the NSA agents are like most men they were probably only pretending to listen to what she was saying anyway.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: They ought to take all of the guys who are so good at hacking into phone calls and put them to work fixing HealthCare.gov. We need to reallocate our nerds.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new report, more than 700 fake Obamacare websites have been created. Security experts say it's simple to identify the phony sites because they are easy to log on to.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The White House said today that one of the reasons the Obamacare website has had so many problems is because it's so popular that it was overwhelmed. Really? How come Psy's "Gangnam Style" video never had any problems? He got 2.5 billion hits!

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Have you tried to log on to the Obamacare website? It’s slow. It is slower than my watch during an interview with Paris Hilton.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Obamacare website is not the only one crashing. The NSA website went offline Friday after suspected hackers broke into it. Hey, NSA: It’s not so much fun when people are sneaking into YOUR computer, is it?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Over the weekend it came out that the U.S. has been listening in on German Chancellor Angela Merkel’s cellphone since 2002. At this point, I feel like the only world leader our government DOESN'T listen to is President Obama.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The U.S. has been spying on German Chancellor Angela Merkel for more than 10 years. Merkel actually called Obama to say that eavesdropping on allies “is not acceptable.” Then Obama said, "Yeah, well that's not what you said to England."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Halloween is just a couple of days away. A new survey found that 10 percent of Americans actually plan on wearing a costume to work for Halloween. Because if there's anything better than getting fired on Halloween, it's getting fired by a clown.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: One poll says 74 percent of Americans will hand out candy to trick-or-treaters. While the other 26 percent plan to spend three hours hiding in the living room with the lights out.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's great to be back. We had reruns last week. No, what are they called? Encore presentations.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Last week I was in Canada. I was doing stand-up and solving crimes. Actually, there's no crime in Canada.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Two American icons celebrate birthdays today. The Statue of Liberty turns 127 years old. And Bruce Jenner, who of course is also 127 years old.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Statue of Liberty and Bruce Jenner are very different, of course. One is made of copper and steel and needs constant work done to prevent it from crumbling and cracking — and the other one's the Statue of Liberty.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: All week we're celebrating 20 years of being on late-night TV. This week we celebrate 20 years of jokes and 20 years of Andy Richter's fake laughing.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: We are posting online many of our rare or never-before-seen clips from the show's past 20 years. You can see them online but if you really want a laugh, go to HealthCare.gov. That's where the good chuckles are.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It has been 20 years on the air and everyone in my family is very emotional. My dad called me this morning and he told me something he has never said to me before. He said, "Son, we don't have cable TV." I wept for an hour.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Just when you thought the state of American healthcare couldn't get any worse, Dr. Conrad Murray, Michael Jackson's doctor, has been released from jail.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: For years President Obama has been saying that no one would lose their healthcare plan. Now the White House has admitted that in fact many people will lose their plans. But there is a way to keep the great coverage you have. Just become a member of Congress. Then the taxpayers pay for the whole thing.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There was some good news today for embattled Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius. Obamacare will cover all her injuries after the White House throws her under the bus. She is totally covered.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Have you tried to get on the Obamacare website? Oh, it is slow! It is so slow that by the time you sign up for Obamacare you’ll be eligible for Medicare. It's slower than a ticket scalper at a Jacksonville Jaguars game.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Bob Barker will appear on "The Price Is Right" to mark his 90th birthday. Bob said he'll do something he should have been done long ago — spay and neuter Drew Carey.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: President Obama is still in trouble for this spying stuff. You can tell he is getting tired of talking about this scandal. Today he said, "Anyone want to talk about my birth certificate?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Obama is also being criticized for the Obamacare website. You know what's wrong with that website? A lot of the people trying to sign up for Obamacare are elderly. So you've already lost them at "website."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Jonas Brothers have broken up. The music industry is in mourning. It's kind of like when the Beatles announced they were breaking up — minus the part where people gave a crap.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Guess who's out of prison? Dr. Conrad Murray. He was sentenced to four years in prison, and he served only two years. But he had to serve his time in the prison waiting room.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Krispy Kreme says it will give a free doughnut to any customer who shows up wearing a costume on Halloween. So if you're the kind of person willing to take the time to dress up in a costume just to get a free doughnut, then yes, you've hit rock bottom.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that eating pasta can actually cause depression. Though not as much as that other thing — dressing up like Batman to get a free doughnut.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Americans are expected to spend more than $2 billion on Halloween candy this year. And those Americans are Honey Boo Boo and Mama June.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A blooper reel from the original "Star Wars" movies was leaked online this week. That's right — a series of embarrassing "Star Wars" mistakes caught on film. Or as fans call that: the last three "Star Wars" movies.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Red Sox are up 3-2 in the World Series with the last two games at home in Boston. Cardinals fans are not feeling good, but it ain't over until the lady who is actually a healthy weight but made to feel fat adhering to impossible standards set by advertisers sings.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: As baseball wraps up, a new NBA season tips off. It's the special time when we have baseball, football, and basketball at the same time — the holy trinity of ignoring our families.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight the Lakers played the Clippers. Here's an interesting fact: When L.A. basketball teams play each other, a new baby Kardashian is born.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: According to the National Retail Federation, around 158 million people will celebrate Halloween in the United States this year, down from 170 million last year. How does the National Retail Federation know this? I don't know if I am going to celebrate Halloween — but they do?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Scientists from New Zealand have discovered a new species of dolphin. They say it's delicious.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tickets for tonight's World Series game cost more than any baseball tickets in history. The average price was $2,000. So you could sell your car to buy a couple or grow a disgusting beard and pretend you are on the Red Sox and sneak in.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Cardinals were very late getting into Boston last night. A mechanical problem delayed their flight for six hours and they didn't get in until 11 p.m. Ironically, the team named after a bird had trouble flying.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If the Cardinals win tonight, Game 7 will be on Halloween. How great would it be if the players dressed up for Halloween? Imagine seeing Batman hit a home run off Frankenstein.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It's really trick-or-treat time at the White House. President Obama tricked us into thinking we'd be able to afford treatment.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Con artists are using Obamacare confusion to sign people up for fake health insurance. The scammers lure victims with false promises like, "If you like your healthcare plan, you can keep your healthcare plan." The scammers will tell you that, so you have to be careful.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A lot of people are accusing the president of being less than truthful. In fact, a couple of weeks ago President Obama called me and told me personally that if I like my current job, I can keep my current job. And I believed him!

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The president said he didn't know that we were spying on our allies. He didn't know about the problems with the healthcare website. Have you heard the latest? Now the president claims he doesn’t know how "Breaking Bad" ended.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Halloween is tomorrow night, and a woman from North Dakota says she's planning on giving overweight trick-or-treaters a letter explaining that sugar is bad for them — instead of giving them candy. Then those kids will hand HER a letter saying, "Toilet paper or eggs?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Wal-Mart just announced that it is giving 25,000 employees a promotion. Wal-Mart employees said, "You mean we get to go work at Target?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Wal-Mart will promote 25,000 of its employees, which means they're getting more responsibilities. In fact, greeters will also get to say “goodbye.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that 30 percent of Americans admit to getting most of their news on Facebook. You can tell news anchors are trying to compete with Facebook because tonight Brian Williams' top story was just a picture of his cat.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Halloween's eve is also known as mischief night. Kids are supposed go around playing pranks tonight. That's great, just what teenagers need — another excuse to be jerks.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Some grocery stores refuse to sell eggs to teenagers on mischief night. Isn't that terrible? It makes me feel bad for well-behaved kids just looking to make an omelet.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: One of the big mischief things is writing on people's cars with soap. I always think that's hilarious. So let me give you the address of Jay Leno.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: You know who's known for playing pranks? George Clooney. He pulls pranks on movie sets. He played one on me once. It's a true story. Back in 2007, I actually paid 10 bucks to see "Oceans 13." You got me, George!

name: David Letterman
monologue: Did everybody have a good Halloween? I'm just not into the Halloween spirit. What I did was I went to bed early after I turned on the electric fence.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Did you all have a fun Halloween? One little kid came to my door dressed as Justin Bieber. Then I realized that it WAS Justin Bieber.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Six kids showed up for Halloween with no costumes at all, just dressed like ordinary people. They said, "We're the six people who signed up for Obamacare on the first day."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to CBS News, only six people enrolled in Obamacare on the first day of the rollout. Six! That means more people have walked on the moon than have signed up for Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: This is my favorite part. Hand to God, this is the absolute truth. The White House said that the number six is not official. Really, aren't they better off saying nothing? Not official? What, if we wait it could go as high as seven?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This weekend is the end of daylight saving time. Or, put another way, your microwave is about to have the right time on it again.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night the Obamas gave out dried fruit to more than 5,000 trick-or-treaters. In a related story, today workers outside the White House had to sweep up a bunch of dried fruit.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: That same study also found that fruit has become the second most popular food in the U.S. The first most popular food in the U.S.? NOT fruit.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There are reports that a spin-off of “How I Met Your Mother” is in the works called "How I Met Your Father." I think I’ve seen that show already. It’s called “Maury.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today is World Vegan Day. It’s the day we're all supposed to think about a vegan diet . . . There, I thought about it. It's not for me.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Vegans can't eat eggs. They can't eat dairy. From what I've seen, they can't even shave their legs.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Ozzy Osbourne recently started a vegan diet. Right now up in animal heaven, there's a bat without a head saying, "Oh, so now he's vegan."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Mike Tyson is a vegan. Apparently, vegans can't eat meat or dairy, but it's OK to occasionally nibble on Evander Holyfield's ear.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Forbes magazine has named evil Russian President Vladimir Putin as the most powerful person in the world. Vladimir Putin, the most powerful person in the world. Number two: Kelly Ripa.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday everybody gained an hour from daylight saving time. Well, now you're about to waste one, so it's going to come out perfectly even.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This weekend had the first YouTube awards. Eminem won. Second runner-up was a cat walking across a piano.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: On Sunday, the New York City Marathon was won in both the men's and women's divisions by Kenyans. Coming in a close second were some other Kenyans.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: British scientists are saying King Tut died in a chariot accident. I think he was texting.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Did you all turn your clocks back an hour over the weekend? It is easy to remember "spring ahead, fall back." It's like trying to log on to Obamacare. You spring ahead, make a little progress, then you fall back.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to CBS news, on the first day of open enrollment for Obamacare, only six people signed up. Today they released their names: They are Sneezy, Sleepy, Happy, Bashful, Grumpy, and Doc. That’s according to the creator of the website: Dopey.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NSA leaker Edward Snowden got a new job in Moscow. Not only that, but he was also able to sign up for "PutinCare."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new study out of Harvard, it is easier for people to be moral in the morning. They say people are more moral at the beginning of the day, but they become more dishonest as the day goes on. So when people say Congress is as dishonest as the day is long, we now have scientific proof.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: We have Arizona Senator John McCain on the show tonight. We'll talk to him about the government shutdown, Obamacare, and of course his surprise third-place finish at yesterday's New York City Marathon.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie is hoping to win re-election tomorrow, and polls show that he's winning by a 19-point margin. Christie was really excited to hear that — but only because he thought someone said "margarine."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Chris Christie has really worked hard on the campaign. I heard he spent all weekend shaking hands and kissing bagels.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I just heard that the Kellogg’s cereal company is cutting 7 percent of its workforce because of low revenue. Or as one guy put it, “Not Grrreeat!”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Today is one of my favorite days of the year — the day after daylights saving time ends. There is one negative. It marks the beginning of a four-month period of my clock on my microwave being an hour wrong.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The new iPad came out on Friday. It's the iPad Air. This is what I think is the most interesting thing about it — it's just a box full of air. There's nothing in it. Apple wanted to see what they could get away with and we fell for it again.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I hope you had a fun and festive Halloween. I have a lot of leftover candy. Every day when the mailman comes, I hand him some and tell him his costume is great.

name: David Letterman
monologue: New York City is going to get a new mayor. It's between some tall white guy and some short white guy. That's all I know.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: New Jersey re-elected Governor Chris Christie. Or as Christie put it, "I came back for seconds."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Rand Paul has been accused of cheating in three separate instances. When asked about the charges, Paul said, "Four score and seven years ago . . ."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Some health experts believe being an NFL coach might be the most stressful job in America. The second most stressful job in America is being an NFL parole officer.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Members of "Duck Dynasty" are releasing their own brands of wines. Wine experts are saying that it's red wine with varmints and white wine with critters.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There's now growing concern in Iran about the health of 74-year-old Ayatollah Khamenei, the country's supreme leader. He has a chronic illness. You think healthcare is bad in this country, try seeing a doctor under Ayatollah-Care. See how that works.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: NSA whistle-blower and traitor Edward Snowden, living in asylum in Russia, has released a manifesto directed at the United States claiming that telling the truth should not be a crime. And believe me, there's no better place to celebrate free speech, truth, and equal rights than in Russia.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Scientists say that women with larger butts are smarter. I believe the study was funded by the Kardashian Institute for Scientific Research.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Toronto Mayor Rob Ford has admitted that he smoked crack cocaine. He said, “Yes, I smoked crack, but I was in a drunken stupor when I did it.” Well, at least he had a good excuse.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The White House announced that Joe Biden will travel to Asia to make up for President Obama's trip that was canceled because of the government shutdown. Seriously? That's like Justin Timberlake canceling a show and sending the banjo players from those Geico ads to take his place.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last week CNN had its lowest ratings in more than a year with just 385,000 viewers. You can tell they're worried about money by Wolf Blitzer's new show: "The Situation Roommate."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Rand Paul, the senator from Kentucky, keeps getting into trouble. They say he actually plagiarized an entire section of his 2012 book, “Government Bullies.” When asked for comment, Paul said, "It was the best of times, it was the worst of times."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A school in Tennessee is facing criticism for separating students with bad grades from students with good grades at lunch. That’s crazy! You don’t use grades to separate kids. Everyone knows that kids should be separated by clothes, looks, and how much money their parents make.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In New York they elected a new mayor. He is Bill de Blasio, the first Democrat mayor in 20 years. Now 20 years ago Times Square was filled with strip clubs and porno theaters. So I'm counting on the new mayor to restore it to its former glory.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In New Jersey, they re-elected Chris Christie by a HUGE margin. Is there any other way?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Toronto Mayor Rob Ford fessed up to smoking crack. He said he smoked the crack when he was in "a drunken stupor." Is that a defense? That doesn't absolve you of your behavior. It's like saying, "I killed the guy, but I was drunk." "Well Ok, run along then. Don't do it again."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: How come Rob Ford guy is still in office? I guess Canadians are too polite to tell a crackhead to step down.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Half of the state of Colorado voted to secede from the United States. This is what happens when you legalize marijuana.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The new mayor of New York City is a progressive Democrat with an African-American wife who used to be a lesbian. Or as Fox News reported, the apocalypse is upon us.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The new mayor is married to a woman who used to be a lesbian. His campaign slogan: “If I turned her around, imagine what I can do for New York City!”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Marvel Comics is introducing its first major superhero who is a female Muslim. The female Muslim superhero can fly, which comes in handy because she's not allowed to drive.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie was re-elected by a huge margin. He gave a great speech last night. He said he learned a lot in the last four years — for example, that lap-band surgery doesn't always work.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Chris Christie won by such a wide margin that pundits say this will give him the impetus he needs to run for president. And he's got a new slogan: "Put the oval in the Oval Office."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama's approval rating is down to 39 percent. And Toronto Mayor Rob Ford, who admitted to smoking crack cocaine, went up to 49 percent. How does this make Obama feel? He’d be better off smoking crack than passing Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Miami Dolphins player Richie Incognito has been suspended as the NFL investigates claims of bullying another teammate. The NFL will not tolerate bullying — to which the Jacksonville Jaguars said, “Hey, we get bullied every Sunday!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Bill de Blasio became New York City’s first Democratic mayor in 20 years by getting an amazing 73 percent of the vote. They’re saying a lot of the voting machines were malfunctioning. In fact, there were so many glitches, Bill de Blasio won the mayor’s race AND "Dancing With The Stars."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The mayor of Toronto, Rob Ford, has admitted that he smoked crack a year ago when he was in a quote, “drunken stupor.” Geez, if that guy smokes crack when he's drunk, I'd hate to see what happens when he smokes crack.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Chris Christie won a second term as New Jersey governor last night. We like him. He’s a good guy. Christie said he couldn't have done it without his biggest supporter — and then his belt said, "Happy to help, man."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Chris Christie won a second term as New Jersey governor. And in honor of his big win, I promise no more fat jokes about him tonight. But seriously, the margin of victory was so big, even he could walk through it.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Mayor of Toronto Rob Ford's approval ratings have skyrocketing since he announced that he's smoking crack cocaine. Is EVERYBODY up there on crack? Is that the deal?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today Matt Lauer and Al Roker had prostate exams live on the "Today" show. So the "Today" show has finally cracked the code on what people want to see first thing in the morning.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Colorado, voters have approved a tax on marijuana to fund the building of schools. So kids, don't do drugs but stay in the schools funded by them.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Happy birthday to the Lamborghini automobile company. Lamborghini is now 50 years old. You can tell Lamborghini is 50 because it bought itself a Porsche.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Apparently there is a huge crack cocaine problem in Toronto. Luckily, it’s just confined to the mayor’s office.

name: Jay Leno

monologue: The postal service is now saying that they are raising the price of a stamp from 46 cents to 49 cents. They would have made it an even 50 but that would have made the line at the post office go too fast.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Mayor de Blasio says he wants to get rid of horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, saying they are inhumane. Meanwhile, thousands of unemployed New Yorkers are saying, "I'll pull the carriages. How much an hour?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Winter Olympics are around the corner. President Vladimir Putin says people will be allowed to protest the Winter Olympics as long as they stay in a designated protesting zone. When they asked where the zone is located Putin said, "Poland."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This is our first show of the year. What year is it now? 2014? You know, ever since Dick Clark passed away I can't keep track of it.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Most people resolve to lose weight or spend time with their family. Or to spend more time telling their family to lose weight.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I didn't make a formal resolution for New Year's. What I do, I look for small areas in which I can improve. I find none and then I go back to eating full jars of peanut butter in the middle of the night. My New Year's resolution is "Keep up the good work, Jim."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: With the wind chill it got down to 63 below zero in parts of Montana. At that temperature, if you remove your hat your thoughts will actually freeze inside your brain.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Dennis Rodman has brought some former NBA stars to North Korea. Not to promote diplomacy — to avoid child support payments.

monologue: In Las Vegas, "Transformers" director Michael Bay stormed offstage after a teleprompter wasn't showing his speech. They said he hasn't walked out on anything since he saw the last "Transformers" movie.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Seattle, a woman ate nothing but Starbucks food for a year. Not intentionally. It just took her that long to get to the front of the line.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You know it’s New Year's when Father Time makes way for the “New Year’s baby.” Or as NBC calls that, ''Leno and Fallon.''

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In advance of the Winter Olympics in Sochi, the Russian government announced that, contrary to popular belief, people in Russia will be allowed to protest. But only in a special protest zone — known as "Siberia."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: According to a new international survey, among Catholics Pope Francis has an approval rating of 88 percent. That is unless he comes out with FrancisCare. Then the whole thing could plummet.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: There was a nuclear meltdown in North Korea today. But enough about Dennis Rodman.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Health experts are calling 2014 "the year of the flu." I think it needs a better name.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Apparently, the dominant strain of the flu this year is the swine flu.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I thought the swine flu was history. But just when we thought it left us, now it has come back to make people sick and wreak more havoc. It's like Dennis Rodman.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Dennis Rodman and the North Koreans — is this an episode of “Scooby-Doo”?

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's 8 degrees today. Tomorrow's going to be 28 degrees. Thank God I didn't put away my tank top.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It’s so cold that doctors are telling people to avoid drinking alcohol if they go outside because it can lead to frostbite. Then parents who've been stuck inside with their kids for three days were like, “It's worth the risk.”

monologue: Today President Obama invited unemployed Americans to the White House for a discussion about income inequality. Because if there's one way to show sympathy for the unemployed, it's to invite them to a giant white mansion that you get to live in for free.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: First lady Michelle Obama is staying at Oprah’s house in Hawaii this week. Oprah told her housekeeper to make sure Michelle has clean linens at all times — then Stedman said, “Yeah yeah, heard you the first time.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Dennis Rodman is back in North Korea. And now he’s facing a lot of criticism over a new interview where he said that North Korea is “not that bad.” Even Kim Jong Un was like, “Uh, yeah, it kind of is.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was 73 degrees here in Hollywood today. I almost started to feel guilty but then I remembered that a lot of you may have the cold to deal with, but here in California we have Gary Busey to worry about and that's all year long.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Dennis Rodman took six former NBA players to North Korea to play against a local team in celebration of Kim Jong Un's 31st birthday. I guess after years of playing alongside Michael Jordan, Rodman is very comfortable with totalitarian dictators.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Dennis Rodman is like the uncle that Kim Jong Un never had killed.

name: David Letterman

monologue: Everyone is fine but Honey Boo Boo's family was involved in a minor traffic accident. Apparently their home rear-ended their neighbor's home.

monologue: McDonald's restaurants in Japan have started selling cheese fries that you can't get here in the United States. That makes me wonder: Who really won World War II?

monologue: The government is accusing the makers of several weight loss products of deceiving the public. Probably the most deceptive of these companies — Cinnabon.

monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie doesn't know yet if he's running for president in 2016. I guess he'll cross that bridge when he comes to it.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Pundits are saying this could hurt his 2016 presidential campaign. The ironic thing is this: Now that Christie is denying everything he sounds even more presidential, doesn’t he?

monologue: After his denial, Christie quickly left the news conference to deal with a more personal crisis: the Velveeta cheese shortage.

monologue: Chris Christie is dealing with a scandal after it was revealed that a top aide shut down access to the George Washington Bridge to get back at a mayor for not endorsing him. Christie was furious when they blocked the bridge. He thought they said they were blocking the FRIDGE.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Chris Christie held a press conference today to address the bridge scandal. He insisted that he is not a bully — and he will sit on anyone who says otherwise.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday, President Obama gave photographers a rare chance to take pictures of his weekly lunch with Joe Biden. Then Biden told his friends, "Told you I knew the president."

monologue: Chris Christie is embroiled in a scandal involving lane closures near the George Washington Bridge. The scandal could damage Christie's chances of getting nominated for president in 2016, but he'll probably bounce back. He seems like a pretty bouncy person.

monologue: Iran is encouraging families to have more children to boost the population. They have a plan to give a gold coin to any family that has a baby. name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Right now Iran's population is around 80 million. Their supreme leader wants to get it up to 150 million. If he wants more pregnancies, he should start by legalizing alcohol over there.

monologue: Christie apologized and promised the bridge will stay open for cars, trucks, and the buses he's throwing his staff under.

monologue: A Japanese company bought the Jim Beam whiskey distillery for $16 billion. This morning the Japanese company woke up in an alley and said, "I did what?"

monologue: Justin Bieber could be facing felony charges after egging his neighbor's home. In his defense, his neighbor was blasting Justin Bieber music.

monologue: Did you all watch the Golden Globes last night? The big winner was “American Hustle,” a film about the marketing of Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: We're learning more about this George Washington Bridge scandal. During the traffic jam, a two-block commute that would normally take five minutes took 45 minutes to an hour. As we call that in L.A., “making pretty good time.” We would kill for that on the 405 Freeway.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In the wake of this embarrassing scandal, Governor Chris Christie has fired the person responsible. To which President Obama said: "You can do that?"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: A big hit at the Consumer Electronics Show is an ultra-HD TV with four times the resolution of today's TVs. They say it should be available in a few weeks, just in time to see a brighter and more vivid . . . Jimmy Fallon!

monologue: Alex Rodriguez has been suspended for all of next year's baseball season. And he says he's taking Major League Baseball to federal court. Experts say A-Rod's case is fairly weak. But that'll change when he injects himself with steroids.

monologue: There's usually an asterisk next to my name anyway. It says "creepy foreigner."

name: David Letterman
monologue: Did you watch the Golden Globes show last night? What a wonderful show, what a tremendous show. Three hours of actors thanking their agents.

monologue: Tomorrow Chris Christie is expected to unveil his agenda for this year. When asked what he’s planning for next year, Christie said, “I’ll close that bridge when I get to it.”

monologue: Yeah, French President Francois Hollande had an affair with a younger woman. When asked about it, he said, "At least I did not eat pizza with a knife and fork!"

monologue: Last night was the annual Golden Globes. It was, I have to say, unbelievable how much of this show was spent watching people try to get to the stage. Some of the winners are still making their way to the stage.

monologue: Alex Rodriguez of the Yankees is being suspended 162 games without pay for using performance-enhancing drugs. And those are baseball games. Think about how long one baseball game is. Multiply that by 162. We'll be living on Mars by the time A-Rod can play again.

monologue: A-Rod's suspension is the longest doping penalty in the history of baseball. So another record for A-Rod. What a career he's had.

monologue: Between A-Rod and Dennis Rodman this has been a bad week for people with "Rod" in their names.

monologue: We have a breakdown of the regimen of banned substances that Alex Rodriguez took daily. Four injections of performance-enhancing drugs. Two testosterone lozenges. two different skin creams. A handful of anti-aging pills. And a Tic-Tac.

monologue: It was announced that President Obama is going to visit Pope Francis. Obama said he can't wait to tell the Pope, "You know, they liked me a lot, too, that first year."

monologue: President Obama will visit Pope Francis. The president said, "I'm looking forward to meeting the one old white guy who's not bashing Obamacare."

monologue: Justin Bieber reportedly caused $20,000 in damage to his neighbor's home by egging it. It's being called the most pointless use of an egg since the fertilization of Justin Bieber.

monologue: The Labor Department reported that last month 347,000 people quit looking for work. And in New Jersey, 50,000 people quit DRIVING to work.

monologue: Today New Jersey Governor Chris Christie delivered his state of the state address: he said the state is improving, but admitted that it's still New Jersey.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Governor Christie said he wants to do all he can to keep people from leaving New Jersey. That’s why he closed the bridge. He was trying to do some good.

monologue: Last week in Miami, Beyoncé crashed a karaoke bar and started singing one of her own songs. Not to be outdone, Britney Spears crashed the same bar and lip-synced one of her own songs.

monologue: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie continues to push his agenda. Today he proposed a longer school day for children in his state. In fairness, kids in New Jersey probably need a longer day since their buses spend three hours stuck on a bridge.

monologue: A new report found that more than half of the people who have signed up for Obamacare are older than 45. Which is no big deal until you find out they were 25 when they first tried to log onto the website.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week Beyoncé wrote an essay online where she calls for women and men to get paid the same amount. When they heard that, men were like, “Sweet! We'd love to get paid as much as Beyoncé.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that couples who don’t have kids end up having happier marriages. So to anyone whose parents got divorced, I guess it WAS your fault.

monologue: Justin Bieber was accused of egging his neighbor's house. The neighbor claimed he caused about $20,000 in damage. He throws Fabergé eggs only.

monologue: About a dozen of the sheriff's deputies showed up at Justin Bieber's house with a search warrant. I guess they were looking for eggs, I don't know.

monologue: The rollout of the Affordable Care Act continues to be terrible. Now comes news that not enough young, healthy Americans are signing up. Did they expect young people to buy insurance the same time that Play Station 4 comes out?

monologue: Alex Rodriguez has a lot of trouble. He is suing everybody in baseball, and meanwhile he is terribly out of shape. He hasn't played ball in a long time. Gee, I wonder what a guy like that does to get back into top physical condition.

monologue: Country music star Trace Adkins was on a cruise ship. He got in a brawl with a Trace Adkins impersonator. Nobody is exactly sure who won.

monologue: Oprah's movie "The Butler" was not nominated for the best picture Oscar. Oprah is said to be very disappointed but she's being comforted but her 700 REAL butlers.

monologue: The movie "Gravity" received 10 nominations. It's the film where Sandra Bullock achieves what every Hollywood actress dreams of — true weightlessness.

monologue: Justin Bieber's egg-throwing scandal is rocking the judicial world. If Justin is convicted of a felony, he could be deported back to Canada. American officials are hopeful they can get "deported" changed to "catapulted."

monologue: The White House announced that President Obama will visit Pope Francis in the near future. Pope Francis thinks Obamacare can be a success. Sure, he’s the Pope. He has to believe in miracles.

monologue: Health authorities say they're seeing a massive increase in antibiotic drug-resistant diseases and are predicting a worldwide epidemic of diseases we can no longer treat. That's great news, huh? We finally get healthcare and now we've got diseases you can't treat.

monologue: They say that most airline seats on planes today are meant for 170-pound passengers. The last time the average American weighed 170 pounds, the Wright Brothers were flying the plane.

monologue: Health officials are now warning that pot smoking can cause apathy. In fact, a recent poll shows that most pot smokers couldn't care less.

monologue: This week country singer Trace Adkins was on a country music-themed cruise when he got into a fight with a Trace Adkins impersonator. It was a nasty brawl. In fact, it took five Elvises to pull them apart.

monologue: The Oscar nominations came out today. The movies up for Best Picture this year include “Gravity,” “Her,” and “American Hustle.” Or as my mom refers to them, “Doctor from 'ER' in space,” “The guy who talks to his voice mail,” and “Your father used to dress like that when we were dating.”

monologue: A new study found that more than 11 million people have quit Facebook in the last three years. And unfortunately, none of them were your parents.

monologue: Award nominations and search warrants are the only things that wake celebrities up early nowadays.
