monologue: Yesterday the Denver Broncos and the Seattle Seahawks advanced to the big game, which means this year’s Super Bowl will have teams from the two states where recreational marijuana is legal. Or as pizza delivery men put it, "Pray for us."

monologue: If you're planning to drive across the river and cross the George Washington Bridge to attend the Super Bowl, you'd better leave now.

monologue: Olympic gold medalist Carl Lewis says Governor Chris Christie canceled a position for him when he did something Christie didn't like. When asked what he did, Lewis said "a sit-up."

monologue: The former president of Trader Joe's is opening a store that sells only expired food. The new store will be known as 7-Eleven.

monologue: France's first lady is suffering from extreme fatigue after learning of her husband's affair with an actress. I don't know why she's tired. He's the one juggling two women.

monologue: We are so lucky to live here in California with a huge snowstorm back east. Actually, Governor Chris Christie is very happy about this weather. He's got something else to blame the road closures on.

monologue: Yeah, 14 hours about President Roosevelt. Which sounds like too much until you realize there's been over 30 hours of TV dedicated to Honey Boo Boo.

monologue: Meteorologists say New York City is experiencing “blizzard-like conditions.” I'm no expert, but by gosh, isn't that a blizzard?

monologue: Target just announced that it is dropping health insurance for part-time employees and they’re blaming it on Obamacare. I guess now if Target employees need to pay for healthcare, they'll just have to use their customers' credit cards.

monologue: Justin Bieber was arrested in Miami Beach on a DUI. He was also busted for resisting arrest and drag racing. Justin was clocked going 60 miles an hour in a Lamborghini. Wow, 60 miles an hour in a Lamborghini? Hey Justin, it’s called second gear. Try it sometime.

monologue: Really, 60 miles an hour? But to be fair, Bieber was in Florida. Anything over 20 miles an hour is considered drag racing.

monologue: Over the weekend the Miami Heat took away Justin Bieber's courtside seats. When asked why, a spokesperson for the Heat said Bieber is not acting like an NBA fan. He's acting like an NBA player.

monologue: The mayor of Sochi, Russia, said that his city has no gay people. Yeah. Then his son said, "Dad, we need to talk."

monologue: The company making the food for this year’s Super Bowl says it will offer healthy choices like kale sandwiches. So if you're hungry at the Super Bowl, now you know where the shortest line for food will be.

monologue: I saw that Oprah Winfrey will celebrate her 60th birthday this week. Yep, 60, so just five more years until she can start collecting that sweet Social Security.

monologue: Health officials are now saying that Britain's obesity rate is almost the same as the rate in the U.S. Yeah, the average British person weighs 190 pounds. Or to us, 300 dollars.

monologue: Couples of all sexual orientations were married on the telecast of the Grammys in a mass ceremony. Getting married during the Grammys is a great way to save money on the videographer. You just have to program the DVR.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was a strange show. Daft Punk won five Grammy awards. Neither one of these guys ever showed his face. By the way, this is how the robots will enslave us. First they take our Grammys. And then they take our freedom.

monologue: How do we even know that was Daft Punk? I mean, it could have been anybody in an outfit. I don't believe Daft Punk even exists, to tell you the truth.

monologue: A lot of fake Super Bowl merchandise is out there, so be very careful to check the serial number before you buy that Peyton Manning bobblehead doll.

monologue: President Obama's chief speechwriter said the president started working on his State of the Union address around Thanksgiving. In a related story today, Joe Biden finished GIVING a speech he started around Thanksgiving.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's tradition that one cabinet member does not attend the State of the Union address and is kept in a secret, undisclosed location. So this year the cabinet member will be on a prime-time show on NBC.

monologue: The royal family has reportedly burned through its money and is now strapped for cash. In fact, Queen Elizabeth needs money so badly she's now co-starring in the next Nicolas Cage movie.

monologue: Toronto Mayor Rob Ford is in the news. He claims he found a way to bring in $50 million for Toronto. America will pay him to take Justin Bieber back.

monologue: Earlier tonight President Obama gave his State of the Union address. Or, as Fox News called it, "Lame Duck Dynasty."

monologue: In his speech tonight, President Obama urged Congress to raise the minimum wage. Now don't confuse that with congressional minimum wage. See, that's doing the minimum for your wage. That's completely different.

monologue: This was a very important speech for the president tonight and he gave it at a time when he's losing support from his own party. In fact, congressional Democrats were warned tonight that if they didn't applaud the president's speech, he would go out and campaign for them.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Iran says they want to encourage more tourism from the United States. They might want to change that "Death to America" slogan. A lot of families are not comfortable with that.

monologue: The president’s State of the Union address was tonight. And just three weeks after the "Bridge-gate" scandal, the mayor of Fort Lee, New Jersey, was invited to attend the speech. When he heard that, Chris Christie said, “Good luck getting there.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actually, that Fort Lee mayor should feel right at home in Congress — you know, since they're a bunch of gridlocked people who are angry with the guy in front of them.

monologue: During a speech yesterday, Hillary Clinton said she still doesn’t know if she’s running for president in 2016. You know, just like I still "don't know" if I'll have a beer on St. Patrick's Day.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The big TV event tonight — not too many people want to watch but it's on every channel so we do anyway — is the president's annual State of the Union address.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The first address broadcast live on TV by a president was given by Harry Truman in 1947, and since then it's really just an annual competition between Democrats and Republicans who see who can fake clap the loudest.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: President Obama did not touch upon the ongoing Justin Bieber crisis.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A petition on the WhiteHouse.gov website asks the U.S. to deport Justin Bieber. If they get 100,000 signatures, the White House has to respond. They already have 87,000. The Canadian military is scrambling jets and mobilizing troops along the border to make sure this doesn't happen.

name: David Letterman
monologue: How many of you folks watched the State of the Union speech last night? How many of you watched just for the commercials?

monologue: At last night's State of the Union address, President Obama renewed his call for a path to citizenship for illegal aliens. Yeah, that was popular. Even more popular, though, was his roadblock to citizenship for Justin Bieber. That went over huge.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: You heard about the snowstorm in Georgia. A snowstorm in Atlanta resulted in a 10-hour traffic jam. To which people in Los Angeles responded, "You guys need snow for that?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In anticipation of the Winter Olympics, a female curling champion released some sexy photos of herself curling in lingerie. When asked for comment, Americans said they're still not going to watch curling.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The owner of the Ringling Brothers circus has become America's latest billionaire. Yeah, he got rich by paying his workers peanuts.

monologue: As you know, President Obama gave his State of the Union address last night. Obama says he wants to give “America a raise.” He’s just waiting, of course, for final approval from China. As soon as they say it’s OK, then we’ll move ahead.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The president said that unemployment is dropping, but critics claim it doesn't include people who have left the workforce. How about people who were asked to leave the workforce like me? Are we included in that?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: President Obama asked that Americans pitch in and help those who are most down on their luck — like the Lakers. I think he mentioned them by name.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It seems that England's royal family is running out of money. They are down to just $1.6 million. Well sure, that's what happens when nobody in your family has had a job for the last thousand years.

monologue: Last night of course was the State of the Union address, and during his speech, President Obama promised to focus on economic growth, education, and healthcare. Or as people tuning in put it, "Oh, it's a rerun."

monologue: Fans are expected to eat 21,000 hot dogs on Super Bowl Sunday. So, don’t be surprised when this year’s Budweiser ad doesn’t feature any horses.

monologue: I heard that Justin Bieber is moving out of his $7 million home after he was accused of egging his neighbor's house earlier this month. His neighbors are very happy, while his neighbors' daughter is SO not talking to her parents EVER again.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Oprah turned 60 years old today. Seven more years and she can finally start cashing those Social Security checks.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Justin Bieber was booked for assault for an incident that happened in December. Boy, this kid is on a real crime spree. He's become a menace to society. I liked him better when he was just a menace to music.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: By the way, when you have Justin Bieber and Rob Ford in the same place, it's like Gotham City getting attacked by the Joker and the Penguin at once.

monologue: Yesterday Justin Bieber turned himself in at a Toronto police station for an assault charge. There was confusion when he first arrived. They asked him, "Hey, little girl, have you lost your mommy?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Justin Bieber has been charged with assaulting his Toronto limo driver. The driver is reportedly suffering from minor injuries and from being the laughingstock of the Toronto limousine industry.

monologue: The Super Bowl this year will be played in Governor Chris Christie's home state of New Jersey. It's a state that lately has gotten used to 300-pound guys blocking things.

monologue: This week in New Orleans, Hillary Clinton said she still doesn't know if she's running for president in 2016. Isn’t that unbelievable? With 315 million Americans, what are the odds she’s the only one in the country who doesn’t know she’s running for president in 2016?

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Canadian bad-boy Justin Bieber was arrested in Toronto for beating up a limo driver. Which, of course, is really embarrassing — for the limo driver. He has to admit in open court he got beat up by Justin Bieber.

monologue: A petition to have Justin Bieber deported got over 100,000 signatures, which means the White House now has to legally rule on it. So finally a chance for Obama to issue an executive order that both Republicans and Democrats can agree on.

monologue: Music industry executives are now defending Justin Bieber, saying that he was arrested because he was profiled by the Miami police. Well, how much longer will we put up with "the man" targeting rich white kids in Lamborghinis? When is that going to stop?

monologue: You'd think with technology they'd update Groundhog Day just little. Maybe have Phil stay down in his hole and just tweet out his prediction.

monologue: There's more trouble for Justin Bieber. Last night he was arrested in Toronto for assaulting a limo driver. First a DUI, now an assault charge. If Bieber keeps this up he's never going to get into a good college.

monologue: Justin Bieber recently retired from music to focus on building up his criminal record.

monologue: Once again, President Obama will grant an interview to a journalist from the network broadcasting the Super Bowl. The game is on Fox this year, so Bill O'Reilly will do the interview. I'm taking O'Reilly with the points.

monologue: There are still more than 11,000 Super Bowl tickets unsold. Why they would have trouble selling $1,500 tickets to an outdoor event being held in a blizzard that you can watch on TV for free, I don't know, but they are.

monologue: Sunday is Groundhog Day, coincidentally with Super Bowl Sunday. I'm very excited. I get up early on Groundhog Day. I stuff the groundhog and I put it in a medium oven, and I'm ready to go.

monologue: You want to be careful if you gamble on the Super Bowl. Last year I made a Super Bowl bet with Jimmy Fallon. I think we know how that turned out.

monologue: It is still cold all across the nation. It was so cold today that Al Gore called global warming a hoax.

monologue: House Republicans unveiled a new plan that would allow undocumented immigrants to become citizens if they learn about American history. Which will be great, because then they can teach it to Americans.

monologue: Sunday is the Super Bowl. As I like to call it, "the Oscars for straight people."

monologue: I like the Broncos' logo. It is aggressive. There is nothing like a severed horse head to show the opponent you mean business.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is amazing that both Peyton Manning, Broncos quarterback, and younger brother Eli Manning grew up to be NFL quarterbacks like their dad. I have two sons. If they someday both end up hosting late-night talk shows, that will make me unbelievably sad.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is the Broncos vs. the Seahawks. That raises an interesting question. What is a Seahawk? A hawk that somehow learned to swim? Or a mutant fish that has grown wings?

monologue: Let's talk about the big game yesterday. The Seahawks beat the Broncos 43-8. The Broncos are blaming it on a traffic study.

monologue: On Saturday before the Super Bowl, Peyton Manning received the NFL's MVP award for the season. Yeah, unfortunately it was immediately intercepted by a Seahawk.

monologue: After appearing in a commercial during last night's Super Bowl, people are accusing Bob Dylan of selling out. Today Dylan responded by saying, "Everyone needs to calm down, have a Bud Light, and relax at a Sandals Resort."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It wasn't much of a Super Bowl game. The Seahawks beat the Broncos 43-8. You know how after the game the winning players go to Disney World? Some of the Seahawks went halfway through the third quarter.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It cost $4 million for a 30-second ad during the Super Bowl. I'm always surprised at which companies elect to pay that. How did a pistachio company afford $4 million? What kind of mark-up are they getting on those nuts?

monologue: The Super Bowl was on Fox, so the traditional pre-game sit-down with President Obama went to Bill O'Reilly. The interview got off to a rocky start. O'Reilly asked Obama, "Where you were born was football played with your feet?" And it went downhill from there.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: At the end of the interview O'Reilly said he thinks Obama's "heart is in the right place." What does that mean? That's basically saying that I don't think he’s destroying America intentionally.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Did you all see that game yesterday? Was that the worst Super Bowl ever? It was 43 to 8. The Puppy Bowl on Animal Planet was more competitive than that.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Broncos couldn’t move the ball. The last time I saw a Bronco going that slow, OJ was driving it through L.A.

monologue: While he was at the game, Governor Chris Christie was up to his old tricks. It turns out he blocked three lines at the concession stand.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: Jimmy Fallon is here tonight. He’s not here to talk. He’s helping me pack.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: How about that Super Bowl? Some of you may expect me to make jokes about the Broncos. I won't do that. To me it's just beating a dead horse.

monologue: Well done, Seattle. I think they needed this to cement their reputation. Before last night, the meanest guy from Seattle was "Frasier."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Poor Broncos. Experts said they haven't seen something crushed like that in New Jersey since Chris Christie's beanbag chair.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Broncos looked so bad, even the L.A. Lakers said, "This is kind of embarrassing to watch." Peyton Manning had such a bad night that Tim Tebow said, "I could have done that."

name: David Letterman
monologue: Is the Super Bowl pre-game show still on?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Sunday's game was the most watched Super Bowl in history. It was a hit with fans of both football and whatever the Broncos were playing.

monologue: People are worried that Sochi in Russia is not ready for the Olympics. They have a mall there where the only store that's currently open is a Cinnabon — or as Americans refer to it, a mall that caters to all of our needs.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Hillary Clinton is encouraging Hispanic families to read to their kids. She's also telling Asian families to ease up on the math so the rest of us can catch up.

monologue: Today it was announced that Bill Gates is stepping down as chairman of Microsoft. He starts working at the gap next Tuesday.

monologue: Today is the 10th anniversary of Facebook. Facebook was started in a Harvard dorm room by Jesse Eisenberg in "Spider-Man 2."

monologue: Actually, Mark Zuckerberg started Facebook. He was a 19-year-old student in a hoodie. Now he's a 29-year-old billionaire in a hoodie.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: More than anyone, Mark Zuckerberg revolutionized the way we avoid doing work in this country.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Yet another winter storm is dumping snow on two dozen states right now. The storms were supposed to end last Friday, but they were so popular they decided to extend their run.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: With all the hoopla over the Super Bowl, did you know Sunday was Groundhog Day? What happened was the groundhog saw his shadow and then kept watching it. He thought it would be more exciting than watching that stupid Super Bowl.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: The Seahawks had a great slogan: "Why not us?" That's what they would say to each other before the game. That is much better than the Broncos' slogan: "Hey, why not hike it over the quarterback's head?"

name: Jay Leno
monologue: In spite of being a terrible game, the Super Bowl was the most watched TV event in history. So apparently it’s true — if we do start televising executions, people will watch.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: People were partying in Seattle on Sunday night after the game. They were singing, they were laughing, they were hugging complete strangers, dancing in the streets. Basically, the same thing they've done every night in Seattle since they legalized marijuana.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Facebook is 10 years old today. You know who else is celebrating a birthday today? Eric Garcetti, the mayor of Los Angeles. Facebook and Los Angeles are very different. One was considered cool a long time ago but is still a good place to waste time with fake friends — and the other one is Facebook.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm not on Facebook. I've never been on it. There are people on Facebook who claim to be me. To them I say, "Aim higher."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm old fashioned. I don't want my personal information out there for everyone. I share details of my life with a very small group of people — the audience of this show.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Teenagers are proving they don't need Facebook. They're finding other sites. They'll keep hopping from one site to another until they're 70 years old. Then they can settle into the warm embrace of the CBS demographic.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Tomorrow night the Olympics begin from Sochi. A lot of people over there say the hotels stink. The problem is there are only three hotels in Sochi. Of course, you have the Ritz Chernobyl. You have the Sheraton Gulag. And really the best one over there, The Two Seasons.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Olympics start airing tonight on NBC. It's a big deal. NBC will finally get to show somebody who is OK with passing the torch.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There are 12 new events in this year's Winter Olympics, 12. The new events include women's ski jumping, luge-team relay, and finding a working toilet.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: We're very excited to have the cast of "The Walking Dead" tonight. Normally, if you want to see the walking dead in L.A., you have to go to the mall of Tarzana.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: I don’t like goodbyes. NBC does. Well, tonight is our last show for real. See, I don’t need to get fired three times. I get the hint.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: You know, being together all these years, the staff is very close. It's kind of like graduating high school — a high school for really stupid people that have been in the same class for 22 years.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: And the worst thing about losing this job, I'm no longer covered by NBC. I have to sign up for Obamacare.

name: Jay Leno
monologue: When I started hosting, Justin Bieber wasn’t even born yet. That's why we call those “the good old days."

name: Jay Leno
monologue: It was revealed this week that in the past couple years Hugh Grant has fathered three children with two different women. How ironic is that? I end my run the same way it began — asking Hugh Grant, "What the hell were you thinking?" Twenty-two years later, I ask him the same question.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Olympic torch arrived in Sochi yesterday, after going on a four-month relay around the world. That's when you know things are bad — when even the TORCH is putting off going to Russia.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I guess it isn’t going well over there. In fact, I heard there’s even a shortage of pillows. The shortage is so bad that visitors are being asked to give their pillows to the Olympic athletes, because there's nothing more comforting than waking up in Russia to see a stranger coming at you with a pillow. "How was your sleep, Mr. Bond?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: After facing backlash from customers, Subway says it will remove a chemical in its bread that’s also found in yoga mats. Some people were like, “You mean I’ve been eating a dangerous chemical?” While most people were like, “You mean I can eat my yoga mat?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It was also weird when bread came in regular, whole wheat, and Lululemon.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This is the last night Jay Leno is hosting "The Tonight Show." Good luck, Jay. The lesson here is if you work hard and succeed, someday you will be fired.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: That's why I'm happy right here. They can't fire you if they don't know you're on the air.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new LEGO movie is coming out. I've heard some people say, "This LEGO movie is basically just a two-hour commercial." These people are completely wrong. It's only 90 minutes.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I think this LEGO movie will do very well. Because people love watching movies that remind them of their childhood. That's why I'll see any movie about binge drinking and scurvy.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Welcome to the show. I'm Dave Letterman, the fifth Beatle.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It’s our last episode of Late Night. You know, I’m really going to miss being on TV at 12:37. I'll especially miss the battle for late-night ratings with my fierce rivals — Craig Ferguson and a Veggie Chopper infomercial.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yep, tonight is the 969th and final episode of “Late Night.” Or as my dad put it, “Couldn’t make it to a thousand, huh? Quitter.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: We’ve done over 10,000 monologue jokes over the last five years. And in case you missed any of them, the best way I could summarize those jokes is that Joe Biden needed Obamacare after Anthony Weiner texted Justin Bieber a picture of Chris Christie dating a Kardashian on the Jersey Shore — with Rob Ford.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There's a new survey that found that 50 percent of doctors admit to going on Wikipedia to look up medical information. While the rest behave like professionals and use WebMD.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I didn't learn to ski until I was 45. I fell down a lot. But I'm used to falling on my face in front of people.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Skiing makes me feel like a rugged adventurer. The wind on my cheeks, the ice-crusted goggles, those little mini marshmallows in my cocoa.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Organizers for the Sochi Olympics have had trouble filling seats for the biathlon. This is because Vladimir Putin is warning people away from any event containing "bi."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There are rumors that the Russian government placed cameras in the hotel bathrooms in Sochi. Russia said, "Don't worry, our cameras don't work either."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today at the Winter Olympics, temperatures reached almost up to 60 degrees. In other words, the only thing higher than the temperature were the U.S. snowboarders.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A top NFL prospect has announced that he is gay. Then someone explained to him that having a crush on Tom Brady doesn't make you gay.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I'm glad you were able to tear yourselves away from the Winter Olympics. The sporting event that answers the question, How many different ways can white people injure themselves on ice?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: One Sochi elevator has two up buttons. If you want to go down, you have to stand on your head.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There's a pillow shortage in Sochi too. They don't have enough pillows for the beds. How do you not foresee a demand for pillows? Although in their defense it is Russia. When you sleep wherever you happen to pass out, pillows aren't so important.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A shipment containing 5,000 containers of Greek yogurt was supposed to be delivered to the U.S. Olympic team, but the Russian government blocked it because they said they didn't fill out the required paperwork. Once again, the Russian government is doing everything they can to repress live and active cultures.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Lego Movie is No. 1 at the box office. I saw it. I'm a little disappointed. I liked the first half of "The Lego Movie" but it sort of came apart at the end.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Olympics opening ceremonies were amazing. There was a trippy ride through Russian history, like if Yakov Smirnoff was flying through Narnia.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Before the games, a lot of people were worried that hotels in Sochi wouldn't be ready. For the most part, things seem to be working well. The only problems occur when people try to do something crazy like, you know, open a door.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's actually been warm in Sochi, 63 and sunny — just like the average CBS viewer.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Bob Costas had to take a break from hosting the Olympics coverage due to an eye infection. In fact, his eyes are so bloodshot, he's been made an honorary member of the U.S. snowboarding team.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The family of openly gay NFL prospect Michael Sam say they found out he was gay from watching ESPN. Meanwhile, Michael Sam found out he was gay from watching Bravo.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Los Angeles newscaster had to apologize to Samuel L. Jackson for mistaking him for Laurence Fishburne. Yeah, he said "I'm sorry, but everybody makes mistakes, even our great president, Morgan Freeman."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: To stop the spread of disease, the city of Vancouver has allowed crack pipes to be sold in vending machines. The plan is being called dangerous by the mayor of New York City and genius by the mayor of Toronto.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It was 15 degrees cooler in Atlanta when they had the Summer Olympics than it is in Sochi where they had the Winter Olympics. It got up to 60 degrees today. It was so warm some of the people staying in the hotels thought the heat started working. But it turns out it was just the sun.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Because of the warm weather, some of the ski jumpers were actually landing in puddles of water. They turned into water skiers mid-flight.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Poor Bob Costas. He hosts the prime-time portion of the Olympics for NBC. When the game started he had an infection in his eye. Then it spread to his other eye. Turned out to be a serious case of pink eye, which is a problem because Vladimir Putin now thinks his eyes are gay and wants them removed.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Today in New York was the finals of the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show. This was the 138th Westminster Dog Show, which proves that no matter how boring something is, you can still do it over and over again.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This year the dogs competed in a variety of categories including talent, evening gown, and swimsuit.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm loving the Winter Olympics on that other network. But it's not the only huge sporting event going on. Right now in New York City, the best are going up against the best. And the claws are coming out — at the 138th annual Westminster Dog Show.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The favorite dog to win is a Komondor. I would love a dog like that. Use it as a mop and your floors would be spotless.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This year at Westminster they are allowing mixed breeds to compete. Owners breed dogs within families. They reward inbreeding. That's not healthy, and creates weird-looking specimens. Same problem I have with the royals.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday Matt Lauer jokingly blamed Bob Costas' eye infection on Russian President Vladimir Putin. Yeah, and today police are wondering: Where in the world is Matt Lauer?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Slovenian woman who won the gold medal in alpine skiing is also a pop star in her country. So Justin Bieber is not the only pop star going downhill fast.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: At a McDonald's in Michigan, a woman fired a gun at a drive-through worker for forgetting bacon on her order. In the woman's defense, the worker did forget her bacon.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Researchers say that at least four species of crocodiles are able to climb trees. And there is a cobra that can pick locks.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Sochi, a man who criticized the Sochi games was sentenced to three years in a prison colony. After hearing the sentence, the man said it's still better than a hotel in Sochi.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Some McDonald's restaurants are taking reservations on Valentine's Day. They are getting a lot of tables for one.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In California, an openly gay candidate is running for office as something called "a new generation Republican." Or as their known in the rest of the country, a Democrat.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Scientists are working on a new contraceptive for women that works for 90 days straight. They are referring to this new contraceptive as sweatpants.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It happened again — today I get a call from my mom. She says, "David, did something happen to Jay?"

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I want to start by wishing everyone a happy Presidents Day because it seems like the right thing to do, even though none of you are actually presidents.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I spent my Presidents Day the same way I always do. I spent it quietly hating everyone who has the day off today.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: There's another huge winter storm this week with more than a foot of snow in parts of Massachusetts. Chicago is frozen solid. It's almost like its winter or something.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Humans aren't the only species having trouble keeping warm. Even Boston Terriers don't want to be in Boston anymore.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is a day to remember all our presidents. And also to get a terrific deal on mattresses.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I wonder what ex-presidents do on Presidents Day. Probably have a big cookout at the ex-presidents clubhouse. Clinton, Carter, and the two Bushes all live together in a big house.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's just like late-night talk-show guys live together in the late-night clubhouse. I haven't seen Leno recently, although one of his cars is still in the driveway. Maybe he's coming back.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There is good news from Sochi. Bob Costas has defeated pink eye. He's back to anchoring the Winter Olympics. I'm surprised NBC let him come back. Usually when they replace a host, they stick with their decision.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today at the Olympics the Russian men's hockey team, which was favored, was eliminated by Finland. Then an hour later, the Russian men's hockey team was eliminated by Putin.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today the Russian hockey team lost and was knocked out of the Olympics. People in Russia haven't been this depressed since last week.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Florida, a 101-year-old man is planning to run for Congress. His slogan is "Vote for me and then vote again in two months."

name: David Letterman
monologue: America is leading all the other countries at the Olympics in gold medals. Great, another reason for the rest of the world to hate us.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Canadians are good at ice dancing. Austrians are good at skiing, of course. Americans, freestyle buffet, very good.

name: David Letterman
monologue: This weekend is George Washington's birthday. Washington had probably the hardest job of any other president because he had no predecessor to blame things on. He was out there all on his own.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Charlie Sheen's getting married to an adult film star. Her parents are mortified, but they're getting married anyway. If you want to get something for the happy couple, they are registered at J.C. Penicillin.

name: David Letterman
monologue: One of the Knicks players, Raymond Felton, was arrested for carrying a concealed gun. That makes him the first openly stupid player on the Knicks.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Oscars are coming up. Or as they're officially called: "Hoarders, the Meryl Streep Edition."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A former Target employee is accusing the store of hiring only attractive people as managers. Apparently he's talking about a Target store I have never been to.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In California the owner of a Christian medical marijuana dispensary says God told him to sell pot. The dispensary owner said it's right there in the book of Dude-eronomy.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In a new interview, the Dalai Lama says watching TV is a waste of time. And I'm like, "What? How dare you, Mr. Lama!" What does the Dalai Lama care about wasting time? He's eternally reborn. He's got all the time in the world.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: What we should do is make more shows that appeal to the Dalai Lama. How about shows like "Two and a Half Monks," "The Big Buddha Theory" and "CSI: Tibet"? Or what about "Parks and Reincarnation"?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A married couple in California were walking through their backyard and they found a treasure trove of rare gold coins. It's the biggest discovery of valuable coins since Stedman cleaned out Oprah's couch.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Imagine finding gold in your own backyard. Right now there's a leprechaun saying, "What happened to me pot o' gold?"

name: David Letterman
monologue: How about that mess in the Ukraine, and now Viktor Yanukovych gets scared and runs. The Russians have given him asylum and they are putting troops on alert. That doesn't sound like the Russians I know.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The very first Academy Awards ceremony lasted 15 minutes. And thanks to the fast-forward button on my DVR, so will this year's.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Workers in the special effects industry are unhappy about seeing their jobs go overseas, so they'll be protesting at the Oscars. Only five will be at the protest, but with CGI special effects, it will look like hundreds.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Jason Collins, the NBA's first openly gay player, has the top-selling jersey in the league store. Yeah, that's great — finally a gay man who's not afraid to stand up and say "I have my own clothing line."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In California the owner of a Christian medical marijuana dispensary says God told him to sell pot. As proof, he cited the story from the Bible where Jesus miraculously turns water into pizza.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Big news out of NASA yesterday — the Kepler space telescope has discovered 715 new planets. Either that or somebody sneezed on the lens.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you suddenly find 715 new planets, is that a discovery or were you just not looking hard enough in the first place.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This planet discovery is terrible news for all the school kids who just finished making models of the solar system. For them, it's back to work.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This Sunday is the 86th and final Academy Awards. This is the last year they're doing it. They decided there are enough Oscar winners already and they don't want to dilute it for those who have them.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new study says going vegetarian is the best way to lower high blood pressure. Pretty much every study says vegetarians live longer. But that's just because meat eaters’ lives get shortened from being harassed by angry vegetarians.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Vegetarians aren't the only people finicky about staying healthy and being thin. They have a name for them — single people. Once you're married, it doesn't matter. "I do . . . want fries."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Hardcore vegans even avoid honey because a very small number of bees are accidentally killed in its production. You know what beekeepers call these incidents? Honey boo-boos.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I saw at the supermarket something called "vegan burgers." Really? It's an oxymoron — unless they're burgers made from vegans. Taste the smug superiority!

name: David Letterman
monologue: They've discontinued Moviefone. If you folks are sad, press 1. If you couldn't care less, press 2.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Oscars are on Sunday. They are kind of like the Westminster Dog Show, except with more blow dryers.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Some people call the Oscars "the gay Super Bowl." I don't think that's fair. I think it's balanced. This year Ellen DeGeneres is hosting. Bette Midler is performing. There will be a tribute to "The Wizard of Oz." OK, I take it back. Even the Tony Awards are saying, "This is a pretty gay awards show."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: This year's Oscars are being held a week later than usual. That was so they don't have to go up against the Winter Olympics. Good move on the Academy's part. Never make viewers choose between seeing a bunch of A-list movie stars and the curling semi-finals.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Did you like the women's curling last week in the Olympics? That is only time you'll see a woman sweep these days.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Anybody see the Academy Awards last night? I watch every year to make sure I'm not in the dead actors montage.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I'm Conan O'Brien. Or as John Travolta calls me, Kevin O. Zeme.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In his acceptance speech, Matthew McConaughey said his hero is always himself 10 years from now, so by the time last night's Oscars finished, he was his own hero.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Russia suspended coverage of the Oscars last night. They didn't show it. And I'm going to guess they're not going to show the Tony Awards either.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Last night was the fourth time Leonardo DiCaprio was nominated for an Oscar and the fourth time he has lost. Being Leonardo DiCaprio must be a living hell. I don't know how he goes on.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight we get a visit from the mayor of the great city of Toronto, Rob Ford. I feel like I've been waiting for this night my whole life.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I have a lot to ask Mayor Ford. I don't think I've had this many questions since the series finale of "Lost."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: When Mayor Ford gets out here, distract him and I'll take his passport. And that way he never leaves us, OK?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Last night the Academy Awards telecast was more than three hours long. They actually had to do a second “In Memoriam” montage because quite a few actors passed away during the broadcast.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I would like to thank you and the Academy and my agent.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Oscars are finally over. At least I think they're over.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I stopped watching when they made the joke about Liza Minnelli. I will not stand for that. Liza Minnelli is my spirit animal.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: From what I hear, the stars really let loose at the after-parties. There are rumors in Hollywood right now that Angelina Jolie ate a carb.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Welcome to the Ed Sullivan Theater, now under Russian control.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The New York Times has apologized for a spelling error they made 161 years ago. They spelled “Larry King” with one "r".

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Arnold Schwarzenegger revealed that he's filming a new "Terminator" movie next month. In this one the Terminator travels 10 years into the future and meets Matthew McConaughey's hero.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: RadioShack has announced plans to close 1,000 stores throughout the U.S. RadioShack customers were very upset when they got the news on their pagers.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We had an interesting night last night. The mayor of Toronto, Rob Ford, was here. Then after the show, apparently he was upset. Why, I'm not exactly sure. I asked him about drinking and smoking crack. What were we supposed to talk about? His other hobbies?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It's hard to tell whether Rob Ford is mad because his face is always bright red. It doesn't change colors.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: It's Mardi Gras in New Orleans. This is the night when women traditionally penalize their fathers for not paying enough attention to them by exposing themselves to strangers in exchange for beads.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A puff of glittery smoke billowed up from the chimney of the Vatican this morning to announce a new cast on "Dancing With the Stars." Usually you have to tear through old issues of magazines at the dentist office to figure out who they are.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight is Mardi Gras, the biggest celebration in New Orleans. Thousands of visitors descend upon New Orleans to drink themselves stupid and behave badly. So it's just like every other weekend.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Mardi Gras is French for Fat Tuesday. People stuff themselves right before Lent, when Catholics traditionally fast. Every religion has a holiday where people fast to prove their devotion. Catholics have Lent. And here in L.A., we have Oscar season.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Catholics all over the world celebrate Mardi Gras. There's a big festival in Rome. Italians take to the streets, shouting, waving their arms. Then Mardi Gras starts.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Even the Pope gets involved in Mardi Gras. He's really the most interesting Pope in the world. "I don't always throw beads off my balcony. But when I do, it's at Mardi Gras."

name: David Letterman
monologue: John Kerry, secretary of state, is visiting Ukraine and today he met with Adele Dazeem.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Today is the second day of the 40-day Catholic holiday of Lent. You know what I'm giving up this year? The 40-day Catholic holiday of Lent.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There's a new app that will help you find the nearest bathroom. It's called the Starbucks app.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The White House announced a change to Obamacare. They keep making adjustments. They say people can now keep their insurance plans for two more years. When asked what would happen after two years, Obama said, "After two years, I don't give a damn."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Meteorologists say 90 percent of the Great Lakes are frozen over. People from Chicago are being urged to stay off the frozen lakes, but if you want to see someone from Chicago in thin ice, just go to the White House.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm kidding. I'm kidding. No, Obama is not from Chicago. He is from Kenya.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Obama's approval rating is at an all-time low. He has a plan to make him look better. It is called letting Joe Biden make a speech.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There is no point to doing a monologue. Everybody is doing monologues these days. The late-night guys come out and do monologues. That's what they do. We're just like any other show — just a middle-aged white guy in a suit telling jokes from cue cards.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Russian President Vladimir Putin is claiming Russia did not invade the Crimean peninsula. What are those guys, neighborhood watch? Mall cops?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Here's a study that probably didn't need to take place. According to the annual traffic scorecard report, L.A. has the worst traffic in America. L.A. residents spend 17 hours more than average sitting in traffic. How can we have the worst traffic and the most high-speed chases? Wouldn't one cancel the other out?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Next week in Denver there's a job fair that will cater exclusively to the cannabis industry. Fifteen marijuana-related businesses will be hiring people for a variety of job openings. It's a little different. These companies actually test to make sure you are on drugs.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The fair will take place on March 13. It starts around 3-ish, whatever, dude. Attendance is free. Although they're expecting to make $600,000 from the bake sale.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Here's some strange fashion news. According to The New York Times, the monocle is back in style. Online monocle retailers have increased sales lately. Monocles are great if you're looking for eyewear that falls into your coffee every time you sneeze.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Unless you're a “Batman” villain or a giant salted peanut, you should not wear a monocle.

name: David Letterman
monologue: The mayor of Toronto, crack-smoking Rob Ford sent out a tweet about Daylight Saving Time reminding people to turn their clocks back. In fact, you're supposed to turn your clocks forward. And then he tweeted back and he said, "Well, who cares what I'm talking about. I'm on crack!"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday was Daylight Saving Time, when we lose an hour for no apparent reason. By the way, losing an hour for no apparent reason is also the motto for this show.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: President Obama was paying tribute to Aretha Franklin when he messed up the spelling of her iconic song "Respect." President Obama blamed his speech coach, John Travolta.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Over the weekend, North Korea held elections. Kim Jong Un was re-elected with 100% of the vote. Kim Jong Un credits his win to the slogan: Vote for me or you will be murdered.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: While working on the L.A. subway, construction workers discovered fossils from the Ice Age. The fossils belong to the last creature to ever use the Los Angeles subway.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's not such a great day for a family in Florida recovering after eating steak laced with LSD. About halfway through dinner they realized there was a problem when someone asked for a side of mashed potatoes, and that someone was the steak.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I don't think LSD works though if you get it warm. It doesn't work. You have to keep it in the fridge. But I've said too much.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Kim Jong Un was re-elected today in North Korea. He got 100% of the vote. His slogan was, "Vote for me or you'll be eaten by rabid dogs." It's awkward because that was going to be Hillary's slogan.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: We just had the finale of "The Bachelor." It was a doozy. It was a fight for love between two very different women, a blonde and a blonde.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I admit I don't watch "The Bachelor." If I wanted to see a bunch of floozies kiss up to a guy they don't really care for, and aren't interested in, I'd go to the Playboy mansion.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Everybody's in a good mood because of the day outside. It's 55 but not that cool. You know, like Kenny G.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The country of New Zealand is voting on whether to change their flag. Apparently New Zealand's current flag is a sign that says, “No, no, you're thinking about Australia. We're not Australia.”

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A barber shop in Colorado is refusing to serve anybody who smells like marijuana. Today they went out of business.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A clothing company is going to release a $99 wedding dress. The $99 wedding dress is the perfect way to tell your man, "I do, I guess."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This is our second of five nights broadcasting from Austin, Texas. But the truth is we're not here to do a show. The real reason we came here is because this is an intervention. You have a drinking problem, Austin. You need to stop.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A real Texas legend, the great Jimmie Vaughan, is sitting in with our band. We can never have enough Jimmys on the show.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Our non-musical guests tonight are actress Rosario Dawson and Texas Governor Rick Perry. I hear some booing. I hope you're not booing Rosario Dawson because that would be weird.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The mission statement here is "Keep Austin weird." Back home in L.A. we don't have to worry about keeping it weird. That's what Gary Busey is there for.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A family in Oregon called 911 after they were trapped in a bedroom by their cat. I'll say it again. They were trapped in their bedroom by their cat. Apparently the cat held the family hostage until its demands were met. Its demands were food and sleep.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The cat was apprehended and received a sentence of four to nine lives.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In Denver this week they're hosting a marijuana job fair. Who will be attending? Companies that want to hire stoners and stoners who want to work. So I don't think anyone's going, really.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A marijuana job fair? Is TV watching a job?

name: David Letterman
monologue: Today President Obama went shopping at The Gap. There hasn't been so much security at The Gap since the time Lindsey Lohan showed up.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Toronto an 18-year-old girl is running against Rob Ford in that city's mayoral election. Her campaign slogan is "Vote for me. I'm not a crack addict."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Florida, the town of Hampton has been found to be so corrupt the state may dissolve it, basically ending the town's existence. Which of course begs the question: How bad of a town do you have to be to be an embarrassment to Florida?

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Archeologists just discovered a leather belt believed to be 4,000 years old. So now we know why Larry king wears suspenders.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We're here from Austin, Texas. I stand before you half man, half brisket.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: You know you've been in Austin too long when you start randomly finding rib bones in your pockets, which I did tonight.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I can't button my suit. I can't fit in my clothes anymore because of this place.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Internet turns 25 today. Whatever you do, don't send it an e-card. Even the World Wide Web hates e-cards.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Internet revolutionized man's ability to sell useless crap.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Web has changed our lives. In the old days you actually had to go to the mall and watch old people fall down escalators in person.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A lot of the information is wrong on the Web. For example, on the IMDB website it says I'm 51 years old — which is ridiculous!

name: David Letterman
monologue: Pope Francis is the hip Pope. He is celebrating his first anniversary of being Pope. He refers to Lent as "March Madness." That is how wacky he gets.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This is our fourth of five nights broadcasting from Austin, Texas, during the South by Southwest festival. I had to get a bigger shirt because my shirts don't fit anymore. In Texas, pork is considered a condiment.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We'll get a visit from Lady Gaga. She didn't bring the meat dress or the giant egg. She didn't want to be turned into a giant breakfast taco.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I haven't seen this many hipsters in one place since I took a home pickling class at an artesian cheese shop.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: People have been selling fake parking spaces. They charge people to park in spots that they have no ownership of. Here's a tip to avoid becoming a victim of this fraud. If you find a parking space during the festival, it's a scam.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: What a fantastic ovation from the studio audience. You guys have clearly never been here before.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A new study says Americans spent a record $56 billion on their pets last year. That may sound like a lot but think about what you get in return. You get the unconditional love of dogs, the exotic beauty of a tropical fish, and whatever a cat gives you — disdain, I guess.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Every year reality TV gets more extreme. Back in the old days, married couples on shows slept in separate beds. But "The Brady Bunch" were hooking up with each other in real life. They should have called it "All in the Family.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: The average American citizen — you hear the statistic all the time — works six months out of the year for the government. That's how difficult the taxes are in this country. We work six months out of the year. Government employees don't even do that.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We've been broadcasting from Austin all week, and I'm sad to say this is our last night here. I would cry but my tear ducts are clogged with queso right now.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: We head home and then on Monday I'm going on "The Biggest Loser" to work some of this weight off. You know it's a good trip when you have to request a seat belt extender for your flight back.

name: Jimmy Kimmel

monologue: Yesterday President Obama made an unscheduled stop at a Little League game while he was on his way to a fundraiser. Yeah, because there's nothing parents love more than their kid's Little League game getting even longer.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Over the weekend, Beyoncé and Jay-Z released a trailer for their upcoming tour together. When asked what they like most about the video, they said, “We actually knew we were making this one.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: CNN had to fire an editor after discovering that she plagiarized 50 stories. CNN said, “Can you imagine if somebody actually SAW them?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Scientists in London say they have invented a process that can actually turn light into matter, but warned people that their results won’t be visible to the human eye. Well, in that case, I invented it too.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I was at a website looking at the sale section and I came across this item: a chocolate Easter Bunny reduced from $14.95 to $9.99. Who is buying chocolate Easter Bunnies in May? It's not like chocolate isn't available in other shapes.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If you did buy a chocolate bunny, an out-of-season candy rabbit, would you order it by mail? I mean, if your chocolate bunny isn't an impulse purchase, what is?

monologue: Yesterday the NBA formally notified Donald Sterling of its intention to terminate his ownership of the L.A. Clippers. And they also let him know that his face looks like a bag of melted silly putty.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The NBA gave Donald Sterling until Tuesday to respond. His lawyer asked for a three-month extension to prepare. I'll tell you what's happening here. He is stalling. Sterling is going to keep this in court until he dies. He is basically trying to run out the clock on being alive.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A 24-year-old-cat in England has been named the world’s oldest cat. That cat is so old, if you give it a ball of yarn, it knits.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A man in Florida has been arrested for inappropriately touching two women outside a Walmart while claiming to be a psychic. Though to his credit, when the police picked him up he said, “I knew this was going to happen.”

monologue: The FBI has reversed its policy and will now hire people who have smoked pot in the past three years. When asked why, the FBI said, "Because we couldn't find anyone who hasn't smoked pot."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Nashville a woman named Peyton Manning was arrested for possession of cocaine. Either that or football's Peyton Manning likes to switch things up.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In a new interview, Angelina Jolie said she would not rule out running for office someday. She said she will wait until her children are grown and make up 51 percent of the voting population.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's the first day of Fleet Week. Fleet week is when New York City honors its men in uniform — unless they play for the Mets.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: During Fleet Week, New York City gets pretty rowdy. All that yelling, drinking, and raising hell. And then when they're done taping "The View," Fleet Week starts.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's also National Waiter and Waitress Day. So be extra nice to your server. Say "Thanks, sugar" and give them a little slap on the butt.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Mr. T turns 62 today. Mister T was so beloved in the 1980s he had his own breakfast cereal. They had to pull it off the shelves though. Kids kept breaking their teeth on the little crunchy gold medallions.

name: David Letterman
monologue: It's Fleet Week here in New York City. All the armed forces are here, 1500 military personnel. They're here to defend us against Godzilla.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Pope Francis will bring a rabbi and a Muslim leader with him when he travels to the Holy Land this week. Or as bartenders put it, "We've been expecting you."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Kraft is recalling more than a million cases of cottage cheese because they weren’t stored at the right temperature. Isn’t that how you MAKE cottage cheese?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Researchers have found that eating two large meals helps you lose more weight than eating six small meals. Or as doctors put it, “Please just exercise.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A Russian businessman has been ordered to pay his wife $4.5 billion in what is being called the world’s most expensive divorce. Then L.A. Clippers owner Donald Sterling said, “Stay tuned.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: On "Dancing With The Stars," double amputee Amy Purdy, who has not one but two artificial legs, made it all the way to the final two and then she lost to an Olympic gold medal-winning ice dancer. Is that fair? I don't think it is.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Good news for fans of "Frozen." Disney announced this fall they will debut a live show called "Frozen on Ice." I haven't seen it, but wasn't "Frozen" already on ice?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: For 40 years Burger King has been saying "Have it your way" in their ads. They're changing the slogan from "Have it your way" to "Be your way." I don't get it. Am I ordering a Whopper or coming out to my family?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I would be mad if I was in charge of supplies for Burger King. Because they're changing two words in the slogan, I now have to print 8 trillion new cups. Does Burger King know that they could not even have a tag line and as long as they have hamburgers literally no one would care?

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: It’s Fleet Week in New York. And you know what that means: Next week is Penicillin Week.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: One day after recalling 2.4 million vehicles, GM has announced it’s recalling another 218,000 Chevy Aveos. Apparently, their defect is that they’re Chevy Aveos.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Yesterday a group of 50 Brooklyn school kids gave an impromptu recorder recital on the subway during morning rush hour. Because sometimes New York is full of great surprises and other times it’s full of children playing the recorder on the subway in the morning.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Golfer Rory McIlroy broke off his engagement to a pro tennis player Caroline Wozniacki days after sending out wedding invitations. Because he realized that, to her, love means zero.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In a new interview about the Donald Sterling scandal, Dallas Mavericks owner Mark Cuban said, "I know I'm prejudiced, too." In fact, Cuban admits he's so racist, he's trying to have his last name deported.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: It's been reported that Beyoncé gets paid $100,000 just to sit in the front row at a fashion show. Meanwhile, her sister, Solange, is getting paid that amount by Jay-Z to take the stairs.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A woman got a DUI while driving a car that belongs to Toronto Mayor Rob Ford. So, I'm starting to think maybe it's the car that has the problem.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Google is continuing its mission to make sure we're never NOT looking at ads. Google says it hopes to put ads on refrigerators, dashboards, glasses, watches, and other items. This is what the smartest people in the country are working on. Instead of winning a Nobel Prize, their obituary is going to say, "Bill used his 187 IQ to figure out how to put commercials on your windshield.”

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In other invasive technology news, Facebook has a terrifying new feature. It uses the microphone in your smartphone to listen to what music, movies, or TV shows you're watching or hearing, and then it posts them to your Facebook page. You have to hand it to Facebook. Each time I figure Facebook has become as creepy as possible, somehow they find a way to be even creepier.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Toronto Mayor Rob Ford's car was involved in a DUI. Somehow a woman named LeAnne McRobb wound up in his car. You know what a McRobb is? It's half Rob Ford, half McRib.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This Rob Ford is something else. His car gets pulled over for DUI even when he's not in it. It's over. The machines have won. I mean, for God's sake, Rob Ford's Cadillac Escalade is drunk.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: It’s Fleet Week, when New York City plays host to the crews of three U.S. Navy ships and two Coast Guard clippers. But don’t worry, the Coast Guard clippers are NOT owned by Donald Sterling.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A group of scientists have started attaching sensors to sharks to help predict hurricane intensity. They’re hoping the information they gather will save enough lives to offset the number of lives lost attaching sensors to sharks.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: According to a new survey, fewer than 2 percent of hiring managers said they were actively recruiting graduates with liberal arts degrees. Said liberal arts graduates, “Latte for Karen.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Fans of “The Price is Right” got angry at President Obama yesterday because a speech he was giving interrupted the show. So let me fill them in on what they missed: Three people you don't know got called down, and they were extremely happy about it. That’s all you missed.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that legalizing marijuana in Colorado has created more than 10,000 jobs. And that's just selling lava lamps at Spencer's Gifts.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The organizing committee for the 2016 Olympics in Rio just announced that 38 percent of the venues are completed. When asked if they’d be done in time for the Summer Games, Rio said, “Wait — SUMMER games?”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's Pac-Man's birthday. He's an icon of the 1980s, like the Rubik's Cube and "Knight Rider." So if you're a fan of video games, you're going to enjoy the show tonight. But then if you're a fan of video games, you're not watching this show. You're playing video games.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Pac-Man had his own cereal and his own cartoon show. In Japan he's still very popular. But then, this show's popular in Japan too.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I did a sitcom in Japan with Pac-Man. We played roommates, both of us ravaged by years of drug abuse.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's Memorial Day. Or as CBS calls it, "Make the immigrant go to work" day.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: If I have to be here, I'm just phoning it in. In other words, just like every other night for the past decade.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: On this day in 1897, Bram Stoker's "Dracula" was published. Happy birthday, Dracula! You know who else's birthday it is? Lenny Kravitz. Dracula and Lenny Kravitz are very different, of course. One's an elegantly dressed scoundrel who swoops into my dreams at night and bites me on the neck. And the other one: Dracula.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I've read Bram Stoker's "Dracula." It's a really creepy book. A tremendous sense of menace runs through it. The sense of menace in the book is like the sense of menace you get when you're alone with a house cat.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I've always loved the name "Bram Stoker." Nobody calls their kid Bram anymore. Come to think of it, nobody calls their kid Dracula anymore either. Your move, Gwyneth Paltrow.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for Kim and Kanye. To them I'd like to say, "Congratulations on your wedding unless this is a rerun, in which case my condolences on your divorce."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: They got married in Florence. The name Florence holds special meaning for Kim because it's the name that Bruce Jenner goes by.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Congratulations to the remarkable Jessie White. She's a woman from Maine who just graduated college, and she's 99 years old. I said she's 99, so cheer a little bit louder, everybody.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Jessie White was asked what she was going to wear to her first job interview. She said "Depends."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The mayor of New York has overturned the city's ban on ferrets. I didn't know you could ban ferrets. I've been going New York illegally taking my ferrets with me, I suppose. The mayor says he's trying to bring the hairy little weasels out of the shadows.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In a new documentary, Robert DeNiro reveals his father was gay. He realized it after he asked his dad what his favorite part of "New York, New York" was. And his dad went "Li-iiiiiiiza!"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Casinos in Las Vegas are now taking bets on when Kim and Kanye will divorce. I think that is outrageous. It's terrible. But if I were betting man, I'd put 20 bucks on "fall sweeps."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Guys from the band One Direction were caught on video smoking pot. Sounds like the one direction they're going is straight to Bieber-ville.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A woman in New York is suing a Manhattan salon for $1.5 million over a bad haircut. The last time I saw a disaster like that with clippers was Donald Sterling.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: What's the difference between a bad haircut and a good haircut? About a week.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The L.A. Clippers have been sold. Yes, I also don't really care. Everyone is like, "Oh, OK."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The Clippers have been sold for $2 billion. That got your attention.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Donald Sterling paid only $12 million to buy the Clippers. This deal is very uncomfortable for the former owner because it puts him in the black.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: President Obama had lunch today with Hillary Clinton. Hillary told the president, "After phoning my top advisers, I think I'll run for office." And the president said, "I know. I listened in."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A lot of people in Washington were shocked by this Obama-Hillary meeting. I'm not sure about Nancy Pelosi. She looks shocked all the time.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day here in Los Angeles, the City of Angels, the giant urban crap heap.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Clippers fans are celebrating their new owner, billionaire Steve Ballmer. Even though Ballmer is from Seattle, he promises to keep the Clippers in L.A. That's a relief. Otherwise L.A. wouldn't have a professional basketball team. I mean, well, I suppose there are the Lakers.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It makes sense that Ballmer would own a basketball team. He's got "Ball" in his name. That would be like Tom Cruise buying a cruise ship. Or Tiger Woods buying a zoo.

name: David Letterman
monologue: In New York City it's now legal to own a ferret, ladies and gentlemen. I'm telling you, it's just a matter of time before ferrets are pulling carriages through Central Park.

monologue: Today Apple announced a new feature that will let your iPhone monitor your diet and track your calorie intake. Or you can pay extra for an iPhone that minds its own business. Can you imagine Siri talking to you like, "Hey, Chunky."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Spain's king, Juan Carlos, has stepped down from the throne to make way for his son, who is more popular. Which, by the way, would be the worst "Game of Thrones" episode ever.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In Texas a family was attacked by a swarm of bees in a town called Beeville. That's true. The family said they're fed up with Beeville and they're moving to Wolftown.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A lot of people this weekend were talking about the hammock bear, a bear that wandered into someone's backyard and got into their hammock. It's very sweet. He's like, "what do I do now?" The bear is having a midlife crisis. "What does it all mean?"

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: This week it was announced that golfer Phil Mickelson is under investigation by the FBI for insider trading of Clorox stock. By the way, insider trading of Clorox stock by a professional golfer is the whitest collar crime possible.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: The Clippers are gonna be bought by the former CEO of Microsoft. Apparently he's looking for something to occupy himself while Windows is installing "critical updates."

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: This morning President Obama announced a new 600-page proposal to lower carbon emissions and help stop global warming. Step one: Stop printing 600-page proposals.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: This Sunday, Donald Sterling attended services at a traditionally black church in Los Angeles. And just today, the church was sold for $2 billion.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Marijuana dispensaries in San Jose, California, will give out free weed to people who vote in tomorrow’s municipal election. Which should backfire when the winner of the election is "Pizza."

monologue: Newly leaked documents show the NSA has been collecting millions of pictures of people online for its sophisticated facial recognition program. Americans said it's a huge violation of their privacy — then they went back to posting selfies every 30 minutes.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama said Hillary Clinton would be very effective if she ran for president. And Joe Biden said, "Thank you very — wait, what?"

monologue: In a new interview, President Obama revealed that his daughter Malia recently went to her first prom. She wore a corsage on her wrist while her date wore a red laser dot on his head.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Justin Bieber was caught on tape making a racist joke. In Bieber's defense, the video was made when he was young and stupid.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Since word of this got out, Bieber has received a ton of criticism. And also an Instagram request from Donald Sterling. In fact, Bieber should receive the same punishment as Donald Sterling. Someone should give him $2 billion.

monologue: We're learning more about the sale of the L.A. Clippers. Insiders say it came down to a bidding war between Steve Ballmer and Oprah. I'll let you guess who Donald Sterling rooted for.

monologue: Last weekend Donald Sterling attended an African-American church. This was like seeking Mel Gibson at a Hanukkah party, like seeing Arnold Schwarzenegger at an acting class, like seeing the "Duck Dynasty" guys in a gay pride parade.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new study just came out that shows that hurricanes named after women are more deadly. Mainly because when they leave, they take half your stuff.

monologue: Pope Francis said that married people should have more kids. When asked for comment, married people said the Pope should have a kid and then get back to us.

monologue: There's reportedly a film in the works about Edward Snowden. Then today the script was leaked by Edward Snowden.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A new report out of Chicago reveals that the crime rate plummets during an NFL game. Mainly because the most dangerous criminals are busy on the field.

monologue: President Obama is in Poland. He's not doing anything official. He just wants to go before Putin invades. Poland shares a border with Ukraine, which shares a border with Russia. It's kind of like living two doors down from Alec Baldwin. Eventually you're getting attacked, right?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Happy birthday to CNN's Anderson Cooper. Friends threw him a party today. There was an awkward moment when they yelled "Surprise!" and he said, "What, somebody's watching CNN?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The man who created the drug Ecstasy died at the ripe old age of 88. See, kids? That's what drugs will do to you.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In Massachusetts, a 3-month-old German shepherd drove his owner's car into a pond. Let me be the first to say, "Bad dog!"

name: David Letterman
monologue: Lindsey Lohan is moving to London. Before long, she'll be slurring in a British accent.

monologue: Pope Francis is now telling married couples to have children, because only having pets could lead to anger or bitterness in old age. As opposed to having kids, which leads to anger AND bitterness in old age.

monologue: Last Friday CNN had its worst 10 p.m. ratings of all time, with only 35,000 viewers tuning in. I left it on for my dog, and when I came back, she was reading a newspaper.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: CNN got just 35,000 viewers. Even worse, most of those views came from monitors left on in the background on CNN.

monologue: Tim Tebow said that he’s staying in shape in case he gets another opportunity to play in the NFL. Then his boss said, “That’s great, but these Waffle Tacos ain’t going to make themselves, so . . .”

monologue: Statistics for the 47 most damaging hurricanes revealed that those with female names killed twice as many people. The study found that when a hurricane has a woman’s name we take it less seriously and don't prepare as well. Either that or the female hurricanes want to hang around and cuddle afterwards.

monologue: Last week Apple bought Beats headphones for $3 billion. Guess what? They already lost it. They think they left it on the plane.

monologue: Yesterday Apple unveiled its new operating system for the Mac Yosemite. It monitors your heart rate, weight, and sleep — and if you sit on it, it can give you a colonoscopy.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A new book called "Rebels: City of Indra" from Kylie and Kendall Jenner was released today. That's right. Kylie and Kendall Jenner wrote a book, according to loose definitions of the words "wrote" and "book." Listen, I agree to keep up with the Kardashians, but my contract said nothing about having to keep tabs on the Jenners too.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A new study shows hurricanes with female names are more fatal because people subconsciously assume that they are less dangerous. Though I’d bet people would evacuate pretty quickly for Hurricane Solange.

monologue: The NRA is accusing a Texas gun rights group of going too far after the group has posted YouTube videos of their members walking into restaurants with semi-automatic rifles. The NRA saying you’ve gone too far is like Johnny Depp telling you you’re wearing too many scarves.

monologue: Donald Sterling is now facing another lawsuit after a former aide filed for sexual harassment yesterday. Apparently, he told her she was so sexy that he wouldn’t mind if she brought black guys to Clippers games.

monologue: Yesterday French President Francois Hollande announced that he will be having two consecutive dinners on Thursday night in order to keep President Obama and Vladimir Putin separate. It’s an old trick he learned from having a wife and a mistress.

monologue: We bring back a POW, Sgt. Bowe Bergdahl, from Afghanistan and to get him back we traded five Taliban thugs. And now everybody's gone crazy. People say it's the most controversial trade that has taken place since NBC traded me here to CBS.

monologue: Last week a 13-year-old girl became the youngest female to climb Mount Everest. She didn't mean to. She was just texting her friend and the next thing she knew she was on top of Mount Everest.

monologue: The co-founder of Burt's Bees was forced out of the company for having an affair with an employee. He says everyone should mind their own beeswax.

monologue: You want more? Hey, the co-founder of Burt's Bees was forced out of the company for having an affair with an employee. He was caught during a sting operation.

monologue: This summer marks the 75th anniversary of Little League Baseball. Or to put it in Little League terms, six innings.
