Andrew Cuomo a package of rice cakes. Cuomo would give Brown some chicken-wing sauce if the Kings win. That's just crap in their pantries that no one ate.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: French President Francois Hollande will host two dinners tomorrow night, the first one for President Obama, followed by one for Vladimir Putin. Hollande was pretty worried about keeping them separate. Then his girlfriend and his mistress said, “You'll figure it out.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A Republican candidate for Congress in Arizona, who is white, recently changed his name to Cesar Chavez to appeal to Latino voters. It backfired when Arizona’s governor immediately deported him.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The World Cup starts next week. A wildlife center in China says that its baby panda will correctly predict the outcome of the World Cup games. When asked what will happen, the panda said, “None of the stadiums will be ready and all the games will be canceled.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: There are rumors that Robert Pattinson from the "Twilight" movies may be the next Indiana Jones. If there is one thing I want with my rugged action heroes, it's a little bit of sparkle!

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I think Robert Pattinson would make a great Indiana Jones. Instead of searching for the lost ark, he could go searching for a deal on moisturizer.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Instead of battling Nazis, Pattinson could battle flyaway bangs.

monologue: Today is National Cheese Day. A lot of celebrities are very excited. There's Monterey Jack Nicholson. Rush Limburger. Brie-oncé. Mozzar-Ellen DeGeneres. And Parma-Sean Connery.

name: David Letterman
monologue: CBS is trading me for five Taliban prisoners.

monologue: Last night the Los Angeles Kings won game one of the Stanley Cup finals in overtime. Fans in L.A. went crazy after they heard about it this morning at work.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Donald Sterling has agreed to sell the L.A. Clippers for $2 billion. Let that be a lesson to your kids. If you make a racist remark to your mistress, you will get a check for $2 billion.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: When asked about criticism from Hillary Clinton, Russia's President Putin said he doesn't like to argue with women. Putin is either being a misogynist, or else ladies he's the perfect catch.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Japanese clothing company has been criticized for labeling United States sizes skinny, fat, and jumbo. After a huge outcry they changed them to "small, medium, and American."

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Tonight the Miami Heat and the San Antonio Spurs faced off in Game 1 of the NBA Finals. It’s the NBA’s annual contest to determine whose city will be set on fire.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A Danish firm has developed an underground beer fridge called the eCool that takes advantage of underground conditions to keep beer cold. So congratulations, I guess, for inventing the “hole.”

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Scientists in Australia have rediscovered a bat species that was originally thought to be extinct for over 120 years. And thanks to the quick reflexes of one of the scientists, it’s extinct again.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The NFL just released a logo for Super Bowl 50 that features the number instead of the standard Roman numeral. The Roman numeral is just "L." They say it's a "Loser."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Now that the Super Bowl 50 logo uses just the number and no Roman numeral, people in Rome are saying, "Whew. Now we know what number it stood for."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A company in Japan says it will start selling human-like robots that can babysit your children. That story again: Japan is making a robot that can turn on a TV.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The robot babysitters apparently keep your kids quiet by making them hide in fear.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Everyone in Los Angeles is very excited. We're celebrating last night's victory in Game 1 of the Stanley Cup finals. Everyone in Los Angeles is now pretending they watch hockey.

monologue: The game went into overtime. L.A. hockey fans were very tense. More tense than Donald Sterling at the Apollo. More tense than the countries on the edge of Russia. More tense than Bruce Jenner's face.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Donald Sterling says he won't sue the NBA for forcing him to sell the Clippers for $2 billion. Apparently he decided this after a short meeting where someone explained to him that he was getting $2 billion.

monologue: Disney announced they're making a live action "Beauty and the Beast." Of course we're all familiar with the story. An attractive woman falls for a horrible monster and then forces him to sell his NBA team for $2 billion.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night was Game 1 of the NBA Finals between the Miami Heat and the San Antonio Spurs. The air conditioning stopped working during the game, which made it feel like 90 degrees inside. name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: That’s right, LeBron James sat on the bench for the final four minutes of the game. And what’s crazy is his teammates still kept passing him the ball.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I can’t believe how hot it got during that game. It was so hot that even the LOSING team dumped Gatorade on its coach.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tomorrow is the Belmont Stakes. California Chrome will try to become the first horse in 36 years to win the Triple Crown. And he's going to have to do it without air conditioning.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is a great day here in Los Angeles. Gay Pride Weekend starts today, and Sunday night right here on CBS is the Tony Awards. Coincidence?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The new Tom Cruise movie opens today. It's called "Edge of Tomorrow." Tom Cruise is an intergalactic warrior fighting to save our planet from aliens. I have no idea who he plays in the movie.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Edge of Tomorrow is about a guy who's forced to relive the same thing over and over and over again, day after day after day. I can't relate at all.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today's a great day for Sweden. It's their "National Day." It's the day Sweden celebrates independence from Denmark. Sweden's about 400 miles from Russia. That means they've still got a few years before Putin gets to them.

name: David Letterman

monologue: A new show premieres Saturday night on the Learning Channel. If you know anything about me, you know I'm always watching the Learning Channel. I want to learn something!

monologue: Today, Lay’s announced that cappuccino is one of the finalists for their new chip flavor contest. And if you think that sounds bad, wait until you try Starbucks' new Sour Cream and Onion Latte.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama called German Chancellor Angela Merkel yesterday to talk about improving relations with our country after this latest spying scandal. Obama made her a pretty good offer. He said, "Look, we'll stop spying if we can borrow your soccer team."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Speaking of Obama, yesterday Congressman Raul Labrador said that impeaching President Obama isn't a good idea, because, quote, "no one wants President Joe Biden." And that's when Biden realized why Obama picked him as a running mate.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I just saw that minor league baseball players have filed a class-action lawsuit to demand better pay — as opposed to the OTHER way they could get better pay: being better at baseball.

name: David Letterman
monologue: People love the new Pope, but I think it's safe to say he's gone crazy. Now he's thinking about doing away with celibacy for priests. Are you like me? Are you thinking "Real Housewives of the Vatican?"

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Today is the 30th anniversary of the National Minimum Drinking Age Act, which raised the drinking age to 21. Also turning 30 today: a 16-year-old boy, according to his fake ID.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A federal judge ruled yesterday that California's version of the death penalty is unconstitutional. Apparently the difference is California's version has avocado on it.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: According to a new report, 81 percent of people would cheat on their partner if there were no consequences, while 19 percent of people are pretty sure this is a test.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Even though both Israel and Hamas fired on one another during the five-hour humanitarian period yesterday, the U.N. secretary general said both sides "mostly respected" the cease-fire. That's like leaving the house without pants and saying you're "mostly dressed."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: This week, our pal Rob Ford faced off against his four challengers in a debate for Toronto mayor. His opponents were, of course, pretty critical of his performance, but Ford said, "Hey, my record slurs for itself."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Chris Christie warned against presidential candidates running too soon. Then earthquake experts warned Chris Christie against running at all. "Cities just aren't equipped to deal with it."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama said that his strategy for foreign policy is to be patient and determined. Which is also his strategy when it comes to Biden's bedtime.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: There are reports that Amazon is coming out with a new service for the Kindle that will be like a Netflix for books. You can look at a bunch of different books but you don't have to buy them. Or, as Barnes & Noble calls that, "Our business model."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's not only David Hasselhoff's birthday, it's also the birthday of Angela Merkel, the chancellor of Germany. One is Germany's most powerful leader, but is not afraid to look feminine. And the other one is Angela Merkel.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for a man in Brazil. He's 126 and has been called the world's oldest person. He says the highlight of his life was playing goalie for Brazil in this year's World Cup.

name: David Letterman
monologue: President Kennedy said let's put a man on the moon, and by God, 10 years later we put a man on the moon. Yesterday was the 45th anniversary. Nowadays a big deal for us is we combined the croissant and the doughnut to get a cronut.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Star Wars fans are very upset that the story line of the upcoming new "Star Wars" movie has been leaked. Apparently the movie starts with R2-D2, Chewbacca, and Han Solo all waking up in Vegas.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Officials are concerned that people in Los Angeles are too apathetic about the drought. We're not doing anything about it. Of course, that will change next week when we announce that the drought is killing all the marijuana crops.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden is back in the news. He says the military at the NSA often shared nude photos that Americans had emailed to one another. So if your girlfriend won't send you naked pictures, just tell her, do it for the troops.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: In a recent interview, President Obama said Joe Biden "would be a superb president." In a related story, Hillary Clinton punched a hole in a door.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: The Chicago Cubs have filed a lawsuit against a man who got into a bar fight while unofficially dressed as the team's mascot. They could tell he wasn’t affiliated with the Cubs because he won.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: According to a new poll, two-thirds of people in Colorado think it should be illegal to smoke marijuana in public, while the other one-third are still laughing at the word "poll."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: President Obama was giving an interview recently, and get this, he said he thought that Joe Biden would be a good president. When asked why, he was like, "Because he'd make me look AMAZING."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Edward Snowden is back with yet another spying scandal. In a new interview, Snowden revealed that NSA employees regularly pass around nude pictures of people they spy on. It got even weirder when German Chancellor Angela Merkel said, "So, vat do you think?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I heard that Rob Ford's nephew is planning to run for a seat on the Toronto City Council. He has an interesting campaign slogan: "I'm adopted!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night, a 105-year-old woman threw out the first pitch at the San Diego Padres game. It got a bit weird when she turned to 50 Cent and said, "Now THAT'S how you throw a baseball!"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A professor from U.C. Berkeley said we are on track for having the worst drought in 500 years. Which explains why Larry King was overheard saying, "This again?"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: You can tell this drought is getting really bad. Today at lunch, my waiter asked if I wanted a glass of water or a future for my children. I took the water.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: There's a lot of speculation about the new iPhone. It's expected to have a larger screen and a better operating system. Yes, the new iPhone will be called last year's Samsung Galaxy.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Netflix is testing a new feature that will allow you to hide what you've been watching. You just click the button and it says, I want to stay married.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A judge wrote an opinion today in favor of Obamacare, saying that getting healthcare from the state or federal government is the same as ordering from Pizza Hut vs. Domino's. I’m not sure I agree. THEIR websites always worked.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Today, Secretary of State John Kerry traveled to Egypt and had to pass through a metal detector before he could meet with officials. Which is ridiculous. Everyone knows he's made of wood.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Today is National Hammock Day. And just like a hammock, I can't get into it.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: The 17-year-old daughter of one of the "Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" was arrested today for DUI and driving on a suspended license. She's expected to receive 12 months of probation and a spinoff.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I saw that Hillary Clinton visited the headquarters of Twitter and Facebook yesterday. Hillary would also have visited LinkedIn, but she already knows what job she wants.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Netflix revealed earlier this week that it now has more than 50 million users — and one actual subscriber. I love Netflix!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A JetBlue pilot was arrested this week and charged with heroin possession. Passengers could tell something was up when, during their flight, he announced, "To your left you'll see the Grand Canyon, and to your right you'll see a fire-breathing dragon."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I just read about this student at MIT who's created a new robot that can play Connect Four. Yes, an emotionless machine that can occasionally sit down and play a board game with you, or as I called that growing up — my Dad.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: These huge white flags were placed on top of the Brooklyn Bridge. And late this afternoon, word came from the FBI that the New York Mets have surrendered.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Happy birthday to England's Prince George, who turns 1 today. The prince’s first birthday party was a little different. His bouncy castle was an actual castle. And the pony rides were on Camilla.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Queen Elizabeth's horse tested positive for morphine and a mix of other powerful drugs. Sources say the queen is in denial. She thinks someone confused her horse's urine sample with Prince Harry's.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: So remember, horses, when it comes to drugs, just say Neigh.

name: David Letterman
monologue: According to the Centers for Disease Control, the largest single transmission of deadly germs is a handshake. You're lucky, because the most popular form of greeting here in New York is the middle finger.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: The New York Times came out in favor of marijuana legalization. Apparently, someone told them that marijuana users are really into "buying papers."

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Supporters of former Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez have released a new font in the style of his handwriting. Although I'm surprised he wrote anything by hand since he was so used to dictating.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A restaurant in New York has created the Rice Burger, which replaces normal burger buns with rice patties. The restaurant also replaces customers with empty chairs.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Last week a man in Florida was arrested for trying to steal sushi that he had shoved down his pants, although I bet the wasabi was punishment enough.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The New York Times published an editorial calling on the federal government to legalize recreational marijuana. They don't really care about weed, it's just the only way they can keep selling papers.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Times said the government should legalize marijuana because the current laws against weed are useless and outdated. Then they said, "You know, like a newspaper."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Game of Thrones announced that it is adding nine new characters for the next season. Aaaaaand they're already dead.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Seventeen siblings from New Jersey just won $20 million in the lottery. When asked how they plan to spend the money, they said, "Remodeling the shoe we grew up in."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The New York Times published its first of a six-part series that calls for federal legalization of marijuana. You remember newspapers, those things we used to read before BuzzFeed asked us which sandwich we were.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The Times editorial board argued, after weighing the pros and cons, that the scale tips in favor of legalizing marijuana nationwide. You know how long it's going to take people to finish The New York Times crossword puzzle NOW?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Comic-Con wrapped up over the weekend in San Diego. If you don't know, Comic-Con is the world's largest gathering of people who know the difference between a modem and a router.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: According to Time magazine, the number of women attending Comic-Con has doubled in the last five years — it went from four to eight.

name: David Letterman
monologue: There's a dating site called OK Cupid. It's for folks who are looking for someone who is just OK.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A new poll shows that younger Americans sympathize less with Israel than older generations did. But then again, most young Americans think Israel is the cat on "The Smurfs."

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A Los Angeles judge has ruled in favor of Donald Sterling’s wife and will allow her to sell the L.A. Clippers. That leaves Sterling in the awkward position of hating a white person.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A company in India is releasing the first-ever “smart shoe” that connects with Google Maps to track your footsteps. “Merry Christmas,” said your wife.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last night was the finale of "The Bachelorette." It came down to two guys, Josh and Nick. But ultimately Andi went with Josh. She said after looking into her heart and doing a lot of soul searching that he was the person she wants to spend the rest of her publicity tour with.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Of course, Nick says he's heartbroken, lonely, devastated, and whatever else he has to say to be the next “Bachelor.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: LeBron James announced that he will wear his original jersey number 23 when he returns to the Cavaliers this season. Of course, it was awkward when he discovered that even HE burned his old Cavaliers jersey.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The TSA is offering a $5,000 reward for the best idea on how to speed up airport security lines. So far the best idea is making a line for people who know what they're doing and another line for people who have never been to an airport before.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: In Siberia locals recently discovered a giant hole in the ground. Now two more Siberian holes have appeared. Scientists don't know what's causing these holes. Astronomers blame falling meteorites. Archaeologists blame underground gas explosions. Fox News blames Obamacare. Mel Gibson blames Jewish people.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Graceland will auction some of Elvis Presley's personal memorabilia. Let's play "Books That Elvis Checked Out." There's "Hound Dog of the Baskervilles." "The Blue Suede Shoes of Madison County." "A Hunka-Hunka Huckleberry Finn." "Fifty Shades of Graceland." "Are You Lonesome Dove Tonight?"

name: David Letterman
monologue: At Times Square they now have people dressed up as superheroes. Over the weekend Spider-Man beat up a cop and was thrown in prison. Today he was in court with his lawyer — Shyster-Man.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Yesterday there was a water main break right next to UCLA. Water was shooting out of the ground for four hours before it was turned off. They say 20 million gallons of water flooded the campus. I didn't even know L.A. had that much water.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: In Washington the House passed a bill today to go forward with a lawsuit against President Obama. Who says Congress can't get anything done? They're suing the president.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: That lawsuit against the president is ridiculous — unless they do the trial on "Judge Judy." Then I'm all for it.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: According to new estimates, Beyoncé and Jay-Z will make $84 million from their world tour. Which is good because 84 million is an easy number to divide by 2.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Cleveland Browns wide receiver Josh Gordon claimed he failed his most recent drug test because he ingested secondhand marijuana smoke. Said Gordon, “That’s right, I smoked some with one hand, and then I smoked some with my second hand.”

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: According to French officials, the gardens at the Louvre have become overrun with rats. Officials later apologized and promised to refer to us as Americans in the future.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Wikipedia is now accepting donations using the online currency Bitcoin. So now you can support information you’re not sure is true with currency you’re not sure is money.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Actor Orlando Bloom threw a punch at Justin Bieber last night during an argument at a night club in Spain. Orlando's hand was pretty sore today, you know, from all the high-fives he got.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Bieber and Bloom got into a fight. Luckily, a stranger broke it up. He said, "Girls, girls, stop it . . . I mean gentlemen."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: In New Jersey a woman dressed like a clown walked away with minor injuries after she crashed her car into a utility pole. Unfortunately, the other 300 people in the car weren't so lucky.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that having a sense of purpose can actually help you live longer — While having a sense of porpoise can help you swim longer.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Everyone's reeling from the big fight between two Hollywood tough guys: Orlando Bloom and Justin Bieber. They engaged in fisticuffs today in Spain. Who won the fight? I think WE did, America.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Orlando approached Justin and started throwing punches. It was brutal. Mascara was flying everywhere. There were no broken bones. But sadly, a few broken nails.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Every great fight needs a great name. What should we call this one? The commotion near the ocean. The girly taunt in the restaurant. The effeminate fray in the café. The not-a-scratch-on-ya in España.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's Arnold Schwarzenegger's birthday. Arnold celebrated quietly at home with his friends and his families.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Congress is now getting ready to take a month off. From what?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Congress is about to head off on their August recess, which seems appropriate. Adults go on vacation, children go on recess.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Congress will take the whole month of August off. From what, exactly, I don't know.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A new study found that most Internet-connected home gadgets and appliances are vulnerable to hackers. It's only a matter of time before your blender steals your credit card number.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Right now, available only in San Francisco, is an app where you can get marijuana delivered right to your door. Whoever pairs this with a pizza delivery app probably will get the Nobel Prize.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Today marks the last day before Congress takes its summer recess. They're taking five weeks off. Five weeks. I hope they can get used to doing nothing.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg told reporters that despite her age she does not plan on retiring and is likely to remain on the court for a while — after which she was immediately traded to the New York Knicks.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A Chinese farmer lost 170 of his prized pigs when lightning struck his barn while he was feeding them. Though on the bright side — instant bacon.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A woman in New Mexico pulled a gun on a Comcast technician because she didn't want to pay her cable bill. Wow! That woman doesn't need HBO. She IS HBO.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: North Korea has opened a summer camp where kids from around the world can swim, play volleyball, and learn about the country's culture. It's the first camp in history where kids tell ghost stories to feel safer.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: I read that PETA is now saying they’ll pay off people’s water bills if they agree to go vegan for 30 days. Or in other words, you can get PETA to pay off your water bill if you can lie for 30 days.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday the House of Representatives voted to sue President Obama for abusing his executive powers. Experts are calling this a meaningless political stunt that's a huge waste of taxpayer money, while Congress is saying, "Yep. That's what we do."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The House voted 225-201 to sue President Obama. That's the bad news. The good news is that Congress actually passed something.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: We're getting more news about the Orlando Bloom-Justin Bieber fight. Apparently the fight was witnessed by Paris Hilton, P. Diddy, and Lindsay Lohan. I'm confused. Did this fight take place in Spain or in 2003?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Today in Las Vegas is the start of the annual "Star Trek" convention. I go every year. I walk up to everyone dressed in a full "Star Trek" costume and say, "May the force be with you."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A woman in Oklahoma called police to complain about the quality of her meth. I'm thinking: How bad could the meth be if it made her high enough to call the cops and complain about it?

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: A Massachusetts man was arrested for illegally keeping over 400 birds in his home. He tried to keep it a secret, but he couldn't keep the birds from tweeting about it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Toronto Mayor Rob Ford is facing criticism for accidentally showing the phone numbers of his supporters in a new campaign commercial. In response, people said, “No biggie — I gave him a fake number, anyway.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Home Depot is now selling 3D printers. You know, so you can print out an employee to help you find stuff at Home Depot.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yeah, Home Depot is now selling 3D printers, which customers can use to print out tools and parts. It's all part of Home Depot's plan to immediately go out of business.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Kia is recalling more than 50,000 cars because of an issue with the steering system caused by the wrong type of adhesive holding together certain parts. Then Kia drivers said, "Wait, these cars are GLUED together?”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a great day for Pope Francis. He released his top 10 tips for feeling happier. I didn't know Popes did that.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Most of the Pope's tips were what I expected, like No. 7, "Respect nature." No. 3, "Be calm." Except No. 1 — start every day by watching the video of Justin Bieber getting punched in face.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Beyoncé's dad, Mr. Beyoncé, is teaching a college course on how to "Become the next Beyoncé." Beyoncé's dad explains the two-step process. Step 1, start a hugely successful girl group and sell millions of records. Step 2, fire the other girls.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: We have the cast of "Orange Is the New Black" tonight. The show features a cast of ruthless women who are constantly at each other's throats. And for once, I'm not talking about "The View."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Orange Is the New Black has helped usher in a new TV trend called "binge watching." Binge watching blends nicely with another trend in America — unemployment.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This is not the first show I have watched about a women's prison. However, it is the first show about a women's prison I didn't have to delete from my browser history.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Happy birthday to President Obama. He turned 53 today, according to his birth certificate. The truth is he's actually 55 years old but Congress blocked his last two birthdays.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Tonight President Obama blew out the candles on the gluten-free broccoli and carrot loaf from Michelle, and then cried himself to sleep. She did let him smell a piece of cake.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: ABC premiered a new show tonight called "Bachelor in Paradise." I'm glad they're finally doing a bachelor show in paradise. Normally they do them in Third-World countries and industrial parks.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Some people criticize ABC for putting shows like "Bachelor in Paradise" on the air. But the truth is you can't always get down to the baboon exhibit at the zoo. Sometimes they need to be brought to you.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Happy birthday to President Obama. He turned 53 today, if you believe the birth certificate.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: President Obama is turning 53 while his face and hair are turning 68. Congratulations to all three of them.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Congress wanted to surprise President Obama on his birthday so they passed a bill.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: The owner of a prominent paparazzi agency is saying he won't use drones to take pictures of celebrities because he has too much respect for them. And by "them" he means the drones.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Tonight is our 100th episode. To celebrate, people sent us flowers and a big cake — which I immediately passed on to Rob Ford and Chris Christie. We couldn’t have done it without them.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Of course, we’re not the only ones celebrating. President Obama turned 53 years old today. Obama blew out his candles and made a wish. But when he opened his eyes, he was still president.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Sesame Street says it may take legal action against people in Times Square who dress up like its characters. Seriously? Look at the people they’d be suing. What do they expect to win in the lawsuit? A flask of whiskey and an IOU to a bookie?

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new iPhone app gives advice to people going through a divorce. So if you’re someone who relies on an app for advice during difficult times, well maybe that's why you're getting a divorce.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It is our president's birthday. It's also the birthday of NASCAR champ Jeff Gordon. Jeff Gordon and President Obama are very different, of course. One's a guy who spent his whole life turning left and is hated by NASCAR fans. And the other one? Jeff Gordon.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I love it when people here in L.A. pretend to know what NASCAR is. They'll say, "Is that the one with the car?" Or: "Do those cars run on gasoline? I can't endorse this. Can't they use Priuses and fuel them with kale?"

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally starts August 4. But times have changed. Now even biker gangs are into recycling. When the motorcycle rally is over, the gangs go around responsibly collecting trash, bottles, and broken teeth.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: These days any group of bikers can call themselves a motorcycle gang. Some gangs are really bad, like Sons of Anarchy. Other gangs are just orthodontists who go up the highway on a Sunday afternoon.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Scrabble is adding 5,000 new words including "chillax" and "selfie." So kids, there's never been a better time to challenge your grandparents to a game of Scrabble.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A Republican congressman has accused Democrats of waging a war on whites. As proof, he pointed to the recent bombing of the kale aisle at a Trader Joe's.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: LinkedIn has agreed to pay a $6 million settlement to employees. Unfortunately, the employees haven't heard about it because like everyone else they automatically delete all emails from LinkedIn.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: This week a giant tortoise was on the loose here in Southern California. Drivers on the freeway were shocked to see something moving so quickly.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: This week 5,000 new words will be added to the Scrabble Dictionary. One of the words is "mix tape." Why add mix tape now instead of back in 1985, when it was actually a thing that existed?

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Scrabble discovers cool words around the same time my mom discovers them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The worst addition to the Scrabble Dictionary is "bromance." That is what two guys who like each other and have a personal relationship are called. No, they're called friends. I blame Facebook. Thanks to Facebook, the word "friend" doesn't mean anything, which left the door open for "Us Weekly" to infect us with "bromance."

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Can we get someone from Scrabble on the show tomorrow? I want to put a stop to this.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Officials from Hamas and Israel have agreed to a 72-hour cease-fire. Of course, we won’t have true peace in the Middle East until there’s a cease-fire that lasts longer than a mattress sale.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: On Friday, a truck on an Indianapolis highway spilled over 45,000 pounds of butter onto the road. The governor called for a clean-up, while Paula Deen called for a national day of mourning.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Paris Hilton and Kim Kardashian have ended their so-called feud after eight years. Then John Kerry said, “Man, that was rough. Now on to the Middle East.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Scrabble is adding more than 5,000 words to its dictionary, including “buzzkill.” As in, "Anyone who reads the dictionary for Scrabble is a total buzzkill."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Buffalo is getting ready to host the National Scrabble Championship this weekend. They weren’t planning to host it, but it was raining and some of the Monopoly pieces were missing.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Last week New York’s Museum of Natural History hosted a sleepover for adults. Sleeping at a museum — or as kids call that, “going to a museum.”

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Earlier tonight I was watching the "CMA Music Festival." It was two hours of country music, big hats, and big belt buckles.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The CMA Music Festival is country music's biggest night — if you don't count the Country Music Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards, the CMT Music awards, and the American Country Awards.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight's CMA Music Festival was held in Nashville — which is a coincidence because I was held in Nashville once.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Keith Urban is the country singer from Australia. I have a difficult time imagining a country music star from Australia. He'd sing lyrics like, "I lost my truck, my dingo eats babies, my boomerang's broke, and Russell Crowe has rabies."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A company has announced a new service where you carpool with strangers. It's a new cutting-edge technology called "taking the bus."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Yesterday photos were leaked of the Dallas Cowboys owner, 71-year-old Jerry Jones, with two much younger women. The photos were leaked by Jerry Jones.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: According to a new survey, 50 percent of people believe that robots will actually create more jobs in the long run. When they heard this, robots said, "Oh, good, they're buying it. They will serve us soon, those fools."

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The San Antonio Spurs have made history by becoming the first team in the NBA to hire a female assistant coach. She is the first woman to get that close to that many NBA players without being a Kardashian.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: A Russian crime ring has stolen 1.2 billion user names and password combinations, which I'm pretty sure is all of them.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The crime ring stole the information from hundreds of thousands of websites. Experts recommend that you change all your passwords just to be safe. I have to say I would almost rather have all my information stolen than to have to change all my passwords.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Here's what I've never understood. Why do leakers expose national security information? Why not leak stuff like the Colonel's fried chicken recipe? I would like to have that.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Last week it was revealed the CIA has been spying on the Senate Intelligence Committee, which is the committee that's supposed to supervise the CIA. Who do these people think they are? Facebook?

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: President Obama's approval rating is now at an all-time low. It's so bad that last night he gave his daughter Sasha a ride to a friend's house and she asked him to drop her off two blocks away.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A 44-year-old mother in New York was arrested after she left her 7-year-old unattended at a Long Island Lego store. Luckily by the time the police found the child, he had already built a better mother.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: Dunkin' Donuts announced they have created their first-ever coffee-flavored doughnut. First ever? Your name is Dunkin' Donuts. They're all coffee flavored! Your name is a recipe for coffee-flavored doughnuts.

name: Seth Meyers
monologue: A man in New Zealand whose pregnant girlfriend threw a knife at him so hard that it became lodged in his skull told reporters he was confident their relationship would continue. I guess it's true what they say: Some people never learn because there's a knife lodged in their skull.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: While speaking at an African leadership summit yesterday, Vice President Joe Biden accidentally referred to Africa as a country instead of a continent. To be fair, most of what he knows about Africa is based on “The Lion King.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new poll found that President Obama's approval rating has hit a new low of just 40 percent. Or as Obama put it, "60 under par!"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: LeBron James reportedly lost a lot of weight since he announced he was returning to Cleveland. When asked how much he dropped, he said, "How much do Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh weigh?"

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Police in Ohio are looking for two women who tried to rob a bakery but left with only two glazed donuts because there was no money in the register. The cops are offering a small reward for information on the women, and a huge reward for info on those doughnuts.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Tonight was the premiere of "Top Chef Duels." I think they're running out of ideas for cooking shows. It turns out that "Top Chef Duels" is just two chefs slapping each other with spatulas.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: Let's play TV shows that are chef shows. There's "How I Minced Your Mother." "Murder She Roast." "Real Hamhocks of New Jersey." "Game of Scones."

monologue: Today is Jamaican Independence Day. Today in Jamaica, everyone spent the day smoking, drinking, and having a great time. Then they remembered it was Independence Day.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: People think everyone in Jamaica smokes marijuana. That's just not true. Some of them eat it.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: A bear was attacking a Russian man, and he was able to repel the attack by playing his Justin Bieber ringtone. The man is OK, and no, the bear is NOT a Belieber.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: You know that button on your cable remote that gives you information about what you're watching? I was watching "Crossfire," hit the button, and it said, "Congratulations, you're our first viewer tonight!"

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: I hit the info button on "America's Got Talent" and it said, "America's got talent, but we hide it and present this instead."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: The Russian government said Edward Snowden can stay for three more years. Or as Obama put it, "Eh, that was gonna be his prison sentence, anyway."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: TMZ has released the transcript from Kanye West's deposition for an assault charge he's facing, and apparently he referred to himself as "the smartest celebrity." And that was after the lawyer said, "Please state your name."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: It seems like every day Kanye says something weird, and every day I end up talking about it and — you know what? He IS the smartest celebrity! We keep talking about him!

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Pope Francis is calling on young people to get off the Internet and start doing something productive with their lives. Teens were like, "Uh, how do you think we saw you say that? We watched it on YouTube, dude!"

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Welcome to those who are visiting LA. We're going to have a good time in beautiful Los Angeles, which has just been named the 16th coolest city in America by Forbes magazine. We finally tied San Jose.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: You know what city Forbes says is the coolest? The No. 1 coolest city in America is Washington, D.C. How did that happen? Did Obama start smoking again?

monologue: Forbes bases its rankings on factors like how many entertainment options a city has. Makes sense. In Washington, between Joe Biden and John Boehner alone, it's like a nonstop Burning Man festival.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I like that Forbes magazine is deciding which city is the coolest. That's like Good Housekeeping naming the snowboarder of the year.

monologue: President Obama is planning to break up his vacation in Martha's Vineyard by returning to D.C. for two days for meetings. Yeah, two days away from his family vacation — or as that's also known, a "vacation." If you’ve been on vacation, then you know.

name: Jimmy Fallon

monologue: Timex announced that it's creating a new smart watch that can track your speed, distance, and GPS. People said, "Does it tell time?" And Timex was like, "I knew we forgot something!"

monologue: I don't know a lot about ninja turtles. I know they're named after artistic Italian men: Michelangelo, Donatello, Madonna.

monologue: And ninja turtles live in the sewers of New York City. If they want to hide out somewhere that New Yorkers never go to, they should try a Mets game.

monologue: I had a pet turtle when I was a kid. He taught me a lot. For instance, he taught me I love the taste of turtle soup.

monologue: The game was so long, even Ken Burns said, “This is just too much baseball.”

monologue: Scientists have figured out how to suppress the appetites of mice. They bring them to a Long John Silver's.

monologue: Rob Ford also said that he is committed to living a healthier life, and his days of going to the liquor store are over. Which would be great, if he weren't addicted to crack.

monologue: Apple announced it will ban two toxic chemicals that are used in the production of iPhones. In a related story, that iPhone in your pocket right now is made of toxic chemicals.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: The Kardashians are outraged that they've been robbed three times this year but the police have not caught the culprits. Kim Kardashian said, "We just want back what's wrongfully ours. We didn't earn that money and we should get to keep it."

monologue: Kobe Bryant and Nike have teamed up to make a Beethoven-themed sneaker. They're motto is "Play basketball like an 18th century deaf German."

monologue: An Oregon man called Portland police Monday to report that traffic was being held up by a chicken attempting to cross a road. Then on Tuesday, he called back to report a priest and a rabbi walking into a bar.

monologue: People are still fighting about immigration. Congress is suing the president. I'm not saying things are bad, but the Middle East just sent diplomats to negotiate peace in OUR country.

monologue: The White House says President Obama won't make any major announcements during his brief trip back to D.C. this weekend. Reporters said, “Isn't THAT an announcement?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Oh this isn’t good. The Secret Service just arrested 13 people in New Jersey who were making counterfeit money. Which got worse when the counterfeiters said, "Are you sure this isn't something a seven-dollar bill can't get me out of?"

monologue: This week a town in Minnesota elected a dog named Duke as its mayor. Yeah, they elected a mayor that pees on the street, sleeps on the floor, and eats out of the garbage. Then Toronto said, "Been there!”

monologue: A new poll found that Rob Ford has fallen into second place in the race for Toronto mayor. Yeah, it’s bad news for Ford, and even worse news for my monologue.

monologue: ABC will air a one-hour special that goes behind the scenes to show how the movie “Frozen” was made. Yeah, they say it’s all part of their plan to ruin the movie for kids.

monologue: It looks like Rick Perry's chances in 2016 might be in trouble. Or as Hillary put it, "One down, four more to go."

monologue: Mr. T reported for jury duty in Chicago last week, but ultimately was not picked for the trial. I guess prosecutors thought he'd show too much pity.

monologue: How about Johnny Football? Anybody see Johnny Manziel for the Browns? I got nothing against the kid but I saw him play last night. I think they ought to change his name to "Johnny Bench."

monologue: Analysts say that President Obama has been ignoring Hillary Clinton's advice for years — which is why we've yet to see him in a pantsuit.

monologue: In response to criticism of its treatment of killer whales, SeaWorld said it will build them a larger habitat. When asked for comment, a killer whale said, "Hey, you know what's a larger habitat? The ocean!"

monologue: In South America a tribe of Amazon Indians has made contact with the outside world for the first time. The tribe was shocked by skyscrapers, cars, and that "Grey's Anatomy" is still on the air.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Off the coast of Russia, a 200-year-old bottle of booze was found in a shipwreck and it is still drinkable. Isn't that amazing? Of course in Russia everything is still drinkable — antifreeze, you name it.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Hillary Clinton is returning to Iowa next month for the first time since her failed presidential run in 2008. Hillary denies just being there for politics. She said, “I love Iowa for their . . . OK, I'm running for president.”

monologue: Missouri Governor Jay Nixon apparently sent the National Guard to Ferguson without letting the White House know first. When he heard he was left out of such an important decision, Obama said, “Holy crap, I’ve been Bidened!”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Yesterday the Clippers' new owner, former Microsoft executive Steve Ballmer, promised fans that the team will win an NBA championship. He says he has a great strategy for rebuilding the team — Control-Alt-Delete.

monologue: Yankee Stadium says it will start adding metal detectors as a way to beef up security. And then they went back to selling beer and baseball bats to New Yorkers.

name: David Letterman
monologue: You can now buy booze at Starbucks. So apparently my letter-writing campaign paid off.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: Next weekend Los Angeles is holding its first riverboat race. All that's missing is a river in Los Angeles with water.

monologue: Whole Foods has started selling rabbit meat. They're killing them humanely. They're using only rabbits that died of shock after seeing the prices at Whole Foods.

monologue: The man who created the first Internet pop-up ad now says he's sorry. The man also says that a 15-minute call to Geico could save you 15 percent on car insurance.

name: Conan O'Brien
monologue: In South America, a tribe of Amazonian Indians have made contact with the outside world for the first time. Their first words were, "What happened to Bruce Jenner's face?"

monologue: Yesterday Egypt's foreign ministry called on the United States to show respect for the rights of protesters in Ferguson, Missouri. Yeah, Egypt said that. Man, talk about living in glass pyramids.

monologue: A new study found that it costs $245,000 to raise a child until age 18. Or about $600 if you just give them an iPad.

monologue: A man in Massachusetts was arrested this week for breaking into a family’s house after a night of drinking and passing out in their living room. Or as most people in Boston call that, “Uncle Mike's here.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: SeaWorld just announced that it will soon double the size of its killer whale habitats. The whales say it's almost as good as their previous tank — the ocean.

name: David Letterman
monologue: Summer is nearly over and it's back-to-school time. If you can, send your kids to college so they get a degree and at least then they will know what kind of work they're out of.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Rob Ford is running for mayor in Toronto, and some people think he’s still on drugs. So yesterday one of the candidates facing Ford challenged him to take a drug test before the election. Then Ford said, “Sweet! I love testing out drugs! Let’s go!"

monologue: It seems everyone’s upset with President Obama. Congressman Paul Ryan claimed that Americans are having buyer's remorse about President Obama. I think they might be right because today I saw Obama just standing next to an ice cream maker and a Bowflex.

monologue: Hulk Hogan and David Hasselhoff are going to be starring in a new movie together. The film's expected to be released in June . . . of 1985.

monologue: A medical marijuana store in California has a new iPhone app that lets people get marijuana delivered to their door. The first step: remembering where you put your iPhone. The app is called, "I Know a Guy."

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Disney's stock just reached a new high this week of $90.37 a share. That's when you know tickets to Disney World are too expensive — when it's actually cheaper to own part of the company.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Not quite as good news for the pet supply chain PetSmart, which may soon be sold to a larger company. Or as they told their employees, “Your jobs are going to a farm upstate.”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A new study found that having a big wedding boosts your chance of having a good marriage. While having a destination wedding boosts your chance of having friends who hate you.

monologue: The Duggars from “19 Kids and Counting” just announced that their daughter Jill is expecting her first child. In a statement, the Duggars said, “We’re excited to meet the baby and welcome him into our army — family! We mean family.”

name: David Letterman
monologue: Did you hear about the earthquake in California's Napa Valley? That's wine country. The Red Cross now says they want some donations of Merlot.

monologue: How about the Emmy Awards last night? Almost every show on TV was nominated for an Emmy, and once again I'd just like to say it's an honor to be ignored by your peers.

monologue: Last night was the 66th annual Emmy Awards. An night of which all of television makes beautiful, sweet love to itself.

For those of you too young to know, music videos are something MTV used to play before it turned into a network for pregnant teenagers.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The VMAs are a chance for all of the former Disney stars to show up with their new tongue piercings.

monologue: A rare copy of Action Comics No. 1, which was the first published appearance of Superman, just sold on eBay for $3.2 million. That's a lot of disposable income. To buy a comic about Superman, you have to be as rich as Batman. I think that means Superman wins, right?

monologue: You can now buy a pack of beer containing 99 cans. A 99-can pack of beer. Who says America has lost its competitive edge?

monologue: According to a report from the United Nations, the damage from global warming could be irreversible. It's clear we need to do something. We need to give the Earth the ice bucket challenge.

monologue: It's Labor Day weekend. Labor Day, of course, is a holiday where people take three days off from being unemployed.

name: Jimmy Kimmel

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: If Rob Ford doesn't win re-election, I'm going to try to book him to perform at our office holiday party.

monologue: According to an anthropologist from the University of Hawaii, who spent years studying this, Hello Kitty is not actually a cat. I hope the anthropologist was studying other stuff, too.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: The anthropologist said she was preparing for a museum exhibit and according to the company that makes Hello Kitty, she is not a cat. She is a cartoon character. And a little girl. But not a cat. That makes as much sense as Hasbro announcing that Mr. Potato Head wasn't a potato.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Hello Kitty is a cat. I don't know why they would take that position. Maybe there's a translation issue.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's Labor Day. How do we celebrate? Immigrant working. It's the day we say "Thank you" to the typical American worker. So, "Gracias."

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: It's a big holiday today. President Obama spent the day golfing. Then he remembered it was a holiday.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: The weather is changing in L.A. It is hot here. How hot is it? Just yesterday, the cloud started raining nude celebrities.

monologue: In case you haven't heard, there are nude celebrities all over the Internet. I never thought I'd see the day. Someone hacked "the cloud." The cloud is something I don't really understand. It's like whatever language Honey Boo Boo speaks.

name: Craig Ferguson
monologue: I'm telling you, Hollywood hasn't been rocked like this since the great kale shortage.

monologue: The man who released the nude photos of celebrities is admitting he's on the run. However, he's been given asylum by a shadowy group known only as “guys.”

monologue: Justin Bieber was arrested and charged with assault after his vehicle hit a mini-van. On the plus side, it was the first hit he's had in a while.

monologue: Happy birthday to Keanu Reeves. He turned 50 years old today. He announced his next movie, "Bill and Ted's Excellent Prostate Exam."

monologue: In Los Angeles we got our first Dunkin' Donuts shop. I can think of one reason why Dunkin' Donuts might not be successful here. It's the people of Los Angeles. They'll say, "Do you have kale doughnuts?" "Is it organic?" "Were these doughnuts raised humanely?"

name: David Letterman
monologue: What an awful day today. It's 90 and insufferable. No, wait a minute. That's me.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Welcome to The Tonight Show. I'm your host, former iCloud user Jimmy Fallon.

monologue: Over the weekend a hacker got into Apple’s iCloud and leaked nude photos of a number of celebrities, including Jennifer Lawrence and Kim Kardashian. Jennifer wants to sue the hacker for damages, while Kim wants to pay the hacker for his trouble.

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: Texas Senator Ted Cruz has invited President Obama to play golf on the U.S.-Mexico border. Cruz thought it was a funny way to point out problems the president hasn't fixed yet. While Obama said, “So are we playing or not?”

name: Jimmy Fallon
monologue: A woman in Mexico claims that she turned 127 years old over the weekend. She says she’s still pretty happy, but worried that she's still single and almost in her 130s.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: I had a relaxing Labor Day weekend. It was a big weekend at the barbecue grill. I made Italian sausage with peppers and onions. And I ate and I ate. The object of Labor Day is to eat so much that I feel like I'm going into labor.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Nude photos of Jennifer Lawrence and other female stars were leaked online over the weekend. I think you can tell how good or bad a person you are based on how many seconds you wait to Google Jennifer Lawrence nude after hearing the news. Anything under 60, you're going to hell.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Early reports suggest that the culprits obtained photos by hacking into the Internet cloud through Apple's iPhone app. Apple is denying that. They're claiming hackers broke in by finding out email passwords. I think the CEO of Apple should be forced to apologize in the nude.

name: Jimmy Kimmel
monologue: Next week they're expected to announce a new iPhone with a virtual wallet. Apple is believed to be partnering with American Express. The wallet would replace having to carry credit cards around. You can lose your naked pictures and all your money in one easy step.

name: Seth Meyers
